issues.quote: Three western wood-warblers perch across a deciduous branch hung with round red berries

metadataIssues.evidence: 1827 is the start of the whole double elephant folio (Commons gives 'between 1827 and 1838'). Plate 395 belongs to the last part of the series and depicts species from Townsend and Nuttall's 1834-36 western expedition, so it cannot date from 1827. proposals.imageObservation: A folio plate, 'No. 79 / PLATE CCCXCV', with wide blank margins: six small warblers perch on a leafy branch hung with round red fruits, several of them split open. Top left is a blue-grey bird with a yellow crown patch and yellow throat; a plainer pale bird faces it at the right; two yellow-headed birds occupy the middle; and two boldly black-and-white striped birds sit at the lower right and bottom. Three species are named in the engraved caption below.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Spot-check of an earlier 'fabricated-fixed' rewrite; the rewrite is broadly right but undercounts the birds. I verified the count at magnification. The Townsend/Nuttall provenance of these three species is standard and the Commons imageDescription confirms the three species named. 'Round red berries' is fine as far as it goes, though several of the fruits are split open showing seed — spindle-like rather than plain berries.

proposals.title: I. Lazuli Finch - 2. Crimson-necked Bull-Finch - 3. Gray-crowned Linnet - 4. Cow-pen Bird - 5. Evening Grosbeak - 6. Brown Longspur (Plate 424)

proposals.imageObservation: A hand-coloured folio plate on a large cream sheet with wide margins: seven finches perched on one bare, budding branch — a blue-winged Lazuli finch at top right, a crimson-throated bullfinch below it, a brown streaked bird at the left, a grey-crowned pink-flanked linnet at the right, a pale bird with a bold black-and-white wing at the centre, a yellow-and-black Evening Grosbeak at lower left and a brown streaked longspur at lower right. proposals.reviewerNotes: This one carried a prior 'accurate' verdict; the only thing I found against it is the bird count, which is genuinely seven. If the original wording was meant as 'six species', a reviewer might prefer to leave it — but as written it counts birds. I did not touch the second sentence: plate 424 does sit near the end of the 435-plate folio and the western-species point is consistent with the birds named. My identification of the centre bird as a second Evening Grosbeak is an inference from its bill and wing pattern, not from a source, so a reviewer may want to check it before applying.

proposals.title: Great Horned Owl (Plate 61)
proposals.currentDescription: A pair of great horned owls perches on a lichen-covered branch in Plate 61 of John James Audubon's Birds of America, their prominent ear tufts erect and yellow eyes directed toward the viewer. The warm brown and buff barring of their plumage is finely graduated against a pale ground, showing the Havell workshop's control of tonal colour printing. The plate is one of the larger raptors in the series and presents both birds nearly face-on to emphasise the species' intense, forward-facing gaze.
proposals.proposedDescription: A pair of great horned owls perches on a lichen-covered branch in Plate 61 of John James Audubon's Birds of America, their prominent ear tufts erect and yellow eyes directed toward the viewer. The warm brown and buff barring of their plumage is finely graduated against a pale ground; the plate was engraved, printed and coloured in Robert Havell's London workshop, and the caption identifies the two birds as male and female. Both are turned nearly face-on, emphasising the species' forward-facing gaze.

issues.quote: showing the Havell workshop's control of tonal colour printing
issues.problem: The Birds of America plates are engravings with etching and aquatint, printed and then coloured by hand in Havell's workshop; describing the colour as printed misstates the technique.
issues.evidence: image - the engraved credit at lower right reads 'Engraved, Printed & Coloured by R. Havell'; knowledge - the double elephant folio plates were hand-coloured

proposals.imageObservation: Two great horned owls on a lichen-hung branch, ear tufts erect, both facing the viewer with yellow eyes; finely barred grey-brown and buff plumage on a plain cream ground. Engraved captions: plate number top right, 'Great Horned Owl / STRIX VIRGINIANA / Male 1. Female 2.' below, with the Audubon and Havell credit lines at the lower left and right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Spot-check of a prior 'minor-fixed'. Everything else holds - plate 61 is confirmed by the sheet's own 'No. 13' fascicle marking and the plate number, and the pair/posture description matches. Only the printing-technique clause was reworded; if the reviewer prefers, 'coloured by hand' could be said explicitly.

proposals.title: Columbia Jay (Plate 96)
proposals.currentDescription: A male and female Columbia Jay (Corvus bullockii) display their rich blue plumage and long, graduated tail feathers as they perch on leafy branches in this striking double-page composition. The birds' prominent crests and elongated tails give the plate an ornamental quality unusual among Audubon's passerine plates. Plate 96 of John James Audubon's Birds of America, held at the University of Pittsburgh.
proposals.proposedDescription: A male and female Columbia Jay (Corvus bullockii) perch on leafy branches, their deep blue plumage and very long graduated tails running down the sheet; the engraved caption below names them 'Male 1. Female 2.' Plate 96 of John James Audubon's Birds of America, from the copy held at the University of Pittsburgh.

issues.quote: in this striking double-page composition
issues.problem: The plate is a single double-elephant-folio sheet, not a double-page spread; there is no gutter or second leaf.
issues.evidence: image - one sheet, single plate number XCVI, caption centred at the foot

issues.quote: striking
issues.problem: Empty intensifier.
issues.evidence: house style

proposals.imageObservation: A single folio plate: two long-tailed blue jays with black crests perch on a leafy branch, the upper bird bending down, the lower spreading its wing, tails of four or five very long feathers trailing. Engraved caption below: 'Columbia Jay / CORVUS BULLOCKII / Male 1. Female 2.'; 'PLATE XCVI' at upper right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Ledger says minor-fixed, but the 'double-page composition' claim survived that pass. Species name, sexes and plate number are all legible in the plate itself. I dropped the 'ornamental quality unusual among Audubon's passerine plates' clause as unsupportable subjective comparison, though it is harmless if the reviewer prefers to keep it.

proposals.title: Studio Interior
proposals.currentDescription: William Merritt Chase (American, 1849-1916). Studio Interior, ca. 1882.
proposals.proposedDescription: A woman in a white dress and bonnet sits on a bench in the artist's studio, looking down at a large open portfolio propped on a blue patterned rug. Behind her the walls are crowded with framed pictures, hanging plates, a mandolin and a plaster bust, and a carved dark cabinet holds brushes and vases; a potted palm stands in a brass planter at the left. Oil on canvas, about 1882, 71.2 by 101.9 cm, in the Brooklyn Museum.

issues.quote: William Merritt Chase (American, 1849-1916). Studio Interior, ca. 1882.
issues.problem: The whole description is a scraped museum credit line. It says nothing about what the picture shows, which is what house style asks the first sentence to do.
issues.evidence: catalogue record - the text is a verbatim copy of the Commons imageDescription's opening clause

proposals.imageObservation: A studio interior: a woman in a white dress and bonnet sits on a bench looking down at a large open portfolio propped on a blue patterned rug; the walls are crowded with framed pictures, hanging plates, a mandolin and a plaster bust, a carved dark cabinet holds brushes, vases and small pictures, and a potted palm stands in a brass planter at the left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Nothing in the existing text is false, which is why the verdict is minor and not major - the artist dates, title and ca. 1882 all match Commons. The medium, dimensions and Brooklyn Museum ownership in my replacement come verbatim from the Commons imageDescription and match realDimensions in the record.

proposals.title: 1872 Vereshchagin Triumphierend anagoria
proposals.currentDescription: Set in Samarkand's Registan square, a victory ceremony unfolds before the great madrasa portals while Russian soldiers' heads stand impaled on poles in the foreground. Vereshchagin pairs the splendour of Timurid tilework with documentary atrocity, a recurring strategy of his Turkestan cycle.
proposals.proposedDescription: Set in Samarkand's Registan square, a victory ceremony unfolds before the great madrasa portals while Russian soldiers' heads stand impaled on poles in the foreground. Vereshchagin pairs the splendour of the madrasa's tilework with documentary atrocity, a recurring strategy of his Turkestan cycle.

issues.quote: Timurid tilework
issues.problem: The building shown is the Sher-Dor Madrasa - identifiable by the tiger-and-sun mosaics above the arch - built in the 17th century under the Ashtarkhanids, not in the Timurid period.
issues.evidence: image (tiger-and-sun spandrels) plus knowledge of the Registan ensemble; only the Ulugh Beg madrasa on the square is Timurid

proposals.imageObservation: A sunlit square before a tall tiled madrasa portal flanked by minarets and ribbed domes, its spandrels carrying the tiger-and-sun mosaics of the Sher-Dor. A dense crowd of turbaned men, camels, horses and dogs fills the foreground, and tall poles rising among them carry severed human heads.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Ledger said accurate and the substance holds: the Commons image description confirms the Registan setting and the impaled heads of Russian soldiers, and the poles with heads are visible rising through the crowd. Only the word 'Timurid' is changed. If the reviewer prefers, 'Timurid' could be replaced with 'seventeenth-century' rather than dropped.

proposals.title: Self-portrait
proposals.currentDescription: Leighton shown bearded in the red robe and President's chain of the Royal Academy, a fragment of the Parthenon frieze behind him. Oil on canvas painted in 1880 by invitation for the Uffizi collection of artists' self-portraits in Florence, where it remains.
proposals.proposedDescription: Leighton shown bearded in the scarlet gown of an Oxford honorary doctorate, wearing the chain and medal of the President of the Royal Academy, a cast of part of the Parthenon frieze behind him. Oil on canvas painted in 1880 by invitation for the Uffizi collection of artists' self-portraits in Florence, where it remains.

issues.quote: the red robe and President's chain of the Royal Academy
issues.problem: The scarlet gown is Oxford academic dress (Leighton's honorary doctorate of 1879), not Royal Academy regalia; only the chain and medal belong to the Presidency of the Royal Academy.
issues.evidence: web:https://chronicle250.com/1880 | describes the picture as showing 'the chain and medal of office of the president of the Royal Academy, the gown of an Oxford Doctor of Common Law'; Commons also categorises the file under 'Academic dress of the University of Oxford in portrait paintings'

proposals.imageObservation: Half-length self-portrait of a grey-bearded man in a voluminous scarlet gown with black velvet facings, a gold medal on a chain at his breast, in front of a pale relief frieze of horsemen.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The Uffizi commission, the date and the Parthenon frieze are all confirmed (the frieze is a cast Leighton kept in his studio, which is why I wrote 'a cast of part of'). Only the ownership of the robe was wrong. Commons categories place the painting in the Uffizi self-portrait rooms, matching 'where it remains'.

proposals.currentDescription: Paul Cézanne, French, 1839–1906 Pine Tree in Front of the Caves above Château Noir, ca. 1900 Watercolor and graphite on cream wove paper 46. 5 x 35.
proposals.proposedDescription: Two pine trunks cut diagonally across the pale rocks below the caves above Château Noir, the forms drawn in graphite and washed in with detached patches of blue, green and rust that leave much of the paper bare. Watercolour and graphite on cream wove paper, about 46.5 by 35.5 cm, made around 1900. The sheet is in the Princeton University Art Museum (anonymous gift, x1941-166).

issues.quote: Paul Cézanne, French, 1839–1906 Pine Tree in Front of the Caves above Château Noir, ca. 1900 Watercolor and graphite on cream wove paper 46. 5 x 35.
issues.problem: The description is a raw museum label pasted in, not prose, and it says nothing about what the sheet shows.
issues.evidence: commons — the imageDescription field is this exact label text ('...46.5 x 35.5 cm. (18 5/16 x 14 in.) Anonymous gift x1941-166').

issues.problem: The dimensions are mangled and truncated in transfer: the source reads 46.5 x 35.5 cm, so the height is given as '35' and the unit is lost.
issues.evidence: commons — imageDescription gives '46.5 x 35.5 cm. (18 5/16 x 14 in.)'.

metadataIssues.proposed: Pine Tree in Front of the Caves above Château Noir
metadataIssues.evidence: commons — the file name begins with the year, which has been parsed as the title; Commons objectName is 'Pin et rochers près des grottes au-dessus de Château Noir' and the label gives the English title.

proposals.imageObservation: A sparse watercolour over graphite on cream paper: two dark pine trunks cut diagonally across pale rock masses, drawn in loose pencil contours and washed with detached patches of blue, green, rust and violet, with much of the sheet left bare.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Everything in my replacement comes from the Commons label already quoted in the record plus the image itself. The title metadata bug ('1900') is worth fixing at the same time — it will read as the work's name everywhere in the site.

proposals.currentDescription: Paul Cézanne, French, 1839–1906 Study of a Skull, 1902–04 Watercolor and graphite on buff wove paper 22. 9 x 31 cm. (9 x 12 3/16 in.
proposals.proposedDescription: A human skull, drawn in graphite and washed in ochre, grey and blue, the dome of the cranium left as bare paper. Watercolour and graphite on buff wove paper, 22.9 by 31 cm, made in 1902-04. It belongs to the Henry and Rose Pearlman Collection, on long-term loan to the Princeton University Art Museum.

issues.quote: Paul Cézanne, French, 1839–1906 Study of a Skull, 1902–04 Watercolor and graphite on buff wove paper 22. 9 x 31 cm. (9 x 12 3/16 in.
issues.problem: The description is a raw museum tombstone label scraped from Commons, broken mid-measurement ('22. 9') and cut off before the closing bracket. It is not a sentence and describes nothing.
issues.evidence: commons - identical to the file's imageDescription label block

metadataIssues.evidence: commons objectName '1902, Cezanne, Study of a Skull' and the label text; the current title is just the year

proposals.imageObservation: A watercolour and pencil study of a human skull seen slightly from the left, the cranium left as bare paper with ochre, grey and blue washes blocked in around it; the sheet's edges are unpainted.
proposals.reviewerNotes: All the facts in the replacement come from the Commons label (Rewald 613 / Venturi 1130, L.1988.62.36); only the first clause is mine, from the image. The catalogue 'title' field being the bare string '1902' is a separate metadata defect.

proposals.currentDescription: Paul Cézanne, French, 1839–1906 Still Life with Carafe, Bottle, and Fruit, 1906 Watercolor and soft graphite on pale buff wove paper 48 x 62. 5 cm. (18 7/8 x 24 5/8 in.
proposals.proposedDescription: Watercolour and soft graphite on pale buff wove paper: a glass carafe and a dark bottle stand behind a loose heap of grapes and round yellow-green fruit on a table, the transparent washes stopping short of the pencil contours so that much of the sheet stays bare. Cézanne made the sheet in 1906, the last year of his life. It measures 48 by 62.5 cm and belongs to the Henry and Rose Pearlman Foundation, on long-term loan to the Princeton University Art Museum.

issues.quote: Paul Cézanne, French, 1839–1906 Still Life with Carafe, Bottle, and Fruit, 1906 Watercolor and soft graphite on pale buff wove paper 48 x 62. 5 cm. (18 7/8 x 24 5/8 in.
issues.problem: This is not a description - it is the museum's tombstone label pasted in raw, cut off mid-sentence with an unclosed parenthesis and a broken number ('62. 5 cm'). It says nothing about what the sheet shows.
issues.evidence: commons - the imageDescription field is the same label text, continuing '...framed: 75.3 x 90 x 3.8 cm ... The Henry and Rose Pearlman Foundation, on long-term loan to the Princeton University Art Museum L.1988.62.47'

metadataIssues.proposed: Still Life with Carafe, Bottle, and Fruit
metadataIssues.evidence: Commons objectName is '1906, Cézanne, Still Life with Carafe, Bottle, and Fruit'; the current title is the leading year, sliced off the file name.

proposals.imageObservation: A watercolour over pencil on pale buff paper: a tall glass carafe and a dark bottle stand behind a loose heap of blue-purple grapes and round yellow-green fruit on a table, with a second table edge below; the washes are transparent and stop well short of the drawn contours, leaving much of the sheet bare.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Nothing here is fabricated - every fact in the pasted label is confirmed by the Commons record. The problem is that it is a label, truncated and malformed, doing duty as a description. All facts in my replacement come from that same Commons label plus the image; 'the last year of his life' follows from the 1839-1906 dates in the label itself.

proposals.title: 2560px-冨嶽三十六景 上総の海路-At Sea off Kazusa
proposals.currentDescription: A woodblock print from Katsushika Hokusai's series Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji (Fugaku sanjūrokkei), created circa 1830–32. This seascape depicts the Kazusa Province coastline in Japan, exemplifying the ukiyo-e tradition with characteristic compositional balance and atmospheric perspective.
proposals.proposedDescription: Two heavy cargo boats with red hulls and pale sails ride a green swell, and a small white Mount Fuji sits on the far horizon between them. The woodblock print comes from Katsushika Hokusai's series Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji (Fugaku sanjūrokkei), made circa 1830-32; the title cartouche and the artist's signature are printed at the upper left. The impression is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art.

issues.quote: This seascape depicts the Kazusa Province coastline in Japan
issues.problem: The print's subject is two large cargo boats under sail with Fuji small on the horizon; the coastline is a thin distant strip. Describing it as a view of the coastline misses everything a viewer actually sees, and the boats and Fuji are never mentioned.
issues.evidence: image — two ships fill the composition; Fuji is a small white cone on the horizon

issues.quote: exemplifying the ukiyo-e tradition with characteristic compositional balance and atmospheric perspective
issues.problem: Catalogue boilerplate that says nothing specific about this print.
issues.evidence: catalogue record — no supporting detail; house style asks for grounded context

proposals.imageObservation: A woodblock print dominated by two heavy red-hulled cargo boats with tall masts and pale sails on a green-blue sea; a small white Mount Fuji sits on the low horizon between them, with a thin strip of coast either side. A title cartouche and the artist's signature are at the upper left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: No fabrication — the description was simply generic. Collection added from the Commons credit line (donated by the Metropolitan Museum of Art) and the 'Japanese prints in the Metropolitan Museum of Art' category; drop that sentence if the project does not want collection claims sourced from Commons categories.

proposals.title: 2560px-Vincent van Gogh - Vissersboten op het strand van Les Saintes-Maries-de-la-Mer
proposals.currentDescription: Beached fishing smacks on the Mediterranean sand at Les Saintes-Maries-de-la-Mer, their masts and rigging picked out in clean primary colour. Made on a five-day excursion from Arles in June 1888, the picture marks Van Gogh's first encounter with the sea in the South of France.
proposals.proposedDescription: Beached fishing smacks on the Mediterranean sand at Les Saintes-Maries-de-la-Mer, their masts and rigging picked out in clean primary colour, with more boats already under sail offshore. Van Gogh drew the boats on the beach during a short stay at Saintes-Maries at the start of June 1888 — his first sight of the Mediterranean — and painted this canvas back in Arles later that month.

issues.quote: Made on a five-day excursion from Arles in June 1888
issues.problem: The canvas was not made on the excursion. Van Gogh drew the boats on the beach at Saintes-Maries and painted this oil back in his studio in Arles in late June; the stay itself also ran from the end of May into the first days of June, not through June.
issues.evidence: web:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saintes-Maries_(Van_Gogh_series) and the standard catalogue account — oil on canvas 65 x 81.5 cm, made in Arles in late June 1888 from sketches taken on the beach

proposals.imageObservation: Four fishing boats pulled up on pale sand, the nearest with a red and white hull and a yellow mast, their spars crossing against a pale green-blue sky; further boats sail on the sea at the right, with surf along the shore. A yellow crate in the foreground carries the signature 'Vincent'.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Carried a prior 'accurate' verdict; the only thing I am changing is where and how the picture was made. Subject, location, palette and the Van Gogh Museum provenance in the record are all sound, and 'June 1888' matches the Commons date. I could not fetch the Van Gogh Museum object page directly (it renders client-side), so the studio-in-Arles point rests on the standard catalogue account rather than the museum's own wording.

proposals.title: 名绘集珍册 9 宋 李迪 春潮带雨
proposals.currentDescription: A Southern Song album leaf depicting a spring tide laden with rain, attributed to the court painter Li Di. Soft ink wash and atmospheric distance reflect the lyrical small-format landscape tradition cultivated at the Hangzhou academy.
proposals.proposedDescription: Breaking waves fill the silk from edge to edge: long swells drawn in grey wash with their crests picked out as pale curling scallops, under a smoky sky and with no land in sight. The album leaf is attributed to the Song court painter Li Di and carries a red collector's seal at the lower right and a title slip reading 春潮帶雨, spring tide bearing rain. It belongs to the National Palace Museum.

issues.quote: Soft ink wash and atmospheric distance reflect the lyrical small-format landscape tradition
issues.problem: The leaf is a study of breaking waves with no landscape and no recession into distance — no ground, hills, trees or receding planes. 'Atmospheric distance' and 'landscape tradition' describe a different kind of picture.
issues.evidence: image — the whole sheet is water and sky, with crests as the only motif

issues.quote: A Southern Song album leaf depicting a spring tide laden with rain
issues.problem: This restates the title rather than saying what is visible (waves, the title slip, the collector's seal).
issues.evidence: image — nothing beyond the title is described

proposals.imageObservation: A horizontal album leaf on silk showing nothing but water: long swells with breaking crests drawn as pale curling scallops against dark ink washes, the sky above worked in smoky grey. A red seal sits at the lower right and a title slip with the characters 李迪 春潮帶雨 is mounted at the right edge.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The Southern Song attribution and the Hangzhou academy connection are plausible for Li Di but are not in the record or the Commons metadata (the Commons date field is empty and the record's year is null), so I reduced the replacement to 'Song court painter', which the Commons category 'Paintings of the Song Dynasty in the National Palace Museum' supports. National Palace Museum comes from the record's provenance.

proposals.title: Bosphorus
proposals.currentDescription: Sailing vessels and a small rowing boat drift on the hazy waters of the Bosporus, their reflections dissolving in a pearly morning mist, while figures rest on the waterfront quay of Constantinople at the right. Aivazovsky painted this canvas in 1878, during one of several extended stays in the Ottoman capital where his marine panoramas attracted considerable patronage. The composition exemplifies his mastery of atmospheric light over water, a quality that made his Bosphorus views among the most sought-after of his later career.
proposals.proposedDescription: Sailing vessels and a small rowing boat drift on the hazy waters of the Bosporus, their reflections dissolving in a pearly morning mist, while figures rest on the waterfront quay of Constantinople at the right. Aivazovsky signed and dated the canvas 1878; he painted Constantinople repeatedly from the 1840s onward and worked for Ottoman patrons, and views of the Bosphorus recur throughout his career.

issues.quote: during one of several extended stays in the Ottoman capital
issues.problem: Asserts that Aivazovsky was in Constantinople in 1878. He visited the city many times between 1845 and 1890, but nothing here places him there in 1878 - a year in which Russia and the Ottoman Empire were at war - and the picture could equally have been painted in Feodosia from earlier studies.
issues.evidence: web search on Aivazovsky's Constantinople visits lists 1845, 1857, 1874 and later trips with Ottoman commissions, but not 1878; the Commons record says only '1878'

issues.quote: a quality that made his Bosphorus views among the most sought-after of his later career
issues.problem: A market claim with no source behind it.
issues.evidence: commons record carries only an auction-house link, no such statement

proposals.imageObservation: A hazy seascape: a two-masted sailing vessel with pale sails lies in mist mid-channel with further ships dissolving behind, a rowing boat with three figures in the left foreground, and at the right an Ottoman waterfront house with a vine-shaded terrace where figures sit; signed and dated lower right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: First sentence is a good, accurate reading of the picture and is preserved verbatim. Only the biographical framing needed loosening. Commons lists the work as in a private collection (Koller auction), which the description sensibly does not claim.

proposals.title: The Seine in Bougival
proposals.currentDescription: The Seine at Bougival, low banks and a pale sky reflected in still water. Sisley painted the riverside in 1876 during the years he worked the villages downstream of Paris, oil on canvas, the broken touch typical of his mature landscapes.
proposals.proposedDescription: A double row of slender trees in early leaf along a grassy bank of the Seine, with a road and a red-roofed building behind them, a few figures on the grass and the towpath, and the river opening at the right under a blue sky of tall white clouds. Signed and dated 1876, from the years Sisley worked the villages downstream of Paris; oil on canvas, in the broken touch typical of his mature landscapes.

issues.quote: low banks and a pale sky reflected in still water
issues.problem: The sky is a saturated blue crowded with tall white clouds rather than pale, and the water occupies a narrow strip at the right with no prominent reflection; the actual subject of the frame - the avenue of trees and the figures on the bank - goes unmentioned.
issues.evidence: image

proposals.imageObservation: A double row of slender trees in early leaf lines a grassy bank; a road runs behind them past a red-roofed building, a few small figures stand on the grass and the towpath, and the river opens at the right under a blue sky filled with tall white cumulus. Signed and dated at lower right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Nothing in the original is provably false - it is a weak rather than a wrong first sentence - so this is a low-severity rewrite for accuracy of emphasis. The Bougival location comes from the catalogue title and the Commons object name and is retained. The date 1876 is legible in the signature.

proposals.title: Hay Stacks
proposals.currentDescription: Two haystacks stand in a stubble field at Moret under a wide sky, casting long shadows across the cut ground. Sisley painted the pair in 1895, working the thatch in broken strokes of gold and russet. The horizon sits low, giving most of the canvas to the changing light overhead.
proposals.proposedDescription: Two haystacks stand in a stubble field under a wide cloudy sky, casting long shadows across the cut ground, with a small figure carrying a pitchfork on the path beyond. Sisley painted them in 1895, working the thatch in broken strokes of gold and russet. The low tree line divides the canvas near the middle, giving the sky as much room as the field.

issues.quote: at Moret
issues.problem: The location is not given by the record, the title or Commons (which tags the place as unknown). Moret is a reasonable guess for Sisley in 1895 but is asserted as fact.
issues.evidence: commons - categories include 'Template Unknown (place)'; no location in the record

issues.quote: giving most of the canvas to the changing light overhead
issues.problem: The horizon sits near the middle: the sky occupies roughly the upper half, not most of the canvas.
issues.evidence: image

proposals.imageObservation: Oil painting: a tall russet haystack (with one or two more cropped at the left edge) on a stubble field, long shadows across the cut ground, a small figure with a pitchfork standing on the path in the middle distance, a low tree line and a high cloudy sky filling roughly the upper half; signed 'Sisley' lower right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Date and signature are consistent with the record. If a catalogue entry places the picture at Moret-sur-Loing, the location can go back; I removed it only because nothing available here supports it.

proposals.title: Grapes and Walnuts on a Table
proposals.currentDescription: A still life of black grapes and walnuts spread on a white cloth, a knife laid across the table edge. Sisley rarely painted still life, making the 1876 canvas unusual in his output, which is dominated by river and village landscapes.
proposals.proposedDescription: A still life of pale green grapes heaped on a metal platter with a few red-cheeked fruits, walnuts scattered across the white cloth beside a knife and a nutcracker. Sisley rarely painted still life, making the 1876 canvas unusual in his output, which is dominated by river and village landscapes.

issues.quote: black grapes
issues.problem: The grapes are pale green-gold (white grapes), not black. This is the first thing the description names.
issues.evidence: image

issues.quote: spread on a white cloth
issues.problem: The grapes sit heaped on a metal platter; only the walnuts lie on the cloth. The description also omits the red fruits and the nutcracker.
issues.evidence: image

proposals.imageObservation: A still life on a white cloth: a large bunch of pale green-gold grapes heaped on an oval metal platter with two or three red-and-yellow fruits, four walnuts on the cloth in front, a knife with a bone handle and a metal nutcracker at the lower right, against a warm red-brown wall; signed 'Sisley' at lower left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The second sentence is correct and preserved verbatim — Sisley's still lifes are genuinely rare. Only the visual sentence needs replacing. Commons categories place the picture in the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, which the description does not claim, so nothing to check there.

proposals.title: Bank of the Seine in Autumn
proposals.currentDescription: The bank of the Seine under autumn foliage, reflections breaking across the water in short horizontal strokes. Sisley painted the riverside subject in 1876, oil on canvas, working in the loose touch he developed alongside Monet in the villages west of Paris.
proposals.proposedDescription: The bank of the Seine in late autumn, bare leaning trunks along the near shore and a small boat with a standing figure out on the pale water, the reflections broken into short horizontal strokes. Sisley painted the riverside subject in 1876, oil on canvas, working in the loose touch he developed alongside Monet in the villages west of Paris. The canvas is in the Städel Museum, Frankfurt.

issues.quote: The bank of the Seine under autumn foliage
issues.problem: The trees in the picture are essentially bare — long leafless trunks and branches with only sparse ochre leaves on the far bank — so 'under autumn foliage' overstates what is shown. The season is late autumn, not the canopy the phrase implies.
issues.evidence: image — bare leaning trunks dominate the left and centre

proposals.imageObservation: A cold-toned riverside: bare, leaning tree trunks along the near bank, a few ochre remnants of leaves on the far trees, a small boat with a standing figure on the pale water, houses and a low hill in the distance; the near bank looks dusted with snow or pale earth.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Date 1876 confirmed (Wikidata Q19820284, Städel inv. 1350, oil on canvas, 46 x 65 cm), despite some Commons categories saying 1879. The Städel attribution is grounded in Wikidata and the Commons categories, so I added it. Only the 'autumn foliage' phrasing changed substantively.

proposals.title: The Road to Hampton Court
proposals.currentDescription: A road running past garden walls towards Hampton Court, figures walking under a high, clouded sky. Painted during Sisley's 1874 stay near London, when he produced a series of nearly twenty views of the non-tidal Thames, oil on canvas, now in the Neue Pinakothek, Munich.
proposals.proposedDescription: A broad road running along the bank of the Thames towards Hampton Court, figures walking on it and a rowing crew out on the water, under a high, clouded sky. Painted during Sisley's 1874 stay near London, when he produced a series of nearly twenty views of the non-tidal Thames, oil on canvas, now in the Neue Pinakothek, Munich.

issues.quote: past garden walls
issues.problem: There are no garden walls; the road is edged by a low wooden post-and-rail fence on one side and by the open river on the other.
issues.evidence: image — zoomed on the left edge: weathered timber posts and rails, grass behind them

issues.quote: figures walking under a high, clouded sky
issues.problem: The river occupies the whole right half of the canvas (with a rowing four on it) and goes unmentioned, which is what the picture is largely about.
issues.evidence: image

proposals.imageObservation: A broad pale road curves along an embankment beside a river; small figures walk on it, a wooden post-and-rail fence runs along the left edge with grass beyond, a long pale building and trees stand across the water at the right, a rowing crew is on the river, and a high sky of pink-grey cloud fills the top half.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The context sentence is sound: Sisley's four-month 1874 English stay produced nearly twenty views of the non-tidal Thames, and the painting is in the Neue Pinakothek (Commons file title; Wikipedia's Sisley/Hampton Court coverage gives the 'nearly twenty' figure).

proposals.title: Vollard avec un foulard rouge
proposals.currentDescription: The dealer Ambroise Vollard wrapped in a red headscarf, the bare head and heavy features set against a warm ground. Renoir painted Vollard, who handled much of his work after 1900, in 1906; oil on canvas, now in the Petit Palais, Paris. The close-keyed reds and softened modelling are typical of the artist's late Cagnes years.
proposals.proposedDescription: The dealer Ambroise Vollard in a red headscarf, his bearded head bowed in profile against a pale grey-green ground. Renoir painted Vollard, who handled much of his work after 1900, in 1906; oil on canvas, now in the Petit Palais, Paris. The warm reds and softened modelling are typical of the artist's late work in the south of France.

issues.quote: the bare head and heavy features set against a warm ground
issues.problem: The same sentence has just said Vollard is 'wrapped in a red headscarf', so 'the bare head' contradicts it — his head is covered. And the ground is a cool pale grey-green, not warm.
issues.evidence: image

issues.quote: typical of the artist's late Cagnes years
issues.problem: In 1906 Renoir was wintering in Cagnes but did not buy Les Collettes and settle there until 1907, so calling a 1906 portrait typical of 'the late Cagnes years' is loose.
issues.evidence: knowledge; catalogue record dates the work 1906

proposals.imageObservation: Bust-length portrait of a bearded, moustached man in profile with his head bowed, wearing a red cloth tied around his head, a brown jacket, white collar and dark tie; the background is a loosely brushed pale grey-green.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The identification, date, medium and Petit Palais location are all supported (Commons credit 'Petit Palais, Paris', date 1806-> 1906 field matches). Only the visual clause needed correcting. If 'bare head' was meant as 'hatless', it still reads as a contradiction next to the headscarf.

proposals.title: Ariko weeps on her boat
proposals.currentDescription: Print 38 from Tsukioka Yoshitoshi's "100 Aspects of the Moon" (Tsuki Hyakusen), a celebrated series of ukiyo-e woodblock prints. The composition depicts Ariko, a character from classical Japanese narrative, weeping in a boat illuminated by moonlight—a poignant moment capturing the intersection of human emotion and natural beauty.
proposals.proposedDescription: A woman with long loose hair kneels in a small boat on choppy water and hides her face in her sleeve, a biwa propped against her shoulder and a poem inscribed in the cartouche above. This is print 38, 'Ariko weeps as her boat drifts in the moonlight', from Tsukioka Yoshitoshi's woodblock series One Hundred Aspects of the Moon (Tsuki hyakushi), published in 1886.

issues.quote: Tsuki Hyakusen
issues.problem: Wrong romanisation of the series title. 月百姿 is Tsuki hyakushi (also given as Tsuki no hyakushi); Commons files the print under 'Tsuki hyakushi 38'. 'Tsuki Hyakusen' is not a reading of the title.
issues.evidence: commons — category 'Tsuki hyakushi 38 (Aliko weeping in boat)'

issues.quote: weeping in a boat illuminated by moonlight
issues.problem: Paraphrases the print's title rather than the print: there is no moon and no moonlight in the image, and the biwa — the attribute that identifies Ariko as a court musician and is the most conspicuous object after the figure — is not mentioned.
issues.evidence: image

issues.quote: a poignant moment capturing the intersection of human emotion and natural beauty
issues.problem: Empty evaluative filler.
issues.evidence: n/a — no factual content

metadataIssues.evidence: commons — date '1886-09' and credit 'Original publication: 1886 Japan'. The series as a whole ran 1885-1892, but this sheet is dated to September 1886.

proposals.imageObservation: A woman with long loose black hair kneels in the stern of a plain wooden boat on choppy grey-green water, hiding her face in her sleeve; a biwa (a short-necked lute) rests against her shoulder, her black robe is patterned with fans and roundels, and a poem cartouche, series cartouche, signature and red seal are set into the upper right and lower right. No moon is shown.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The substantive identification (Yoshitoshi, print 38, One Hundred Aspects of the Moon) is right; only the romanised title is wrong, and the description is otherwise pure paraphrase of the print's own title. If the year field is corrected to 1886 the description should say 1886 too. I left Ariko's story out of the replacement because I could not verify a specific narrative source for her from what I have.

proposals.title: Hope
proposals.currentDescription: تابلوی امید اثر « جرج فردریک واتس » متعلق به ۱۸۸۶ است، در این تابلو امید در قالب زنی مجسم شده که چنگی با تنها یک رشتهٔ سالم در دست دارد. او سرش را نزدیک به آلت موسیقی گرفته است، تا بتواند نوای ضعیف موسیقی برخاسته از تک‌تار سالم را بشنود.
proposals.proposedDescription: A blindfolded woman sits hunched on top of a globe, bending her head to a lyre that has one string left, listening for the sound it still makes. Watts and his assistants painted this version of Hope in 1886; it is in the Tate collection, London.

issues.quote: اثر « جرج فردریک واتس »
issues.problem: Given as by Watts alone; the source records this version as by Watts with studio assistants.
issues.evidence: commons | the file is titled 'Assistants and George Frederic Watts - Hope' and the artist field reads 'George Frederic Watts and workshop'; the credit points to Tate N01640

issues.quote: در این تابلو امید در قالب زنی مجسم شده که چنگی با تنها یک رشتهٔ سالم در دست دارد
issues.problem: The stored text is a scraped Persian caption, so the catalogue carries no English description; it also omits the two defining features of the picture, the globe she sits on and the blindfold over her eyes.
issues.evidence: image | the figure is blindfolded and seated on a globe, neither of which the caption mentions

metadataIssues.evidence: commons | artist field 'George Frederic Watts and workshop'; the Commons file name begins 'Assistants and George Frederic Watts'

proposals.imageObservation: A blindfolded woman in pale green-grey drapery sits hunched on top of a large globe, bare feet tucked under her, bending her head over a lyre from which a single string remains; blue-grey sky and a faint star at the upper left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The Persian caption is factually right about what it does describe (a figure, an instrument with one sound string, her head bent to hear it), so the only substantive problem is the sole attribution to Watts; the language and the omissions are the reason I supplied a replacement. Tate is grounded in the record's credit line, which cites tate-images N01640. I did not state which version this is beyond the 1886 date in the record.

proposals.title: In the Summer
proposals.currentDescription: A dark-eyed young woman sits outdoors in a loose white blouse and striped skirt, her long dark hair pinned back, gazing calmly at the viewer against a lush green background. Painted in 1868 and now at the Alte Nationalgalerie in Berlin, the work casts Renoir's model Lise Tréhot as a summer bohémienne and retains a solidity of form that still recalls Courbet's influence.
proposals.proposedDescription: A dark-eyed young woman sits outdoors in a loose white blouse and red-striped skirt, her long dark hair falling in ringlets over her shoulders and held off her face by a red ribbon, gazing calmly at the viewer against a lush green background. Painted in 1868 and now at the Alte Nationalgalerie in Berlin, the work casts Renoir's model Lise Trehot as a summer bohemienne and retains a solidity of form that still recalls Courbet's influence.

issues.quote: her long dark hair pinned back
issues.problem: Her hair is not pinned up or back - it falls loose in long ringlets over her shoulders and chest, kept off her face only by a red ribbon, and that loose hair is the picture's most conspicuous feature.
issues.evidence: image.

proposals.imageObservation: Oil: a young dark-eyed woman sits on a wooden chair outdoors in a white off-the-shoulder blouse and a red-and-white striped skirt, hands clasped in her lap; her long dark hair hangs loose in ringlets over both shoulders, held off her face by a red ribbon; green foliage behind.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Spot-check of a prior 'minor-fixed' verdict. Only the hair phrase is off; 1868, the Alte Nationalgalerie (also in the record's provenance block), Lise Trehot and the Courbet remark all stand. Small fix - apply only if the ledger cares about this level of detail.

proposals.title: La Balançoire
proposals.currentDescription: A young woman stands on a rope swing in a garden talking with a man seen from behind, sunlight falling in patches of blue and rose through the leaves. Renoir painted it in the summer of 1876 in the gardens below the Moulin de la Galette, oil on canvas, now in the Musée d'Orsay.
proposals.proposedDescription: A young woman in a white dress trimmed with blue bows stands beside a rope swing, one hand on the rope, talking with a man seen from behind in a straw hat; a second man leans against the tree and a small child watches at left, sunlight falling in patches of blue and rose through the leaves. Renoir painted it in the summer of 1876 in a Montmartre garden, oil on canvas, now in the Musee d'Orsay.

issues.quote: A young woman stands on a rope swing
issues.problem: She stands on the ground next to the swing; the swing's plank seat hangs empty at knee height beside her.
issues.evidence: image

issues.quote: talking with a man seen from behind
issues.problem: Two men are present (one seen from behind in a straw hat, one leaning on the tree) plus a small child in the foreground; the description mentions only one figure besides her.
issues.evidence: image

proposals.imageObservation: Oil painting: a young woman in a white dress trimmed with blue bows stands on the ground beside a rope swing, one hand on the rope, the empty swing plank hanging at knee height; a man in a straw hat seen from behind faces her, a bearded man leans against the tree at left, a small child stands at lower left, and figures talk in the sunlit garden behind. Dappled blue and rose light throughout.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Musee d'Orsay confirmed by the Commons categories. I softened 'the gardens below the Moulin de la Galette' to 'a Montmartre garden' because the picture is usually placed in the garden of Renoir's house in the rue Cortot rather than at the Moulin itself; if the original phrasing is preferred it is not badly wrong, only loose.

proposals.title: The Toilet
proposals.currentDescription: A seated nude attended by two servants, one kneeling to dry her foot, the other holding cloth, in a curtained interior. Oil on canvas, 130 by 128 cm, painted between December 1869 and March 1870 and now in the Musée Fabre, Montpellier.
proposals.proposedDescription: A seated nude attended by two servants, one kneeling to fit a green slipper to her foot, the other standing with a large flowered robe held open, against a hung oriental carpet. Oil on canvas, 130 by 128 cm, painted between December 1869 and March 1870 and now in the Musee Fabre, Montpellier.

issues.quote: one kneeling to dry her foot
issues.problem: The kneeling servant is handling a green slipper at the nude's foot, not drying it; there is no towel in her hands and a matching green mule lies on the floor beside her.
issues.evidence: image, plus commons category 'Mules (footwear) in art'

issues.quote: in a curtained interior
issues.problem: The backdrop is a large hung oriental carpet, not curtains — a detail that matters here because the carpet is what makes the picture read as orientalist.
issues.evidence: image, plus commons category 'Orientalist paintings in France'

proposals.imageObservation: A seated nude on a pile of furs; at lower left a Black servant in a yellow headscarf and a striped wrap kneels and handles a green slipper at the nude's foot (a second green mule lies on the floor); at right a woman in a brown-and-white striped dress stands holding up a large dark robe patterned with flowers. The background is a hung red-and-blue oriental carpet. Signed and dated lower left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Medium, dimensions, dates and collection are all confirmed by the Commons record ('Холст, масло. 130 x 128 см. Музей Фабра, Монпелье'; date 'December 1869 - March 1870') and are preserved verbatim in substance. Whether the kneeling servant is putting the slipper on or taking it off is not determinable from the image, so I wrote 'fit ... to her foot' rather than choosing.

proposals.title: Portrait of Edmond Maître
proposals.currentDescription: Bazille's friend Edmond Maître seen in full profile, seated and reading a book in his lap, the ground darkening toward the upper left. Oil on canvas painted in 1869, now in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.
proposals.proposedDescription: Bazille's friend Edmond Maître seen in full profile, seated in a dark suit with a spray of violets at his lapel, a cigarette held up in one hand and the other resting on an open book on a red-draped table, the ground darkening toward the upper left. Oil on canvas painted in 1869, now in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.

issues.quote: seated and reading a book in his lap
issues.problem: The book lies open on a red-draped table in front of him, with his left hand resting on it — not in his lap. The description also omits the cigarette he holds up, which is the most conspicuous thing in the frame after the profile.
issues.evidence: image — open book on a table covered with red cloth; right hand raised holding a cigarette

proposals.imageObservation: A bearded man in strict left profile, seated in a dark suit with a spray of violets pinned to his lapel, holding a lit cigarette up in his right hand while his left hand rests on an open book on a red-draped table at the lower left; a chair back at the right, the background dark at the left and warm brown at the right, signed and dated in red at the upper left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The Commons categories independently describe the sitter as holding a book with the left hand and note the cigarette or cigar, and place the painting in the National Gallery of Art; both are consistent with the image. The signature at the upper left appears to read 1869, matching the record.

proposals.title: View of the Village
proposals.currentDescription: A young woman in a striped dress seated on a stone ledge above the village of Castelnau-le-Lez, the Hérault landscape spread behind her. Oil on canvas, painted in 1868 at the Bazille family property near Montpellier and now in the Musée Fabre.
proposals.proposedDescription: A young woman in a striped white dress with a red sash, seated on the ground beneath a pine above the village of Castelnau-le-Lez, the Hérault landscape spread behind her. Oil on canvas, painted in 1868 at the Bazille family property near Montpellier and now in the Musée Fabre.

issues.quote: seated on a stone ledge
issues.problem: She is sitting on bare earth and grass at the foot of a pine, with her skirt spread on the ground. There is no stone ledge under her.
issues.evidence: image — magnified, the ground beneath the skirt is brown earth with tufts of grass; a rock appears only behind her at the right.

proposals.imageObservation: A dark-haired young woman in a white dress finely striped in pink, with a red sash and a red hair ribbon, sitting on bare earth and grass under a pine at the right, a sprig of flowers in her hands; below and behind her a river, wooded slopes and a sunlit village of pale houses. Signed and dated F. Bazille 1868 at lower centre.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The striped dress is right (fine pink stripes on white, visible when magnified), as are Castelnau-le-Lez, the Herault, the 1868 date, Meric near Montpellier and the Musee Fabre. Only the seat is wrong. I added the red sash because it is the most conspicuous thing in the figure and the description skipped it.

proposals.title: Nature morte au héron
proposals.currentDescription: A dead heron and other birds laid on a table, a study in greys and browns. Oil on canvas, 98 by 78 cm, painted in 1867 and held by the Musée Fabre, Montpellier. Bazille painted it in a Paris studio alongside Sisley, who treated the same heron in his own canvas.
proposals.proposedDescription: A dead heron hangs head-down from a cord tied under a table, its wings spread wide over a white cloth where a magpie and two jays lie. Oil on canvas, 98 by 78 cm, painted in 1867 and held by the Musée Fabre, Montpellier. Bazille painted it in a Paris studio alongside Sisley, who treated the same heron in his own canvas.

issues.quote: A dead heron and other birds laid on a table
issues.problem: The heron is not laid on a table - it is suspended head-down by a cord tied to the table above, wings spread; only the smaller birds lie flat, and they lie on a white cloth. The suspension is the picture's whole armature.
issues.evidence: image - the cord and knot are visible running from the heron's feet up to the table

proposals.imageObservation: A dead grey heron hangs head-down by a cord tied under a dark table, its wings spread wide over a white cloth; a magpie and two jays with blue-barred wing feathers lie on the cloth below it. Greys, browns and white throughout. Signed 'F. Bazille 67' at the lower left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Dimensions (98 x 78 cm), date and the Musee Fabre are confirmed word for word by the Commons imageDescription. The Sisley anecdote is real - Sisley painted the same bird, and his version is also in the Musee Fabre - so I kept that sentence verbatim. The species of the small birds is my reading of the image (the blue-barred wing coverts are diagnostic of jays); if that feels too confident, 'smaller birds' is a safe substitute.

proposals.title: Fisherman with a Net
proposals.currentDescription: A nude male fisherman casting a circular throw-net at the water's edge, his back to the viewer. Bazille painted the canvas in 1868; it later entered the Rau Foundation for the Third World in Zurich, and stands among his experiments with the open-air male figure.
proposals.proposedDescription: A nude male fisherman stands at the water's edge with his back to the viewer, a circular throw-net gathered in his hands; a second nude figure sits on the grass behind him. Bazille signed and dated the canvas July 1868; it later entered the Rau Foundation for the Third World in Zurich, and stands among his experiments with the open-air male figure.

issues.quote: casting a circular throw-net
issues.problem: The fisherman is holding the gathered net at his side, before the cast; no net is in flight.
issues.evidence: image

issues.quote: A nude male fisherman
issues.problem: A second nude figure sits on the bank at right; the description gives the picture only one figure.
issues.evidence: image

proposals.imageObservation: Oil painting: a nude man stands at a grassy river bank with his back to the viewer, a circular throw-net gathered in his hands and hanging at his left side; a second nude figure sits on the grass behind him at right; water lilies in the water at lower left; signed 'F. Bazille juillet 68' lower right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The Rau Foundation, Zurich placement comes from the Commons description ('Фонд Ро для стран третьего мира, Цюрих'). The July 1868 date is legible in the signature and matches the record year.

proposals.title: Studio in the Rue de Furstemberg
proposals.currentDescription: A corner of a sparsely furnished studio with two armchairs and a doorway opening onto a bedroom and a grey winter sky. Oil on canvas, painted in 1865 and held by the Musée Fabre, Montpellier. The room is the studio at 6 Place de Furstenberg that Bazille shared with Monet, in the building that now houses the Musée national Eugène Delacroix.
proposals.proposedDescription: A corner of a studio hung edge to edge with small unframed studies, a black stove burning at the left, a green-covered table and stool in the middle, a green armchair and an open paintbox lying on the floor. Oil on canvas, painted in 1865 and held by the Musée Fabre, Montpellier. The room is the studio at 6 Place de Furstenberg that Bazille shared with Monet, in the building that now houses the Musée national Eugène Delacroix.

issues.quote: a doorway opening onto a bedroom and a grey winter sky
issues.problem: No sky is visible through the doorway in this reproduction — only a green flowered hanging and an indistinct pale area that might be bedding or a lit wall. The 'grey winter sky' is not supported by anything in the image or the record.
issues.evidence: image — the doorway aperture is small and dark, with no window or sky visible

issues.quote: A corner of a sparsely furnished studio with two armchairs
issues.problem: Undersells and mis-frames the picture: the walls are covered edge to edge with the painters' own studies, and there is a lit stove, a draped table, a stool and an open paintbox on the floor. The hung canvases, not the seating, are the subject.
issues.evidence: image

proposals.imageObservation: A studio interior: a black cast-iron stove with a glowing firebox at the left, walls hung with a dozen unframed oil studies (landscapes, a nude, a figure) above a red-brown dado, three small framed pictures below, a table with a green cloth, a wooden stool, a green upholstered armchair, a chair draped in red at the far right, an open paintbox with brushes lying on the floor, and a dark doorway showing a green flowered hanging and a pale patch beyond.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Sentences two and three are kept verbatim and check out: musée Fabre gives inv. 85.5.3, oil on canvas, 80 x 65 cm, the studio shared with Monet until January 1866, at 6 rue/place de Furstenberg above Delacroix's former apartment (fr.wikipedia uses '6, Place de Furstenberg', so I did not treat the address wording as an error). Sources: https://www.museefabre.fr/recherche/musee:MUS_BIEN:3503, https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atelier_de_la_rue_Furstenberg

proposals.title: Venus At Her Birth Attired By The Three Graces
proposals.currentDescription: Venus stands upright on swans amid waves while two female figures above her hold billowing drapery, and a winged putto hovers to one side. The work belongs to West's late mythological output and is recorded through a Sotheby's auction catalogue; no firm date or medium is established in available sources.
proposals.proposedDescription: Venus stands upright on swans amid waves while three female figures above her hold billowing red and white drapery, a winged putto with a bow sits at the lower left and two doves fly in at the right. The work belongs to West's late mythological output and is recorded through a Sotheby's auction catalogue; no firm date or medium is established in available sources, though the canvas carries a painted inscription and date at the lower right.

issues.quote: two female figures above her hold billowing drapery
issues.problem: There are three attendant female figures — one at the upper left in white and two at the upper right — which is also what the title's 'Three Graces' implies.
issues.evidence: image — three attendants; catalogue record title 'Venus At Her Birth Attired By The Three Graces'

issues.quote: no firm date or medium is established in available sources
issues.problem: Defensible for the catalogue sources, but the canvas itself carries a painted two-line inscription with a date at the lower right, so 'no firm date' should not be read as 'the work is undated'.
issues.evidence: image — inscription and a four-digit date at the lower right, too small to read in this reproduction

proposals.imageObservation: Venus stands nude on two large swans in the sea, one arm raised to her hair, a white drape across her hips; three female attendants above and behind her hold up billowing red and white drapery, a winged putto with a bow and a quiver sits at the lower left, and two white doves fly in at the right. An inscription in two lines with a date is painted at the lower right, illegible at this resolution.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The count is the real fix. I magnified the inscription and could not read it reliably — it looks like a signature line over a second line ending in a date around 18-6 — so I described it without transcribing. Anyone with the Sotheby's lot page (in the record's provenance sourceLinks) could settle date and medium properly.

proposals.title: Viktor Vasnetsov. Battle between the Scythians and the Slavs
proposals.currentDescription: Mounted warriors locked in combat, lances raised and horses entangled across the steppe. Vasnetsov painted this Battle of the Slavs and Scythians in 1881, oil on canvas, now in the State Russian Museum, St Petersburg. The subject draws on the Primary Chronicle and the artist's interest in early Russian legend.
proposals.proposedDescription: Mounted warriors locked in combat, one swinging a mace above a rearing black horse, others with raised spears and a red shield, a fallen figure in the grass below. Vasnetsov painted this Battle between the Scythians and the Slavs in 1881, oil on canvas, now in the State Russian Museum, St Petersburg. It belongs to the group of legendary early-Russian subjects he took up around 1880.

issues.quote: The subject draws on the Primary Chronicle
issues.problem: A specific literary source is asserted with nothing to back it; the Scythian-Slav conflict is not a Primary Chronicle episode, and the record and Commons say nothing about a source text.
issues.evidence: catalogue record / commons - no source text named

issues.quote: lances raised
issues.problem: Spears are raised at right, but the central weapon is a mace (bulava), which the description does not mention.
issues.evidence: image; commons category 'Bulawa'

proposals.imageObservation: Oil painting: mounted warriors fighting on the steppe - a rider swinging a mace over a black horse, another with a red rectangular shield and raised spear, more horsemen with spears at right, a dead or fallen figure lying in the grass at lower left. Signed lower left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Russian Museum holding is supported by the Commons categories ('History paintings in the Russian Museum'). I replaced the Primary Chronicle attribution with a general statement about his early-Russian subjects rather than substituting another source I cannot verify.

proposals.title: Богоматерь с младенцем в розах
proposals.currentDescription: The young Mary stands by a low stone wall, the Christ Child against her, roses banked behind them. Bruni painted this oil, 'Madonna with Child in Roses', in 1843; it measures roughly 64 by 40 cm and is held in the State Tretyakov Gallery, Moscow.
proposals.proposedDescription: The young Mary, veiled and in a red robe and blue mantle, stands behind a low stone ledge with the Christ Child standing beside her; both hold a stem of white lilies, and pink roses climb up the sides and across the foreground. Bruni painted this arched-topped oil, 'Madonna with Child in Roses', in 1843; it measures about 65 by 40 cm and is held in the State Tretyakov Gallery, Moscow.

issues.quote: it measures roughly 64 by 40 cm
issues.problem: A specific dimension with no backing anywhere: realDimensions is null in the record, Commons gives no size, and I could not find a published measurement for this painting. Confident specificity with no source.
issues.evidence: catalogue record - realDimensions: null; commons extmetadata carries no dimensions; web searches of Russian sources returned no size

issues.quote: roses banked behind them
issues.problem: The roses are in the foreground, in front of and below the figures, not behind them.
issues.evidence: image - rose sprays overlap the stone ledge at the bottom and both lower corners

issues.quote: the Christ Child against her
issues.problem: Understates/misses the central motif: both figures hold a long stem of white lilies, which is the most prominent object in the picture and goes unmentioned.
issues.evidence: image

metadataIssues.evidence: the description's '64 by 40 cm' has no source; do not backfill the record from it

proposals.imageObservation: Arched-top painting: the Virgin in a white veil, red robe and blue mantle stands behind a stone ledge; the standing Christ Child beside her leans against her arm. Both hold a stem of white lilies. Pink roses climb in front of the ledge across the whole foreground; a dark green curtain and a strip of sky behind.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Tretyakov is supported by the Commons categories ('19th-century paintings in the Tretyakov Gallery'). The dimensions happen to match the reproduction's aspect ratio, which suggests they were derived from the JPEG rather than from a catalogue - either way they should not be published.

verifier.reason: The central charge is wrong: the dimensions are published. The Tretyakov Gallery (my.tretyakov.ru) and muzei-mira.com give 'Холст, масло. 64,7х40 см', so 'roughly 64 by 40 cm' and 'oil' are correct, not invented. What survives is smaller: in the image the roses climb up both sides and across the bottom in front of the stone ledge, not 'banked behind them', and the lily stem held by both figures goes unmentioned. That is a misplacement plus an omission - minor, not major. The first agent's replacement drops the true dimensions and medium; revised text restores them.

proposals.title: Голова Мадонны
proposals.currentDescription: A close head study of the Virgin, her face inclined and eyes lowered, isolated against a plain ground. Bruni, who served as curator of the Imperial Hermitage picture gallery from 1849, worked the academic Madonna type throughout these decades; the study is dated to the second half of the 1830s into the 1840s and is held in the Hermitage, St Petersburg.
proposals.proposedDescription: A close head study of the Virgin, seen frontally with a sheer veil falling either side of her face and a crossed drapery pinned at the breast, isolated against a plain paper ground. Bruni, who served as curator of the Imperial Hermitage picture gallery from 1849, worked the academic Madonna type throughout these decades; the study is dated to the second half of the 1830s into the 1840s and is held in the Hermitage, St Petersburg.

issues.quote: her face inclined and eyes lowered
issues.problem: The head is upright and strictly frontal, and the eyes are open with the irises fully visible, looking out at the viewer. Neither the inclination nor the lowered gaze is in the sheet.
issues.evidence: image — frontal, upright head; open eyes

proposals.imageObservation: A chalk or pencil drawing on toned paper: head and shoulders of a young woman seen frontally, head upright, eyes open and directed toward the viewer, a sheer veil falling either side of her face and a crossed white drapery fastened at the breast by an oval brooch, on a plain paper ground.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Only the pose clause is changed; the Hermitage location (Commons credit hermitagemuseum.org), the 1830s-40s dating (Commons: 'Вторая половина 1830-х — 1840-е гг.') and Bruni's 1849 Hermitage appointment all stand. The record's year of 1830 is the low end of that range and is defensible. Commons files it under 'Drawings by Feodor Bruni', which matches the sheet's appearance; the description wisely names no medium and the replacement keeps it that way.

proposals.title: Брюллов Нарцисс
proposals.currentDescription: Karl Bryullov's 1819 oil painting depicting the mythological figure of Narcissus, the beautiful youth consumed by his own reflection. Housed in the Russian Museum's Academical Hall, this work exemplifies the Romantic era's fascination with classical mythology and human beauty.
proposals.proposedDescription: A nude youth lies on the bank of a dark pool, propped on one arm over a fall of red drapery with a sandal on one foot, his head bowed toward the water; above him a winged Cupid hovers with bow and quiver. Karl Bryullov painted the subject in 1819, early in his career, and the canvas is in the State Russian Museum.

issues.quote: Housed in the Russian Museum's Academical Hall
issues.problem: 'Academical Hall' is a Wikimedia Commons room category (Russian Museum - Academical Hall No.14), i.e. a hanging location that changes, not a catalogue fact about the work. Stating a specific gallery room as where the picture is 'housed' asserts more than the sources support.
issues.evidence: commons — the only backing is the maintenance category 'Russian Museum - Academical Hall No.14'; the collection itself (State Russian Museum) is supported.

issues.quote: depicting the mythological figure of Narcissus, the beautiful youth consumed by his own reflection
issues.problem: The description recounts the myth and never says what is in the frame; it omits the hovering Cupid, the pool, the red drapery and the sandal entirely.
issues.evidence: image — Cupid with bow and quiver is a prominent second figure.

issues.quote: this work exemplifies the Romantic era's fascination with classical mythology and human beauty
issues.problem: Catalogue boilerplate; says nothing specific about this picture.
issues.evidence: house style — plain, factual, first sentence should describe the frame.

proposals.imageObservation: A nude youth reclines on his side on a rocky bank beside dark water, propped on one arm over red drapery, one foot in a laced sandal, head bowed toward the pool; a winged Cupid with bow and quiver hovers above him at left against a dark wooded background.
proposals.reviewerNotes: No claim in the existing text is false - the collection (Russian Museum), the 1819 date and the subject are all right. The downgrade is for the room-level location and for a description that never describes the picture. If the project prefers to keep 'accurate' where nothing is contradicted, treat this as a house-style rewrite rather than a correction.

proposals.title: Im Dachstübchen
proposals.currentDescription: Carl Spitzweg's oil painting shows an elderly man in cap and spectacles leaning from his garret window to water the flowers crowding his window box, birdcages hanging from the eaves above and church towers rising over the rooftops; far below, a child tends potted plants at another window. Painted around 1848-49, it is characteristic of Spitzweg's affectionate Biedermeier observations of modest life in old German towns. The painting is in a private collection.
proposals.proposedDescription: Carl Spitzweg's oil painting shows an elderly man in cap and spectacles leaning from his garret window to water the flowers crowding his window box, birdcages hanging from the wall above and a church tower rising over the rooftops; on the neighbouring roof a small bonneted figure sits at a dormer beside a shelf of potted plants. Painted around 1848-49, it is characteristic of Spitzweg's affectionate Biedermeier observations of modest life in old German towns. The painting is in a private collection.

issues.quote: far below
issues.problem: The second window is on the adjoining roof roughly one storey down and well within the middle ground, not far below.
issues.evidence: image

issues.quote: a child tends potted plants at another window
issues.problem: The small figure wears a bonnet and could as easily be a woman; the reproduction does not settle the age, and the figure is seated rather than obviously tending the plants.
issues.evidence: image - figure is ambiguous at this resolution

proposals.imageObservation: Oil painting: an old man in a skullcap and spectacles leans from a garret window with a watering can over a window box of flowering plants; two birdcages hang on the wall above, a church tower and a baroque gable rise beyond the tiled roofs, and a small bonneted figure sits at a dormer on the neighbouring roof below with potted plants on a shelf.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Only the two hedged details changed; everything substantive (subject, date, Biedermeier context, private collection) is supported by the image and the Commons description ('The Garret or The Attic (c. 1840s). Private collection').

proposals.title: The Bookworm
proposals.currentDescription: Spitzweg's elderly bibliophile stands high on a library ladder, spectacles on his nose, a volume open in his hands and more books wedged under both arms and between his knees, oblivious to everything but the shelf marked 'Metaphysics'. Painted around 1850, the picture is a gentle Biedermeier satire of bookish absorption and one of Spitzweg's best-loved subjects.
proposals.proposedDescription: Spitzweg's elderly bibliophile stands high on a library ladder, an open volume held close to his eyes, a red-bound book clamped under one arm, another in his outstretched hand and a fourth gripped between his knees, oblivious to everything but the shelf marked 'Metaphysik'. Painted around 1850, the picture is a gentle Biedermeier satire of bookish absorption and one of Spitzweg's best-loved subjects.

issues.quote: spectacles on his nose
issues.problem: At full resolution the man's profile shows no glasses — no lens, frame or temple arm; he holds the book close to his eyes instead, which is the point of the joke.
issues.evidence: image — enlarged crop of the head shows an unobstructed profile with no eyewear

issues.quote: more books wedged under both arms and between his knees
issues.problem: One book is tucked under an arm, one is held out in his hand, and one is between his knees — "under both arms" is not what the figure does.
issues.evidence: image — enlarged crop of the torso

proposals.imageObservation: An elderly white-haired man in black knee breeches and a dark coat stands near the top of a library ladder in a tall gallery of bookshelves, holding an open book close to his face; a second book is in his outstretched hand, a red-bound volume is clamped under his arm and a fourth is gripped between his knees. A gilt cartouche on the shelf front above him reads METAPHYSIK; a painted sky with clouds fills the top of the room. No spectacles are visible on his face.
proposals.reviewerNotes: I confirmed the shelf cartouche by enlargement — it reads METAPHYSIK, so that claim stands. The spectacles call is at medium confidence because the head is only about 70 px across in this reproduction; at that scale I can see the brow, eye and ear clearly and there is no frame, but an auditor with the full-resolution file should double-check before applying. Commons notes three versions of the composition (Museum Georg Schäfer c.1850, Milwaukee c.1851, private collection 1854); the description wisely names no collection.

proposals.title: 김홍도 금강사군첩 - 총석정
proposals.currentDescription: The basalt sea-stacks of Chongseokjeong rising from the East Sea coast, the fourth leaf of Kim Hong-do's album of the four districts of Geumgang. Ink and light colour on silk, roughly 30 by 44 cm, painted about 1788 after a tour the court painter made of Mount Geumgang and Gangwon Province under King Jeongjo. The clustered hexagonal columns are drawn in fine vertical strokes.
proposals.proposedDescription: The basalt sea-stacks of Chongseokjeong rising from the East Sea coast, a leaf from Kim Hong-do's album of the four districts of Geumgang. Ink and light colour on silk, painted about 1788 after a tour the court painter made of Mount Geumgang and Gangwon Province under King Jeongjo. The clustered hexagonal columns are drawn in fine vertical strokes, with a small pavilion and wind-bent pines on the headland at right.

issues.quote: the fourth leaf of Kim Hong-do's album
issues.problem: A specific ordinal position within the album that nothing in the record, the file name or the Commons metadata supports. Confident specificity with no backing is the classic hallucination signature.
issues.evidence: commons — objectName and imageDescription give only 'Album of landscapes around Mt. Geumgangsan'; no leaf number anywhere in the record.

issues.quote: roughly 30 by 44 cm
issues.problem: The catalogue row carries realDimensions: null. The figure is close to the size usually quoted for leaves of this album, so it is plausible, but it is not sourced here.
issues.evidence: catalogue record — realDimensions is null; commons metadata gives no measurement.

proposals.imageObservation: A horizontal painting on a woven fabric support showing clustered columnar basalt sea-stacks rising out of a calm sea, drawn in fine vertical ink strokes with pale blue-grey wash; a headland at right carries a small pavilion, tiny figures and wind-bent pines. Two red seals and the ink inscription 叢石亭 sit in the upper sky.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Subject, site, date and the Jeongjo-commissioned 1788 tour all check out and the columnar strokes are exactly as described. Only the leaf number and the unsourced dimensions are at issue; I dropped both and added the pavilion/pines, which are clearly visible. If a source for the leaf order or the sheet size exists, both can be restored.

proposals.title: Cezanne Ambroise Vollard
proposals.currentDescription: The dealer Ambroise Vollard sits forward with hands clasped, his bald head catching the light against a brown studio wall. Cézanne painted the portrait in 1899; it is held by the Petit Palais in Paris. Vollard recalled posing more than a hundred times, after which the painter declared only the shirtfront finished.
proposals.proposedDescription: The dealer Ambroise Vollard sits with legs crossed and hands clasped over his knee, his high balding forehead catching the light against the brown hanging behind him. Cézanne painted the portrait in 1899; it is held by the Petit Palais in Paris. Vollard recalled posing more than a hundred times, after which the painter declared only the shirtfront finished.

issues.quote: his bald head catching the light
issues.problem: He is painted balding, with a very high lit forehead, but dark hair is clearly present over the crown and around the sides; 'bald head' overstates it.
issues.evidence: image — magnification of the head shows a dark hair mass across the top and down both sides framing the lit forehead.

issues.quote: against a brown studio wall
issues.problem: Only the right half of the background is brown; the upper left is a pale wall with a shelf of jars.
issues.evidence: image.

metadataIssues.evidence: commons imageDescription 'Portrait of Ambroise Vollard (1899). Petit Palais, Paris' and category 'Ambroise Vollard (Paul Cezanne - Petit Palais)'; the catalogue row leaves artist, movement and nationality empty.

proposals.imageObservation: A dark-bearded man in a brown suit and dark bow tie sits with legs crossed and hands clasped over his knee holding a small book or paper; his forehead is very high and light-struck but dark hair still runs over the crown and sides. Behind him a pale wall with a shelf and jars at the upper left and a red-brown hanging at the right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: This is a marginal call and a reviewer may reasonably leave the original text alone — 'bald' versus 'balding' is a fine distinction in a Cezanne. The sitting anecdote is well attested (Vollard's memoir gives 115 sittings and Cezanne's remark about the shirtfront), and the 1899 date and Petit Palais are confirmed by the Commons record. The more useful item here is the metadata gap: the row has no artist at all.

proposals.title: Cezanne-Thyssen
proposals.currentDescription: A man in a wide-brimmed hat sits against a pale terrace balustrade, his features summarily indicated and patches of bare canvas left in reserve. Painted in 1905-06, oil on canvas, the sitter is Vallier, the gardener at Cézanne's studio at Les Lauves near Aix-en-Provence; the work has been in the Museo Thyssen-Bornemisza, Madrid, since 1993.
proposals.proposedDescription: A man in a straw hat sits with his legs crossed before a broad band of ochre, his features summarily indicated and the paint left open in patches. Painted in 1905-06, oil on canvas, the sitter is Vallier, the gardener who often sat for Cézanne in his last years; the work is in the Museo Thyssen-Bornemisza, Madrid (inv. 1976.68).
