issues.quote: the work has been in the Museo Thyssen-Bornemisza, Madrid, since 1993
issues.problem: The museum's own catalogue gives the inventory number 1976.68 and says the picture entered the Thyssen-Bornemisza collection in 1976; nothing supports 1993 as the date it arrived.
issues.evidence: web:https://www.museothyssen.org/en/collection/artists/cezanne-paul/seated-man | title 'Seated Man', 1905-1906, oil on canvas, 64.8 x 54.6 cm, inv. 1976.68, previously with Ambroise Vollard

issues.quote: against a pale terrace balustrade
issues.problem: The band behind the sitter is a saturated ochre-yellow and has no balusters; calling it a pale balustrade reads more into the passage than the picture shows.
issues.evidence: image

metadataIssues.evidence: web:https://www.museothyssen.org/en/collection/artists/cezanne-paul/seated-man | the current title is the Commons filename, not a title

proposals.imageObservation: A man in a straw boater sits with legs crossed on a chair in front of a broad ochre-yellow horizontal band, dark green foliage and a tree trunk behind; the face is barely indicated and the paint is laid in open blue, green and ochre patches.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The Thyssen's page confirms the date, the medium and Vallier as the sitter, and gives 1976 as the collection date; 1993 is the year the Spanish state bought the Thyssen-Bornemisza collection, which is probably where the number came from, but it is not this picture's acquisition date. I dropped 'Les Lauves' from the replacement because the museum text does not say the sitting took place there, only that Vallier was Cézanne's gardener.

proposals.title: The Temple of Segesta with the Artist Sketching
proposals.currentDescription: The unfinished Doric temple at Segesta in western Sicily stands in a broad valley landscape with mountains and a distant lake behind it, while at lower right a seated figure — Cole himself — sketches the ruins, accompanied by a companion and a donkey. Cole worked up the canvas from drawings made during his European travels, and the composition blends precise archaeological observation with the warm Sicilian light of late afternoon. The painting is in the collection of the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.
proposals.proposedDescription: The unfinished Doric temple at Segesta in western Sicily stands in a broad valley landscape with mountains along the horizon and a pale stretch of water at the far left, while at lower right a seated figure — Cole himself — sketches the ruins, accompanied by a companion and a donkey. Cole worked up the canvas from drawings made during his European travels, and the composition blends precise archaeological observation with the warm Sicilian light of late afternoon. The painting is in the collection of the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.

issues.quote: a distant lake behind it
issues.problem: The water in the picture lies at the far LEFT edge, not behind the temple, and Segesta looks out over the Gulf of Castellammare — sea, not a lake. Nothing in the image identifies it as an enclosed body of water.
issues.evidence: image — a pale stretch of water at the left horizon; knowledge — Segesta's outlook is toward the Tyrrhenian coast

proposals.imageObservation: A Doric temple stands on a green rise in a wide valley, with a chain of blue mountains across the horizon and a pale stretch of water at the far left. In the right foreground, on a rocky bank above a ravine, a man in a dark coat sits sketching on a board while a companion in a red cap sits beside a donkey; a green portfolio and a straw hat lie on the rocks. Warm low light.
proposals.reviewerNotes: This one already carries ledgerStatus 'minor-fixed' and is broadly sound: the sketching self-portrait, the companion and the donkey are all in the frame, the MFA Boston attribution matches the record's credit field, and Cole's 1841–42 Italian trip supports the 'European travels' sentence. My replacement changes only the water clause, and deliberately says 'stretch of water' rather than substituting 'sea', since the image alone cannot settle it.

proposals.title: Ellen Terry
proposals.currentDescription: Dame (Alice) Ellen Terry ('Choosing') , by George Frederic Watts (died 1904). The subject is (Alice) Ellen Terry (1847-1928). See source website for additional information.
proposals.proposedDescription: Ellen Terry in profile with her eyes closed, raising a large red camellia to her face, while her lowered hand holds a small bunch of violets. Watts painted her, known as 'Choosing', around the time of their marriage in 1864, when she was sixteen; the showy scentless camellias and the humble scented violets stand for the choice between worldly display and quieter values. The portrait is in the National Portrait Gallery, London (NPG 5048).

issues.quote: See source website for additional information.
issues.problem: The whole description is the National Portrait Gallery's boilerplate caption pasted in, including a dangling instruction to consult a 'source website' that the reader of this catalogue has no access to. It never says what the picture shows — and the picture's entire point, the choice between scentless camellias and fragrant violets, is absent.
issues.evidence: catalogue record — description text is byte-identical to the Commons imageDescription's opening lines

issues.quote: by George Frederic Watts (died 1904)
issues.problem: The only date the description offers is Watts's death year, and the record's `year` field repeats it as if it were the date of the picture. The portrait dates to about 1864, when Watts married Terry.
issues.evidence: web:https://www.npg.org.uk/collections/search/portrait/mw06269/Ellen-Terry-Choosing — 'Choosing', by George Frederic Watts, 1864, NPG 5048; Commons date note also says the portrait was painted around the 1864 marriage

metadataIssues.evidence: NPG 5048 dates 'Choosing' to 1864; 1904 is Watts's death year, taken from the Commons PD boilerplate ('author died in 1904'). Commons' own date field says the portrait was probably painted around the 1864 marriage.

proposals.imageObservation: A young woman in profile with loose golden-brown hair, eyes closed, lifting a large red camellia to her face with her raised right hand; her lowered left hand holds a small posy of violets. Dark green foliage and further red camellias fill the ground, and she wears a grey-green dress with an amber bead necklace.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Nothing in the existing text is false — it is accurate boilerplate — so the verdict rests on the date confusion the '(died 1904)' parenthetical creates together with the record's year field, plus the dangling source reference. The camellia/violet reading is taken from the NPG and from the Commons imageDescription, not invented. If the catalogue's year is corrected to 1864, note that this will also move the work between eras in any year-based grouping.

proposals.title: Académie de femme debout
proposals.currentDescription: A pen study of a standing female nude seen from behind, holding a staff from which a veil falls. Made during Dürer's first Italian journey, the sheet shows him grappling with classical proportion and the contrapposto idealised by his Venetian contemporaries.
proposals.proposedDescription: A pen study in ink and grey wash of a standing female nude seen from behind, her raised hand on a staff from which a veil falls. The sheet is dated 1495 and carries Dürer's monogram at the lower left; it is one of the early nude studies he made from the living model rather than from an ideal type, and is now in the Louvre.

issues.quote: Made during Dürer's first Italian journey
issues.problem: The sheet is dated 1495, the year Dürer returned from Venice to Nuremberg, so the drawing could equally have been made after his return. The record gives only the year; nothing places it in Italy.
issues.evidence: image (the inscribed date 1495) and catalogue record; web:https://collections.louvre.fr/en/ark:/53355/cl020109115 — the Louvre entry gives 1495, pen and black ink with grey wash, and notes the sheet came from Peter Vischer the Younger's Nuremberg sketchbook.

issues.quote: grappling with classical proportion and the contrapposto idealised by his Venetian contemporaries
issues.problem: Runs against the Louvre's own reading of the sheet, which stresses that before about 1500 Dürer drew from the live model without idealising.
issues.evidence: web:https://collections.louvre.fr/en/ark:/53355/cl020109115.

proposals.imageObservation: A pen-and-ink drawing with grey wash on aged paper: a standing female nude seen from behind, hair bound up, her raised right hand grasping a tall vertical staff from which a long veil hangs and loops around her body. Inscribed 1495 with the AD monogram at the lower left, plus a small collector's stamp.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The visual description is exact and I kept it. The two things I changed are both interpretive: the Italian-journey placement (unprovable from a sheet dated in the year he came home) and the 'idealised contrapposto' framing, which the Louvre's own catalogue entry contradicts. A reviewer who prefers the traditional Venice framing could keep it if a scholarly source is added; I could not find one in the record.

proposals.title: dürer dragon fight
proposals.currentDescription: Saint Michael Fighting the Dragon is a celebrated woodcut from Albrecht Dürer's Apocalypse series, created in 1498. The composition depicts the archangel Michael vanquishing a demonic dragon below, rendered with Dürer's characteristic precision and dramatic intensity. This iconic image exemplifies Northern Renaissance printmaking and has become one of the most recognizable representations of the saint in Western art.
proposals.proposedDescription: Saint Michael and three companion angels battle a swarm of horned, winged beasts in the sky, Michael driving his long spear down through the head of one of them. Below the fight, a wide landscape of a walled town, wooded hills and a lake with small boats lies untouched. The sheet is from Albrecht Dürer's Apocalypse woodcut series of 1498; this impression is coloured by hand and carries Dürer's AD monogram on a tablet at the lower centre.

issues.quote: The composition depicts the archangel Michael vanquishing a demonic dragon below
issues.problem: The sheet shows four angels fighting a whole group of dragons and beasts, not Michael alone against a single dragon; the entire lower third of the sheet — a town and lake landscape — goes unmentioned.
issues.evidence: image — four haloed/winged angels (spear, sword, bow, club) and at least five distinct monsters, plus a landscape band below

issues.quote: This iconic image exemplifies Northern Renaissance printmaking and has become one of the most recognizable representations of the saint in Western art.
issues.problem: Empty superlative boilerplate; adds no fact a reader can check and replaces description of the image.
issues.evidence: house style — first sentence should say what is literally in the frame

proposals.imageObservation: Hand-coloured woodcut: four winged angels — one in a rose robe driving a long spear downward, one with sword and shield, one drawing a bow, one with a raised weapon — fight five or six horned, winged, reptilian beasts in the sky; below the melee a quiet landscape of a walled town, wooded hills, a river and a lake with boats, with the AD monogram on a tablet at lower centre.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Nothing in the description is fabricated — the series, date and subject are right — but it never describes the sheet and gets the cast wrong. The Commons file title places this impression at the Cleveland Museum of Art (1922.94.13); I left the collection out of the replacement because the catalogue record has no credit field, but it could be added from the Commons file title if the auditor trusts it.

proposals.title: Двери Тимура
proposals.currentDescription: A painting by Russian orientalist master Vasily Vereshchagin from his celebrated Turkestan Series, depicting the ornately carved doors of the legendary Central Asian conqueror Timur (also known as Tamerlane). Executed in 1872, the work exemplifies Vereshchagin's meticulous attention to architectural and decorative detail during his travels in the Caucasus and Central Asia.
proposals.proposedDescription: Two guards stand either side of a tall pair of wooden doors carved edge to edge with arabesque, in striped and embroidered robes, with bows, quivers of arrows and round studded shields, long spears tufted red and white leaning across the doorway. An inscribed tile band runs above the door frame and the pale paving stretches toward the viewer. Vereshchagin painted the scene in 1872 for his Turkestan series, drawn from his years in Central Asia; the canvas is in the Tretyakov Gallery.

issues.quote: during his travels in the Caucasus and Central Asia
issues.problem: The Turkestan series comes out of Vereshchagin's Central Asian journeys of 1867-1870; nothing in the record or the Commons metadata connects this canvas to the Caucasus, and folding it in blurs where the work came from.
issues.evidence: commons — categories give 'Turkestan series by Vasily Vereshchagin' and 'Carved doors in Uzbekistan', with no Caucasus reference.

issues.quote: depicting the ornately carved doors of the legendary Central Asian conqueror Timur
issues.problem: The two armed guards flanking the doors are the dominant figures in the picture and go unmentioned; the description restates the title instead of describing the frame.
issues.evidence: image — two full-length guards occupy the left and right thirds of the canvas.

issues.quote: Russian orientalist master
issues.problem: Empty honorific, joined by 'celebrated' and 'exemplifies ... meticulous attention' — house style avoids this register.
issues.evidence: catalogue record — corpus house style is plain and factual.

proposals.imageObservation: Two guards in striped and heavily embroidered robes stand either side of a tall pair of wooden doors carved edge to edge with arabesque; each carries a bow, a quiver of arrows, a round studded shield and a long spear tufted with red and white horsehair, and an inscribed dark tile band runs above the doorway over a pale paved floor.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Nothing in the original is flatly contradicted — Timur's doors, the Turkestan series and the 1872 date all check out — so this is a minor verdict driven by the Caucasus add-on and by the description skipping the picture's two main figures. The Tretyakov attribution in my replacement comes from the record's own provenance block (collection: Tretyakov Gallery, inventory 1995).

proposals.title: The End of the Song
proposals.currentDescription: ] Although The End of the Song illustrates no specific incident in history or literature, it recalls two well-known literary subjects, Tristram and Iseult and Paolo and Francesca . [. ]» (Christie's)
proposals.proposedDescription: A blonde woman in a pink and gold gown and an ermine-lined red cloak sits on a stone bench with her hands clasped round her knee, while a young harper in a brown and gold tunic leans toward her, his instrument propped against the step; a crowned, bearded man watches from the trees behind. Edmund Blair Leighton signed and dated the canvas 1902. Christie's notes that the picture illustrates no specific incident in history or literature but recalls two well-known literary subjects, Tristram and Iseult and Paolo and Francesca.

issues.quote: ] Although The End of the Song illustrates
issues.problem: The description is not a description. It is a mangled scrape of the Commons image caption, opening with a stray bracket and carrying the ellipsis brackets and closing guillemet of the original quotation; it never says what the picture shows.
issues.evidence: catalogue record description field vs Commons imageDescription, which reads the same but with intact '[...]' markers

issues.quote: (Christie's)
issues.problem: A bare auction-house attribution left dangling at the end of a fragment; nothing in the sentence is framed as the site's own text.
issues.evidence: catalogue record description field

metadataIssues.evidence: Commons date field '1902 date QS:P571,+1902-00-00T00:00:00Z/9'; the canvas is also signed and dated 1902 at lower left, visible in the image, and the filename carries (1902).

proposals.imageObservation: A blonde woman in a pink and gold brocade gown with an ermine-lined red cloak and a jewelled circlet sits on a stone bench, hands clasped round her knee; a young man in a brown and gold tunic leans beside her with a large dark harp resting against the step. In the background at right a bearded, crowned man watches from among the trees, chin on hand. A fur rug lies on the paving. Signed 'E. BLAIR LEIGHTON' and dated 1902 at lower left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Nothing in the existing text is false - it is a faithful, if corrupted, transcription of the Christie's line quoted on Commons - so this is not a fabrication; it is an unusable fragment. The replacement keeps that quotation's substance and adds the missing visual first sentence. I did not name the crowned watcher as King Mark in the replacement, although Commons files the image under 'King Mark of Cornwall', because that identification sits oddly with Christie's own statement that no specific literary incident is illustrated. The year field should be filled in as 1902.

proposals.title: Laocoön
proposals.currentDescription: El Greco's dynamic interpretation of the Laocoön myth, depicting the Trojan priest and his sons in a dramatic struggle with serpents. Painted between 1610 and 1614, this oil canvas exemplifies the artist's characteristic elongated forms, intense emotionality, and spiritual intensity. The work is held in the National Gallery of Art, Washington, D.
proposals.proposedDescription: El Greco's version of the Laocoon myth: the Trojan priest and his sons twist on the ground with the serpent while a group of standing nude figures watches from the right, all set before a view of Toledo under a storm-grey sky. Painted between 1610 and 1614, the oil canvas shows the elongated bodies and cold, blanched flesh of the artist's late manner. It is held in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.

issues.quote: The work is held in the National Gallery of Art, Washington, D.
issues.problem: The description is cut off mid-abbreviation; the last sentence ends on 'Washington, D.' with no closing.
issues.evidence: catalogue record - the description field itself terminates there

issues.quote: intense emotionality, and spiritual intensity
issues.problem: Redundant intensifiers ('intense ... intensity') and no concrete visual information; the picture's most striking features (the Toledo cityscape behind the group, the standing figures at right) go unmentioned.
issues.evidence: image - city view and standing nudes are prominent

proposals.imageObservation: Three pale nude male figures struggle with a serpent in the foreground (one lying at centre, one falling at left, one prone at right), two or three standing nude figures watch at the right edge, and a walled city with a small horse sits on a green rise under a storm-grey sky.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Only real defect is the truncated final sentence; the myth, medium, date (Commons: 'between 1610 and 1614') and the Washington location (Commons categories: Google Art Project works in National Gallery of Art, Washington) all check out. The Toledo background is standard, well-established El Greco scholarship.

proposals.title: Incontro di Giobbe ed Esaù
proposals.currentDescription: The painting illustrates Jacob's return to his homeland, asking forgiveness from his brother Esau for having deceived his birthright. Biblical subjects had a lot of luck around the mid-nineteenth century, as the suffering of the Jewish people recalled the Italian political situation.
proposals.proposedDescription: Two men embrace at the right, one bowing low into the other's arms, watched by a bearded figure in a white turban; at the left a crowd of women and children waits beside laden camels under a bare mountain range at dawn. The painting shows Jacob's return to his homeland and his reconciliation with the brother he had cheated of his birthright. Hayez painted it in 1844; the canvas is about 210 by 298 cm.

issues.quote: Biblical subjects had a lot of luck around the mid-nineteenth century, as the suffering of the Jewish people recalled the Italian political situation.
issues.problem: A sweeping art-historical generalisation stated as fact, carried over verbatim (and awkwardly translated - 'had a lot of luck' renders 'ebbero molta fortuna', i.e. were popular) from the uploader's own Commons caption; nothing in the record or the source supports it as a claim about this painting.
issues.evidence: commons | the imageDescription field is the uploader's own text, credited 'Own work'

issues.quote: The painting illustrates Jacob's return to his homeland
issues.problem: The description never says what is in the frame - the embrace, the crowd of women and children, the camels, the mountain landscape.
issues.evidence: image

metadataIssues.evidence: commons | 'Giobbe' is Job; the subject and the englishTitle are Jacob (Giacobbe), and the Commons category on the file is 'Incontro tra Esau e Giacobbe by Francesco Hayez'. The error is in the Commons filename the title was taken from.

proposals.imageObservation: A wide canvas at dawn: at the right two men embrace, one bowing low into the other's arms, watched by a bearded man in a white turban and olive cloak; at the left a crowd of women, children and infants stands beside laden camels, with a bare mountain range and pale sky behind.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Subject identification is right and the dimensions come from the record's realDimensions (298 wide by 210 high). I deliberately did not name which embracing figure is Jacob and which is Esau - I cannot tell from the picture. The Risorgimento reading may well be defensible in the literature, but it is presented here as settled fact on the authority of a Commons uploader, so I dropped it rather than rewrite it.

proposals.title: François boucher
proposals.currentDescription: A Rococo oil painting depicting the moment Diana emerges from her bath, exemplifying Boucher's characteristic fluid brushwork and sensual treatment of mythological subjects. The work showcases the artist's mastery of light and color in rendering the goddess's attendants and the luxurious bathing scene. Housed in the Louvre, Paris (INV 2712), this painting measures 57 × 73 cm and represents a quintessential example of 18th-century French court painting.
proposals.proposedDescription: Diana rests at the edge of a wooded pool with a single nymph beside her, a red quiver of arrows on the ground at the left and dead game birds, a hare and a bow at the right. Francois Boucher painted it in 1742; the oil on canvas measures 57 x 73 cm. It is in the Louvre, Paris (INV 2712).

issues.quote: the goddess's attendants
issues.problem: There is one attendant nymph, not several. The 1742 Salon entry likewise describes Diana with 'one of her companions'.
issues.evidence: image - two figures only; web:https://pop.culture.gouv.fr/notice/joconde/000PE000201 - 'Diana resting and coming out of her bath with one of her companions'.

issues.quote: the luxurious bathing scene
issues.problem: The setting is a plain wooded stream bank with drapery and hunting spoils, not a luxurious bath.
issues.evidence: image.

issues.quote: The work showcases the artist's mastery of light and color
issues.problem: Catalogue boilerplate; says nothing about the picture.
issues.evidence: corpus house style.

proposals.imageObservation: Framed Rococo oil: two nude women at a wooded pool, the seated Diana at right with a crescent-and-pearl headdress and a string of pearls, a single nymph bending at her feet; a red quiver of arrows on the ground at the left, dead game birds and a hare with a bow at the right, blue drapery hanging behind.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The checkable facts in the original all verify: Louvre INV 2712, 57 x 73 cm, 1742. Only the plural attendants and the 'luxurious bathing scene' framing needed correcting.

proposals.title: Portrait of an anonymous as a Troubadour
proposals.currentDescription: A bust-length portrait of a young man costumed as a medieval troubadour, his collar and cap evoking the Romantic revival of the type. The sitter is identified as the poet Paul Verlaine; Bazille painted the canvas in 1868, and it is now in the Dallas Museum of Art.
proposals.proposedDescription: A bust-length portrait of a young man costumed as a troubadour, his collar and slashed cap evoking the Romantic revival of the type. The sitter was long identified as the poet Paul Verlaine, though the picture is now catalogued as an unidentified man; Bazille painted the canvas in 1868, and it is in the Dallas Museum of Art.

issues.quote: The sitter is identified as the poet Paul Verlaine
issues.problem: Stated as settled fact, but the catalogue row's own title - and the Commons object name it came from - is 'Portrait of an anonymous as a Troubadour' / 'Portrait d'un inconnu comme un troubadour', i.e. the sitter is recorded as unidentified. The Verlaine name survives in the file name and in older museum literature; it is a contested traditional identification, not a fact.
issues.evidence: catalogue record | title field reads 'Portrait of an anonymous as a Troubadour'; commons | objectName gives the same French and English titles while the file name and one category still say Verlaine

proposals.imageObservation: Bust-length oil portrait of a young bearded man against a dark ground, turned three-quarters to the viewer, wearing a puffed red-and-yellow slashed cap, a white standing collar and a dark coat; a faint sketched plant form is visible at the left edge.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The Dallas Museum of Art holding and the 1868 date are supported by the Commons categories ('Paintings by Frederic Bazille in the Dallas Museum of Art', '1868 oil on canvas paintings in the United States'). The identification is genuinely muddled in the sources: AMICA/older DMA records title it 'Portrait of Paul Verlaine as a Troubadour', while Wikidata (which the row's title follows) calls the sitter anonymous, and the Bazille catalogue raisonne site treats a differently dated Verlaine portrait (1867, private collection since a 2015 Sotheby's sale) as the Verlaine picture. Hedging is the safe fix; do not assert either identification flatly. I also dropped 'medieval' from 'medieval troubadour' since the cap is a Renaissance-revival type.

proposals.title: The Little Gardener
proposals.currentDescription: A boy in white breeches, a pink shirt and a boater stands in a planted garden under a bright sky. Oil on canvas, about 128 by 169 cm, painted in 1866 to 1867 and held by the Museum of Fine Arts, Houston. Bazille left the foreground unfinished, the bare canvas still visible.
proposals.proposedDescription: A boy in a pink shirt, pale trousers and a broad straw hat stands at the right edge of a garden, a large shrub in pink blossom filling the left under a bright sky. Oil on canvas, about 128 by 169 cm, painted in 1866 to 1867 and held by the Museum of Fine Arts, Houston. Bazille left the foreground unfinished, the bare canvas still visible.

issues.quote: A boy in white breeches, a pink shirt and a boater
issues.problem: The boy wears full-length pale trousers, not knee breeches, and a soft broad-brimmed straw hat rather than a flat-topped boater.
issues.evidence: image — trousers reach the ankle; the hat has a soft, drooping brim

proposals.imageObservation: A garden under a bright blue sky: a large shrub covered in pink blossom at the left, a dark conifer at centre right, a lawn, and at the right edge a boy in a soft broad-brimmed straw hat, pink shirt and full-length pale trousers standing with his back half turned. The lower-left foreground is thinly and sketchily painted.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Only the costume wording changes; the date range matches the Commons date field (1866/1867) and MFA Houston matches the Commons categories. I could not verify the 128 x 169 cm figure from the supplied evidence (realDimensions is null) — it is close to the published size for this picture, so I left it, but it is the one unbacked number here.

proposals.title: Biondina
proposals.currentDescription: A close head-and-shoulders study of a fair-haired young Italian girl, her white blouse laced with a dark bodice, titled with the Italian for the blonde one. The oil belongs to the Hamburger Kunsthalle and is dated by the museum to 1879.
proposals.proposedDescription: A close head-and-shoulders study of a fair-haired young Italian girl, her white blouse laced with a dark bodice trimmed in pink ribbon, titled with the Italian for the blonde one. The oil is in the Hamburger Kunsthalle; it is usually dated 1879, though this catalogue records it as 1870.

issues.quote: is dated by the museum to 1879
issues.problem: The 1879 date is attributed to the Hamburger Kunsthalle, but the only sources carrying it are WikiArt (the Commons credit link) and Art Renewal Center; the museum's own record could not be reached, and Commons and this catalogue row both give 1870.
issues.evidence: commons — date field "1870", categories "Girls in 1870", "1870 paintings in Hamburg"; web:wikiart.org/en/frederic-leighton/biondina-1879 is the Commons credit link

metadataIssues.evidence: Commons date field and categories say 1870; WikiArt and ARC say 1879, both locating it at the Hamburger Kunsthalle. The description and the record contradict each other; neither side could be settled against the museum's own catalogue.

proposals.imageObservation: Bust-length portrait of a girl with light golden-brown wavy hair against a plain brown ground; she wears a loose white blouse with full sleeves under a dark blue-purple laced bodice, with pink ribbons at the shoulders and down the front lacing.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The picture, the sitter type and the Hamburger Kunsthalle are all fine — the finding is purely that the description asserts a museum dating it cannot support while the record says something else. If the auditor can reach the Hamburger Kunsthalle's online collection, resolving the year would let both the description and the record be fixed properly; the replacement above deliberately flags the conflict rather than picking a side. The closing clause may read oddly in a public description — an alternative is to drop the date sentence entirely until the year is settled.

proposals.title: Fritillaria imperialis in Les liliacees
proposals.currentDescription: A crown imperial (Fritillaria imperialis) with its ring of pendent orange bells beneath a tuft of upright leaves, drawn life-size against a plain ground. Plate from Redouté's Les Liliacées, the eight-volume folio issued in Paris between 1802 and 1816. The image is a colour stipple engraving after Redouté's watercolour on vellum, finished by hand.
proposals.proposedDescription: A crown imperial (Fritillaria imperialis) with its ring of pendent scarlet bells beneath a topknot of upright leaves, the stem rising from a rosette of strap-shaped leaves against a plain ground; the plate is lettered Fritillaria Imperialis / Fritillaire Impériale. Plate from Redouté's Les Liliacées, the eight-volume folio issued in Paris between 1802 and 1816. The image is a colour stipple engraving after Redouté's watercolour on vellum — the sheet credits de Gouy as engraver — finished by hand.

issues.quote: drawn life-size against a plain ground
issues.problem: Nothing supports 'life-size', and it is implausible: a crown imperial stands roughly a metre tall while the Liliacées folio sheet is about half that, and the plant in the plate is cut off at the base with no bulb. The record carries no dimensions for this sheet either.
issues.evidence: catalogue record (realDimensions null) + image — the stem is truncated at the foot of the sheet

issues.quote: ring of pendent orange bells
issues.problem: The bells read scarlet-red with orange highlights rather than orange.
issues.evidence: image

proposals.imageObservation: A crown imperial: a whorl of pendent scarlet-to-orange bells with yellow stamens hanging below a topknot of upright green leaves, on a purplish stem rising from a rosette of strap-shaped leaves; plain cream ground; engraved captions 'Fritillaria Imperialis / Fritillaire Impériale' below, with 'P.J. Redouté pinx.' at the lower left and 'de Gouy sculp.' at the lower right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The Les Liliacées facts (eight volumes, Paris, 1802-1816, stipple engraving after watercolours on vellum) are correct and confirmed by the Commons credit line. Only 'life-size' was removed, and the engraver's name added because it is lettered on the plate itself. Commons categories place the plate in volume 3.

proposals.title: 冨嶽三十六景 尾州不二見原-Fujimigahara in Owari Province
proposals.currentDescription: A woodblock print from Hokusai's iconic series Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, depicting the view of Mount Fuji across the rice fields of Owari Province. Created circa 1830-32, this Japanese print showcases the distinctive composition and color palette characteristic of the ukiyo-e tradition. Sourced from the Metropolitan Museum of Art's open access collection.
proposals.proposedDescription: A cooper crouches inside a huge half-built tub, working on its inner wall, while a tiny Mount Fuji appears far off through the ring of the tub, across a plain of rice fields. The sheet comes from Hokusai's series Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, made circa 1830-32, and is from the Metropolitan Museum of Art's open access collection.

issues.quote: depicting the view of Mount Fuji across the rice fields of Owari Province
issues.problem: There are no rice fields, and the subject of the print is the tub-maker working inside a giant barrel through which Fuji is framed; the description omits the figure entirely and invents the field.
issues.evidence: image | the foreground is occupied by a cooper and his half-finished tub on bare ground; the middle distance is a flat plain and a low tree line, not paddy

issues.quote: showcases the distinctive composition and color palette characteristic of the ukiyo-e tradition
issues.problem: Empty catalogue boilerplate that could describe any ukiyo-e print; combined with 'iconic' it replaces description with praise.
issues.evidence: catalogue record

proposals.imageObservation: A cooper squats inside a huge half-built barrel, planing a stave with a drawknife; hoops, a plane, a chest and a mallet lie on the ground around him, and tiny Mount Fuji is visible far off through the ring of the barrel, above a flat plain with trees, under a graded blue-to-cream sky. A red title cartouche and signature run down the left edge.
proposals.reviewerNotes: This is the well-known 'Fuji View Field in Owari Province' design; the Commons category on the file uses that title. The series, the date range and the Met open-access sourcing in the existing text are all correct - only the described scene is wrong.

verifier.reason: The first agent's central claim is wrong: the image shows a flat plain ruled by dike lines between the tub and the distant tree line, and the Met's own text for this print says Fuji is framed in the tub 'across a plain of rice fields'. So 'across the rice fields' is correct, not invented. The real defect is omission: the description never mentions the cooper working inside the giant half-built tub, which fills the foreground, and it pads with boilerplate ('showcases the distinctive composition...'). Nothing in it is false, so this is minor, not major. The proposed replacement wrongly drops the fields and says 'planing a stave'; the Met describes the man sealing the seams, and the tool is not clearly a plane, so the revision avoids naming the action.

evidence.objectKey: collection-of-beauty/冨嶽三十六景_尾州不二見原-Fujimigahara_in_Owari_Province_(Bishū_Fujimigahara),_from_the_series_Thirty-six_Views_of_Mount_Fuji_(Fugaku_sanjūrokkei)_MET_DP141033.jpg

proposals.title: G. Caillebotte - Intérieur
proposals.currentDescription: An interior scene by Gustave Caillebotte depicting a woman at a window. The painting exemplifies Caillebotte's characteristic interest in domestic interiors and unusual compositional angles.
proposals.proposedDescription: A woman stands at a window with her back to the room, arms folded, looking out at the lettered facade of the building opposite; at the right a man sits in an armchair absorbed in his newspaper. A lace curtain and a heavy drape frame the view, and the two figures share the room without acknowledging each other — the sort of domestic interior and off-centre framing Caillebotte returned to repeatedly.

issues.quote: depicting a woman at a window
issues.problem: The picture has two figures. The seated man reading a newspaper occupies the entire right-hand third of the canvas and is the reason the composition is usually discussed at all; the description does not mention him.
issues.evidence: image; Commons categories list both 'Paintings of females looking through windows' and 'Portrait paintings by Gustave Caillebotte'

issues.quote: The painting exemplifies Caillebotte's characteristic interest in domestic interiors and unusual compositional angles.
issues.problem: Generic filler in place of what is actually in the frame (the lace curtain, the lettered facade opposite, the two figures ignoring each other).
issues.evidence: image

metadataIssues.evidence: The composition (woman at the window seen from behind, man reading in an armchair at right) is Caillebotte's 'Intérieur' / 'Interior, Woman at the Window', consistently dated 1880 in the literature; Commons has 'Unknown date' but files it under the Berhaut 1994 catalogue numbering. Medium confidence — confirm against a Berhaut number before applying.

proposals.imageObservation: An interior seen against the light: a woman in a dark dress stands with her back to us at a window, arms folded, looking out at a building opposite whose gold lettering is partly visible; a lace curtain and a heavy blue drape hang at the right; a bearded man sits in an armchair at the lower right reading a newspaper.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Not contradicted so much as half-blind: the description names one of two figures. Nothing in the replacement goes beyond the image except the closing generalisation, which is carried over in substance from the original sentence.

proposals.title: G. Caillebotte - Villas à Trouville
proposals.currentDescription: Pastel seaside villas line the Normandy coast at Trouville, a fashionable resort favoured by Parisians on holiday. Caillebotte's looser handling and brighter palette here reflect his shift from urban scenes toward the open-air subjects of his later career.
proposals.proposedDescription: Two red-brick villas with steep slate roofs stand on a grassy slope above Trouville, seen from high on the hillside with the sea filling most of the canvas. Trouville was a fashionable resort favoured by Parisians on holiday; Caillebotte's looser handling and brighter palette here reflect his shift from urban scenes toward the open-air subjects of his later career.

issues.quote: Pastel seaside villas line the Normandy coast at Trouville
issues.problem: The villas are red brick with dark blue-grey slate roofs, not pastel; and there are two of them clustered on a hillside rather than a line of houses along a coast. The description also omits the sea, which occupies most of the canvas, and the raised viewpoint that is the picture's whole device.
issues.evidence: image

proposals.imageObservation: Seen from high on a grassy slope: two red-brick villas with steep blue-grey slate roofs, dormers and turrets sit at the lower left among shrubs, while a pale green-grey sea with a small sailing boat fills the upper two-thirds of the canvas under a grey sky.
proposals.reviewerNotes: ledgerStatus 'accurate' — the earlier pass did not check the colours against the image. The 1884 date and the Trouville subject are confirmed by Commons; the interpretive second sentence is preserved.

proposals.title: The Galata Tower by Moonlight
proposals.currentDescription: The Galata Tower rises over the Golden Horn under moonlight, masts and rooftops picked out in silver across the water. Aivazovsky painted this view in 1845 after visiting Constantinople with Grand Duke Konstantin Nikolaevich; the oil measures about 52 by 80 cm.
proposals.proposedDescription: The Galata Tower stands in dark silhouette above the Golden Horn while the moon burns low over the water, laying a broad gold track across the harbour; figures in Ottoman dress rest on the slope in the foreground. Aivazovsky painted this view in 1845 after visiting Constantinople with Grand Duke Konstantin Nikolaevich; the oil measures about 52 by 80 cm.

issues.quote: masts and rooftops picked out in silver across the water
issues.problem: The moonlight in this canvas is warm gold-amber, not silver; the masts and rooftops read as dark silhouettes against a gold sky and a gold reflection on the water.
issues.evidence: image

issues.quote: The Galata Tower rises over the Golden Horn under moonlight
issues.problem: The group of figures in Ottoman dress in the right foreground, which carries the picture's scale, goes unmentioned.
issues.evidence: image

metadataIssues.evidence: Sotheby's London, 26 November 2012, lot 5 (the record's own credit line) lists the canvas as 52 x 80 cm — the same figures the description already gives

proposals.imageObservation: A nocturne over Constantinople: the Galata Tower in dark silhouette at the left above a mass of rooftops, the moon a small golden disc low in the sky with a broad gold track across the water, minarets and domes on the far shore, cypresses and a wooden house at the right, and small figures in Ottoman dress on the slope in the foreground. Signed lower right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The dimensions check out (52 x 80 cm, Sotheby's London 26 Nov 2012 lot 5), as does the 1845 date; Aivazovsky's 1845 voyage to Constantinople and the Aegean with Grand Duke Konstantin Nikolaevich is well documented. Only the 'silver' palette and the missing foreground figures are changed.

proposals.title: Self Portrait
proposals.currentDescription: The artist at seventeen, with loose hair and a fixed gaze, the face firmly modelled while the clothing is left as bare canvas. Watts painted this oil, his first self-portrait, in 1834; it measures 53.3 by 38.1 cm and remains at the Watts Gallery in Compton, Surrey.
proposals.proposedDescription: The artist at seventeen, with loose hair and a fixed gaze, the face firmly modelled while the collar and jacket are laid in thinly and left unresolved. Watts painted this oil, his earliest known self-portrait, in 1834; it measures 53.3 by 38.1 cm and remains at the Watts Gallery in Compton, Surrey.

issues.quote: the clothing is left as bare canvas
issues.problem: Overstated. The collar, neckcloth and jacket are all painted, if thinly and loosely; nothing in the clothing is actually unprimed or unpainted canvas.
issues.evidence: image — the white collar and dark neckcloth are fully worked, and the jacket carries thin pinkish-grey paint with visible brushmarks.

issues.quote: his first self-portrait
issues.problem: A 'first' claim with no backing in the record. It is usually described as his earliest known self-portrait, which is a weaker statement than being his first.
issues.evidence: commons — objectName is 'Self Portrait, Aged 17 (also known as Self-Portrait As a Young Man)'; no priority claim anywhere in the record.

metadataIssues.evidence: web:https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:George_Frederick_Watts_001.jpg — the file page gives 53.3 x 38.1 cm, confirming the figure in the description.

proposals.imageObservation: Bust-length self-portrait of a young man with long loose dark curls looking straight out, painted against a scrubbed pinkish-grey ground; open white collar and a dark blue-grey neckcloth over a thinly brushed pale jacket, the lower area of the canvas left sketchy and unresolved.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The 53.3 x 38.1 cm figure, which looked like a classic invented dimension, checks out against the Commons file page, and the Watts Gallery attribution is confirmed by the Commons category. Only the 'bare canvas' overstatement and the unhedged 'first' needed changing. Worth adding the dimensions to the catalogue row, which currently has none.

proposals.title: Ginger Pot with Pomegranate and Pears
proposals.currentDescription: A glazed ginger jar bound with cord stands among pears and a split pomegranate on a rumpled white cloth. Oil on canvas of 1893, held by The Phillips Collection in Washington. Cézanne tipped the tabletop forward so the fruit reads against the dark ground rather than receding into it.
proposals.proposedDescription: A glazed ginger jar bound with cord stands among pears and a pomegranate on a rumpled white cloth, against a pale blue-grey drapery. Oil on canvas of 1893, held by The Phillips Collection in Washington. Cézanne tipped the tabletop forward so the fruit rides up the picture plane rather than receding into it.

issues.quote: so the fruit reads against the dark ground rather than receding into it
issues.problem: The ground is not dark. The backdrop behind the still life is a pale blue-grey drapery, lighter in value than most of the fruit; only a small area under the chest at the upper left is dark.
issues.evidence: image

issues.quote: a split pomegranate
issues.problem: The pomegranate is whole. At 3x zoom it shows an unbroken red-and-yellow skin with a dark curled calyx; no cut face and no seeds are visible.
issues.evidence: image - zoomed crop of the central fruit

proposals.imageObservation: A stoneware ginger jar bound with cord stands at the left on a table draped with a rumpled white cloth with a red stripe; pears and a whole pomegranate with a dark curled calyx lie in front of it, a white dish behind, and the backdrop is a pale blue-grey drapery with a patterned hanging at the upper right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The Phillips Collection and the 1893 date are confirmed by the Commons imageDescription. Both fixes are visual and easy to check against the file.

proposals.title: La Primavera
proposals.currentDescription: A profile bust composed entirely of spring blossoms, with a face of pink and white rose petals, a collar of small white flowers, and a torso of green leaves and flowering branches. Painted in 1573 as part of the Four Seasons series presented to Emperor Maximilian II, the panel exemplifies Arcimboldo's Mannerist conceit of building a human likeness entirely from natural produce.
proposals.proposedDescription: A profile bust composed entirely of spring blossoms, with a face of pink and white rose petals, a collar of small white flowers, and a torso of green leaves and flowering branches. Painted in 1563 as part of the Four Seasons series presented to Emperor Maximilian II, the panel exemplifies Arcimboldo's Mannerist conceit of building a human likeness entirely from natural produce.

issues.quote: Painted in 1573
issues.problem: The version shown is the Real Academia de Bellas Artes de San Fernando panel, which the Academia dates 1563 (inv. 0606, oil on panel, 66 × 50 cm). 1573 belongs to the later set of which the Louvre Spring is a member. The description's own next clause — the series presented to Maximilian II — fits the 1563 set, not the 1573 one, so the sentence is internally at odds.
issues.evidence: web:https://www.academiacolecciones.com/pinturas/inventario.php?id=0606 — 'Date: 1563 … Oil on panel … 66 × 50 cm'; image — the iris forming the sword pommel at lower left and the cabbage-leaf sleeve match the Academia's own description of their panel

metadataIssues.evidence: Real Academia de Bellas Artes de San Fernando catalogue, inv. 0606; Commons places the file in that collection

proposals.imageObservation: A profile bust built entirely from plants against a black ground: the face is made of pale pink and white blossoms with a rose at the cheek and a bud for the ear, the hair is a mass of mixed flowers with a white lily projecting at the upper right, the collar is a ruff of white daisies and narcissi, and the torso is green leaves with a large cabbage leaf for the sleeve. A brown-purple iris rises at the lower left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The visual half of the description is exact. The date is the issue, and note that the catalogue row repeats it, as does the Commons date field — so the error is upstream, not invented by the description writer. I identified the version from two details the Academia's own catalogue names: the iris forming the sword pommel at lower left and the cabbage leaf for the sleeve, both present in the image. If a human decides the asset is instead the Louvre 1573 panel, leave both date and description alone. 'The panel' is correct either way for the Madrid version (oil on panel).

proposals.title: Главная улица в Самарканде с высоты цитадели ранним утром
proposals.currentDescription: A landscape painting by Russian artist Vasily Vereshchagin depicting the main thoroughfare of Samarkand viewed from the citadel in the golden light of early morning. Executed between 1869 and 1870, the work is part of Vereshchagin's Turkestan series, capturing the architectural character and atmospheric conditions of this historic Silk Road city.
proposals.proposedDescription: A view over Samarkand from the citadel in the flat pale light of early morning: a sentry with a shouldered rifle stands among small cannon on the bare terrace, a tiled minaret with a blue inscription band rising at the left, while the domes and ruined facades of the city recede into dust-haze beyond. Vereshchagin painted it between 1869 and 1870 for his Turkestan series; it is in the Tretyakov Gallery.

issues.quote: in the golden light of early morning
issues.problem: The picture is painted in cool, flat, whitish-grey and pale ochre; there is no golden light in it.
issues.evidence: image — bleached sky, grey-blue haze over the city, no warm cast

issues.quote: capturing the architectural character and atmospheric conditions of this historic Silk Road city
issues.problem: Boilerplate that also skips the picture's actual content — an armed sentry and artillery on the citadel terrace, which is what makes it a Turkestan-series subject.
issues.evidence: image

proposals.imageObservation: A view from a citadel terrace over Samarkand at dawn: a tiled minaret base with blue Kufic inscription at the left, a brick dome below it, a sentry with a shouldered rifle and several small cannon on the bare terrace, and the low city with domes and ruined facades receding into pale dust-haze under a whitish sky.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Date range and series are confirmed by the Commons metadata and categories; the Tretyakov attribution comes from the record's own provenance block (Q24084651, inv. 1908).

proposals.title: Martyrdom of Saints John and Paul
proposals.currentDescription: A pen and brown ink with wash drawing shows an executioner raising a sword over a kneeling martyr while a second figure lies fallen to the right. The study, made by Guercino between 1630 and 1632, depicts the martyrdom of Saints John and Paul and is held at the Courtauld Institute of Art. The loose, energetic draughtsmanship and dramatic lighting typical of Guercino's preparatory works are evident in the quick contour lines and brown wash modelling.
proposals.proposedDescription: A pen and brown ink with wash drawing shows a nude executioner gripping a kneeling martyr with one hand, his sword held low at his side, while a beheaded body lies to the right with its severed head on the ground. The study, made by Guercino between 1630 and 1632, depicts the martyrdom of Saints John and Paul and is held at the Courtauld Institute of Art. The loose, energetic draughtsmanship of Guercino's preparatory work is evident in the quick contour lines and brown wash modelling.

issues.quote: an executioner raising a sword over a kneeling martyr
issues.problem: The sword is not raised and is not over the kneeling man: the executioner holds it low and away to his right, blade angled down, while grasping the kneeling figure with his other hand. The moment shown is the grip before the blow, not the blow itself.
issues.evidence: image | sword held at arm's length low to the right, well below shoulder height

issues.quote: a second figure lies fallen to the right
issues.problem: Understates and slightly mis-states what is there: the figure on the right is not merely fallen but decapitated, its severed head drawn separately on the ground - which is what identifies the subject as a double martyrdom.
issues.evidence: image | headless body with a detached head beside it; commons | category 'Decapitations of people in engravings'

proposals.imageObservation: Pen and brown ink drawing with brown wash on cream paper: a nude executioner seen from behind grips a kneeling, bowed figure at the left with one hand while his other arm extends down and to the right holding a sword low, its blade angled toward the ground; a beheaded body lies at the lower right with its severed head beside it, and blocks of architecture fill the right background.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Medium, date range, subject and collection all match the Commons record ('Sepia drawings', '1630s drawings', 'Drawings in the Courtauld Institute of Art', date 1630-1632). Only the action is misread. I also trimmed 'dramatic lighting', which is a stretch for a wash drawing with no strong light source, while keeping the rest of the final sentence.

proposals.title: Hawaiian Fisherman
proposals.currentDescription: A Hawaiian fisherman stands at the water's edge, holding a cast-net as he faces the open sea under a luminous sunset sky. Bartlett produced this shin-hanga woodblock print in 1916, combining the Western artist's compositional sense with the Japanese publisher's flat planes of colour and serene atmosphere.
proposals.proposedDescription: A Hawaiian fisherman strides through the shallows at the water's edge, a large cast-net gathered over his arms, the sea flat to the horizon under a pale sky of gold-lit clouds. Bartlett produced this shin-hanga woodblock print in 1916, combining the Western artist's compositional sense with the Japanese publisher's flat planes of colour and serene atmosphere.

issues.quote: stands at the water's edge
issues.problem: He is walking - one leg forward, the other heel lifted, wading through the shallows.
issues.evidence: image

issues.quote: under a luminous sunset sky
issues.problem: The sky is pale with warm gold-lit clouds; nothing identifies it as sunset rather than sunrise, and no source states a time of day.
issues.evidence: image; commons imageDescription is only 'Hawaiian Fisherman'

proposals.imageObservation: A woodblock print: a barefoot fisherman in profile strides through shallow water at the shoreline, a large pale cast-net gathered over his arms and shoulder, a flat blue sea behind him to the horizon and gold-lit clouds in a pale sky. Title 'HAWAIIAN FISHERMAN', artist's monogram and a pencil signature at the foot.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Low-stakes downgrade: the two flags are small and 'sunset' may well be right, it just is not supported. The second sentence is kept verbatim; the 1916 date and the Watanabe Shozaburo publisher reference are supported by the Commons date field and the 'Shozaburo Watanabe' category.

proposals.title: Hiroshige Kozuke
proposals.currentDescription: Print No. 26 from Hiroshige's series "Famous Places in the Sixty-odd Provinces," depicting Mount Haruna in Kōzuke Province blanketed in snow. A landmark work of the Tōsandō group within the series, created in August 1853 during the artist's mature period.
proposals.proposedDescription: Snow buries Mount Haruna from foot to summit: a red-railed bridge carries two small travellers across a gorge below a red shrine building set among snow-laden pines, with a blue stream running through the ravine at the bottom. Print No. 26 of Hiroshige's series Famous Places in the Sixty-odd Provinces, in the Tosando group, published in August 1853. This impression is in the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.

issues.quote: A landmark work of the Tōsandō group within the series
issues.problem: 'Landmark' is an evaluative claim with nothing behind it; the source only records that the print is No. 26 in the Tosando group of the series.
issues.evidence: commons - imageDescription reads 'Part of the series Famous Places in the Sixty-odd Provinces, No. 26 (Tosando group)'

issues.quote: created in August 1853 during the artist's mature period
issues.problem: The description never describes the image, and 'mature period' adds nothing checkable.
issues.evidence: house style

proposals.imageObservation: A vertical print of a snow-covered mountain filling the sheet: a red-railed bridge with two tiny travellers spans a gorge, a small red shrine building stands among snow-laden pines above, and a blue stream runs through the ravine below. Red title and signature cartouches at the upper right and left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Series number, Tosando group, August 1853 and the MFA Boston source all come from the Commons record. Everything I added to the first sentence is read straight off the image.

proposals.title: 冨嶽三十六景 東海道保土ケ谷-Hodogaya on the Tōkaidō
proposals.currentDescription: A woodblock print from Katsushika Hokusai's iconic series Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, depicting the town of Hodogaya along the Tōkaidō road. The composition features one of Hokusai's characteristic elevated perspectives with strong compositional depth. This Metropolitan Museum of Art example (DP141025) represents the series at its artistic zenith during the Edo period.
proposals.proposedDescription: Travellers, a laden packhorse and a palanquin move along the Tōkaidō at Hodogaya, framed by a row of tall pines, with snow-capped Mount Fuji rising between the trunks beyond. A colour woodblock print from Katsushika Hokusai's series Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, made about 1830-32. This impression is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art (DP141025).

issues.quote: one of Hokusai's characteristic elevated perspectives
issues.problem: The viewpoint here is at road level, level with the travellers, not raised or bird's-eye. This is the description's only concrete claim about the composition.
issues.evidence: image — the horizon sits behind the figures at their own height and the road recedes flat from the viewer

issues.quote: represents the series at its artistic zenith during the Edo period
issues.problem: Empty superlative with nothing behind it; nothing in the record or source ranks this sheet within the series.
issues.evidence: commons — the record carries only title, date, medium and MET provenance

issues.quote: depicting the town of Hodogaya along the Tōkaidō road
issues.problem: No town is shown — a line of pines, travellers and a handful of roofs at the right edge. Mount Fuji, the point of the series and plainly visible in the print, is never mentioned.
issues.evidence: image

proposals.imageObservation: A colour woodblock print seen from roughly eye level along a road: a screen of tall pines with pink trunks, travellers on foot, a green palanquin with bearers, a laden horse with a rider, and snow-capped Mount Fuji rising between the trunks in the middle distance; title cartouche at upper right, a few roofs at the right edge.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Series, artist, medium and the MET impression are all confirmed by Commons ('circa 1830-32', Metropolitan Museum donation). The 'elevated perspective' claim is the substantive error; I read the viewpoint as ground level with confidence, though someone could argue the road plane is seen from very slightly above.

evidence.sourceUrl: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:冨嶽三十六景_東海道保土ケ谷-Hodogaya_on_the_Tōkaidō_(Tōkaidō_Hodogaya),_from_the_series_Thirty-six_Views_of_Mount_Fuji_(Fugaku_sanjūrokkei)_MET_DP141025.jpg
evidence.objectKey: collection-of-beauty/冨嶽三十六景_東海道保土ケ谷-Hodogaya_on_the_Tōkaidō_(Tōkaidō_Hodogaya),_from_the_series_Thirty-six_Views_of_Mount_Fuji_(Fugaku_sanjūrokkei)_MET_DP141025.jpg

proposals.title: Holbein Danse Macabre 4
proposals.currentDescription: A woodcut from Hans Holbein the Younger's celebrated Dance of Death cycle, designed in the 1520s and first published at Lyon in 1538. Skeletons drag the living from every social rank, the moral message compressed into miniature scenes carved with extraordinary economy of line.
proposals.proposedDescription: Adam digs stony ground with a mattock while a skeleton works at his side, gripping a bough; behind them Eve sits nursing a child, and an hourglass stands on the ground at the left. The sheet belongs to Hans Holbein the Younger's Dance of Death, designed in the 1520s and first published at Lyon in 1538, a cycle in which death comes for every social rank in miniature scenes cut with great economy of line.

issues.quote: Skeletons drag the living from every social rank
issues.problem: True of the cycle, but placed as the only description of this sheet it misleads: this block is the labour of Adam after the Fall, with a single skeleton working alongside Adam while Eve nurses a child. Nobody is being dragged, and no social rank is at issue.
issues.evidence: image + commons categories 'Woodcuts of Adam and Eve' and 'Adam and Eve Forced to Labour'

metadataIssues.evidence: the description and the Commons categories ('Danse Macabre (Holbein)', 'Paintings by Hans Holbein der Juengere with fur') both identify the cycle; the record currently has no artist at all
standard publication history of the Lyon Trechsel edition, also asserted by the existing description

proposals.imageObservation: Small woodcut in a ruled border: a bearded man in a loincloth digs stony ground with a mattock while a skeleton beside him grips a long bough; behind them a woman sits on a bank nursing an infant, an hourglass stands on the ground at the left, and bare tree trunks fill the right side.
proposals.reviewerNotes: ledgerStatus 'accurate' — the earlier pass checked the cycle, not the sheet. The historical facts (designed in the 1520s, first published at Lyon in 1538) are right and are kept. The blocks were cut by Hans Luetzelburger after Holbein's designs, which is why the proposed artist field says 'Hans Holbein the Younger' as designer; apply with that caveat.

proposals.title: Holbein Danse Macabre 5
proposals.currentDescription: Plate from Holbein's Dance of Death, the influential moralising sequence designed in Basel in the 1520s. Death descends without warning on princes and labourers alike, a theme intensified by the woodcut's confined format and emphatic shadows.
proposals.proposedDescription: A crowd of skeletons blows trumpets and beats a pair of kettledrums among the arcades of a charnel house, bones and skulls scattered over the ground. This is the fifth sheet of Holbein's Dance of Death, the moralising sequence he designed in Basel in the 1520s, where the drums and trumpets open the dance; the plates that follow set Death against every rank of society in turn.

issues.quote: Death descends without warning on princes and labourers alike
issues.problem: Describes the theme of the series, not this plate. This sheet has no victim and no living person in it at all - it is the skeletons' concert that opens the cycle - so a reader is led to expect a scene the image does not contain.
issues.evidence: image; web:http://www.dodedans.com/Eholbein05.htm - plate 5 of Holbein's Dance of Death is 'All men's bones', the skeletons sounding drums and trumpets in a charnel house

proposals.imageObservation: A woodcut: a crowd of skeletons in a vaulted charnel arcade blowing long trumpets and a shawm, one beating a pair of kettledrums in the foreground with bones and a skull scattered on the ground. No living figure appears anywhere in the print.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The series-level facts in the original (Basel, 1520s, moralising sequence) are correct and preserved. The plate identity as 'All men's bones' is corroborated by dodedans.com's numbering of plate 5 and by the file name 'Holbein Danse Macabre 5'. I dropped 'emphatic shadows', which is a poor fit for a pure line-hatched woodcut.

proposals.title: The brig Mercury encounter after defeating two Turkish ships of the Russian squadron
proposals.currentDescription: The brig Mercury rejoins the Russian squadron after its 1829 escape from two Turkish line ships near the Bosphorus, sails crowding the horizon. Aivazovsky painted this commemoration in 1848, an oil of about 123.5 by 190 cm now in the State Russian Museum, St Petersburg.
proposals.proposedDescription: The brig Mercury under sail on a moonlit swell after its 1829 escape from two Turkish ships of the line near the Bosphorus, the Russian squadron it is rejoining just visible as faint masts on the far horizon. Aivazovsky painted this commemoration in 1848, an oil of about 123.5 by 190 cm now in the State Russian Museum, St Petersburg.

issues.quote: sails crowding the horizon
issues.problem: The squadron is a handful of barely visible masts in the far distance at the left; nothing crowds the horizon. The description also omits the painting's dominant feature, that it is a moonlit night piece.
issues.evidence: image; Commons category 'Night in seascape paintings'

metadataIssues.evidence: Russian Museum virtual catalogue entry for 'Бриг «Меркурий» после победы над двумя турецкими судами встречается с русской эскадрой', 1848, холст, масло, 123,5 x 190 см (https://rusmuseumvrm.ru/data/collections/painting/17_19/ayvazovskiy_ik_brig_merkuriy_1848_zh_2209/)

proposals.imageObservation: A night seascape: a single two-masted brig under sail on a moonlit swell at the right, a broad path of moonlight running toward the viewer, towering banks of cloud, and a few very faint masts of a distant squadron low on the horizon at the left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The historical and physical facts check out — the Russian Museum record gives 1848, oil on canvas, 123.5 x 190 cm — so the only change is to the visual clause. The 1829 action (brig Mercury, Captain-Lieutenant Kazarsky, against two Turkish ships of the line) is correct.

proposals.title: Portrait of Pope Pius VII
proposals.currentDescription: Pope Pius VII sits three-quarter length before the viewer, clothed in richly embroidered red papal vestments over a white rochet, his hand resting on the gilded arm of a throne-like chair. Inscribed 'PARISIIS 1805', the portrait was painted by Jacques-Louis David in Paris while the pontiff remained in the city following Napoleon's coronation. A restrained and penetrating characterisation, it shows the measured authority that made David the pre-eminent portraitist of the Napoleonic era.
proposals.proposedDescription: Pope Pius VII sits half-length before the viewer, clothed in richly embroidered red papal vestments over a white rochet, a folded paper in his right hand and his left resting on the gilded arm of a throne-like chair. Inscribed 'LUD. DAVID / PARISIIS 1805', the portrait was painted by Jacques-Louis David in Paris while the pontiff remained in the city following Napoleon's coronation. A restrained and penetrating characterisation, it shows the measured authority of David's Napoleonic-era portraiture.

issues.quote: sits three-quarter length before the viewer
issues.problem: The canvas is cut at roughly hip level, which is a half-length portrait; 'three-quarter length' conventionally means the figure shown to below the knees.
issues.evidence: image

issues.quote: the pre-eminent portraitist of the Napoleonic era
issues.problem: A superlative asserted rather than supported; the record and Commons say nothing of the kind.
issues.evidence: catalogue record; commons

proposals.imageObservation: A seated pope in a red velvet mozzetta over an embroidered red-and-gold stole and white rochet, wearing a white zucchetto, his right hand holding a folded paper inscribed 'Pio VII', his left resting on the gilded arm of a carved chair, against a plain dark ground; inscribed at upper left 'LUD. DAVID / PARISIIS 1805'. The figure is cut off at about hip level.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Spot-check of a prior 'minor-fixed' pass. The substance is right: the inscription is legible in the image exactly as quoted (the full inscription reads LUD. DAVID / PARISIIS 1805), the date matches the record, and Pius VII did remain in Paris into 1805 after the December 1804 coronation. Only the length descriptor and the superlative needed touching; Commons categories place the picture in the Louvre (INV 3701), which the description does not claim.

proposals.title: 'January' by Grant Wood
proposals.currentDescription: January is a painting by American artist Grant Wood, created between 1940 and 1941. The work is housed in the Cleveland Museum of Art and represents Wood's characteristic style blending regionalism with modernist elements.
proposals.proposedDescription: Snow-capped corn shocks stand in receding rows across a white field under a dark sky, each one drawn in fine crosshatched stalk detail, with lines of small animal tracks crossing the drifts in the foreground. Grant Wood painted January between 1940 and 1941; it is in the Cleveland Museum of Art.

issues.quote: January is a painting by American artist Grant Wood, created between 1940 and 1941.
issues.problem: The description is an encyclopaedia stub. It never says what the picture shows — snow-covered corn shocks and rabbit tracks — which is the whole point of the work.
issues.evidence: image.

issues.quote: represents Wood's characteristic style blending regionalism with modernist elements
issues.problem: Vague interpretive boilerplate with nothing behind it; 'modernist elements' is not anchored to anything in the picture or the record.
issues.evidence: catalogue record — nothing in the row or the Commons metadata supports this framing.

metadataIssues.evidence: commons date field: 'between 1940 and 1941'. The single-year value loses the range, though a single number may be all the schema takes.

proposals.imageObservation: Rows of conical corn shocks capped and streaked with snow recede across a white field under a dark sky, each shock rendered in fine crosshatched stalk detail; lines of small animal tracks cross the smooth snow in the foreground and middle distance.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The two factual claims (dates, Cleveland Museum of Art) are both correct and confirmed by the Commons record and the provenance block. I have deliberately not named the medium: the row does not give it and sources differ over canvas versus Masonite for this picture, so I left it out rather than guess.

proposals.title: Calling Home the Cows
proposals.currentDescription: A herder driving cattle homeward at the close of day, the animals strung out along a low horizon. Pastel and Conté crayon on wove paper, about 55.9 by 41.3 cm, made around 1866 and held by the National Gallery of Art, Washington, in the Corcoran Collection. It comes from the William A. Clark holdings of Millet pastels.
proposals.proposedDescription: A herdsman stands on a rise at sunset blowing a horn to call the herd in, leaning on his staff, with two cows large in the foreground and sheep scattered behind. Pastel and Conté crayon on wove paper, about 55.9 by 41.3 cm, made around 1866 and held by the National Gallery of Art, Washington, in the Corcoran Collection. It comes from the William A. Clark holdings of Millet pastels.

issues.quote: driving cattle homeward at the close of day
issues.problem: The herdsman is standing still and blowing a horn - the act the title names - not driving the animals along.
issues.evidence: image - he holds a horn to his lips with both the horn and staff clearly drawn

issues.quote: the animals strung out along a low horizon
issues.problem: The two most prominent animals are large in the immediate foreground; the horizon sits high in the sheet, not low.
issues.evidence: image

proposals.imageObservation: A pastel/crayon drawing: a herdsman stands on a grassy rise blowing a horn against a pink sunset sky, leaning on a staff; two cows fill the near foreground and sheep and further cattle spread across the middle ground; signed 'J.F. Millet' at lower right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Everything after the first sentence is verified and preserved verbatim: NGA lists 'pastel and conte crayon on wove paper', 22 x 16 1/4 in. (55.9 x 41.3 cm), c. 1866, Corcoran Collection (William A. Clark Collection, 1926) (web:nga.gov/artworks/168820-calling-home-cows via search).

proposals.title: The Stolen Kiss
proposals.currentDescription: A young woman in a silvery silk gown turns to receive a clandestine kiss in a doorway, the card party visible through the room beyond. Long attributed to Fragonard and now generally given to his sister-in-law and pupil Marguerite Gérard, the late-1780s panel passed through the Stanisław August collection to the Hermitage, where it still hangs.
proposals.proposedDescription: A young woman in a silvery silk gown turns to receive a clandestine kiss in a doorway, reaching for a striped shawl as a gathering is visible through the room beyond. Long attributed to Fragonard and now often given to his sister-in-law and pupil Marguerite Gerard, or to the two of them together, the late-1780s canvas passed through the collection of Stanislaw August to the Hermitage, where it still hangs.

issues.quote: the late-1780s panel
issues.problem: The Hermitage picture is oil on canvas, about 45 by 55 cm, not a panel.
issues.evidence: web:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Stolen_Kiss_(painting) | oil on canvas, 45 x 55 cm, Hermitage Museum

issues.quote: now generally given to his sister-in-law and pupil Marguerite Gérard
issues.problem: Overstates the consensus: the attribution is shared or disputed rather than settled on Gerard alone, and the source evidence names both artists.
issues.evidence: commons | artist field reads 'Jean-Honore Fragonard / Marguerite Gerard'

proposals.imageObservation: Interior in oils: a young woman in a silvery-white satin gown, caught in a doorway, leans back as a man half-hidden behind the door kisses her cheek; she reaches right for a striped shawl draped over a chair, and through a further doorway at the right a group of seated figures is visible in a lit room. A red curtain hangs at the left, a patterned carpet below.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The provenance is right: the picture belonged to Stanislaw August Poniatowski at the Lazienki Palace in Warsaw, entered the Russian imperial collections and was transferred to the Hermitage in 1895. Gerard was indeed Fragonard's sister-in-law and pupil. Only the support (canvas, not panel) is a hard error; the attribution wording is softened rather than replaced. The 'card party' reading of the group in the next room is plausible but not clearly legible in this reproduction, so my replacement says 'a gathering' - restore 'card party' if a museum source backs it. Accents dropped in Gerard/Stanislaw here for encoding only.

proposals.title: The Field of Waterloo
proposals.currentDescription: Night falls on the battlefield as women search the heaped dead by torchlight, three years after the engagement. Turner had walked the ground himself; the picture quotes Byron's Childe Harold and refuses any patriotic triumph.
proposals.proposedDescription: Night falls on the battlefield as women search the heaped dead by torchlight. Turner exhibited the picture three years after the battle, having walked the ground himself; it quotes Byron's Childe Harold and refuses any patriotic triumph.

issues.quote: women search the heaped dead by torchlight, three years after the engagement
issues.problem: As written, the clause dates the depicted scene three years after the battle. The picture shows the night of the battle itself; it is the painting that came three years later (exhibited 1818, battle 1815).
issues.evidence: image and catalogue record — the scene is the immediate aftermath by torchlight; the record's year is 1818

proposals.imageObservation: A dark battlefield at night: a heap of dead and dying soldiers fills the foreground, a woman among them holding up a flaring torch, other figures searching; a burst of white light breaks through the black clouds above, a building burns at the right, smoke and darkness elsewhere.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Only the placement of 'three years after' is wrong, and the fix is to move it onto the painting rather than the scene. Turner's 1817 visit to the battlefield and the Childe Harold quotation in the 1818 Royal Academy catalogue are both well established; the Tate/N00500 provenance is in the record. Prior ledger status 'accurate' is defensible if the clause is read as being about the painting, so treat this as a wording fix, not a factual rescue.

proposals.title: Julie de Graag December 1917
proposals.currentDescription: A woodcut print by Dutch artist Julie de Graag depicting a sleeping cat. Part of a series of December-themed works, this 1917 print exemplifies the artist's characteristic technique and intimate subject matter from her prolific career in printmaking.
proposals.proposedDescription: A two-colour woodcut of a ginger cat curled asleep, its body reduced to flat orange shapes inside heavy black outlines against a hatched dark ground, with DECEMBER lettered underneath and the artist's initials and the date 1917 in the corners of the block. The sheet measures about 9 by 12 cm and the impression is in the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam, from the 1927 gift of M. J. de Graag.

issues.quote: Part of a series of December-themed works
issues.problem: Nothing supports a series of works about December. The Rijksmuseum subject index reads 'cat. December; Decembre (Ripa)', which points to a months-of-the-year set - one print per month - not several December prints.
issues.evidence: commons - Rijksmuseum record: "Onderwerp Wat: cat. December; 'Decembre' (Ripa)"

issues.quote: her prolific career in printmaking
issues.problem: De Graag's output was small and her career short; 'prolific' is an unsupported adjective, and neither the record nor the source says anything about her productivity.
issues.evidence: catalogue record and Commons carry no career information

issues.quote: exemplifies the artist's characteristic technique and intimate subject matter
issues.problem: Boilerplate. The description omits the two-colour orange-and-black scheme and the DECEMBER lettering, which are the print's most visible features.
issues.evidence: image

proposals.imageObservation: A small two-colour woodcut mounted on cream paper: a ginger tabby cat curled asleep, drawn in flat orange with heavy black outlines against a black ground hatched with orange lines. Lettered DECEMBER below the image, with 'A.J.D.G.' at lower left and '1917' at lower right inside the block, and a pencil signature on the mount.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Medium, subject, artist and date are all confirmed by the Rijksmuseum record quoted on Commons ('houtsnede', 'Een slapende kat', 1917, blad h 89 mm x b 118 mm, credit line 'Schenking van mevrouw M.J. de Graag', acquired 1927), and the sheet size matches the record's realDimensions of 11.7 x 8.7 cm. I have not asserted a months-of-the-year series in the replacement because the Ripa reference only suggests it; if someone can confirm the set, that would be the right context sentence.

proposals.title: Kanae Yamamoto
