proposals.currentDescription: Oil painting by Japanese artist Kanae Yamamoto, a prominent modernist painter of the early twentieth century. The work is housed in the Municipal Museum Kanae Yamamoto in Ueda, Japan.
proposals.proposedDescription: A blue lake under a clear sky, with a wooded mountain rising across the water, a single small boat carrying one figure at the right, and a sandy foreground bank of grasses. Kanae Yamamoto painted this oil, Early Autumn at Lake Haruna, in 1937. It is in the Municipal Museum Kanae Yamamoto in Ueda.

issues.quote: Oil painting by Japanese artist Kanae Yamamoto, a prominent modernist painter of the early twentieth century.
issues.problem: The description never says what the picture shows — a lake, a mountain and a boat — and reduces to a one-line biography lifted from the Commons caption plus a collection line.
issues.evidence: commons — imageDescription is "Oil painting by Japanese artist Kanae Yamamoto", credit "Municipal Museum Kanae Yamamoto, Ueda"

issues.quote: a prominent modernist painter of the early twentieth century
issues.problem: Yamamoto Kanae is chiefly remembered as the founder of the sōsaku-hanga (creative print) movement and of the peasant art movement; calling him simply a prominent modernist painter is vague and slightly misplaces him.
issues.evidence: knowledge — Yamamoto Kanae's standing rests on the creative-print movement; the record's own movement field ("Shin-hanga") is likewise wrong for him

metadataIssues.proposed: Sōsaku-hanga (or none — this work is an oil painting, not a print)
metadataIssues.evidence: The work is an oil painting per Commons; Yamamoto Kanae is the founding figure of the sōsaku-hanga movement, which stood in opposition to shin-hanga.

proposals.imageObservation: A landscape in oils: a broad blue lake under a pale blue sky, a green and ochre mountain rising across the water with a pale scree slope on its flank, a single small boat with one figure at the right, and a sandy foreground bank with tufts of grass and a small shrub.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Nothing in the old text is false — it is just a caption, not a description. The English title in the replacement is taken from the record's own englishTitle field and the Commons imageDescription. I did not assert which mountain is shown (Haruna-Fuji would be the obvious guess) because the reproduction cannot settle it.

proposals.title: Kanae Yamamoto
proposals.currentDescription: Oil painting by Japanese artist Kanae Yamamoto (1882–1946). The work depicts the landscape near Iizuna in the Kōgen region. Held in the Municipal Museum Kanae Yamamoto, Ueda.
proposals.proposedDescription: A blue-green mountain rises behind lower ridges under a pale clouded sky, with a broad belt of conifers across the foreground. An oil painting by Kanae Yamamoto (1882-1946) of the Iizuna highlands, the subject of its title Kogen - Iizuna. Held in the Municipal Museum Kanae Yamamoto, Ueda.

issues.quote: the landscape near Iizuna in the Kōgen region
issues.problem: There is no 'Kogen region'. Kogen is the Japanese word for highlands/plateau: the title 'Kogen - Iizuna' means 'Highlands: Iizuna', as the record's own englishTitle spells out. The sentence turns a common noun into a place name.
issues.evidence: catalogue record | englishTitle reads 'Highlands: Iizuna (Kōgen — Iizuna)'; knowledge | 高原 kogen = highland/plateau, and Iizuna Kogen is the highland area by Mt Iizuna in Nagano

issues.quote: The work depicts the landscape near Iizuna
issues.problem: Nothing about the picture itself - the blue-green massif, the ridge line, the belt of conifers - reaches the description.
issues.evidence: image | mountain and forest occupy the whole canvas

metadataIssues.evidence: The work is an oil painting, not a print, and Yamamoto Kanae is the founding figure of the sosaku-hanga (creative print) movement, not of shin-hanga, which was the rival publisher-led school.

metadataIssues.proposed: drop, or replace with a measured figure
metadataIssues.evidence: A print-series default size has been applied to an oil painting; the Commons record gives no dimensions.

proposals.imageObservation: Oil landscape in blues and greens: a rounded mountain with a small peak rises behind lower ridges under a pale clouded sky, with a broad band of conifer forest and pale grass across the foreground. Small monogram at lower right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Oil medium, artist, dates and the Ueda museum are all supported by the Commons imageDescription and credit fields. The substantive fix is the phantom 'Kogen region'. The two metadata issues matter more than the text: labelling an oil painting shin-hanga and giving it a print series' default dimensions are both wrong, and the dimensions are the kind of thing the 3D gallery layout consumes.

proposals.title: Ono Waterfall on the Kisokaidō
proposals.currentDescription: Travellers and packhorses pause on the Kisokaidō highway beside the Ono falls, dwarfed by a smooth blue sheet of water. From the Tour of the Waterfalls, the print pairs Hokusai's stylised, almost geometric treatment of cascades with the everyday traffic of one of Edo Japan's great post roads.
proposals.proposedDescription: Travellers in wide straw hats pause with their shouldered bundles on the Kisokaido highway beside the Ono falls, dwarfed by a smooth blue sheet of water. From the Tour of the Waterfalls, the print pairs Hokusai's stylised, almost geometric treatment of cascades with the everyday traffic of one of Edo Japan's great post roads.

issues.quote: Travellers and packhorses pause on the Kiso
issues.problem: There are no horses in the print. The loads are carried by the men themselves; one bundle is stacked on the ground.
issues.evidence: image - 3x crop of the figure group at lower right shows four human porters and no animal.

proposals.imageObservation: Colour woodblock print: a tall blue waterfall falls in a smooth striated sheet at the left; at lower right three or four travellers in wide straw hats, one carrying a shouldered load and one with a stacked white bundle set on the ground, stand on the path by an arched bridge over a stream; a red-and-green roofed building on the slope above.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Spot-check of a prior 'accurate' verdict; the packhorses do not exist in this impression. Everything else - the series, the falls, the highway - holds. Note the quote field is truncated before the accented 'o' in Kisokaido; the full phrase in the description is 'Travellers and packhorses pause on the Kisokaido highway'.

proposals.title: Кочевая дорога в горах Алатау
proposals.currentDescription: A painting by Russian artist Vasily Vereshchagin (1842–1904) depicting a nomadic caravan traversing the Alatau mountain range. Vereshchagin was renowned for his historical and orientalist works, often capturing scenes of Central Asian landscapes and cultures during the 19th century.
proposals.proposedDescription: Three riders on a stony track cut into a steep mountainside in the Alatau: one halted in the middle distance on a white horse, two more further along the ridge, one of them with a rifle across his shoulder. Red and yellow wildflowers cover the bank below the road. Vereshchagin painted it in 1869-70 as part of his Turkestan work; it is in the Tretyakov Gallery, Moscow.

issues.quote: depicting a nomadic caravan traversing the Alatau mountain range
issues.problem: There is no caravan — three individual horsemen strung along a mountain track, with no pack animals or baggage train in view.
issues.evidence: image — enlarged crop of the middle distance shows two riders and the foreground a third; nothing else on the road

issues.quote: Vereshchagin was renowned for his historical and orientalist works, often capturing scenes of Central Asian landscapes and cultures during the 19th century.
issues.problem: Generic biography that says nothing about this picture; the description never mentions the track, the terrain, the flowers or the Tretyakov, all of which are available from the image and the record.
issues.evidence: catalogue record — provenance names the Tretyakov Gallery; Commons categories place it in the Turkestan series

metadataIssues.evidence: commons — date given as 'between 1869 and 1870'

proposals.imageObservation: A stony track cut across a steep, dry mountainside under a clear blue sky. One rider on a white horse has halted in the middle distance; two more riders, one shouldering a rifle and one in pink on a light horse, are further along the ridge. Red and yellow wildflowers grow on the grassy bank at lower left. No pack train or caravan is visible.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The Turkestan-series attribution comes from the Commons category, the Tretyakov from the record's own provenance block (Q24089637). I have avoided calling it an oil study or naming a support, since neither the record nor Commons states the medium.

proposals.title: L'Homme au bonnet de coton
proposals.currentDescription: A seated man in a white cotton cap, his face built up in thick ridges of paint. Oil on canvas, painted in 1866 and held by the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York. The sitter is the artist's uncle Dominique Aubert, whom Cézanne painted in a series of portraits laid in heavily with the palette knife, a phase he later called couillarde.
proposals.proposedDescription: A seated man in a blue and white cotton cap, his face built up in thick ridges of paint. Oil on canvas, painted in 1866 and held by the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York. The sitter is the artist's uncle Dominique Aubert, whom Cézanne painted in a series of portraits laid in heavily with the palette knife, a phase he later called couillarde.

issues.quote: a white cotton cap
issues.problem: The cap is predominantly blue-green with white highlights, not white. The Met's own title for this picture is 'The Man in a Blue Cap'.
issues.evidence: image — the cap reads clearly blue and green with a black tassel; knowledge — the Met titles the work 'The Man in a Blue Cap (Uncle Dominique)'.

proposals.imageObservation: Bust-length portrait of a dark-bearded man in a soft cap that is painted blue-green with white and pale-yellow highlights and a black tassel; he wears a red neckcloth, a black waistcoat and a heavy cream coat, all built in thick knife-laid slabs against a grey-brown ground.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Only the cap colour is wrong; sitter, date, museum and the couillarde palette-knife phase are all correct and confirmed by the Commons categories (Portrait paintings of Dominique Aubert by Paul Cezanne; Paintings by Paul Cezanne in the Metropolitan Museum of Art). The French title 'bonnet de coton' probably drove the 'white' — cotton cap, not white cap.

proposals.title: L-L Boilly Une loge
proposals.currentDescription: Spectators crowd a theatre box on a free-admission performance day, a working-class audience pressed shoulder to shoulder. Boilly titled the panel 'Une loge, un jour de spectacle gratuit'; the small oil measures 32.5 by 41.7 cm and hangs in the Musée Lambinet at Versailles.
proposals.proposedDescription: Spectators crowd a theatre box on a free-admission performance day, a working-class audience pressed shoulder to shoulder. The picture is called 'Une loge, un jour de spectacle gratuit'; the small oil on canvas measures 32.5 by 41.7 cm and hangs in the Musee Lambinet at Versailles.

issues.quote: Boilly titled the panel
issues.problem: The support is canvas, not panel. 'Titled the panel' also attributes the title to Boilly himself, which no source here states.
issues.evidence: web:https://art.rmngp.fr/fr/library/artworks/louis-leopold-boilly_une-loge-un-jour-de-spectacle-gratuit_huile-sur-toile_1830 — RMN records it as huile sur toile, 1830; the Joconde notice (pop.culture.gouv.fr/notice/joconde/04000000016) agrees.

proposals.imageObservation: A theatre box packed with faces of every age - old men, women in caps and headscarves, children - crammed shoulder to shoulder behind the box rail, framed by a pale pilaster and cornice. Signed 'L Boilly' at lower right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Title, dimensions and the Musee Lambinet are all in the Commons image description and confirmed by RMN/Joconde; only the support word changes. Note one Flickr caption places the picture at the Musee Marmottan Monet - almost certainly a loan photograph; Lambinet is the owning museum.

proposals.title: The Virgin of the Immaculate Conception
proposals.currentDescription: The Virgin rises on a billowing cloud attended by four full-sized angels against a dramatic sky, her hands clasped at her breast, with lilies and symbolic objects below her. Begun by El Greco between 1608 and 1614 and completed by his son Jorge Manuel Theotokópoulos, the painting presents the Immaculate Conception in the elongated, intensely spiritual manner of El Greco's late Toledan period, and now hangs in the Museo Thyssen-Bornemisza, Madrid.
proposals.proposedDescription: The Virgin rises on a billowing cloud, her hands raised open before her breast and her feet resting on a knot of cherub heads, while some six angels press in around her and the dove of the Holy Spirit hovers above; a domed rotunda, a fountain and lilies fill the dark landscape below. Begun by El Greco between 1608 and 1614 and completed by his son Jorge Manuel Theotokopoulos, the painting presents the Immaculate Conception in the elongated, intensely spiritual manner of El Greco's late Toledan period, and now hangs in the Museo Thyssen-Bornemisza, Madrid.

issues.quote: attended by four full-sized angels
issues.problem: Six full-length angels are discernible - three at the left (one large praying figure, a head behind it and a smaller one holding a book) and three at the right (a gold-robed figure beside the Virgin, a praying angel and a red-and-blue angel with a staff).
issues.evidence: image — a 2.2x crop of the upper third resolves six angel figures plus the winged cherub heads under the Virgin's feet.

issues.quote: her hands clasped at her breast
issues.problem: Her hands are raised in front of her chest with palms open and fingers apart, not clasped together.
issues.evidence: image — the 2.2x crop shows two separated open hands.

proposals.imageObservation: The Virgin in a dark blue mantle over a red bodice rises on billowing cloud, her hands raised open in front of her breast, standing on a knot of winged cherub heads; the dove of the Holy Spirit hovers above, and at least six full-length angels crowd in at either side, one holding an open book. Below, in near-darkness, are a domed rotunda, a fountain, lilies and roses.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The attribution sentence is preserved verbatim and is supported by Commons ('El Greco / Jorge Manuel Theocupulus', 'between 1608 and 1614') and by the record's museothyssen.org source link. The angel count is a judgement call - two of the six are partly hidden heads - hence 'some six' rather than a hard number in the replacement.

proposals.title: Le Garçon au gilet rouge
proposals.currentDescription: Oil painting by Paul Cézanne created between 1888 and 1890. The work depicts a young boy wearing a distinctive red waistcoat in three-quarter view. This iconic portrait exemplifies Cézanne's mastery of form and color, combining careful anatomical structure with his characteristic approach to pictorial composition.
proposals.proposedDescription: A boy in a broad-brimmed hat, red waistcoat and full-sleeved white shirt with a blue neckcloth stands facing the viewer at three-quarter length, a heavy curtain hanging beside him. Oil on canvas, painted by Cézanne between 1888 and 1890; the picture is in the National Gallery of Art, Washington. The right arm is drawn out well past its natural length to carry the fall of the composition.

issues.quote: This iconic portrait exemplifies Cézanne's mastery of form and color, combining careful anatomical structure with his characteristic approach to pictorial composition.
issues.problem: Pure boilerplate, and 'careful anatomical structure' runs against the picture, where the boy's right arm is famously elongated well beyond anatomical proportion.
issues.evidence: image — the hanging arm reaches nearly to the bottom of the canvas

issues.quote: in three-quarter view
issues.problem: The boy faces the viewer nearly frontally. What is three-quarter here is the length of the figure, not the angle — Commons categorises the work under 'oil paintings of boys at three-quarter length'.
issues.evidence: image; commons category '19th-century oil paintings of boys at three-quarter length'

issues.quote: The work depicts a young boy wearing a distinctive red waistcoat
issues.problem: The hat, the white shirt, the blue neckcloth and the curtain — most of what is actually in the frame — go unmentioned, and the description never names the collection although the record's own title does.
issues.evidence: image; catalogue record title 'Le Garçon au gilet rouge, par Paul Cézanne, National Gallery of Art'

proposals.imageObservation: A boy in a broad-brimmed dark-red hat, red waistcoat, full-sleeved white shirt and blue neckcloth faces the viewer almost frontally, shown down to below the knees, with a heavy grey-blue curtain hanging at the right and patterned drapery behind at the left; his right arm hangs long and unnaturally down the picture's edge.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Date range matches Commons ('circa from 1888 until 1890') and the NGA credit is in the Commons record. The elongated arm is a standard observation about this canvas and is plainly visible; if the reviewer prefers to keep the rewrite strictly descriptive, that last sentence can be dropped without loss.

proposals.title: "Le jardin Hoschedé à Montgeron" d'A. Sisley
proposals.currentDescription: Le jardin Hoschedé à Montgeron Oeuvre d'Alfred Sisley (1839-1899) Montgeron, 1881 Huile sur toile Collection Ivan Morozov, 26 novembre 1904 Musée d'Etat des beaux-arts Pouchkine, Moscou Oeuvre de l'exposition "La collection Morozov. Icônes de l'art moderne", Fondation Louis Vuitton, Paris Conçue par Anne Baldassari, commissaire général, l’exposition déploie cet ensemble dans une muséographie originale occupant la totalité des espaces de la Fondation Louis Vuitton.
proposals.proposedDescription: Tall trees with yellow and rust-tinged foliage frame a sunlit lawn, with a red-roofed house and outbuildings glimpsed among the greenery in the middle distance under a blue sky; the canvas is signed Sisley at the lower right. Alfred Sisley painted the Hoschedé garden at Montgeron in 1881, oil on canvas. The picture entered Ivan Morozov's collection in 1904 and belongs to the Pushkin State Museum of Fine Arts in Moscow; this photograph was taken when it was shown at the Fondation Louis Vuitton in Paris.

issues.quote: Oeuvre de l'exposition "La collection Morozov. Icônes de l'art moderne", Fondation Louis Vuitton, Paris
issues.problem: The whole description is the Commons uploader's transcription of a French wall label plus exhibition marketing copy about the Fondation Louis Vuitton show and its curator. It never says what the painting shows, is not in English like the rest of the corpus, and carries text about an exhibition rather than the work.
issues.evidence: commons — the description is verbatim identical to the Commons imageDescription field

issues.quote: Montgeron, 1881
issues.problem: The description dates the painting 1881 while the catalogue row's year field is 1839, which is Sisley's birth year (also given in the same sentence as '1839-1899').
issues.evidence: catalogue record year=1839 vs description and Commons label 'Montgeron, 1881'

metadataIssues.evidence: The museum wall label transcribed on Commons reads 'Montgeron, 1881'; 1839 is Sisley's date of birth, taken from '(1839-1899)' in the same label.

proposals.imageObservation: An Impressionist garden landscape: tall trees with yellow and rust-tinged foliage frame a sunlit green lawn, a house with a red roof and outbuildings appear in the middle distance among the trees, blue sky with white cloud above; signed 'Sisley' at the lower right. Photographed in its frame.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Nothing in the original is false — it is a faithful label transcription — so this is a style and language fix, plus the year-field correction. Every fact in the replacement comes from that label. Note the file is a CC BY photograph of the framed painting on a wall, not a flat reproduction.

proposals.title: Le Jardinier Vallier
proposals.currentDescription: Vallier, the gardener and odd-job man at Cézanne's house near Aix, sits with hands resting in his lap, the figure built from dark greens and blues. One of six portraits of the sitter, painted in the summer and autumn of 1906, the last months of Cézanne's life. The painter worked on the Vallier series within days of his death that October.
proposals.proposedDescription: Vallier, the gardener and odd-job man at Cézanne's house near Aix, sits in a broad-brimmed hat with his hands folded in his lap, the figure worked in patches of cream, ochre and green against a dark ground. It belongs to the group of portraits Cézanne made of Vallier in 1906, the last year of his life; he was still working on a portrait of the sitter within days of his death that October.

issues.quote: the figure built from dark greens and blues
issues.problem: The figure is built from cream, pale ochre and green patches over dark outlines; it is the surrounding ground that is dark green-brown, and there is very little blue anywhere in the canvas.
issues.evidence: image

issues.quote: One of six portraits of the sitter, painted in the summer and autumn of 1906
issues.problem: The count is not settled — the National Gallery of Art's account of the group gives five paintings of Vallier — and dating the whole group to the summer and autumn of 1906 is a specificity nothing in the record supports (portraits of Vallier are variously dated across 1902-1906).
issues.evidence: web:https://www.arts.gov/stories/blog/2018/spotlight-cezannes-portraits-national-gallery-art — 'Cézanne painted five paintings of his gardener Vallier'

proposals.imageObservation: An old bearded man in a broad-brimmed hat sits turned to the right, hands folded in his lap, his jacket and trousers built up in short patches of cream, pale ochre and green over dark contour strokes, against a very dark green-brown ground.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The subject, the 1906 date (Commons) and the fact that Cézanne was working on a Vallier portrait in his final days are all supportable. I dropped the exact count and the season, and corrected the palette. Whether this particular canvas is in a private collection — as the filename says — is not asserted either way in my rewrite, since the record's provenance field is empty.

proposals.title: Les Grands Boulevards - Renoir - 1875 - NG
proposals.currentDescription: A Paris boulevard busy with strollers and carriages beneath thin spring trees, the rebuilt Haussmann city stretching back along the pavement. Renoir painted it in 1875, oil on canvas measuring about 52 by 64 cm, now in the Philadelphia Museum of Art.
proposals.proposedDescription: A Paris boulevard busy with strollers and carriages under a full canopy of boulevard trees, the rebuilt Haussmann city stretching back along the pavement. Renoir painted it in 1875, oil on canvas measuring about 52 by 64 cm, now in the Philadelphia Museum of Art.

issues.quote: thin spring trees
issues.problem: The boulevard trees are in full, dense leaf across the top third of the canvas, not thin or sparsely leafed.
issues.evidence: image - heavy green and yellow canopy

metadataIssues.proposed: note that this is the Commons photo credit, not the owning collection
metadataIssues.evidence: Commons categories place the painting in the Philadelphia Museum of Art ('The Grands Boulevards (1875) by Pierre-Auguste Renoir in the Philadelphia Museum of Art'); the description's Philadelphia attribution is the correct one, and the record's credit/title 'NG' could mislead a later reader

proposals.imageObservation: A wide boulevard seen at an angle: strollers in dark coats, a carriage with two white horses, a kiosk and lamp-post at left, Haussmann apartment blocks and a shopfront awning at right, and a dense canopy of green-gold foliage over the pavement. Signed 'Renoir 75' lower right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The dimensions given (about 52 by 64 cm) match the Philadelphia canvas closely, and the museum attribution is backed by the Commons category, so only the foliage description changed.

proposals.title: Левитан У омута
proposals.currentDescription: A serene landscape painting by Russian master Isaac Levitan, created in 1892. The work depicts a tranquil pool or small body of water nestled in a wooded setting, exemplifying Levitan's mastery of mood and natural light in landscape composition. Housed in the Tretyakov Gallery, Moscow.
proposals.proposedDescription: A rough log walkway and weir cross a dark pool at the edge of a wood, the far bank in deep shadow beneath a heavy, clouded sky. Levitan painted it in 1892; the canvas is in the Tretyakov Gallery, Moscow.

issues.quote: A serene landscape painting by Russian master Isaac Levitan, created in 1892. The work depicts a tranquil pool or small body of water nestled in a wooded setting
issues.problem: Mood is the opposite of what is painted: the picture is dark and heavy, with a shadowed pool under a clouded sky. It also omits the dominant object in the frame, the rough log footbridge and weir crossing the water.
issues.evidence: image - log walkway occupies the lower third; palette is dark green, brown and grey

issues.quote: exemplifying Levitan's mastery of mood and natural light in landscape composition
issues.problem: Empty praise standing in for description.
issues.evidence: corpus house style

proposals.imageObservation: A dark millpond or river pool crossed by a rough log walkway and weir built of unbarked timber; dense dark woods on the far bank, a bank of grey-white cloud over a strip of pale evening sky, muted greens and browns. Signed and dated lower right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Date and collection are both supported (Commons: 'Landscape paintings in the Tretyakov Gallery', date 1892). The rewrite only fixes the mood and adds the log crossing; I deliberately left out the folklore usually attached to the title, which I could not source.

proposals.title: Portrait of Maximilien de Robespierre
proposals.currentDescription: A presumed portrait of Maximilien de Robespierre in a high cravat, set against a dark ground. Oil on canvas, about 41 by 32 cm, in the Palais des Beaux-Arts de Lille and usually dated around 1791. The attribution and date remain contested, with some scholars placing the canvas before 1789.
proposals.proposedDescription: A full-length portrait of a young man seated at a rolltop desk, papers, inkstand and quill at his elbow, a small spaniel under the chair and an open travelling case on the floor beside him; the sitter is traditionally identified as Maximilien de Robespierre. Oil on canvas, about 41 by 32 cm, in the Palais des Beaux-Arts de Lille and usually dated around 1791. Both the identification and the date remain contested.

issues.quote: in a high cravat, set against a dark ground
issues.problem: Describes a bust-length portrait against an empty background. The picture is a full-length seated portrait in an interior: desk with papers and quill, red chair, a small dog at the sitter's feet and an open case on the floor. Nothing of the actual scene is described.
issues.evidence: image; Commons categories 'Desks in portrait paintings' and 'Portrait en pied ... a son bureau' in French catalogue listings

issues.quote: with some scholars placing the canvas before 1789
issues.problem: Sources that dissent from c.1791 date the picture *to* 1789, not 'before 1789'.
issues.evidence: web:https://www.meisterdrucke.fr/fine-art-prints/Louis-Leopold-Boilly/961290/ - captions the Lille canvas '1789, 41 x 32,5 cm'

proposals.imageObservation: A full-length seated portrait of a young powdered-wig sitter in a blue-grey coat, olive waistcoat and white breeches, on a red-upholstered chair beside a rolltop desk with papers, inkstand and quill; a small black-and-white spaniel stands under the chair and an open black travelling case sits at lower left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Dimensions (41 x 32 cm), medium, collection and the c.1791 dating are confirmed by the Lille museum record (inv. P 396) and RMN. Note the identification as Robespierre is 'presumed' - the museum's own title is 'Portrait presume de Robespierre'; the existing description's 'presumed' hedge is correct and I kept it.

proposals.title: The Triumph of Marat
proposals.currentDescription: A crowd carries the deputy Jean-Paul Marat aloft after his acquittal before the Revolutionary Tribunal in April 1793, banners and pikes raised above the throng. Oil on canvas, dated 1794, in the Palais des Beaux-Arts de Lille. Boilly turned to the multi-figure street scene that would occupy much of his later career.
proposals.proposedDescription: A crowd carries the deputy Jean-Paul Marat aloft after his acquittal before the Revolutionary Tribunal in April 1793, hats and pikes raised above the throng beneath the arcades of a large public building. Oil on canvas, dated 1794, in the Palais des Beaux-Arts de Lille. Boilly turned to the multi-figure crowd scene that would occupy much of his later career.

issues.quote: banners and pikes raised above the throng
issues.problem: No banners appear anywhere in the picture. What is raised above the crowd is hats (several on arms and sticks) and a few plain poles/pike shafts.
issues.evidence: image — repeated crops of the crowd at 2-3x show hats, bare arms and thin poles only; nothing with cloth or lettering.

issues.quote: the multi-figure street scene
issues.problem: The scene is set inside/among the arcades of a large public building, not in a street; the phrase mislabels this picture even though Boilly's later crowd pieces are often street subjects.
issues.evidence: image — vaulted arcades, masonry piers and a sculpted relief on a plinth frame the crowd.

proposals.imageObservation: A dense crowd of men, women and children fills the floor of a tall arcaded stone hall; at right a man in a dark coat and white cravat is held up above the throng, arms out. Hats are waved on raised arms and several thin pole/pike shafts rise diagonally. No flags or banners are visible.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The subject (Marat's triumph after the 24 April 1793 acquittal), the 1794 date and the Lille collection are all supported by Commons (categories include 'Triumph of Marat' and the Lille departement des peintures). Only the word 'banners' and the 'street scene' framing are changed; everything else is preserved verbatim.

proposals.title: Winding the skein
proposals.currentDescription: Two fair-haired women wind a skein of wool on the flat roof of a whitewashed house, a bay and distant hills behind them. Leighton drew on sketches made at Lindos on Rhodes in 1867 and first exhibited the canvas in 1878; it is now in the Art Gallery of New South Wales, Sydney.
proposals.proposedDescription: A dark-haired woman seated on a stool and a fair-haired girl standing opposite wind a skein of wool on the flat roof of a whitewashed house, a bay and distant hills behind them. Leighton drew on sketches made at Lindos on Rhodes in 1867 and first exhibited the canvas in 1878; it is now in the Art Gallery of New South Wales, Sydney.

issues.quote: Two fair-haired women
issues.problem: Only the standing figure is fair-haired. The seated woman has dark brown hair, clearly visible against her white gown.
issues.evidence: image - the seated figure's hair reads dark brown/near-black under a green headband

proposals.imageObservation: Two women on a white flat-roofed terrace above a bay: one seated in a white gown with dark brown hair under a green band, holding the skein; the other standing in a red skirt with fair reddish-blonde hair, winding the wool into a ball. Balls of wool and a basket of coloured cloth lie on the terrace; hills and sea fill the background.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Everything else in the sentence is confirmed: the Art Gallery of NSW records that Leighton visited Lindos on Rhodes in 1867 and sketched models on the roof terrace of a whitewashed house along with the bay and hills beyond, returning to those sketches for this canvas of circa 1878. Only the hair colour needed changing; I preserved the rest verbatim.

proposals.title: After Vespers
proposals.currentDescription: Catalogue Entry: A member of the Royal Academy by 1864 and elected its president in 1878, Frederic, Lord Leighton reached the apex of the British art world at a young age. Knighted in 1878, ennobled in 1886, and elevated to a life peerage as Baron of Stretton (ironically, the day before he died), he rose through the ranks of society in a manner that was unprecedented for a modern British artist. Leighton’s great success coincided with the Aesthetic movement of the 1870s and 1880s, in which a cult of beauty reigned in literature, the fine arts, and especially the decorative arts.
proposals.proposedDescription: A young woman stands in a heavy olive-green gown before a gilded, densely patterned arch, gathering her skirt in one hand and holding a string of red beads in the other. Leighton painted it in 1871, in the years when his classicising, highly finished manner ran alongside the Aesthetic movement's cult of beauty; he was elected President of the Royal Academy in 1878. The picture is in the Princeton University Art Museum.

issues.quote: Catalogue Entry: A member of the Royal Academy by 1864
issues.problem: The whole description is a museum catalogue biography pasted in verbatim, prefixed 'Catalogue Entry:'. It never says what the painting shows — not the green gown, the rosary, or the gilded arch.
issues.evidence: catalogue record / Commons imageDescription — the description string is identical to the Commons imageDescription text

issues.quote: A member of the Royal Academy by 1864
issues.problem: Leighton was elected an Associate (ARA) in 1864; he became a full Royal Academician in 1868.
issues.evidence: knowledge — standard Leighton chronology: ARA 1864, RA 1868, PRA 1878

issues.quote: elevated to a life peerage as Baron of Stretton
issues.problem: Leighton's 1896 peerage (Baron Leighton, of Stretton) was a hereditary barony that became extinct on his death the following day, not a life peerage; the sentence also places the ennoblement in 1886, when he was made a baronet.
issues.evidence: knowledge — Leighton was created a baronet in 1886 and Baron Leighton of Stretton in January 1896

proposals.imageObservation: A young woman stands three-quarter length in a heavy olive-green silk gown with a lace-trimmed bodice and long sleeves, gathering the skirt with her right hand and holding a string of red beads in her left, in front of a gilded arch covered in dense polychrome ornament; a stone parapet with a pale ovoid vessel at the left, a carved capital and column at the right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Graded minor rather than major because the text is not about the wrong painting — it is simply the Princeton catalogue's artist biography with two chronology slips carried over from the source. The collection line in my replacement rests on the record's credit field ('Princeton University Art Museum') and the Commons credit; drop that sentence if the project wants collection claims sourced from provenance only (the provenance field here is empty).

proposals.title: The Movings
proposals.currentDescription: A family hauling its furniture through a Parisian street near the Port-au-Blé, the household goods piled on a handcart. Oil on canvas, 73 by 92 cm, signed and dated 1822, in the Art Institute of Chicago. Boilly exhibited the canvas at the Salon of 1822 in the hope, unrealised, that the state would buy it.
proposals.proposedDescription: A family hauling its furniture through a Parisian street near the Port-au-Blé, the household goods piled high on a horse-drawn cart. Oil on canvas, 73 by 92 cm, signed and dated 1822, in the Art Institute of Chicago. Boilly exhibited the canvas at the Salon of 1822 in the hope, unrealised, that the state would buy it.

issues.quote: the household goods piled on a handcart
issues.problem: The load is on a large horse-drawn wagon — the horse is in harness at the left of the cart and a woman is riding on top of the pile. A handcart would be pushed by hand; the only hand-scale vehicle in the picture is a small dog-drawn cart at lower left, which carries no furniture.
issues.evidence: image — harnessed horse hitched to the loaded four-wheeled cart at centre

proposals.imageObservation: A crowded Parisian street under a bright sky: a large four-wheeled cart drawn by a harnessed horse is piled high with furniture, mattresses and mirrors, with a woman perched on top; some two dozen figures, a hearse-like vehicle, dogs and a small dog-drawn cart fill the foreground, and a domed classical church rises through the haze at the left. Signed and dated at lower right, 'L. Boilly 1822'.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Everything else checks out: the Art Institute's own record gives oil on canvas, 73 × 92 cm, and the Salon of 1822 (cat. 121); its provenance shows the picture still in Boilly's hands at his 1829 sale, and the Wikipedia entry states outright that he hoped in vain the government would buy it for the nation. The Port-au-Blé setting is also supported by the Wikipedia entry. Only the word 'handcart' is wrong.

proposals.title: The Public Viewing David ’s " Coronation " at the Louvre
proposals.currentDescription: A dense crowd of visitors examining Jacques-Louis David's vast 'Coronation of Napoleon' on the wall of the Louvre, a guidebook in the hands of a soldier at left. Oil on canvas, 61.6 by 82.6 cm, in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York. David's painting was shown at the Louvre between 1808 and 1810, the occasion Boilly records here.
proposals.proposedDescription: A dense crowd of visitors examining Jacques-Louis David's vast 'Coronation of Napoleon' on the wall of the Louvre, a woman at left holding an open catalogue beside an army officer in a bicorne. Oil on canvas, 61.6 by 82.6 cm, in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York. David's painting was exhibited at the Louvre's Salon of 1808; Boilly recorded the crowd around it in 1810.

issues.quote: a guidebook in the hands of a soldier at left
issues.problem: The open booklet is held by the woman standing beside the officer, not by the soldier; his hands are not on it.
issues.evidence: image - 4x crop of the left edge shows the pamphlet in the woman's two hands, the officer's arm passing behind her

issues.quote: David's painting was shown at the Louvre between 1808 and 1810
issues.problem: The 1808 Salon showing is well documented; the closed 1808-1810 display span is not supported by the record, Commons, or the sources checked.
issues.evidence: web:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Public_Viewing_David%27s_%27Coronation%27_at_the_Louvre - mentions the Salon of 1808 only, with no display end date

proposals.imageObservation: A dense, tightly packed crowd of men, women and children stands before David's 'Coronation of Napoleon' hanging in a gallery; at the far left an army officer in a bicorne and epaulettes stands beside a woman in a green dress and white cap who holds an open booklet in both hands.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Dimensions (61.6 x 82.6 cm), medium, Met ownership and accession 2012.156 all confirmed by web search. Only the guidebook-holder and the display-span clause are changed; everything else is preserved verbatim.

proposals.title: Madame Saint-Ange Chevrier
proposals.currentDescription: Beskrivning på inventarieblanketten: Målningen föreställer en kvinna i ett landskap, sittande på en sten intill en trädstam.
proposals.proposedDescription: A young woman in a high-waisted white dress with a red sash sits on a rock beside a leaning tree trunk, a yellow straw bonnet resting in her lap and a crimson shawl thrown over the stone behind her. A wooded valley with a waterfall and a hilltop building opens out to the left. Louis-Léopold Boilly signed and dated the canvas at the lower left in 1807; it is in the Nationalmuseum, Stockholm.

issues.quote: Beskrivning på inventarieblanketten: Målningen föreställer en kvinna i ett landskap, sittande på en sten intill en trädstam.
issues.problem: The description field holds the raw Swedish inventory-card text copied verbatim from Commons, prefix and all. Its content is true (a woman in a landscape, seated on a stone beside a tree trunk) but it is untranslated source metadata rather than a description, and it says almost nothing about the picture.
issues.evidence: commons — sourceEvidence.imageDescription is byte-identical to the description field

proposals.imageObservation: Full-length oil portrait of a seated young woman in a high-waisted white Empire dress with a red sash and red hem band, a yellow straw bonnet with a white plume in her lap, a crimson paisley-bordered shawl draped over the rock beside her; she sits on stone beside a leaning tree trunk, with a wooded valley, a waterfall and a hilltop building behind, and a signature and date at lower left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: No fabrication — this is an untranslated metadata dump, so the fix is a translation-plus-observation rewrite rather than a correction. Nationalmuseum is supported by the credit line (Cecilia Heisser / Nationalmuseum) and by the Commons categories. The signature at lower left is legible in the reproduction as "L. Boilly" with a date; the 1807 date also comes from the record and from Commons.

proposals.title: Portrait of Maria Louis de Tassis
proposals.currentDescription: Maria de Tassis is shown in a three-quarter-length portrait, wearing a starched lace ruff collar and a dark gown with gold-striped bodice, holding an ostrich-feather fan. Van Dyck painted the work circa 1629–30, bringing the silvery elegance of his Genoese manner to this Flemish aristocratic commission. The canvas is in the Liechtenstein princely collection at Vaduz.
proposals.proposedDescription: Maria de Tassis is shown in a three-quarter-length portrait, wearing a wired standing collar of starched lace and a white satin gown with gold-braided bodice under a dark overgown, a pearl choker and gold cross at her throat, and holding a large ostrich-feather fan. Van Dyck painted the work circa 1629–30, bringing the silvery elegance of his Genoese manner to this Flemish aristocratic commission. The canvas is in the Liechtenstein princely collection at Vaduz.

issues.quote: a starched lace ruff collar
issues.problem: The collar is a wired standing collar rising behind the head, not a pleated circular ruff.
issues.evidence: image — the lace stands up in a fan behind the neck and is open at the front, over an exposed décolletage

issues.quote: a dark gown with gold-striped bodice
issues.problem: The dominant garment is a white/silver satin gown with gold braid; the dark element is the overgown worn over it. The description inverts the emphasis.
issues.evidence: image

metadataIssues.evidence: commons imageDescription: "Maria de Tassis oil on canvas 129 x 92 cm circa 1629 - 1630" — the height differs from the record's 120 cm by 9 cm.

proposals.imageObservation: Three-quarter-length portrait of a young woman against a dark ground: dark curled hair, a tall standing collar of fine lace wired up behind her head, a pearl choker and long pearl chain, a gold cross pendant and a second dark cross on her breast. She wears a white satin gown with gold braid down the bodice and slashed puffed sleeves, under a black overgown with gold trim, and holds a large pale ostrich-feather fan in her right hand.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Both findings are costume-reading nits, not fabrications; the sitter, date range, fan and collection are all supported (Commons object name identifies her as Maria Louis de Tassis, 1611–1638, daughter of canon Antoine de Tassis; credit "Fürstliche Sammlung Liechtenstein"; the record's provenance block gives Vaduz Castle, GE 58). The dimensions discrepancy is the more actionable item — Commons says 129 × 92, the record says 120 × 93.

proposals.title: MC Escher Convex and Concave
proposals.currentDescription: A lithograph by M. C. Escher exploring visual perception through interlocking geometric forms.
proposals.proposedDescription: A lithograph of an impossible architecture: arcades, columns, staircases and shell-vaults that read as convex from one side of the sheet and as concave from the other, with small figures, two lizards and a hanging banner set among them. M. C. Escher made the print in 1955; the sheet is signed and numbered in pencil below the image.

issues.quote: exploring visual perception through interlocking geometric forms
issues.problem: The sheet does not show interlocking geometric forms; it shows a fully rendered architectural interior/exterior with staircases, vaults, figures and lizards, whose reading flips between convex and concave. The one-sentence description also never says what is depicted.
issues.evidence: image

metadataIssues.current: Commons File:Concave-et-convexe.jpg — a 2010 photograph of the roof of the Chateau de Chambord by Helene Rival
metadataIssues.proposed: no usable Commons record for this sheet (the scraped file is a different work entirely)
metadataIssues.evidence: sourceEvidence — objectName 'Concave-et-convexe', artist 'Helene Rival', date 2010-08-12, categories about slate roofs at Chambord; the image under audit is Escher's lithograph

proposals.imageObservation: A black-and-white lithograph of an impossible architecture: arcades, columns, staircases, shell-vaults and window recesses that flip between reading as convex and concave, populated by small figures (a woman with a basket, a man with a horn, a sleeping figure, two men on ladders), two lizards, a hanging banner and an hourglass-like shell; signed and numbered in pencil below the image, monogram and 'III-55' at upper left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Medium (lithograph) and 1955 are right — the plate carries Escher's monogram with 'III-55'. Important for whoever applies this: the scraped Commons metadata for this record belongs to an unrelated photograph of the Chateau de Chambord roof, so nothing in sourceEvidence can be used to support or contradict this entry. Separately, note that Escher died in 1972, so the 'Public domain' licence claim on this record is worth a look by someone in the rights lane; that is outside this audit.

proposals.title: MC Escher Three Spheres I
proposals.currentDescription: A wood-engraving by M. C. Escher depicting three spheres in spatial arrangement, created in 1945.
proposals.proposedDescription: A wood engraving in which the same gridded sphere appears three times, stacked one above another: whole at the top, squashed to a cushion in the middle, and pressed flat to a disc at the bottom, all in white line on black. Escher cut the block in 1945 and dated it IX-45 in the lower right corner.

issues.quote: depicting three spheres in spatial arrangement
issues.problem: Only the top form is a sphere. The middle one is flattened to a cushion and the bottom one to a flat disc - the whole point of the print is the same sphere progressively squashed onto a plane, not three spheres arranged in space.
issues.evidence: image - the lower two forms are clearly compressed, with the grid squeezed along the vertical axis

issues.quote: A wood-engraving by M. C. Escher depicting three spheres in spatial arrangement, created in 1945.
issues.problem: A single sentence that restates the title, artist, medium and date and says nothing about what the image looks like.
issues.evidence: house style - first sentence should describe what is in the frame

proposals.imageObservation: A black-and-white wood engraving in an upright format: the same sphere covered in a criss-cross grid appears three times stacked vertically - whole at the top, compressed to a cushion in the middle, and flattened to a disc at the bottom. Monogram 'MCE' at lower left, 'IX-45' at lower right inside the block, with a pencil signature and 'eigen druk' on the margin.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Medium and date are confirmed by the Commons file description quoting the Escher Foundation ('Wood-engraving (18x17 cm)', 1945). I did not carry over the collection, since the Commons note gives both 'The Escher Foundation Collection' and a photograph taken at the Museu de Arte Popular in Lisbon and I cannot tell which applies to this impression. Separately worth flagging to a human: Escher died in 1972, so the public-domain status recorded for this file is questionable - the same concern CLAUDE.md already records for the post-1955 artists in the corpus.

proposals.title: 冨嶽三十六景 甲州三島越-Mishima Pass in Kai Province
proposals.currentDescription: A woodblock print from Katsushika Hokusai's celebrated "Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji" series, depicting the dramatic perspective view through Mishima Pass in Kai Province. The composition exemplifies Hokusai's distinctive treatment of landscape and use of Prussian blue, with Mount Fuji visible in the distance framed by the mountain pass. This impression was part of the Metropolitan Museum of Art's acquisition and is now in the public domain.
proposals.proposedDescription: Travellers on the Mishima Pass road in Kai Province stretch their arms around the trunk of a colossal tree, three of them linking hands to span its girth while two more climb the path below with a bundle of brushwood. Mount Fuji rises at the right in bands of Prussian blue above white puffs of cloud. The woodblock print comes from Katsushika Hokusai's Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, about 1830; this impression is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art.

issues.quote: depicting the dramatic perspective view through Mishima Pass in Kai Province
issues.problem: The subject of the print — travellers ringing a colossal tree trunk with their outstretched arms — is never mentioned; "the dramatic perspective view through" the pass describes nothing that is in the frame.
issues.evidence: image — the giant trunk and the chain of figures around it occupy the centre of the sheet

issues.quote: with Mount Fuji visible in the distance framed by the mountain pass
issues.problem: Fuji stands in open sky at the right, not framed by anything resembling a pass.
issues.evidence: image

proposals.imageObservation: Horizontal woodblock print: an enormous tree trunk rises through the centre of the sheet, three travellers with their arms outstretched linking hands around its girth while a fourth watches; two more figures climb the path at the lower left, one shouldering a bundle of brushwood. Mount Fuji, banded in Prussian blue with white cloud puffs at its foot, stands at the right; a graded blue sky runs across the top with the series cartouche at upper left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Nothing in the old text is false — the series, the date, the Prussian blue and the MET provenance all hold (Commons: MET donation, Rogers Fund) — it simply never looks at the picture. The closing "is now in the public domain" is licence boilerplate and does not belong in a description.

proposals.title: Extérieur de la gare Saint-Lazare
proposals.currentDescription: Part of Monet's 1877 Gare Saint-Lazare series, the first concerted Impressionist meditation on industrial modernity. Steam, sunlight, and iron architecture dissolve into one another, the locomotive yard reframed as a study in coloured vapour.
proposals.proposedDescription: An exterior view of the Gare Saint-Lazare in sunlight: a small signal hut and two tall telegraph poles stand in the open yard, pale apartment blocks rise behind, and clouds of white and blue steam drift across the whole scene, a few figures picked out on the tracks. Monet painted it in 1877 as one of the canvases of his Gare Saint-Lazare series, in which the station's steam and light became the subject rather than the trains.

issues.quote: the first concerted Impressionist meditation on industrial modernity
issues.problem: A 'first' claim with nothing behind it. Manet's The Railway (1873) and Monet's own Train in the Countryside and Railway Bridge at Argenteuil (both early 1870s) precede it, and the record and source carry no such assertion.
issues.evidence: catalogue record and Commons contain no interpretive claim; knowledge - earlier Impressionist railway subjects exist

issues.quote: Steam, sunlight, and iron architecture dissolve into one another
issues.problem: This canvas is the exterior view. There is no iron-and-glass train shed in it - only a wooden signal hut, telegraph poles and masonry apartment blocks. The iron architecture belongs to the interior canvases of the series.
issues.evidence: image - no iron structure is visible anywhere in the frame

proposals.imageObservation: An open railway yard in sunlight: a small green-and-yellow signal hut stands at centre with two tall telegraph poles at right and a red signboard between them; pale cream apartment blocks rise behind, and drifts of white and blue steam fill the middle ground. Three or four small figures stand on the tracks. Signed lower left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Spot-check of an earlier 'accurate' verdict, which I am downgrading. The 1877 date and the series membership are confirmed by Commons ('Saint-Lazare Station by Claude Monet', date 1877), and nothing about those is wrong. The two problems are the unsourced 'first' superlative and the iron architecture, which is simply not in this particular canvas. My replacement drops both and adds the visual first sentence the original lacks. I deliberately avoided giving a number for the canvases in the series.

proposals.title: Monet w1032
proposals.currentDescription: Sailboats run before the wind beneath the Aiguille — the slender needle rock that rises off the cliffs of Étretat on the Normandy coast. Claude Monet returned to Étretat repeatedly through the 1880s, treating its arches, rocks, and weather in a sustained series catalogued by Daniel Wildenstein as W.1032 and its neighbours.
proposals.proposedDescription: The arch of the Porte d'Aval and the Aiguille beside it — the slender needle rock off the cliffs of Étretat on the Normandy coast — rise out of pale green water, with a few small sailboats far off in the haze. Claude Monet returned to Étretat repeatedly through the 1880s, treating its arches, rocks, and weather in a sustained series catalogued by Daniel Wildenstein as W.1032 and its neighbours.

issues.quote: Sailboats run before the wind beneath the Aiguille
issues.problem: The sailboats are a handful of tiny distant marks on the horizon, not the subject, and they are beyond the rocks rather than beneath them; meanwhile the dominant element of the composition, the arch of the Porte d'Aval that occupies the right half of the canvas, is never mentioned.
issues.evidence: image | commons — Commons categories are 'Porte d'Aval' and 'Falaise d'Aval, Etretat in art'. The 'sailboats' framing appears to come from the Commons caption title 'Sailboats of the Rock Needle'.

issues.quote: run before the wind
issues.problem: The boats are indistinct specks; their point of sail cannot be read from the picture.
issues.evidence: image

proposals.imageObservation: The chalk cliffs at Étretat in pale haze: the needle rock (Aiguille) stands at the centre left and the arch of the Porte d'Aval fills the right side, both reflected in green-blue water; several very small sailboats are scattered far off on the hazy horizon at the upper left and centre.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Second sentence preserved verbatim; only the opening clause is rebalanced so that the arch, which is more than half the canvas, is named and the distant boats are not made the subject. The Wildenstein number matches the file name and the Commons caption. Catalogue title 'Monet w1032' is the file name rather than a title, but englishTitle already carries the proper one, so I did not raise it as a metadata issue.

proposals.title: Nishikawa Sukenobu
proposals.currentDescription: A page from the Ehon Asakayama (Picture Book of Mount Asaka) of 1739, a woodblock-printed book by Nishikawa Sukenobu, the leading Kyoto designer of pictures of beautiful women. Printed in ink monochrome, this sheet shows a woman at her toilette, her kimono slipped to the waist as she binds up her hair before a lacquer cabinet and a folding mirror stand. The book's two dozen studies of women rank among Sukenobu's most important contributions to the bijin-ga genre.
proposals.proposedDescription: A page from the Ehon Asakayama (Picture Book of Mount Asaka) of 1739, a woodblock-printed book by Nishikawa Sukenobu, the leading Kyoto designer of pictures of beautiful women. Printed in ink monochrome, this sheet shows a woman at her toilette, her kimono slipped to the waist as she binds up her hair before a lacquer cabinet and a folding mirror stand. The album gathers a sequence of such studies of women, the subject on which Sukenobu's reputation rests.

issues.quote: The book's two dozen studies of women
issues.problem: The count appears wrong and is unsupported by the record or the Commons metadata. Auction and museum descriptions of Ehon Asakayama (1739) describe an album of thirty portraits of beauties plus a preface page, not roughly twenty-four; Commons itself holds a page numbered 24 from the same set.
issues.evidence: web:https://www.bonhams.com/auction/30801/lot/531/nishikawa-sukenobu-1671-1751-edo-period-1615-1868-1739/ — '30 portraits of beauties and one page of preface text'; Commons also has 'Nishikawa Sukenobu, 1739, Ehon Asakayama,24 gris.jpg'

issues.quote: rank among Sukenobu's most important contributions to the bijin-ga genre
issues.problem: Unsupported ranking claim; nothing in the record or source evidence establishes relative importance within Sukenobu's output.
issues.evidence: catalogue record + commons — no such assessment present

proposals.imageObservation: Ink-monochrome woodblock book page: a seated woman, her patterned kimono slipped off her shoulders to the waist, arms raised as she binds her hair with a comb/pin, a dark lacquer cabinet behind her at right and a folding mirror stand in front of her; a ruled border frames the sheet.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Everything visual checks out against the image. Only the plate count was wrong; I removed it rather than substituting 'thirty', since the auction figure is not in the record. Rewrite preserves the first two sentences verbatim.

proposals.title: Ohara koson
proposals.currentDescription: A color woodcut of 1933 by Ohara Koson, the leading designer of bird-and-animal subjects in the shin-hanga print movement. A black-and-white cat wearing a red collar and bell crouches on the wooden floor, staring intently into a glass bowl in which orange goldfish circle, a small hand net lying beside it. An impression of the print is in the Cincinnati Art Museum.
proposals.proposedDescription: A color woodcut of 1931 by Ohara Koson, the leading designer of bird-and-animal subjects in the shin-hanga print movement. A black-and-white cat wearing a red collar and bell crouches on the wooden floor, staring intently into a glass bowl in which orange goldfish circle, a small hand net lying beside it. An impression of the print is in the Cincinnati Art Museum.

issues.quote: A color woodcut of 1933
issues.problem: The print's own inscription reads 昭和六年作 - made in Showa 6, that is 1931 - and external sources give the first Watanabe edition as 1931 (Showa 6). The 1933 date comes from the Commons uploader's file name, not from the work.
issues.evidence: image (zoomed inscription reads Showa 6) plus web search: 'inscribed as the work of Showa-6 or 1931', publisher Watanabe, first edition 1931

metadataIssues.evidence: Print inscription 昭和六年作 (Showa 6 = 1931) read from the image, corroborated by external listings giving a 1931 Watanabe first edition. The 1933 in the record traces to the Commons file name written by the photographer, not to a museum record.

proposals.imageObservation: A colour woodblock print: a black-and-white cat with a red collar, red bow and gold bell crouches on a wood-grain floor and stares down into a large bowl at the lower left where five orange goldfish swim; a long-handled hand net and a small planted dish sit at the right. Inscription and red seal at the middle right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Everything except the year is right, including the Cincinnati Art Museum (the Commons photograph is captioned 'Art of Japan in the Cincinnati Art Museum'). Caveat on the date: I am reading a small inscription in a photograph of a framed print, and the impression on display could in principle be a later edition of a 1931 design - but both my reading and the external sources point to Showa 6. If the year field is changed, the file name and title still say 1933.

proposals.title: Paris art deco boilly houdon
proposals.currentDescription: The sculptor Jean-Antoine Houdon at work in his studio, modelling a clay bust of the astronomer Pierre-Simon Laplace. Oil on canvas, about 1803, in the Musée des Arts décoratifs, Paris. Finished casts and tools fill the cluttered workshop behind the seated sculptor.
proposals.proposedDescription: The sculptor Jean-Antoine Houdon at work in his studio, standing at a modelling stand to shape the clay bust of the astronomer Pierre-Simon Laplace, who sits for him at the right. Four women in white Empire dresses watch from the left and a dog sleeps on the flagstones; tiers of finished busts crowd the wall behind. Oil on canvas, about 1803, in the Musée des Arts décoratifs, Paris.

issues.quote: the seated sculptor
issues.problem: Houdon is standing at the modelling stand, not seated. The seated figure in the picture is the sitter at the right.
issues.evidence: image — the sculptor stands in a long coat with both feet on the floor and no chair beneath him; the man in the dark coat at right is the one seated on a chair on the dais

issues.quote: Finished casts and tools fill the cluttered workshop
issues.problem: The shelves hold finished busts and a large seated statue; no tools are conspicuous. The description also omits the four women, the sitter and the sleeping dog, which occupy most of the canvas.
issues.evidence: image

proposals.imageObservation: A studio interior: a man in a long cream working coat stands at a modelling stand, one hand touching the chin of a clay portrait bust; the sitter, an older man in a dark coat and white stockings, sits at the right on a low dais. Four women in white Empire dresses are grouped at the left, a dog sleeps in the foreground, and tiers of busts and a seated classical statue fill the wall behind.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Subject, date and collection are all confirmed by the Commons record ('Houdon modelant le buste de Laplace dans son atelier', circa 1803, Musée des arts décoratifs). Only the sculptor's posture and the thin account of what is in the frame needed fixing. I did not name the women, since nothing in the record identifies them.

proposals.title: Baigneurs
proposals.currentDescription: A group of male nudes along a riverbank, some standing and some reclining, set into an open landscape. Oil on canvas of about 1890, part of the bather series Cézanne pursued from the 1870s onward, now in the Musée d'Orsay, Paris. The figures are built to structure the space rather than to display the flesh.
proposals.proposedDescription: A group of male nudes in an open landscape, some standing with their backs turned, others bending or crouching, one holding up a white cloth, beneath tall summer clouds. Oil on canvas of about 1890, part of the bather series Cezanne pursued from the 1870s onward, now in the Musee d'Orsay, Paris. The figures are built to structure the space rather than to display the flesh.

issues.quote: some standing and some reclining
issues.problem: No figure is reclining; the non-standing figures bend forward or crouch.
issues.evidence: image

issues.quote: A group of male nudes along a riverbank
issues.problem: No water is visible in the picture; the bathers stand on bare ground before trees and sky.
issues.evidence: image

proposals.imageObservation: A group of pale male nudes in a landscape: one bends deeply at the left, two stand with their backs turned in the centre and right, one raises an arm, several crouch or sit in the middle distance, and one holds a white cloth. Tall white clouds and dark green trees fill the upper half; there is no visible water.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Date, series and Musee d'Orsay ownership are all supported by the Commons record ('Circa 1890', category 'Paintings by Paul Cezanne in the Musee d'Orsay'). Only the two visual details are changed; the closing interpretive sentence is preserved verbatim.

proposals.title: Maison Maria with a View of Château Noir
proposals.currentDescription: A small ochre farmhouse, the Maison Maria, sits among pines on the road to the Château Noir near Aix-en-Provence. Oil on canvas of about 1895, in the Kimbell Art Museum in Fort Worth. Cézanne worked the ground and foliage in parallel diagonal strokes of green, blue and orange.
proposals.proposedDescription: A small ochre farmhouse, the Maison Maria, stands on a rocky rise above the track leading to the Château Noir near Aix-en-Provence, framed by two bare trees. Oil on canvas of about 1895, in the Kimbell Art Museum in Fort Worth. Cézanne worked the ground and foliage in parallel diagonal strokes of green, blue and orange.

issues.quote: sits among pines on the road to the Château Noir
issues.problem: The two prominent trees in the canvas are bare and leafless, and the surrounding growth is low green scrub. No pines are identifiable in the picture.
issues.evidence: image — both framing trees are drawn as bare branching trunks against the sky

proposals.imageObservation: An ochre farmhouse with a dark roof stands on a rocky rise above a pale track that runs up from the lower right; a second ochre building shows behind it and a blue-grey slope at the right. Two leafless trees frame the composition at left and right, with low green scrub over the rocks; the sky is worked in short blue and white diagonal strokes.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Kimbell Art Museum and the c.1895 date are supported by the Commons categories ("Paintings in the Kimbell Art Museum", "1895 paintings by Paul Cézanne"). The parallel-diagonal-stroke sentence is accurate to the surface. Medium confidence on the pines only because bare winter pines are not a thing — these are deciduous — but tree identification from a Cézanne is inherently loose, so the fix simply says "bare trees".

proposals.title: Young Italian Woman at a Table
proposals.currentDescription: A young woman in a striped blouse leans on a fabric-covered table, her head resting in her hand. Oil on canvas of about 1895 to 1900, accession 99.PA.40 in the J. Paul Getty Museum in Los Angeles. Cézanne built her bulk from broad blocks of colour while the space behind her shifts and tilts.
proposals.proposedDescription: A young woman in a white blouse with a yellow shawl over one shoulder leans on a table under a boldly patterned cloth, her head resting in her hand. Oil on canvas of about 1895 to 1900, accession 99.PA.40 in the J. Paul Getty Museum in Los Angeles. Cézanne built her bulk from broad blocks of colour while the space behind her shifts and tilts.

issues.quote: A young woman in a striped blouse
issues.problem: The blouse is plain white; there are no stripes. The strong colour accent is the yellow shawl over her shoulder, which the description omits entirely.
issues.evidence: image; web:https://www.getty.edu/art/collection/object/108FPZ (via search summary) — 'The yellow shawl dialogues with the white of the sleeves'

proposals.imageObservation: A dark-haired young woman leans on a table covered with a boldly patterned red-and-green cloth, her head resting in her left hand. She wears a plain white blouse with full sleeves, a yellow shawl over the near shoulder, and a dark blue skirt; the wall behind is brown and tilts.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Everything except the blouse is right and worth preserving verbatim: the Getty confirms oil on canvas, about 1895–1900, accession 99.PA.40, and describes the same pose. Only the garment description needed changing.

proposals.title: The Siesta
proposals.currentDescription: The Siesta shows several Tahitian women resting on a wooden veranda floor, two of them stretched out lengthways while others sit nearby. Painted between 1892 and 1894 during Gauguin's first stay in Tahiti, the canvas uses flat zones of colour and a high viewpoint to dissolve conventional depth. It is held in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.
proposals.proposedDescription: The Siesta shows Tahitian women on a plank veranda: one stretched out on the boards in the foreground under a straw hat, another lying at her side in orange, a third seated with her back turned, while a fourth irons a white cloth at a red-covered table behind them. Dated between 1892 and 1894, the canvas uses flat zones of colour and a high viewpoint to dissolve conventional depth. It is held in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.

issues.quote: several Tahitian women resting on a wooden veranda floor
issues.problem: Not all of them are resting: one woman is ironing a white cloth at a table, which is a conspicuous element of the composition and is left out entirely.
issues.evidence: image

issues.quote: during Gauguin's first stay in Tahiti
issues.problem: Commons and the Met date the canvas 1892-94; Gauguin returned to France in 1893, so a 1894 completion would fall after the first Tahitian stay. Stating it as painted during that stay is more certain than the dating allows.
issues.evidence: commons — 'between 1892 and 1894'

proposals.imageObservation: Five Tahitian women on a plank veranda: one in the foreground in a straw hat and pale blue tunic props herself on the boards with her legs stretched out, another in orange lies on her side beyond her, a third in pink sits at the left with her back turned, a woman in dark purple bends over an iron and a white cloth on a red-covered table behind, and a fifth in white sits at the right edge; a bright green lawn fills the background.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Spot-check of an earlier 'fabricated-fixed' rewrite. Nothing in it is false about the setting or the collection (Commons category 'Paintings by Paul Gauguin in the Metropolitan Museum of Art'), but 'resting' glosses over the woman ironing, and the first-stay framing sits awkwardly with the 1892-94 date range. Low-severity throughout; applying the replacement is optional.

proposals.title: Hercules and the Nemean Lion
proposals.currentDescription: Hercules grapples the invulnerable Nemean lion in a knot of straining limbs, the hero's first labor reduced to its essential close-quarters violence. The Apsley House version follows a Rubens prototype that translates antique sculptural sources, especially the Belvedere Torso, into Baroque flesh and sinew.
proposals.proposedDescription: Hercules grapples the invulnerable Nemean lion in a knot of straining limbs, forcing the animal's head down with both hands while a white cloth slips from his hip; a tree arches over them and a low landscape opens at the left. The hero's first labour is reduced to its essential close-quarters violence. The Apsley House picture is a version after a Rubens prototype, in which antique sculpture is translated into Baroque flesh and sinew.

issues.quote: especially the Belvedere Torso
issues.problem: A specific source for this composition, asserted as fact. Rubens certainly drew after the Belvedere Torso, but nothing in the record, the Commons metadata or any source I could reach connects this Apsley House Hercules to that particular antique.
issues.evidence: commons - no description beyond 'Nemean lion'; catalogue record gives only Apsley House and the inventory number

proposals.imageObservation: Hercules, nude but for a white cloth over his hip, bends and wrestles the lion, forcing its head down with both hands while the animal rears against him and claws at his arm; a tree at the right, a pale sky and a low landscape glimpsed at the left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The Commons file title says '(after)' Rubens, so 'version ... after a Rubens prototype' is right and the record's flat attribution to Rubens is the looser one. I kept the antique-sculpture idea but dropped the named statue. Note also that what looks at first like a small extra figure below the lion is Hercules' own leg - I zoomed to confirm.

proposals.title: Gabrielle mit offener Bluse
proposals.currentDescription: A bust-length study of Gabrielle with her chemise slipped from one shoulder, the flesh rendered in warm pinks against a sketchy ground. The sitter is Gabrielle Renard, cousin of Renoir's wife Aline and the family's nanny from 1894, who modelled often in his later years. Painted about 1907, oil on canvas.
proposals.proposedDescription: A half-length study of Gabrielle with a red flower in her hair and her white chemise open down the front, the flesh rendered in warm pinks against a sketchy green-blue ground. The sitter is Gabrielle Renard, cousin of Renoir's wife Aline and the family's nanny from 1894, who modelled often in his later years. Painted about 1907, oil on canvas.

issues.quote: her chemise slipped from one shoulder
issues.problem: The chemise is open down the front and pushed off both shoulders, leaving both breasts bare; it has not slipped from one shoulder.
issues.evidence: image

issues.quote: A bust-length study
issues.problem: The figure is shown to the waist with both hands visible, closer to half-length than bust-length, and the flower in her hair goes unmentioned.
issues.evidence: image

proposals.imageObservation: Oil painting: a dark-haired young woman seen to the waist, a red-orange flower pinned in her hair, wearing a white chemise or blouse open down the front so that both breasts are bare, hands folded low; softly brushed green-blue background.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Biography of Gabrielle Renard is correct and the circa-1907 date matches Commons. Only the description of the garment and the framing needed fixing. Commons also places this canvas in the Tehran Museum of Contemporary Art, which the description does not mention - could be added if someone wants to verify it.

proposals.title: Ambroise Vollard
proposals.currentDescription: Ambroise Vollard leans over a small statuette of a kneeling nude, examining it as a connoisseur, his bald head and bulbous features softened by Renoir. The bronze is after the sculptor Aristide Maillol. Painted in 1908, oil on canvas, now in the Courtauld Gallery, London.
proposals.proposedDescription: Ambroise Vollard leans over a small statuette of a kneeling nude, examining it as a connoisseur, his bald head and bulbous features softened by Renoir. The statuette is by the sculptor Aristide Maillol. Painted in 1908, oil on canvas, now in the Courtauld Gallery, London.

issues.quote: The bronze is after the sculptor Aristide Maillol.
issues.problem: Two problems in one sentence. 'After' implies a copy or a reproduction — the Courtauld says the statuette is BY Maillol. And the statuette as painted is creamy-white, not bronze-coloured; the Courtauld's record does not identify its material at all.
issues.evidence: image — the statuette is painted in pale cream and white; web:https://gallerycollections.courtauld.ac.uk/object-p-1932-sc-340 — 'examining a statuette of a kneeling female nude', material not stated

proposals.imageObservation: A balding, bearded man in a dark blue-grey jacket leans on a table and holds up a small pale statuette of a kneeling female nude in both hands, studying it. A blue-and-white porcelain bowl and a patterned cloth sit on the table beside him; the wall behind is deep red. Signed at upper left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The Courtauld's own label matches this description closely — Vollard as connoisseur examining a kneeling female nude by Maillol, his features idealised where he was in life mocked for his bald head and bulbous nose — so only the 'bronze … after' clause needs changing. Date 1908, oil on canvas, and the Courtauld are all confirmed by the gallery record (81.6 × 65.2 cm).

proposals.title: Porträt des Charles und Georges Durand-Ruel
proposals.currentDescription: Charles and Georges Durand-Ruel, sons of Renoir's dealer, shown outdoors in three-piece suits against dense green foliage. Oil on canvas painted in 1882; Paul Durand-Ruel, who commissioned the double portrait, was reportedly displeased to find his sons painted out of doors. Charles holds a medallion, Georges a cigarette.
proposals.proposedDescription: Charles and Georges Durand-Ruel, sons of Renoir's dealer, shown outdoors in three-piece suits against dense green foliage. Oil on canvas painted in 1882, a commission from Paul Durand-Ruel. Charles wears a medallion at his cravat and holds an open newspaper; Georges, in dark violet with a flower in his buttonhole, holds a cigarette.

issues.quote: Charles holds a medallion
issues.problem: He does not hold a medallion - he wears one at his cravat, and what he holds is an open newspaper. The attribute has been moved from his collar to his hand and the newspaper dropped.
issues.evidence: image - open printed sheet across his lap, small white disc at the neck; web:https://museeduluxembourg.fr/fr/collection/objet/charles-et-georges-durand-ruel - 'Charles carries a newspaper' and wears 'un medaillon'

issues.quote: was reportedly displeased to find his sons painted out of doors
issues.problem: An anecdote with no source behind it. The Musee du Luxembourg entry on the picture records the commission and the Dieppe setting Durand-Ruel himself arranged, and says nothing about displeasure at the outdoor setting.
issues.evidence: web:https://museeduluxembourg.fr/fr/collection/objet/charles-et-georges-durand-ruel - documents the commission and Durand-Ruel's own letter to Monet about the rented Dieppe house, no reaction to the plein-air setting

proposals.imageObservation: Two young men sit side by side outdoors against dense green and mauve foliage. The elder, in a pale suit with a small white medallion at his cravat, holds an open sheet of newsprint on his lap; the younger wears a dark violet jacket with a flower in his buttonhole and holds a cigarette. Signed and dated at the upper right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The commission is confirmed by the Musee du Luxembourg entry, so I kept it and dropped only the unsourced anecdote. The medallion is real but worn, not held - the fix keeps the detail and puts it where the picture puts it.

proposals.title: Diana
proposals.currentDescription: A nude woman holding a bow, a dead deer and an animal skin at her feet, cast as the huntress Diana. Oil on canvas, 197 by 132 cm, painted in 1867 and held by the National Gallery of Art, Washington. The model is thought to be Renoir's companion Lise Tréhot; the canvas was rejected by the 1867 Salon.
proposals.proposedDescription: A nude woman seated on a rock with a bow in her raised hand and an animal skin draped across her hips, a dead deer pierced by an arrow at her feet, cast as the huntress Diana. Oil on canvas, 199.5 by 129.5 cm, painted in 1867 and held by the National Gallery of Art, Washington. The model is thought to be Renoir's companion Lise Trehot; the canvas was rejected by the 1867 Salon.

issues.quote: 197 by 132 cm
issues.problem: The dimensions are wrong; the picture measures 199.5 x 129.5 cm.
