issues.evidence: web:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diana_(Renoir_painting) — 'Oil on canvas, 199.5 cm x 129.5 cm', National Gallery of Art, Washington

issues.quote: a dead deer and an animal skin at her feet
issues.problem: The skin is not at her feet; it is worn across her hips and thighs. Only the deer lies on the ground.
issues.evidence: image — pelt draped over her lap and belted with a red band

proposals.imageObservation: A nude woman sits on a grey rock in a wooded landscape, gripping a tall bow with her raised right hand, a mottled green animal skin with a red band draped across her hips and thighs. A dead deer with an arrow through it lies across the lower left. Signed and dated at lower right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The Salon rejection of 1867 and the hedged Lise Trehot identification both check out (Wikipedia notes the identification is disputed by some scholars, which the description's 'thought to be' already accommodates). Only the measurements and the placement of the pelt are corrected.

proposals.title: Pierre Paul RUBENS
proposals.currentDescription: A religious oil painting by Flemish master Peter Paul Rubens depicting the miraculous appearance of Saint Justus, who stands at center holding his severed head in his hands with onlookers present. Created by 1640 and held in the Musée des Beaux-Arts de Bordeaux, this work exemplifies Rubens' dramatic Baroque composition and rich color palette.
proposals.proposedDescription: The beheaded Saint Justus stands at the right of the picture, stooping forward with his severed head held in both hands and blood at his neck. A grey-bearded old man leaning on a staff and a bare-chested youth in a brown cloak recoil before him, in front of a ruined arcade, with mounted soldiers riding off in the landscape beyond. An oil painting by Peter Paul Rubens, dated by 1640, in the Musee des Beaux-Arts de Bordeaux.

issues.quote: who stands at center holding his severed head in his hands
issues.problem: The cephalophore saint is at the right of the picture and is bent sharply forward, not standing at centre. The figure at centre is a clothed young onlooker recoiling from him.
issues.evidence: image — decapitated figure occupies the right third, stooping; centre figure has a head and is gesturing away

issues.quote: the miraculous appearance of Saint Justus
issues.problem: The scene is the cephalophore miracle (the beheaded saint carrying his own head), not an apparition of the saint. 'Miraculous appearance' misdescribes the legend the picture illustrates.
issues.evidence: image — the saint is bodily present, carrying his head; commons objectName 'Le Miracle de saint Just'

issues.quote: rich color palette
issues.problem: Catalogue-boilerplate praise, and inaccurate: this canvas is unusually grey and subdued for Rubens.
issues.evidence: image — dominant greys, browns and muted blue

proposals.imageObservation: A beheaded man at the RIGHT of the composition stoops forward, blood at his neck stump, holding his own severed bearded head in both hands; a grey-bearded old man with a staff stands at the left and a bare-chested youth in a brown cloak recoils at centre, before a ruined arcade, with mounted soldiers riding off in the landscape at right. Palette is largely subdued grey-brown with muted blue and ochre.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Attribution, date (by 1640) and Bordeaux collection are all backed by the Commons record and are unchanged. Only the placement/pose of the saint and the palette flourish are corrected. I did not assert a support (canvas vs panel) because neither the record nor Commons states one.

proposals.title: Portrait of Victor Chocquet
proposals.currentDescription: The collector Victor Chocquet seen bust-length against patterned wallpaper, his greying hair and beard built up in close-keyed strokes. Chocquet, a customs official who amassed dozens of Impressionist canvases, was introduced to Cézanne by Renoir in 1875; the portrait dates from about 1876 to 1877.
proposals.proposedDescription: The collector Victor Chocquet seen bust-length against a loosely brushed green and blue-grey ground, his greying hair and beard built up in close-keyed strokes. Chocquet, a customs official who amassed dozens of Impressionist canvases, was introduced to Cezanne by Renoir in 1875; the portrait dates from about 1876 to 1877.

issues.quote: against patterned wallpaper
issues.problem: The ground behind the sitter is an open field of hatched green and blue-grey strokes; no wallpaper pattern, no repeat, no interior detail is visible. Patterned wallpaper belongs to the other, seated Chocquet portrait of 1877, where Chocquet sits at home among his pictures.
issues.evidence: image - the background here is a plain mottled green field; web:https://www.cezannecatalogue.com/catalogue/entry.php?id=294 describes the seated version as the one showing Chocquet at home with patterned surroundings

proposals.imageObservation: Bust-length portrait of a man with a high forehead, grizzled dark hair and a full beard, his face built in orange and pink strokes, in a dark jacket over a white collar, against a loosely brushed green and blue-grey ground with no discernible pattern. Signed at the left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Only the setting phrase is changed; the Chocquet biography and the 1876-77 date (which matches the Commons date range) are correct and preserved verbatim. Medium confidence on the finding because a reproduction can flatten a very loosely painted wall covering - but nothing in this image reads as a pattern.

proposals.title: Portrait of the Artist's Daughters
proposals.currentDescription: Thomas Gainsborough's portrait depicts the artist's daughters in a family study from the early 1760s. The painting shows two young women in fashionable dress seated together in an intimate composition. This work exemplifies Gainsborough's skill in 18th-century portrait painting and is held in the Worcester Art Museum collection.
proposals.proposedDescription: Gainsborough's two daughters: the elder stands behind in a blue-green silk dress, seen in profile, while the younger sits in front in a pale embroidered dress, a drawing stylus in her hand over an open portfolio of papers; a classical statuette stands on a draped table at left. The drawing materials point to the girls' training in their father's profession. Painted probably in the early 1760s, oil on canvas, in the Worcester Art Museum.

issues.quote: seated together in an intimate composition
issues.problem: Only one daughter is seated; the elder stands behind her. The description also omits the drawing stylus, the portfolio of drawings and the statuette, which are the picture's defining content.
issues.evidence: image - one figure clearly standing behind the seated sitter

issues.quote: This work exemplifies Gainsborough's skill in 18th-century portrait painting
issues.problem: Empty appraisal sentence with no grounded content.
issues.evidence: house style

proposals.imageObservation: Two young women before a dark interior: the elder stands behind in profile in a blue-green silk dress, the younger sits in front in a pale embroidered dress holding a drawing stylus over an open portfolio of papers tied with a green ribbon; a classical statuette on a green-draped table at left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Worcester Art Museum holding confirmed (worcester.emuseum.com object 31355); the museum dates it about 1763-64, which is compatible with the record's 1760 / 'probably early 1760s'. Only the posture claim and the missing salient objects were changed.

proposals.title: Преферанс
proposals.currentDescription: A genre painting depicting a gathering of Russian men engaged in a card game of preferans (preference). Viktor Vasnetsov captures an intimate moment of 19th-century Russian domestic life, with figures absorbed in their game in an interior setting. The work exemplifies the artist's attention to social interaction and period detail.
proposals.proposedDescription: Three men sit round a green baize table by the light of a single candle, cards fanned in their hands, while a fourth figure yawns behind a raised hand beside them; a longcase clock, a framed portrait and a lit doorway stand out of the surrounding gloom. Viktor Vasnetsov painted this game of preferans in 1879.

issues.quote: a gathering of Russian men engaged in a card game
issues.problem: Only three of the figures are men at the cards; the yawning figure at right and the standing figure at the back read as women, and neither is playing. 'A gathering of men' flattens the scene.
issues.evidence: image — 2.6x crops of both figures: the yawner wears a dark fur-collared garment with bushy dark hair, the standing figure a long dark dress with an updo. Both readings are probable, not certain, at this resolution.

issues.quote: Viktor Vasnetsov captures an intimate moment of 19th-century Russian domestic life, with figures absorbed in their game in an interior setting
issues.problem: Generic; never mentions the candlelight, the green baize table, the yawning onlooker or the clock that make the picture what it is.
issues.evidence: image + house style.

issues.quote: The work exemplifies the artist's attention to social interaction and period detail
issues.problem: Catalogue boilerplate.
issues.evidence: house style.

proposals.imageObservation: A dim interior at night: three men sit round a green baize table holding cards by the light of a single candle; a fourth figure in a dark fur-trimmed coat yawns behind a raised hand at right, and another figure stands in shadow by the stove at left. A longcase clock, a framed portrait of a woman and a lit doorway fill the background. Signed at lower left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The sexes of the yawning and standing figures are my reading of a 1000px reproduction and could be wrong; the replacement therefore avoids assigning sex to them rather than asserting 'women'. Commons categorises the painting under 'Paintings by Viktor Vasnetsov in the Tretyakov Gallery', which is probably the collection, but I left it out of the replacement because a Commons category is the only evidence I have.

proposals.title: Продажа ребенка-невольника
proposals.currentDescription: A harrowing orientalist painting by Russian artist Vasily Vereshchagin depicting a wealthy Ottoman buyer inspecting a young enslaved boy for purchase. Executed in 1872, this work from the artist's Turkestan series condemns the dehumanization of slavery through unflinching realism.
proposals.proposedDescription: A naked boy stands with his back to us on a white cloth while a grey-bearded merchant in a white turban, seated on carpets and telling a string of prayer beads, looks him over; a second man leans in to whisper, and a third in a bright striped robe presents the child. Painted in 1872 for Vereshchagin's Turkestan series, which he drew from his travels in Central Asia, the picture is in the Tretyakov Gallery, Moscow.

issues.quote: a wealthy Ottoman buyer inspecting a young enslaved boy for purchase
issues.problem: The picture belongs to Vereshchagin's Turkestan cycle and Russian catalogue sources place the scene in a Central Asian shop, with the seated merchant and a slave dealer beside him — not the Ottoman Empire. The description's own next sentence names the Turkestan series, so the sentence contradicts itself.
issues.evidence: web:https://kartiny.rus-lit.com/vereshhagin-vasilij/prodazha-rebenka-nevolnika-vasilij-vereshhagin/ — describes an oriental shop, a grey-bearded merchant with prayer beads and a slave trader whispering to him, painted from Vereshchagin's Turkestan travels; note that Commons itself says 'A rich Turkish man' and files it under 'Slavery in the Ottoman Empire', which is presumably where 'Ottoman' came from

issues.quote: condemns the dehumanization of slavery through unflinching realism
issues.problem: Editorialising in place of description; nothing in the text tells the reader what is actually in the frame — the carpets, the prayer beads, the second man whispering, the slippers.
issues.evidence: image

proposals.imageObservation: A dim interior with carved doors and a plastered wall: a grey-bearded man in a white turban and a gold-patterned Central Asian robe sits cross-legged on carpets fingering a string of prayer beads; beside him a second man leans in whispering, while a third in a bright pink-and-green striped robe presents a naked boy who stands with his back to the viewer on a white cloth. A dark-robed figure stands at the left edge, and slippers lie on the matting.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The 'Ottoman' claim is not a free invention — Commons asserts it — but the weight of the Russian literature and the Turkestan-series attribution put the scene in Central Asia, so I removed the empire rather than substituting another one. The Tretyakov attribution is supported both by the Commons credit line and by the Commons category 'Paintings by Vasily Vereshchagin in the Tretyakov Gallery'. Russian sources give the canvas as 123 x 92.4 cm; the record has no realDimensions, so that could be added if someone wants to source it properly.

proposals.title: Redoute flowers01
proposals.currentDescription: A spray of cultivated flowers drawn life-size against an empty ground, each bloom and leaf described with botanical precision. A plate after Redouté, the botanist-painter attached to the Jardin des Plantes and to the Empress Joséphine's garden at Malmaison. Colour stipple engraving finished by hand, in the technique used throughout his folios.
proposals.proposedDescription: A cut bouquet against an empty white ground: a full pink cabbage rose above a pale yellow-green double bloom and a red double flower with dark maroon outer petals and a green centre, with rose buds and foliage below. A plate after Redouté, the flower painter attached to the Jardin des Plantes and to the Empress Joséphine's garden at Malmaison. Colour stipple engraving finished by hand, in the technique used throughout his folios.

issues.quote: drawn life-size
issues.problem: A specific physical claim with nothing behind it: the record carries no dimensions for this sheet and the source metadata says nothing about scale.
issues.evidence: catalogue record — realDimensions is absent; Commons gives only 'Fleures peintre par Pierre-Joseph Redouté'

issues.quote: the botanist-painter
issues.problem: Redouté was a flower painter and draughtsman attached to the Muséum (Jardin des Plantes), not a botanist; the botanical texts for his folios were written by others.
issues.evidence: knowledge

issues.quote: A spray of cultivated flowers
issues.problem: It is a bouquet of three plainly different flowers, one of them a cabbage rose; 'a spray of cultivated flowers' says nothing a reader could picture.
issues.evidence: image

proposals.imageObservation: A cut bouquet of three flowers against a plain white ground: a full pink cabbage rose at the top, a pale yellow-green double bloom at the lower left, and a red double flower with dark maroon outer petals and a green centre at the right, with rose buds, foliage and a prickly stem below.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The Malmaison and Jardin des Plantes facts are right and kept. Commons files this under 'Rosa centifolia - botanical illustrations' and 'Les Roses (Redouté)', which supports calling the pink flower a cabbage rose; I left the other two flowers unnamed rather than guess a species. 'Colour stipple engraving finished by hand' is kept — it is true of Redouté's published folios generally and matches the Commons category 'Painted engraving of roses' — but note the record's credit says this file is a restoration by Nicholas Rougeux after Redouté.

proposals.title: 冨嶽三十六景 甲州三坂水面-Reflection in Lake at Misaka in Kai Province
proposals.currentDescription: A woodblock print from Hokusai's celebrated series Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, depicting the reflection of the iconic mountain in Lake Misaka in Kai Province. This print exemplifies the series' innovative compositional approach to landscape representation in ukiyo-e tradition.
proposals.proposedDescription: A colour woodblock print from Hokusai's Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji: Fuji stands brown and snowless above a thatched village on the shore, while its reflection in the water below is snow-capped, and a boatman poles a laden boat at lower right. The view is taken from the Misaka Pass in Kai Province, looking across Lake Kawaguchi. This impression, published about 1830-32, is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art.

issues.quote: in Lake Misaka in Kai Province
issues.problem: There is no Lake Misaka. Misaka is the pass from which the view is taken; the water is Lake Kawaguchi. The Japanese title says 'water surface at Misaka'.
issues.evidence: commons - category 'Mount Fuji reflects in Lake Kawaguchi, seen from the Misaka Pass in Kai Province'

issues.quote: the iconic mountain
issues.problem: Hype filler; and the sentence never mentions what makes this print notable - the snowless summer peak against a snow-capped reflection, the village and the boat.
issues.evidence: house style / image

proposals.imageObservation: Colour woodblock print: Mount Fuji rising brown and snowless above a thatched lakeside village, its inverted reflection in the still water showing a snow-capped peak; a boatman poles a laden boat at lower right; title cartouche and signature upper left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The Met holding follows from the Commons credit line (Met open-access donation) and the 'Japanese prints in the Metropolitan Museum of Art' category. Date range from the Commons date field (circa 1830, -32).

evidence.sourceUrl: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:冨嶽三十六景_甲州三坂水面-Reflection_in_Lake_at_Misaka_in_Kai_Province_(Kōshū_Misaka_suimen),_from_the_series_Thirty-six_Views_of_Mount_Fuji_(Fugaku_sanjūrokkei_MET_DP141064.jpg
evidence.objectKey: collection-of-beauty/冨嶽三十六景_甲州三坂水面-Reflection_in_Lake_at_Misaka_in_Kai_Province_(Kōshū_Misaka_suimen),_from_the_series_Thirty-six_Views_of_Mount_Fuji_(Fugaku_sanjūrokkei_MET_DP141064.jpg

proposals.title: Rembrandt Harmensz. van Rijn - Christ Crucified Between the Two Thieves
proposals.currentDescription: A monumental etching depicting the crucifixion of Christ flanked by the two thieves, demonstrating Rembrandt's mastery of dramatic light and shadow. One of the most celebrated prints in Western art history, this work showcases the Dutch master's technique and theological interpretation of the Crucifixion narrative.
proposals.proposedDescription: A drypoint of the Crucifixion, Christ on the central cross between the two thieves, a shaft of light falling from above while soldiers on horseback, mourners and onlookers crowd the darkness below. Rembrandt worked the plate in 1653 and reworked it heavily through successive states, so impressions differ sharply from one another. This impression is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art.

issues.quote: A monumental etching
issues.problem: The Three Crosses is a drypoint (with burin work from the third state); it is not an etching. The Met catalogues this impression as drypoint.
issues.evidence: web:https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/354631 - 'drypoint printed on vellum'; en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Three_Crosses notes the plate was drawn entirely in drypoint with burin corrections from the third state

issues.quote: One of the most celebrated prints in Western art history, this work showcases the Dutch master's technique and theological interpretation of the Crucifixion narrative.
issues.problem: Second sentence is pure superlative boilerplate and adds no grounded information; house style asks for concrete context (states, collection, date).
issues.evidence: catalogue record - no supporting content; corpus house style

proposals.imageObservation: A large print of the Crucifixion: Christ on the central cross between the two thieves, a shaft of light raking down from above, mounted soldiers, mourners and onlookers massed in the dark foreground. Heavily worked in dense drypoint burr; no colour.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Only the medium word and the hype sentence are at issue; subject, artist, date and collection all check out against the image and the Commons/Met metadata.

proposals.title: joseph-durand-ruel-1882.jpg!PinterestLarge
proposals.currentDescription: Joseph Durand-Ruel, eldest son of Renoir's dealer Paul Durand-Ruel, shown as a young man against a leafy ground. Oil on canvas painted in 1882, the year Renoir also portrayed Joseph's younger brothers Charles and Georges. Joseph (1862 to 1928) went on to run the family gallery.
proposals.proposedDescription: Joseph Durand-Ruel, eldest son of Renoir's dealer Paul Durand-Ruel, seated in a pale armchair with a folded paper in his hands against a mottled ground of mauve, blue and green strokes. Oil on canvas painted in 1882 — the signature reads 'Renoir 82' — the year Renoir also portrayed Joseph's younger brothers Charles and Georges. Joseph (1862 to 1928) went on to run the family gallery.

issues.quote: against a leafy ground
issues.problem: The background is an abstract mottled weave of mauve, blue and green brushstrokes with no legible foliage, and the white chair back at the right reads as an interior setting.
issues.evidence: image

proposals.imageObservation: A young dark-haired man with a small moustache sits facing the viewer in a white-upholstered chair, wearing a brown coat over an olive waistcoat with a watch chain and holding a folded paper or pamphlet in his lap. The ground behind him is a mottled haze of mauve, blue and green strokes. Signed and dated 'Renoir 82' at upper right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The biography holds: Joseph Durand-Ruel (1862–1928) was the eldest son and later ran the gallery, and Renoir's double portrait of Charles and Georges Durand-Ruel is also of 1882. The date is confirmed on the canvas itself. 'Leafy ground' is the only thing the image argues against, and it is a judgement call about very loose brushwork — a reviewer who reads that background as garden foliage can leave the sentence alone.

proposals.title: Репин. Украинка у плетня
proposals.currentDescription: Portrait of a Ukrainian peasant woman standing by a woven fence, painted by Russian-born artist Ilya Repin in 1876. The subject wears traditional Ukrainian dress including a decorated vyshyvanka and ornamental headdress, with arms crossed in a confident pose. Now held in the Latvian National Museum of Arts.
proposals.proposedDescription: Portrait of a Ukrainian peasant woman standing by a woven wattle fence, painted by Ilya Repin in 1876. The subject wears traditional Ukrainian dress including a decorated vyshyvanka, strings of beads and a ribboned headdress, with arms crossed in a confident pose. Now held in the Latvian National Museum of Arts.

issues.quote: Russian-born artist Ilya Repin
issues.problem: Repin was born in Chuhuiv, in the Kharkiv region of present-day Ukraine, not in Russia. 'Russian-born' is factually wrong even though the record's nationality field says Russian.
issues.evidence: knowledge | Repin was born in Chuhuiv (Chuguev), Kharkov Governorate, in 1844

proposals.imageObservation: Three-quarter-length oil portrait of a young woman standing before a wattle fence, arms crossed, in an embroidered white blouse, several strands of coral, white and dark beads, a headdress of coloured ribbons and flowers with long pink and striped ribbons falling forward, and a red patterned skirt with a woven apron. Signed and dated lower left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Everything else is confirmed: the vyshyvanka, the headdress, the crossed arms and the wattle fence are all visible, the 1876 date matches the record and the Commons date field, and Commons categorises the painting under 'Paintings in the Latvian National Museum of Arts'. Only the birthplace clause needed removing; I substituted a neutral formulation rather than replacing it with 'Ukrainian-born', which would misstate how Repin is normally described.

proposals.title: Meeting of Artists in Isabey's Studio
proposals.currentDescription: Tableau de Louis-Léopold Boilly représentant des artistes influents sous le Directoire. Les identifications des personnes représentées en annotations d'image sont renseignées sur l'élément wikidata : https://wd-image-positions. toolforge.
proposals.proposedDescription: Some thirty men in Directoire coats and high cravats crowd a studio interior, standing and seated around a table, with a canvas on an easel at the far left and painted arabesques running above the rear wall. Boilly painted the group in 1798; the sitters are identified in the annotations attached to the work's Wikidata item. It is in the Musée du Louvre, inv. RF 1290bis.

issues.quote: https://wd-image-positions. toolforge.
issues.problem: The description is the raw Commons caption and its URL has been truncated mid-address, so the sentence points the reader at a source that does not resolve.
issues.evidence: commons | the full caption reads 'https://wd-image-positions.toolforge.org/item/Q18783510'; the stored description cuts off after 'toolforge.'

issues.quote: Tableau de Louis-Léopold Boilly représentant des artistes influents sous le Directoire.
issues.problem: Scraped French metadata rather than a description: it is not in the catalogue's language and says nothing about the studio, the crowd, the easel or the wall decoration.
issues.evidence: image | catalogue record

proposals.imageObservation: A crowded studio interior: some thirty men in dark Directoire coats and high white cravats stand and sit around a table, with an easel at the far left, a framed relief or portrait high on the rear wall and painted neoclassical arabesques above; one man in a yellow coat sits on a crate in the centre foreground.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The substantive claim (Boilly, artists of the Directoire) is right and matches the Commons record; the problem is that the stored text is an untranslated caption with a broken link. The Louvre and the accession number RF 1290bis come from the Commons file title, and the studio is named as Isabey's in the catalogue title - I left Isabey out of the first sentence because I cannot tell from the picture which figure he is.

proposals.title: Réunion de famille
proposals.currentDescription: Ten of the painter's relatives gathered on a shaded terrace at the family estate of Méric near Montpellier, most of them looking out at the viewer. Oil on canvas, 152 by 230 cm, painted in 1867 and held by the Musée d'Orsay, Paris, under inventory RF 2749. Bazille reworked the canvas before showing it at the Salon of 1868.
proposals.proposedDescription: Ten of the painter's relatives gathered on a shaded terrace at the family estate of Méric near Montpellier, most of them looking out at the viewer; Bazille added himself at the far left. Oil on canvas, 152 by 230 cm, painted in 1867 and held by the Musée d'Orsay, Paris, under inventory RF 2749. It was shown at the Salon of 1868, and Bazille reworked the foreground afterwards, painting out a dog in favour of the hat and bouquet now lying on the terrace.

issues.quote: Bazille reworked the canvas before showing it at the Salon of 1868.
issues.problem: The sequence is inverted. The canvas was exhibited at the Salon of 1868 and reworked afterwards — the dog in the foreground was painted out and replaced by the still life of hat, cane and bouquet that is visible in the picture.
issues.evidence: web:https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/R%C3%A9union_de_famille_(Bazille) — exhibited at the Salon of 1868, then reworked in his Paris studio, the foreground dog effaced in favour of a still life of flowers, hat and cane

proposals.imageObservation: Eleven figures — six women, five men — on a sunlit terrace under a chestnut tree, most looking out at the viewer; a landscape falls away behind the parapet; a straw hat and a bouquet lie on the ground in the foreground; signed lower left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Dimensions (152 x 230 cm), date, museum and inventory number all confirmed. 'Ten of the painter's relatives' is defensible — eleven figures are visible, the eleventh being Bazille himself, whom the original text left unmentioned; I made that explicit. The only real error is before/after the Salon.

proposals.title: Садовая калитка в Чугучаке
proposals.currentDescription: A work by Vasily Vereshchagin depicting a garden gate in Chuguchak (Tacheng), a historical trading city in Central Asia. Vereshchagin's oriental scenes and architectural studies from the region are notable for their ethnographic detail and precise rendering of local customs and geography.
proposals.proposedDescription: A circular moon gate cut through a grey brick wall, its ridge topped by a carved dragon's head, framing a sunlit tangle of overgrown ruins and bare trees; birds cross the sky above. Vasily Vereshchagin painted the gate at Chuguchak (Tacheng), a trading town in what is now Xinjiang, during his Turkestan travels around 1869-70. The picture belongs to the Turkestan series, in which he worked up architectural motifs observed on the spot.

issues.quote: precise rendering of local customs
issues.problem: This painting contains no figures and no customs; the sentence describes the artist's oeuvre in general and says nothing about the picture.
issues.evidence: image

issues.quote: A work by Vasily Vereshchagin depicting a garden gate in Chuguchak (Tacheng), a historical trading city in Central Asia.
issues.problem: The description never says what the painting looks like - the circular moon gate, the dragon-head ornament, the ruins beyond - which the house style asks for in the first sentence.
issues.evidence: house style / image

metadataIssues.evidence: commons categories: 'Oil on canvas paintings in the Russian Museum' and 'Paintings by Vasily Vereshchagin in the Russian Museum' - the two sources disagree about which museum holds it

proposals.imageObservation: Oil painting: a circular moon gate in a grey brick wall topped by a carved dragon-head ridge ornament; through the opening, sunlit overgrown ruins, bare trees and a pink-lit wall, with birds in the blue sky above. No figures.
proposals.reviewerNotes: No claim in the original is false, but it is pure boilerplate with no visual content, and the 'local customs' line does not fit a picture with no people. Note the collection conflict flagged under metadataIssues - I did not name a museum in the replacement because the record and Commons disagree. Date range from the Commons date field (between 1869 and 1870); the Turkestan series membership comes from the Commons category.

proposals.title: Searching for Immortals
proposals.currentDescription: An album leaf from Shitao's (1642–1707) Landscapes series, part of the Metropolitan Museum of Art collection. This work exemplifies the Qing dynasty master's innovative approach to landscape painting, blending Southern school traditions with his distinctive expressionistic style.
proposals.proposedDescription: An album leaf in ink and light colour on paper: a screen of trees with long trailing foliage rises above a rocky bank, tiled roofs stand among trees at the left, and a tiny figure with a staff waits at the foot of the central trunks. The artist's inscription and seals are at the upper right, collectors' seals along the bottom edge. The leaf comes from an album of landscapes by Shitao (1642-1707) in the Metropolitan Museum of Art.

issues.quote: This work exemplifies the Qing dynasty master's innovative approach to landscape painting
issues.problem: The description never says what is in the frame - no trees, no bank, no figure, no seals or inscription. Both sentences are provenance plus generic praise.
issues.evidence: image - the leaf has a specific, describable composition that the text ignores

issues.quote: blending Southern school traditions with his distinctive expressionistic style
issues.problem: A specific art-historical placement that nothing in the record or the Commons metadata supports; Shitao is more usually characterised as an individualist who argued against orthodox-school lineage, so this reads as a filled-in generality rather than a checked fact.
issues.evidence: commons - the file page gives only 'China; Album; Paintings' and 'Paintings by Shitao'; catalogue record adds nothing

issues.quote: exemplifies
issues.problem: Catalogue boilerplate; house style is plain and factual.
issues.evidence: style

metadataIssues.proposed: unverified - leave as is but flag
metadataIssues.evidence: Commons date field is empty and the leaf carries no legible date; 1696 has no visible source in the record.

proposals.imageObservation: A horizontal album leaf in ink and pale blue-green washes on paper: a dense screen of trees with long trailing foliage rises above a rocky bank, tiled roofs sit among trees at the left, a knoll of flat-topped pines fills the lower right, and a tiny standing figure with a staff is at the foot of the central trees. An inscription and two red seals are at the upper right; three collectors' seals run along the bottom edge.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Nothing in the old text is demonstrably false - Shitao's dates and the Met attribution are right - but it is pure boilerplate with no visual content, and the 'Southern school' line is an unbacked art-historical assertion. The replacement keeps only what the image and the Commons record support. I deliberately did not carry over the 1696 date, which no source in the record backs.

evidence.sourceUrl: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:清 石濤(朱若極) 山水圖 冊-Searching for Immortals MET DP162813.jpg

proposals.title: Self-portrait
proposals.currentDescription: A half-length self-portrait in which Watts wears a dark slouch hat and black velvet coat against a plain ground. Oil on canvas, 64.8 by 52.1 cm, painted in 1864 and held by Tate Britain. Watts painted it during his years at Little Holland House in Kensington, drawing on Old Master portraiture such as Raphael's Castiglione.
proposals.proposedDescription: A half-length self-portrait in which Watts wears a dark slouch hat and dark coat, set against a panelled door. Oil on canvas, 64.8 by 52.1 cm, painted in 1864 and held by Tate Britain. Watts painted it during his years at Little Holland House in Kensington, where he lived and worked from the early 1850s.

issues.quote: against a plain ground
issues.problem: The background is not plain: a panelled door/wainscot with mouldings fills it, and the panel edges are clearly drawn.
issues.evidence: image

issues.quote: drawing on Old Master portraiture such as Raphael's Castiglione
issues.problem: A specific source-picture claim that neither the record, Commons, nor the Tate page supports; Watts's self-portraits are more often linked with Titian.
issues.evidence: web:https://www.tate.org.uk/art/artworks/watts-self-portrait-n01561 - no such statement on the Tate page

issues.quote: black velvet coat
issues.problem: The coat's material cannot be judged from the reproduction; it reads dark brown-black.
issues.evidence: image

proposals.imageObservation: Oil portrait: a bearded man in a wide-brimmed dark hat and dark coat, turned slightly left, one hand visible at lower left; the background is a panelled door or wainscot in olive-ochre tones, with the monogram G.F.W. at lower right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Dimensions and Tate ownership confirmed (Tate N01561, 64.8 x 52.1 cm). Little Holland House is well established. I dropped the Castiglione comparison rather than swap in another Old Master name, since I could not source either.

proposals.title: 冨嶽三十六景 相州七里浜-Shichirigahama in Sagami Province
proposals.currentDescription: A woodblock print by Japanese master Katsushika Hokusai depicting the famous Shichirigahama beach in Sagami Province. This iconic image is part of his celebrated series Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji (Fugaku sanjūrokkei), created during the 1830s. The composition showcases the dramatic interaction between human activity and landscape, with Mount Fuji visible in the distant background.
proposals.proposedDescription: A near-monochrome blue-and-green woodblock print: the long beach at Shichirigahama in Sagami Province curves across the foreground under combing waves, a wooded headland carries a cluster of thatched roofs, and Mount Fuji rises snow-streaked at the right. From Hokusai's series Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji (Fugaku sanjurokkei), printed about 1830-32. This impression is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art.

issues.quote: The composition showcases the dramatic interaction between human activity and landscape
issues.problem: There is no human activity in the print - no figures, no boats, no work. The only trace of habitation is a handful of thatched roofs on the hillside. The sentence is generic filler that the image does not support.
issues.evidence: image - the sheet shows beach, sea, headland with roofs, hills and Fuji, and nothing else

issues.quote: This iconic image
issues.problem: Empty praise ('iconic', 'celebrated', 'Japanese master', 'showcases'); the description never says what the print actually looks like.
issues.evidence: house style

proposals.imageObservation: A near-monochrome blue and green landscape print: a long beach with combing waves in the foreground, a wooded headland carrying a cluster of thatched roofs, and snow-streaked Mount Fuji at the right against banded blue sky. No human figures are visible; title and signature cartouches sit at the upper left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Met attribution comes from the Commons credit line (Metropolitan Museum open-access donation) and the file's MET DP number; date 'circa 1830 ... -32' from Commons. I dropped the 'human activity' sentence rather than repairing it.

evidence.fileUrl: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a4/冨嶽三十六景_相州七里浜-Shichirigahama_in_Sagami_Province_%28Sōshū_Shichirigahama%29%2C_from_the_series_Thirty-six_Views_of_Mount_Fuji_%28Fugaku_sanjūrokkei%29_MET_DP140979.jpg/800px-冨嶽三十六景_相州七里浜-Shichirigahama_in_Sagami_Province_%28Sōshū_Shichirigahama%29%2C_from_the_series_Thirty-six_Views_of_Mount_Fuji_%28Fugaku_sanjūrokkei%29_MET_DP140979.jpg

proposals.title: Sir David Wilkie's residence in Kensington London
proposals.currentDescription: A painting by English landscape and genre painter William Collins depicting the Kensington residence of fellow artist Sir David Wilkie, created in 1841 shortly after Wilkie's death. The work documents an important London townhouse associated with a prominent figure in British art history.
proposals.proposedDescription: A house standing among tall trees behind a lawn and flowering shrubs, its garden front catching the light, with a single dark-clad figure at the right. William Collins painted Sir David Wilkie's residence in Kensington in 1841, shortly after Wilkie's death.

issues.quote: The work documents an important London townhouse
issues.problem: What is painted is a detached villa standing in its own garden with lawn and trees, not a townhouse; 'important' is unsupported puffery.
issues.evidence: image — free-standing house with garden on at least two sides, no terrace or street frontage

issues.quote: A painting by English landscape and genre painter William Collins depicting the Kensington residence
issues.problem: The description never says what the picture actually shows.
issues.evidence: style — house style asks the first sentence to describe the image

proposals.imageObservation: Photograph of a framed oil painting: a substantial detached house with a bowed, many-windowed corner block stands among tall trees, seen across a lawn with flowering shrubs and a path; a single dark-clad figure stands at the right edge.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Attribution, subject and date come from the Commons file title (a visitor photograph of the picture, so the metadata is the uploader's own caption rather than a museum record). Wilkie died at sea in June 1841, so 'shortly after Wilkie's death' is consistent. Nothing establishes the collection, so the replacement does not name one.

proposals.title: Snowscape
proposals.currentDescription: A winter landscape of snow-laden peaks and bare trees rising above a misty valley, the foreground pushed to one corner in the asymmetric manner that earned Ma Yuan the nickname 'one-corner Ma'. Attributed to the Southern Song court painter and held in the National Palace Museum, Taipei. Hanging scroll, ink and colour on silk.
proposals.proposedDescription: A winter landscape of snow-laden peaks and bare trees rising above a misty valley, a great snow-covered pine leaning across the centre above a pavilion, with a rider crossing a bridge at the lower right. The foreground is pushed to one corner in the asymmetric manner that earned Ma Yuan the nickname 'one-corner Ma'. Attributed to the Southern Song court painter and held in the National Palace Museum, Taipei. Hanging scroll, ink and colour on paper.

issues.quote: Hanging scroll, ink and colour on silk
issues.problem: The source describes the support as paper, not silk.
issues.evidence: commons — the file name is '雪景图轴.传宋.马远.画.纸本设色.台北故宫博物院藏.jpg', where 纸本设色 means 'ink and colour on paper' (絹本 would be silk).

issues.quote: A winter landscape of snow-laden peaks and bare trees rising above a misty valley
issues.problem: The scroll's most distinctive elements — the great leaning pine, the pavilion and the rider crossing the bridge — go unmentioned.
issues.evidence: image

proposals.imageObservation: A tall hanging scroll in ink with light colour: snow lies on angular rocks and distant peaks, a huge snow-laden pine leans across the centre, a pavilion with figures sits among red-leaved trees at the left, and a rider on horseback crosses a bridge at the lower right; several red collector seals are stamped along the top and sides.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Only the support word changes plus an added clause for what is actually in the frame; the 'one-corner Ma' nickname and the attributed status are both correct (the Commons file name uses 传 'attributed', and the National Palace Museum's own entry notes that the brushwork suggests a Ming painter working in Ma Yuan's manner despite the Ma Yuan signature — worth adding if someone can read the NPM page directly; I could only reach it through a search summary, so I left it out of the replacement). Collection and inventory come from the record's provenance block.

evidence.objectKey: collection-of-beauty/雪景图轴.传宋.马远.画.纸本设色.台北故宫博物院藏.jpg

proposals.title: Sotatsu Dragons and Clouds
proposals.currentDescription: Two dragons coil out of swirling ink clouds across a pair of folding screens by Tawaraya Sōtatsu, the early seventeenth-century founder of the Rinpa school. Working in ink alone, Sōtatsu pooled and blotted washes to make the beasts surface and dissolve in the mist. The screens are held by the National Museum of Asian Art in Washington, D.C.
proposals.proposedDescription: A dragon coils out of swirling ink clouds across a six-panel folding screen by Tawaraya Sōtatsu, the early seventeenth-century founder of the Rinpa school, with waves breaking along the lower edge. It is one of a pair: the second screen carries the dragon's counterpart. Sōtatsu pooled and blotted his washes so the beast surfaces and dissolves in the mist. The screens are held by the National Museum of Asian Art in Washington, D.C.

issues.quote: Two dragons coil out of swirling ink clouds across a pair of folding screens
issues.problem: The reproduction in the catalogue is one six-panel screen carrying one dragon (Freer F1905.229, the left screen). The object as a whole is a pair, but the image a viewer sees shows a single dragon on a single screen, and the record's realDimensions (374.3 x 171.5 cm) are the measurements of one screen, not the pair.
issues.evidence: image — five internal panel seams, i.e. six panels, with one dragon; catalogue record realDimensions 374.3 x 171.5; web:https://asia.si.edu/object/F1905.229 — F1905.229 is the left screen of the pair F1905.229-230, each 171.5 x 374.3 cm

issues.quote: Working in ink alone
issues.problem: The museum records the medium as ink and pink tint on paper, not ink alone.
issues.evidence: web:https://asia.si.edu/object/F1905.229 — 'ink and pink tint on paper'

proposals.imageObservation: A single six-panel folding screen (five visible seams) in monochrome ink: one dragon, head and mane at upper left of centre, body coiling right into scaly hindquarters and clawed legs, emerging from blotted grey cloud; breaking waves run along the lower left and right edges. A small red seal sits at the lower right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The description is not wrong about the object, only about the picture on the page: the credit URL in the record points at F1905.229, the left screen alone, which is what the JPEG shows. If the site ever shows both screens the original wording would be fine. Museum medium line is 'ink and pink tint on paper'; the tint is not visible in this reproduction, so I removed 'ink alone' rather than asserting the tint.

proposals.title: Спящая царевна
proposals.currentDescription: Viktor Vasnetsov's "The Sleeping Queen" (Спящая царевна) is a monumental symbolist painting depicting the Russian fairy-tale princess in enchanted slumber. Created in the early 20th century, the work exemplifies Vasnetsov's mastery of Russian mythological and folkloric themes through luminous color and dreamlike composition. The painting is housed in the Vasnetsov memorial house in Moscow.
proposals.proposedDescription: The tsarevna lies asleep on a raised, richly patterned bed in a painted wooden terem, and her whole court sleeps around her: girls slumped on benches, a jester in red, an old gusli player, a small girl fallen across a huge open book, and a bear at the foot of the dais, with the forest pressing in behind. Vasnetsov took the subject from the Russian fairy tale of the sleeping princess and worked at the canvas over many years, from about 1900. It is in the Vasnetsov memorial house in Moscow.

issues.quote: exemplifies Vasnetsov's mastery of Russian mythological and folkloric themes through luminous color and dreamlike composition
issues.problem: The description never says what is in the picture. The sleeping court, the jester, the gusli player, the bear and the girl asleep over the open book are the whole point of the composition and none is mentioned.
issues.evidence: image

issues.quote: The Sleeping Queen
issues.problem: The record's own englishTitle is 'The Sleeping Princess', and the Russian 'tsarevna' means princess, not queen. The description then contradicts itself by calling her a princess in the next clause.
issues.evidence: catalogue record englishTitle 'The Sleeping Princess'; the title given in the description's own next clause. Commons' objectName does say 'The Sleeping Queen', so the error was inherited rather than invented.

issues.quote: monumental symbolist painting
issues.problem: The record carries no dimensions, so 'monumental' is unsupported, and the record's own movement field is Romanticism rather than Symbolism.
issues.evidence: catalogue record - realDimensions null, movement 'Romanticism'

proposals.imageObservation: A wide horizontal painting of a Russian terem interior open to a forest: the sleeping princess lies on a raised, richly patterned bed at centre, and around her the whole court sleeps - girls slumped on benches at left, a red-clad jester, an old man with a gusli and a bearded elder at right, a small girl fallen face-down across a huge open book, a brown bear at the foot of the dais, and poppies growing in the foreground.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The collection is right - Commons categorises the file under 'Paintings in the Vasnetsov memorial house' - and the long working period is supported by the Commons date 'between 1900 and 1926', which is why I wrote 'over many years, from about 1900' rather than repeating the record's bare 1900. I deliberately left out any dimension, since the record has none and Commons flags the Wikidata item as missing dimensions.

proposals.title: 溥僩丙子夏日寫生
proposals.currentDescription: A summer sketch study created in 1936 (the year of Bingzi in the Chinese zodiac) by the modern Chinese painter Pu Xuan. This work exemplifies the artist's approach to observational painting during a productive period of artistic exploration.
proposals.proposedDescription: Two pigeons stand among rocks and tufted grass beneath a flowering peach branch, where a small brown bird perches with its bill open; bamboo rises behind a pierced garden rock. An inscription and two red seals at the upper right date the picture to a summer day of the bingzi year, 1936.

issues.quote: This work exemplifies the artist's approach to observational painting during a productive period of artistic exploration.
issues.problem: Pure filler: it says nothing about the picture and asserts a 'productive period of artistic exploration' that nothing in the record supports. The description never mentions the pigeons, the flowering branch, the bamboo, the rock or the inscription.
issues.evidence: image; catalogue record carries no biographical information at all

issues.quote: the year of Bingzi in the Chinese zodiac
issues.problem: Bingzi is a year of the sexagenary (stem-branch) cycle, not of the twelve-animal zodiac.
issues.evidence: knowledge; Commons imageDescription gives 丙子年（1936）

metadataIssues.evidence: Commons artist field reads 'Pu Xian' and the file title is 溥僩; 僩 is normally romanised xiàn/xiǎn, not xuan. Low confidence — worth a check against how the artist is listed elsewhere in the catalogue before changing.

proposals.imageObservation: A vertical Chinese bird-and-flower composition: two pigeons on the ground among rocks and tufted grass at the lower centre, a small brown bird with open bill perched on a flowering peach branch above, bamboo behind a pierced garden rock, and a column of inscription with two red seals at the upper right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Nothing in the old text is contradicted, but it is entirely content-free, which is exactly where invented context tends to live ('a productive period of artistic exploration' has no source). I deliberately did not state a medium: it reads as ink and colour on paper, but that cannot be settled from the reproduction. The 1936 date is corroborated by the Commons description.

proposals.title: Sumō-wrestling toads by Hōson
proposals.currentDescription: Ohara Koson's colour woodblock print shows a group of toads in various animated poses — two grappling upright, others leaping or watching — on a grassy ground with a single autumn leaf in the air. Working in the shin-hanga idiom, Koson brings naturalist observation to a comic subject with long roots in Japanese caricature, here dating to around 1930.
proposals.proposedDescription: Ohara Koson's colour woodblock print shows five toads in animated poses - two grappling upright, one at left standing with folded arms, another rearing up with an orange autumn leaf held aloft like a referee's fan, and one squatting in the foreground - on a grassy ground beneath a warm gradient sky. Working in the shin-hanga idiom, Koson brings naturalist observation to a comic subject with long roots in Japanese caricature, here dating to around 1930.

issues.quote: with a single autumn leaf in the air
issues.problem: The orange leaf is not floating: a toad at right holds it up in its hand, brandished the way a sumo referee holds a gunbai fan.
issues.evidence: image

proposals.imageObservation: Colour woodblock print: five toads on a grassy ground under an orange-to-green gradient sky - one at left standing with folded arms, two grappling upright in the centre, one at right rearing up and holding an orange autumn leaf aloft in one hand, and one sitting in the foreground watching. Artist's signature and red seal at right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Date matches the original date string (Showa 5, i.e. about 1930). Only the leaf detail was wrong; the referee reading is offered as a simile ('like a referee's fan') rather than asserted.

proposals.title: Tabi miyage dai sanshū
proposals.currentDescription: A torii gate stands on a rocky shore at Futomi in Awa Province, flanked by a pair of stone lanterns and backed by crashing waves and distant green islands. A small figure shelters beneath the gate, and a wooden boat rests to one side. A woodblock print from Kawase Hasui's Souvenirs of Travel III (1925), the composition centres on the coastal shrine's gateway as a framing device for sea and sky.
proposals.proposedDescription: A torii gate stands on a sandy shore at Futomi in Awa Province, flanked by a pair of stone lanterns and backed by crashing waves and distant green headlands. Two small figures crouch on the sand beneath the gate, and wooden boats are drawn up to one side. A woodblock print from Kawase Hasui's Souvenirs of Travel III (1925), the composition centres on the coastal shrine's gateway as a framing device for sea and sky.

issues.quote: A small figure shelters beneath the gate, and a wooden boat rests to one side.
issues.problem: Two figures crouch together below the gate, not one, and there are at least two beached boats at the right, not one.
issues.evidence: image

proposals.imageObservation: A vertical woodblock print: an orange torii stands on a sandy shore between two stone lanterns on stepped plinths, breaking blue-white waves behind it, a turquoise bay and low green headlands beyond. TWO small figures in kimono crouch together on the sand below the gate, and at least two wooden boats are drawn up on the right. Title and date columns at the left margin, seal and signature at lower right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: This already carries ledgerStatus 'fabricated-fixed' and the rewrite is broadly good — the torii, the paired lanterns, the waves, the headlands, the series and the 1925 date (大正14年出版 = published Taishō 14) all check out against the image and Commons. Only the two counts are off. I also changed 'rocky shore' to 'sandy shore': the foreground is sand with a few rocks at the left edge, so 'rocky' overstates it slightly — treat that as optional.

proposals.title: 冨嶽三十六景 東海道江尻田子の浦略図-Tago Bay near Ejiri on the Tōkaidō
proposals.currentDescription: A woodblock print from Katsushika Hokusai's renowned series "Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji" (Fugaku sanjūrokkei). This print depicts Tago Bay near the town of Ejiri along the Tōkaidō highway, capturing the dramatic coastal landscape with Mount Fuji visible in the distance. Created during the mid-Edo period (1830), it exemplifies the ukiyo-e artistic tradition and Hokusai's mastery of perspective and color composition.
proposals.proposedDescription: Two long boats with their crews ride the choppy blue water of Tago Bay in the foreground, with a village strung along the low sandy shore behind and the snow-streaked cone of Mount Fuji beyond. A colour woodblock print from Katsushika Hokusai's series Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji (Fugaku sanjurokkei), issued around 1830, showing the bay near Ejiri on the Tokaido highway. This impression is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art.

issues.quote: Created during the mid-Edo period (1830)
issues.problem: 1830 is late Edo, not mid-Edo; the period runs 1603-1868 and the Thirty-six Views belong to its last decades.
issues.evidence: knowledge; commons date 'circa 1830 ... -32'.

issues.quote: capturing the dramatic coastal landscape with Mount Fuji visible in the distance
issues.problem: The most prominent thing in the frame - two boats and their crews filling the foreground - is never mentioned.
issues.evidence: image.

issues.quote: Hokusai's mastery of perspective and color composition
issues.problem: Boilerplate.
issues.evidence: corpus house style.

proposals.imageObservation: Colour woodblock print: two long boats with crews ride steep blue waves in the foreground, a low sandy shore with a village and pine trees behind, and the snow-streaked cone of Mount Fuji at upper right; title cartouche and signature at upper left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Metropolitan Museum attribution comes from the Commons credit line and category for this file, which was donated by the Met.

evidence.sourceUrl: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:冨嶽三十六景_東海道江尻田子の浦略図-Tago_Bay_near_Ejiri_on_the_Tōkaidō_(Tōkaidō_Ejiri_Tago_no_ura_ryaku_zu),_from_the_series_Thirty-six_Views_of_Mount_Fuji_(Fugaku_sanjūrokkei)_MET_DP141037.jpg

evidence.objectKey: collection-of-beauty/冨嶽三十六景_東海道江尻田子の浦略図-Tago_Bay_near_Ejiri_on_the_Tōkaidō_(Tōkaidō_Ejiri_Tago_no_ura_ryaku_zu),_from_the_series_Thirty-six_Views_of_Mount_Fuji_(Fugaku_sanjūrokkei)_MET_DP141037.jpg

proposals.title: The Artist's wife
proposals.currentDescription: The painter's wife seated in his studio, surrounded by the props of his trade. Oil on canvas, 40.6 by 32.9 cm, at the Clark Art Institute and dated about 1795 to 1799. Boilly returned often to domestic interiors built around a single figure.
proposals.proposedDescription: The painter's wife standing in his studio, surrounded by the props of his trade: a blank canvas on an easel, a wall lamp, a plaster figure and a chair heaped with drawings. Oil on canvas, 40.6 by 32.9 cm, at the Clark Art Institute and dated about 1795 to 1799. Boilly returned often to domestic interiors built around a single figure.

issues.quote: The painter's wife seated in his studio
issues.problem: She is standing, full length, beside a chair — not seated. The chair in the picture holds drawings, not the sitter.
issues.evidence: image — the figure stands upright in a white dress, her skirt falling to the floor beside the chair

proposals.imageObservation: A woman in a long white empire-line dress stands in a painter's studio, one hand on a stack of drawings propped on a red-upholstered chair; behind her are a blank canvas on an easel, a red drape, a wall lamp, a glove hanging on the wall, a plaster figure and a bust on a table.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Medium, collection and date are all confirmed verbatim by the Commons imageDescription ('The Artist's Wife in His Studio (c.1795-99), Oil on canvas, 16 x 12 15/16 in. (40.6 x 32.9 cm), Clark Art Institute'). Only the posture is wrong.

proposals.title: The Disquieting Muses
proposals.currentDescription: A modernist oil painting by Giorgio de Chirico from 1950, depicting mysterious classical female figures in an enigmatic architectural setting exemplifying his metaphysical style.
proposals.proposedDescription: Two faceless mannequin figures hold a raking ochre platform in low light — one draped like a statue on a fluted plinth, the other seated with an egg-shaped head — beside a blue box, a red ovoid and a box painted in coloured triangles. Behind them a red-brick castle with four towers and a pair of factory chimneys close the horizon under a dark green sky, with a small classical statue on a plinth at the right. De Chirico returned to this metaphysical composition repeatedly; the version here is dated 1950.

issues.quote: mysterious classical female figures in an enigmatic architectural setting exemplifying his metaphysical style
issues.problem: The two principal figures are faceless tailors'-dummy mannequins, one draped and standing on a fluted plinth and one seated with an egg head — not classical female figures (the only classical statue is a small one far off at the right). The rest of the sentence is boilerplate: nothing of the plaza, the castle, the chimneys or the geometric props is described.
issues.evidence: image — two mannequin figures with blank ovoid heads dominate the foreground

issues.quote: A modernist oil painting by Giorgio de Chirico from 1950, depicting mysterious
issues.problem: 'Modernist oil painting ... mysterious ... enigmatic' is empty framing; the description never says what is in the frame.
issues.evidence: catalogue record — no visual content given

proposals.imageObservation: An ochre raked platform in strong late light: a tall draped figure on a fluted plinth with an ovoid mannequin head, and a seated mannequin with an egg-shaped head resting beside it, together with a blue box, a red ovoid form and a box painted in coloured triangles. Behind, a red-brick castle with four towers, two factory chimneys at the left and a small classical statue on a plinth at the right against a dark green sky; signed and dated at the lower right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The 1950 date matches both the record and the Commons date field, and de Chirico's habit of repeating the Disquieting Muses composition over decades is well documented, so I stated it without claiming a date for the first version. I deliberately did not name the towered building as the Castello Estense in Ferrara — that identification is standard in the literature but is not supported by anything supplied here.

proposals.title: The Equatorial Jungle
proposals.currentDescription: Oil painting by Henri Rousseau depicting a lush jungle landscape with exotic animals and stylized vegetation. Painted in 1909, it is part of Rousseau's famous jungle series, though he never traveled to a tropical region—his inspiration came from botanical gardens in Paris and illustrations. The work exemplifies Rousseau's distinctive Naïve Art style and is housed at the National Gallery of Art in Washington, D.
proposals.proposedDescription: Dense jungle foliage fills the canvas, with pink blossoms at the left, a hanging spike of white flowers at the right and spiky pale grasses across the foreground; two animals peer out from behind a frond at the centre, and a small red-clad figure stands among the palms at the upper left. Painted in 1909, it belongs to the jungle pictures Rousseau made without ever leaving France, working from the hothouses and gardens of Paris and from illustrated books. The painting is at the National Gallery of Art, Washington, D.C.

issues.quote: housed at the National Gallery of Art in Washington, D.
issues.problem: The collection statement is cut off mid-word: it should read Washington, D.C. The description string simply ends there.
issues.evidence: catalogue record — the description ends 'Washington, D.'

issues.quote: depicting a lush jungle landscape with exotic animals and stylized vegetation
issues.problem: Generic gloss; the two animals at the centre, the pink and white flowers and the red figure at the upper left are all specific and unmentioned.
issues.evidence: image

issues.quote: The work exemplifies Rousseau's distinctive Naïve Art style
issues.problem: Catalogue boilerplate.
issues.evidence: knowledge

proposals.imageObservation: Dense flat-patterned jungle foliage fills the canvas: fronds, broad leaves, pink blossoms at the left and a hanging white flower spike at the right, spiky pale grasses across the foreground, and at the centre two animals — one dark with pointed ears, one smaller and reddish — peering out from behind a frond; at the upper left a small red-clad form that reads as a standing figure. Signed 'Henri Julien Rousseau' and dated at lower right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: No fabrication: the 1909 date, the NGA and the never-travelled point are all supported (Commons imageDescription gives 'The Equatorial Jungle (1909). Oil on canvas, 140.6 x 129.5 cm. National Gallery of Art, Washington, D.C.'). Graded minor for the truncated collection line. In my replacement I deliberately did not name the animals as apes or monkeys — they are ambiguous at this resolution — and hedged the red form as a figure, which is what it reads as (head, arms, red robe) but cannot be pinned down.

proposals.title: The muscles of the hand
proposals.currentDescription: An anatomical engraving combining a flayed hand after Bernhard Siegfried Albinus with a foot after De Courcelles, the muscles, tendons and bones laid bare for study. Engraved by Robert Bénard for the late eighteenth-century editions of the Encyclopédie, the plate typifies the Enlightenment project of consolidating earlier anatomical illustration into a single compendium.
proposals.proposedDescription: An anatomical engraving of four figures: two flayed hands after Bernhard Siegfried Albinus above, two dissected feet after De Courcelles below, each ringed by lettered reference scales that key the muscles, tendons and bones. Engraved by Benard for the late eighteenth-century editions of the Encyclopedie, the plate typifies the Enlightenment project of consolidating earlier anatomical illustration into a single compendium.

issues.quote: combining a flayed hand after Bernhard Siegfried Albinus with a foot after De Courcelles
issues.problem: The plate carries four figures - two hands and two feet - not one of each.
issues.evidence: image - figures are numbered Fig. 1 to Fig. 4 with the two hands above and the two feet below

proposals.imageObservation: An engraved anatomical sheet lettered 'Pl. VI' with four numbered figures - two dissected hands (Figs 1 and 2) above, two dissected feet (Figs 3 and 4) below - each surrounded by lettered reference scales and fine leader lines, captioned 'Anatomie.' with 'Benard Fecit' at lower right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The singular phrasing follows the Wellcome title verbatim, so this is a low-stakes precision fix rather than a hallucination. Note a source conflict on the engraver's forename: the Wellcome keywords name Robert Benard, while the Commons category reads 'Engravings by Jacques Renaud Benard' - my replacement leaves the forename out for that reason. Attribution to the Encyclopedie is supported by the Commons category 'Images extracted from Encyclopedie' and the Diderot/d'Alembert keywords.

proposals.title: The muscles of the human body
proposals.currentDescription: The muscles of the human body, fourth layer, seen from the front. Colour mezzotint by A. E.
proposals.proposedDescription: A standing écorché figure seen from the front, stripped to the fourth muscle layer: the skeleton is largely bared while deep red muscle remains on the chest, pelvis, thighs and lower legs, the arms held out to either side against a dark green ground. A colour mezzotint of 1773 by Arnauld-Éloi Gautier d'Agoty after his own painting, lettered at lower left 'A. E. G. D. pin. et sculp.'. The sheet comes from the Wellcome Collection.

issues.quote: Colour mezzotint by A. E.
issues.problem: The sentence is a truncated copy of the Commons caption and breaks off mid-name, leaving the printmaker identified only as 'A. E.'. The full attribution is Arnauld-Éloi Gautier d'Agoty, after himself, 1773.
issues.evidence: commons — imageDescription: 'Colour mezzotint by A. E. Gautier d'Agoty after himself, 1773'; categories include 'Arnauld-Éloi Gautier-Dagoty'

issues.quote: The muscles of the human body, fourth layer, seen from the front.
issues.problem: The description is catalogue boilerplate lifted from the file title; it never says what the plate actually shows.
issues.evidence: house style

metadataIssues.evidence: commons — imageDescription and category 'Arnauld-Éloi Gautier-Dagoty'; the plate is lettered 'A. E. G. D. pin. et sculp.'

proposals.imageObservation: A standing écorché figure seen from the front against a dark green-grey ground: the skeleton is largely exposed, with deep red muscle remaining on the chest, pelvis, thighs and lower legs, arms held out to either side. Lettered at lower left 'A. E. G. D. pin. et sculp.' and with a plate number at upper left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: No fabrication here — the existing text is simply a truncated Commons caption. The medium (colour mezzotint) comes from Commons, not from my reading of the reproduction. The lettering at lower left is small in the render; I read it as 'A. E. G. D. pin. et sculp. Cum. Pri. R.' which matches the attribution, but a human should not quote it verbatim without checking the original at higher resolution.

proposals.title: The river
proposals.currentDescription: A male nude seated by water, the figure modelled in warm flesh tones against a loosely brushed bank. Dated 1885, the period when Renoir tightened his contours under the influence of Ingres and Raphael. The study is attributed to Renoir and reproduced from a monograph on the painter.
proposals.proposedDescription: A bearded male nude reclines full length along a bank in the pose of a river god, his raised hand at the mouth of a vessel from which water falls in a white cascade, the setting brushed in loosely around him. Dated 1885, the period when Renoir tightened his contours under the influence of Ingres and Raphael. The study is attributed to Renoir and reproduced from a monograph on the painter.

issues.quote: A male nude seated by water
issues.problem: The figure is not seated: he reclines full length across the whole width of the canvas, in the pose of a river god tipping water from an urn — the detail that gives the picture its title.
issues.evidence: image — zoomed crop shows the vessel's mouth and the cascade under his raised hand

proposals.imageObservation: A long horizontal canvas: a bearded, white-haired male nude reclines full length along a bank, seen from behind, his raised arm at the mouth of a vessel from which a white fall of water pours into the stream at the left; foliage is brushed in loosely behind him.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The Commons imageDescription only says 'Male nude painted by Renoir' and the credit is the vague 'Renoir, book.', so the existing hedge about attribution and source is appropriate and is kept. 1885 sits inside Renoir's Ingresque period, so that sentence stands.

proposals.title: The Virgin with Chancellor Rolin by Jan van Eyck
proposals.currentDescription: A masterwork of Flemish painting depicting the Virgin Mary and Christ Child in a sacra conversazione composition with a kneeling chancellor. This iconic work showcases Jan van Eyck's revolutionary oil painting technique and meticulous attention to luminous detail, set within an elaborate interior and landscape vista that exemplifies Northern Renaissance realism.
proposals.proposedDescription: Chancellor Nicolas Rolin kneels at his open prayer book on the left while the Virgin, in a heavy red mantle, holds the Christ Child and an angel lowers a crown over her head. Behind them a loggia of three arches opens onto a river town, a bridge and distant mountains, the whole set on a patterned tile floor. Jan van Eyck painted the panel in oil around 1435; Rolin was chancellor to Philip the Good of Burgundy. It is in the Louvre, Paris.

issues.quote: in a sacra conversazione composition
issues.problem: This is a donor portrait (Virgin and Child with a kneeling donor and a crowning angel), not a sacra conversazione, which by definition groups saints around the Virgin in a shared space. No saints are present.
issues.evidence: image - the only figures are Rolin, the Virgin, the Child and one angel; no attendant saints.

issues.quote: This iconic work showcases Jan van Eyck's revolutionary oil painting technique
issues.problem: Hype plus the old claim that van Eyck's oil technique was revolutionary/invented by him; he refined an existing medium.
issues.evidence: knowledge - van Eyck perfected rather than invented oil painting; 'iconic'/'showcases' is boilerplate.

issues.quote: A masterwork of Flemish painting
issues.problem: Empty superlative opening; house style asks the first sentence to say what is in the frame.
issues.evidence: corpus house style.

proposals.imageObservation: Oil panel: Chancellor Rolin kneels at left before an open book on a cushion, hands joined; the Virgin in a heavy red mantle sits at right holding the nude Christ Child while a winged angel lowers a jewelled crown over her head; behind them a three-arched loggia opens onto a river town, bridge and distant mountains; patterned tiled floor.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Everything factual in the original holds except the composition label. Louvre attribution comes from the Commons file title and object key, not from a provenance record, so drop that sentence if the ledger wants collection claims sourced.

proposals.title: In the Alatau Mountains
proposals.currentDescription: A view across the Alatau range of the Tien Shan, painted during Vereshchagin's Central Asian travels. The canvas belongs to the Turkestan group of works the artist produced from sketches made on his journeys of 1869 to 1870 through what is now eastern Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan.
proposals.proposedDescription: An antlered stag stands in a high flowering meadow, white and pink blossom around its legs and a bird of prey circling above, with the hazy ridges of the Alatau receding behind. The canvas belongs to the Turkestan group of works Vereshchagin produced from sketches made on his Central Asian journeys of 1869 to 1870. It is in the Tretyakov Gallery.

issues.quote: A view across the Alatau range of the Tien Shan
issues.problem: The picture is not a mountain view: its subject is a stag standing in a flowering meadow, with the mountains reduced to a hazy backdrop. The record's own englishTitle says so - 'In the Alatau Mountains (deer in meadow)' - yet the description never mentions the animal at all.
issues.evidence: image - the stag is the only focal element; catalogue record englishTitle

issues.quote: of the Tien Shan
issues.problem: Neither the record nor Commons says which Alatau this is. The Zailiysky Alatau belongs to the Tien Shan, but the Dzungarian Alatau does not, so the range assignment is a guess.
issues.evidence: catalogue record - no location field beyond 'Alatau'; Commons category is simply 'Alatau'

proposals.imageObservation: A vertical canvas: an antlered stag stands in a flowering alpine meadow of white and pink blossom and dry grass, occupying the middle of the composition; hazy blue-green ridges recede behind and a bird of prey circles in the pale sky.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The contextual second sentence is sound - Commons dates the work 'between 1869 and 1870' and categorises it under 'Turkestan series by Vasily Vereshchagin', and the record's provenance gives the Tretyakov Gallery. My replacement keeps that and only adds the missing subject. I dropped the 'Tien Shan' and the 'eastern Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan' gloss because neither is sourced anywhere in the record; if a later agent can establish which Alatau range this is, it can go back in.

proposals.title: Валентин Александрович Серов - Одиссей и Навсикая
proposals.currentDescription: A gouache painting by Russian master Valentin Serov depicting the classical moment when Odysseus encounters the princess Nausicaa. Created in 1910 and held in the Tretyakov Gallery, this work captures a pivotal encounter from Homer's Odyssey with characteristic elegance and restraint.
proposals.proposedDescription: A mule-drawn cart moves along the wet sand at the water's edge, Nausicaa standing to drive it and her attendants following on foot, while Odysseus stands alone at the right of the shore. Serov painted the scene in 1910 in gouache, thinly and broadly, with the pale sky taking up most of the sheet. It is in the Tretyakov Gallery, Moscow.

issues.quote: depicting the classical moment when Odysseus encounters the princess Nausicaa
issues.problem: The description never says what is actually in the frame — the shore, the mule cart, Nausicaa driving, the attendants, the solitary figure of Odysseus. It names the subject and then stops, against house style.
issues.evidence: image.

issues.quote: with characteristic elegance and restraint
issues.problem: Empty evaluative filler; asserts a quality without describing anything.
issues.evidence: catalogue record — nothing supports or needs this phrase.

issues.quote: Russian master
issues.problem: Boilerplate honorific of the kind the house style avoids.
issues.evidence: n/a — style.

proposals.imageObservation: A long horizontal beach scene in pale greys, ochres and white: a mule-drawn cart driven by a standing woman moves left to right along the wet sand at the water's edge, followed by a group of attendants, while a lone robed figure stands apart at the right; a wide cloudy sky fills the upper two-thirds and the paint is thin and broadly brushed.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Nothing here is factually wrong: gouache, 1910 and the Tretyakov are all supported by the Commons record (categories 'Gouache paintings in the Tretyakov Gallery', credit 'Tretyakovskaya galereya'). The verdict is minor purely because of the overreaching adjectives and the total absence of visual content, which the rubric treats as a detail-level fault. Serov made more than one version of this subject in 1910; I kept the replacement to what this sheet shows.

proposals.title: Various objects
proposals.currentDescription: Letters, an engraving and a sprig of pansies arranged against a wood surface in a trompe l'oeil of pinned papers. Oil on canvas, 72.4 by 60.3 cm, at the Clark Art Institute, among Boilly's earliest illusionistic still lifes. Several of the letters are addressed to a Monsieur and Madame Dandré, and the pensées (French for both pansies and thoughts) suggest a dedication.
proposals.proposedDescription: Letters bundled under a taut cord, a hanging purse, a glass flask, scissors, a folding knife, a pair of dividers, a pinned sheet with a genre scene of a man drinking, and a sprig of pansies, all painted in trompe l'oeil against a plain dark ground. Oil on canvas, 72.4 by 60.3 cm, at the Clark Art Institute, among Boilly's earliest illusionistic still lifes. Several of the letters are addressed to a Monsieur and Madame Dandre, and the pensees (French for both pansies and thoughts) suggest a dedication.

issues.quote: in a trompe l'oeil of pinned papers
issues.problem: Only the small genre sheet at upper right is pinned; the letters are tied under a cord, and the picture's other illusionistic objects (purse, flask, scissors, folding knife, dividers) are not papers at all.
issues.evidence: image | letters are bound by a taut cord, objects hang from nails/loops

issues.quote: against a wood surface
issues.problem: The ground reads as a flat dark brown plane; whether it is a wooden board or a wall cannot be settled from the reproduction, and the Commons record does not say.
issues.evidence: image | no visible grain, join or board edge; commons | imageDescription gives only medium, size and collection

proposals.imageObservation: Trompe l'oeil against a flat dark brown ground: a bundle of letters tied with cord along the bottom (one with a red wax seal, several with written addresses), a sprig of white/pale flowers at lower right, a hanging drawstring purse, a glass flask of green liquid on a cord, scissors, a folding knife, a pair of dividers, a small pinned sheet at upper right showing a genre scene of a man drinking, and a small card at upper left inscribed with the artist's name.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Medium, dimensions and collection match the Commons imageDescription verbatim. The Dandre letters and the pansies/pensees dedication are corroborated by the Clark's own catalogue text (surfaced via search; clarkart.edu returns 403 to direct fetch). The only defects are the object list, which omits the most conspicuous items, and 'pinned papers'/'wood surface'. Note the proposed text drops the accents in Dandre/pensees only because of encoding here - restore them when applying.

proposals.title: Venice - The Dogana and San Giorgio Maggiore by Joseph Mallord William Turner
proposals.currentDescription: A masterwork by the English Romantic painter J. M. W.
proposals.proposedDescription: Gondolas and moored sailing boats crowd the pale water at the entrance to the Grand Canal, with the domed church and campanile of San Giorgio Maggiore across the basin and the corner of the Dogana closing the right edge. Turner painted the view in 1834, dissolving buildings, rigging and reflections into a high-keyed haze of blue, white and warm ochre. The canvas is in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.

issues.quote: A masterwork by the English Romantic painter J. M. W.
