issues.problem: The entire description is a truncated fragment that breaks off mid-name, and what it does say is an empty value judgement ('masterwork') with no visual or factual content.
issues.evidence: catalogue record — the description field ends after 'J. M. W.' with no verb and no object.

proposals.imageObservation: A luminous Venetian view: gondolas and moored sailing boats crowd the pale water at the mouth of the Grand Canal, the domed church and campanile of San Giorgio Maggiore stand across the basin at centre right, and the corner of the Dogana with its figure-topped tower closes the right edge under a blue and white sky.
proposals.reviewerNotes: No claim here is false — the text simply stops mid-sentence, so I treated the truncation plus the hype adjective as minor rather than accurate. The National Gallery of Art attribution is grounded in the Commons credit ('donated to Wikimedia Commons as part of a project by the National Gallery of Art', file name 'NGA 1224') and the 'Images from the National Gallery of Art' category, not from outside knowledge.

proposals.title: Heroes
proposals.currentDescription: The three bogatyrs Dobrynya Nikitich, Ilya Muromets and Alyosha Popovich sit mounted at the edge of the steppe, scanning the horizon for enemies. Vasnetsov worked on the nearly 3 by 4 metre canvas for almost twenty years, finishing it in 1898 in the rebuilt barn-studio Savva Mamontov had given him at Abramtsevo; Pavel Tretyakov bought it for his gallery as soon as it was done.
proposals.proposedDescription: The three bogatyrs Dobrynya Nikitich, Ilya Muromets and Alyosha Popovich sit mounted at the edge of the steppe, scanning the horizon for enemies. Vasnetsov worked on the canvas — roughly 3 by 4.5 metres — for close to twenty years, from 1881 to its completion in 1898; Savva Mamontov had rebuilt a barn at Abramtsevo into a top-lit studio so that a picture that size could be painted at all. Pavel Tretyakov bought it for his gallery in 1898, among the last acquisitions he made.

issues.quote: finishing it in 1898 in the rebuilt barn-studio Savva Mamontov had given him at Abramtsevo
issues.problem: Mamontov's conversion of a barn at Abramtsevo into a top-lit studio is real, but it dates from 1881, when Vasnetsov resumed the canvas — no source places the 1898 completion in that building, and Vasnetsov had his own large Moscow studio by then. The sentence welds a documented fact to an undocumented location.
issues.evidence: web:https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/Богатыри_(картина_Васнецова) — Mamontov rebuilt the barn by the 'Yashkin house' into a studio when work resumed in 1881; the article dates completion to 27 April 1898 but does not say where

issues.quote: the nearly 3 by 4 metre canvas
issues.problem: The canvas is 295.3 x 446 cm — nearly 3 by 4.5 metres. The width is understated by half a metre.
issues.evidence: web:https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/Богатыри_(картина_Васнецова) — 295.3 x 446 cm; the same article describes it as 'три на четыре с половиной метра'

metadataIssues.evidence: commons — 'from 1881 until 1898'; the description itself says the picture was finished in 1898, which sits oddly against a catalogue year of 1881

proposals.imageObservation: Three armoured horsemen abreast on open grassland under a heavy sky: a bearded rider on a white horse at the left with a lance, a broad rider on a black horse at the centre shading his eyes to scan the distance, and a younger rider on a chestnut with a bow at the right; small fir saplings in the foreground, low hills behind.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The identification and order of the three riders is correct and matches the canonical reading. Tretyakov's 1898 purchase is confirmed. I moved the barn-studio to 1881, where it is documented, rather than deleting it; if a source can be found placing the 1898 completion at Abramtsevo the original wording could stand.

proposals.title: Inside the Tent of a Rich Kirghiz
proposals.currentDescription: The interior of a wealthy Kyrgyz yurt, its felt walls hung with patterned textiles and the floor spread with carpets. One of Vereshchagin's ethnographic studies from his Central Asian travels of 1869 to 1870, later worked up as part of the Turkestan series.
proposals.proposedDescription: The interior of a wealthy Kyrgyz yurt: a seated figure in a white turban sits on the carpeted floor with a small child beside him, beneath a painted dome hung with red tassels, the lattice wall behind and carved chests with folded bedding stacked along one side. One of Vereshchagin's ethnographic studies from his Central Asian travels of 1869 to 1870, later worked up as part of the Turkestan series.

issues.quote: its felt walls hung with patterned textiles
issues.problem: The walls shown are the yurt's wooden lattice frame and painted ribs, not felt hung with textiles. The pattern in the picture is painted decoration on the dome and carving on the chests.
issues.evidence: image

issues.quote: The interior of a wealthy Kyrgyz yurt
issues.problem: The two occupants - a seated turbaned figure and a child, the only figures in the picture - are not mentioned.
issues.evidence: image

proposals.imageObservation: The inside of a yurt: a painted, ribbed dome with red tassels above a diagonal wooden lattice wall, carved and painted chests with folded bedding stacked at right, patterned carpets on the floor, and at left a seated figure in a white turban and patterned robe with a small child beside him; a strip of bright daylight shows through the door at far left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The second sentence is kept verbatim and is supported by the Commons date ('between 1869 and 1870') and the 'Turkestan series by Vasily Vereshchagin' category. Only the wall detail and the missing figures drive the downgrade.

proposals.title: Watts marie fox
proposals.currentDescription: Portrait of Mary Fox (1850-1878) (later Princess Marie of Liechtenstein), adopted daughter of Henry Fox, 4th Baron Holland (1802-1859), of Holland House, Kensington, with her Spanish pointer Elia . In her history of Holland House (Liechtenstein, Princess Marie, Holland House, 2 Vols. , London, 1874, p.
proposals.proposedDescription: Mary Fox (1850-1878), later Princess Marie of Liechtenstein, stands on a grassy slope in a white dress with a coral sash and a frilled bonnet, one hand at her side, beside her Spanish pointer Elia, who is as tall as she is. She was the adopted daughter of Henry Fox, 4th Baron Holland, of Holland House, Kensington. Watts painted her about 1854; in her 1874 history of Holland House she remembered Elia as a faithful friend and a wise protector.

issues.quote: In her history of Holland House
issues.problem: The description is the Commons metadata pasted verbatim and it breaks off mid-citation at 'London, 1874, p.' — the sentence never completes and the quotation it was leading to is missing.
issues.evidence: catalogue record — the description string ends with 'p.' and no page number or quotation

issues.quote: Portrait of Mary Fox (1850-1878) (later Princess Marie of Liechtenstein), adopted daughter of Henry Fox, 4th Baron Holland (1802-1859), of Holland House, Kensington, with her Spanish pointer Elia .
issues.problem: Identification only; nothing about what the picture shows (the child's white dress and coral sash, the dog's size beside her, the landscape setting).
issues.evidence: image

proposals.imageObservation: A small girl in a white dress with a coral-orange sash, a frilled bonnet trimmed in orange and coral shoes stands on a grassy slope beside a large brown-and-white pointer that is as tall as she is; trees and a warm sky behind. A printed caption at the upper left reads 'Miss Mary Fox, with Spanish Pointer.'
proposals.reviewerNotes: No fabrication here — every fact in the existing text matches the Commons record — but the text is a truncated metadata paste, which is why I graded it minor rather than accurate. The 'faithful friend and a wise protector' phrase is Princess Marie's own, quoted in the Commons imageDescription, so it is grounded; drop it if the project prefers no quotation. Commons also records the original canvas as 44 x 34 inches, which could be added if wanted (the record's realDimensions is empty).

proposals.title: Windows Open Simultaneously
proposals.currentDescription: A small 1912 oil in which the Eiffel Tower dissolves into a grid of translucent green, pink and ochre prisms, identifiable only by its tapering silhouette. Acquired by the Tate and measuring 45.7 by 37.5 cm, the panel belongs to Delaunay's Simultaneous Windows cycle, the founding works of Orphism.
proposals.proposedDescription: A small 1912 oil in which the Eiffel Tower dissolves into a grid of translucent green, violet, ochre and magenta prisms, identifiable only by its tapering silhouette. The canvas measures 45.7 by 37.5 cm and is in the Tate; it belongs to Delaunay's Simultaneous Windows cycle, the founding works of Orphism.

issues.quote: the panel belongs to Delaunay's Simultaneous Windows cycle
issues.problem: Calling it a panel implies a wood support. The source says oil on canvas.
issues.evidence: commons - imageDescription: 'Robert Delaunay, 1912, Windows Open Simultaneously (First Part, Third Motif) oil on canvas, 45.7 x 37.5 cm, Tate Modern'; the record's Commons categories also include '1912 oil on canvas paintings in the United Kingdom'

issues.quote: translucent green, pink and ochre prisms
issues.problem: The most prominent colour block in the picture is deep violet-blue, which the list omits, and the reds read as crimson-magenta rather than pink.
issues.evidence: image - a large violet plane occupies the upper centre and violet recurs down the left side

proposals.imageObservation: An upright grid of overlapping translucent colour planes - deep violet and blue, yellow-ochre, several greens, crimson-magenta and cream - with a tapering green triangular form rising through the centre that reads as the Eiffel Tower. An inscription and signature in blue run across the lower right corner.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Spot-check of an earlier 'accurate' verdict, which I am downgrading on the support. Date, dimensions and collection are all a verbatim match to the Commons caption, so only 'panel' and the colour list needed changing; the rest is preserved word for word. The Orphism claim is standard - Apollinaire coined the term in connection with the Windows series.

proposals.title: Winners
proposals.currentDescription: Drawn from Vereshchagin's Balkan series, the painting confronts the aftermath of battle: victorious soldiers in red-trimmed coats move among the fallen on a grey, open field. The Russian realist refused to glamorise war, building documentary detail into a deliberately disquieting scene of defeat and death. Painted between 1878 and 1879, the large canvas exemplifies Vereshchagin's unflinching engagement with the human cost of conflict.
proposals.proposedDescription: Drawn from Vereshchagin's Balkan series, the painting confronts the aftermath of battle: soldiers in red fezzes stand and stoop among stripped Russian dead scattered across a field of dry yellow grass, one of them pulling on a dead officer's blue tunic. The Russian realist refused to glamorise war, building documentary detail into a deliberately disquieting scene of defeat and death. Painted between 1878 and 1879, the large canvas exemplifies Vereshchagin's unflinching engagement with the human cost of conflict.

issues.quote: on a grey, open field
issues.problem: The field is dry golden-brown stubble under a bright sky, not grey.
issues.evidence: image — the whole ground plane is ochre/yellow

issues.quote: victorious soldiers in red-trimmed coats
issues.problem: What is red is their headgear — fezzes. The coats are tan, blue and grey; one figure is pulling on a captured dark blue Russian tunic.
issues.evidence: image — every standing figure wears a red fez; no red-trimmed coats are visible

issues.quote: move among the fallen
issues.problem: Understates the subject: the victors are stripping and looting the dead, which is why the Russian title carries the parenthesis Мародёры (Marauders).
issues.evidence: commons — object name label QS:Lru "Победители (Мародёры)"; image shows bodies in undergarments and a soldier donning a Russian tunic

proposals.imageObservation: A wide sunlit field of dry yellow-brown grass strewn with dead and stripped bodies in white undergarments. A knot of soldiers in red fezzes stands at the centre — one pulling on a dark blue Russian officer's tunic, another stooping over a corpse — with more fez-wearing figures scattered back to the ridge line, where a crowd continues the looting. One man kneels in the right foreground beside a body.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The subject identification (Ottoman troops looting Russian dead, tied to the Battle of Telish by the Commons categories "Ottoman Army" and "Battle of Telish", and to the Russian alternate title Мародёры) is well supported, so naming the fezzes is safe. Dates and the Balkan series match the Commons record; the canvas size in the record (301 × 180 cm) supports "large". Verdict kept at minor because the scene, series and dates are right and only the colour details are contradicted.

proposals.title: Water Lilies p
proposals.currentDescription: Claude Monet (French, 1840–1926) Water Lilies, 1919 Oil on canvas; 39 3/4 x 78 3/4 in. (101 x 200 cm) The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York, The Walter H. and Leonore Annenberg Collection, Gift of Walter H.
proposals.proposedDescription: Water lilies spread across the pond in clusters of pale pads and pink blooms, with willow foliage reflected down the middle of the water and no bank or horizon to orient the viewer. Oil on canvas, 101 by 200 cm, painted in 1919; it is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York, from the Walter H. and Leonore Annenberg Collection (1998.325.2).

issues.quote: Claude Monet (French, 1840–1926) Water Lilies, 1919 Oil on canvas; 39 3/4 x 78 3/4 in. (101 x 200 cm) The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York, The Walter H. and Leonore Annenberg Collection, Gift of Walter H.
issues.problem: Raw museum tombstone label scraped from Commons, truncated mid-donor-name. No description of the painting.
issues.evidence: commons - identical to the file's imageDescription label block

proposals.imageObservation: A wide horizontal canvas of a lily pond seen from above with no bank or horizon: clusters of yellow-green pads and pink blooms at the left and right, a broad violet-and-blue reflection down the centre, and dark green willow strokes at the top right. Signed and dated at lower left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Facts in the replacement are all from the record and the Commons label. Dimensions in the record (200 x 101 cm) match the label. Note the Commons 'date' field is the photograph's date (February 2009), not the painting's - the 1919 date comes from the label and Wikidata.

proposals.title: 冨嶽三十六景 東海道吉田-Yoshida on the Tōkaidō
proposals.currentDescription: A woodblock print from Katsushika Hokusai's celebrated series Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji (Fugaku sanjūrokkei). This print depicts Yoshida station on the Tōkaidō road, a major trade route in Edo-period Japan. The work exemplifies Hokusai's mastery of perspective and landscape composition, featuring bold lines and the characteristic blue pigments he favored during this period.
proposals.proposedDescription: Travellers rest inside a roadside teahouse at Yoshida station on the Tōkaidō, one of them turning to look out at the small snow-capped cone of Mount Fuji across the plain while a serving woman crosses the matted floor; the hanging signboard advertises the Fuji view. A colour woodblock print from Katsushika Hokusai's Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji (Fugaku sanjūrokkei), made about 1830 to 1832 and printed largely in the Prussian blue that gives the series its palette. This impression is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art.

issues.quote: The work exemplifies Hokusai's mastery of perspective and landscape composition
issues.problem: The sheet is a figure-filled interior genre scene — a teahouse with seven or eight travellers — in which Fuji appears as a small distant motif. Describing it as an exercise in landscape composition mischaracterises what is in the frame.
issues.evidence: image — teahouse interior with figures occupies nearly the whole sheet; Fuji is a small cone glimpsed at the left

issues.quote: This print depicts Yoshida station on the Tōkaidō road
issues.problem: The description never says what is actually shown (the teahouse interior, the travellers, the tiny Fuji); it names the station and then moves to generic praise.
issues.evidence: image vs description

issues.quote: mastery of perspective
issues.problem: Empty praise of the kind house style avoids.
issues.evidence: house style

proposals.imageObservation: Colour woodblock print of the interior of a roadside teahouse: travellers rest on the matted platform, one turning to look out through the open front at a small snow-capped Mount Fuji across the plain, while a serving woman stands at the centre and porters sit at the right; a hanging signboard reads Fujimi chaya, title and signature cartouches at the upper left, the whole dominated by blue.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Series, subject and the blue-pigment remark were all correct; the problem is that the text never describes the picture and frames a genre interior as landscape. The Met attribution comes from the Commons credit line (donated by the Metropolitan Museum) and the category 'Japanese prints in the Metropolitan Museum of Art'. The signboard reads 不二見茶屋 (Fujimi chaya) in the image; I phrased it as 'advertises the Fuji view' rather than transliterating, in case of a reading error.

proposals.title: Haeckel Nudibranchia
proposals.currentDescription: Sea slugs of multiple aeolid and dorid lineages, including the orange-tipped Facelina auriculata and the spotted Tritonia hombergii. Cerata, rhinophores and branchial plumes are rendered in colour to record pigmentation that fades from preserved specimens.
proposals.proposedDescription: Sea slugs of multiple aeolid and dorid lineages, including Facelina auriculata, whose crimson cerata are tipped with white, and the mottled Tritonia hombergii. Cerata, rhinophores and branchial plumes are rendered in colour to record pigmentation that fades from preserved specimens.

issues.quote: the orange-tipped Facelina auriculata
issues.problem: The Facelina (figure 2 in the plate's key order) has crimson cerata tipped with white, not orange tips. The orange-yellow animal on the plate is a different figure.
issues.evidence: image — enlarged crop of figure 2 shows deep red cerata with clean white tips; commons imageDescription lists 'Aeolis coronata (Forbes) = Facelina auriculata coronata' as the second entry

proposals.imageObservation: Seven numbered sea slugs on a white ground, in colour: a pink branched-ceratal one at upper left, a crimson one with white-tipped cerata at upper right, a large brown-and-cream branched Dendronotus in the centre, an orange-yellow one at left, a pale one with stalked club-shaped appendages at right, a mottled orange animal with white branched gills at lower left, and a grey-green one with yellow gills at lower right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Both species named are in the Commons key for plate 43, so the identifications hold; only the colour of the Facelina's cerata is corrected. Note that the plate mixes in a sacoglossan (Hermaea bifida) and several dendronotids alongside the aeolids and dorids, so 'multiple aeolid and dorid lineages' is an incomplete but not false characterisation — I left it. The claim about pigment fading in preserved specimens is interpretive but standard for this kind of plate.

proposals.title: Allium Bisulcum
proposals.currentDescription: Allium bisulcum, an onion named for its half-cylindrical leaves grooved on both faces, bearing a full spherical umbel of pale-violet bell-shaped flowers. A botanist supplied the descriptive text that accompanied Redoute's plate in Les Liliacees.
proposals.proposedDescription: Allium bisulcum, an onion named for its half-cylindrical leaves grooved on both faces, its slender scape carrying a loose nodding cluster of small pinkish-mauve bell-shaped flowers, with a second head still closed in its drooping spathe and the papery bulb drawn at the base. A botanist supplied the descriptive text that accompanied Redoute's plate in Les Liliacees.

issues.quote: a full spherical umbel of pale-violet bell-shaped flowers
issues.problem: The umbel in the plate is not spherical and not full: the flowers hang loosely and nod to one side on slender unequal stalks, which is the plate's most distinctive feature. A second, still-sheathed head droops on a bent scape beside it.
issues.evidence: image — loose, pendulous, one-sided umbel; no globe of flowers anywhere on the sheet

proposals.imageObservation: A whole allium plant with its papery, purple-tinged bulb and roots at the base, long narrow linear leaves, and at the top a loose, nodding, one-sided cluster of small pinkish-mauve bell-shaped flowers on fine stalks; a second flower head still closed in its spathe droops on a bent stem beside it.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Carried a prior 'accurate' verdict which I think was wrong on the flower head. The etymology (bisulcum, 'two-grooved') and the unattributed 'a botanist supplied the text' are both safe and preserved; c82.net could not be fetched, so I did not try to name the author of the text.

proposals.title: Allium Triquetrum
proposals.currentDescription: Allium triquetrum, the three-cornered leek, its sharply triangular scape carrying a loose umbel of large white bells, each segment marked with a green midrib. The bulb sits in reddish coats, the leaves keeled like a sedge. Redoute drew it for the sixth volume of Les Liliacees (1811).
proposals.proposedDescription: Allium triquetrum, the three-cornered leek, its sharply triangular scape carrying a loose umbel of large white bells, each segment marked with a green midrib. The plate shows the whole plant lifted, its pale bulb and fibrous roots intact and the leaves keeled like a sedge. Redoute drew it for the sixth volume of Les Liliacees (1811).

issues.quote: The bulb sits in reddish coats
issues.problem: The bulb as drawn is white to pale greenish, with no reddish tunics anywhere.
issues.evidence: image | enlarged crop of the bulb shows uniformly white-cream tunics shading to pale green at the neck

proposals.imageObservation: A whole plant lifted with its roots: a white, faintly green-tinged bulb with a fan of fibrous roots, keeled strap leaves, and two three-angled scapes carrying umbels of white bell-shaped flowers, each tepal striped green; two small dissected flower parts are drawn at the lower left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Everything else matches, including the green-striped tepals and the keeled leaves, and the sixth volume of Les Liliacees is consistent with the record's 1811. I could not read the plate's own text (c82.net is blocked), so it is possible Redoute's description mentions reddish tunics; the drawing does not show them, which is what the audit turns on.

proposals.title: Amaryllis Formosissima
proposals.currentDescription: Amaryllis formosissima, the Jacobean lily, its large nodding scarlet flower split so deeply that the three upreared and three drooping segments suggest two lips. The hollow reddish scape rises beside oblong two-ranked leaves. Plate 5 opened the first volume of Les Liliacees (1802).
proposals.proposedDescription: Amaryllis formosissima, the Jacobean lily, its large nodding scarlet flower split so deeply that the three upreared and three drooping segments suggest two lips. The hollow reddish scape rises beside long two-ranked leaves. Plate 5 appeared in the first volume of Les Liliacees (1802).

issues.quote: Plate 5 opened the first volume of Les Liliacees (1802).
issues.problem: Plate 5 cannot have opened a volume — plate 1 does. The sensible claim is that plate 5 appeared in the first volume.
issues.evidence: catalogue record — source file is lilies-005, i.e. the fifth plate of the set; the volume date 1802 matches the record's year

issues.quote: oblong two-ranked leaves
issues.problem: The leaves in the plate are long, narrow and strap-shaped, not oblong; 'two-ranked' is right.
issues.evidence: image

proposals.imageObservation: A deep crimson Sprekelia-type flower fully open with one segment reared up, two spreading and three drooping, the stamens and style curving down and out; a second bloom stands behind on a stout stem, with long strap leaves and a brown tunicked bulb at the base, and a monochrome dissection of style and stamens at the right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Both fixes are small and wording-level; the botany of the description (the bilabiate arrangement of Sprekelia's six segments) is right and matches the plate. I have left 'hollow reddish scape' alone — the scape in the reproduction reads greyish-purple, but hollowness and true colour are not judgeable from a restored scan.

proposals.title: Iris Xyphioides
proposals.currentDescription: Plate 212 shows Iris xyphioides, an ovoid bulb sending up a stem to four or six decimetres with two large blue flowers tinged violet, some specimens speckled with darker spots. Redoute was flower painter to Empress Josephine; this plate belongs to the fourth volume of Les Liliacees, 1807.
proposals.proposedDescription: Plate 212 shows Iris xyphioides, an ovoid bulb - drawn separately at the lower right - sending up a stem to four or six decimetres carrying large blue flowers tinged violet, some specimens speckled with darker spots. Redoute was flower painter to Empress Josephine; this plate belongs to the fourth volume of Les Liliacees, 1807.

issues.quote: with two large blue flowers
issues.problem: The plate shows one open flower, not two. (Two flowers per stem is correct species botany for Iris xiphioides, but the sentence is framed as 'Plate 212 shows...'.)
issues.evidence: image - checked the flower head at 2.2x; a single perianth of three falls and three standards

issues.quote: an ovoid bulb sending up a stem
issues.problem: The plate carries a separate line drawing of the bulb at lower right, which the description does not mention even though it is the only analytical figure on the sheet.
issues.evidence: image

proposals.imageObservation: A single blue iris flower with three spreading falls (white-and-yellow signals, faint darker speckles) and upright standards, on a tall stem with long strap leaves; a separate uncoloured line drawing of an ovoid bulb sits at the lower right of the sheet.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Ledger says accurate; the only real slip is that the plate shows one bloom while the text says two. The speckling the text mentions is genuinely visible on the falls. The plate number, volume and 1807 date come from the (unreachable) c82.net source and could not be independently checked.

proposals.title: Veltheimia Glauca
proposals.currentDescription: Veltheimia glauca, its short ovoid spike of pendent flesh-coloured flowers carried on a scape above glaucous channelled leaves. The plate notes the three-winged seed capsule, each cell holding two seeds. Redoute drew it for the eighth volume of Les Liliacees (1814).
proposals.proposedDescription: Veltheimia glauca, its short ovoid spike of pendent flesh-coloured flowers carried on a scape above a rosette of glaucous, wavy-edged leaves. Two dissection studies at the lower left lay the perianth open to show six stamens and set the pistil beside it. Redoute drew it for the eighth volume of Les Liliacees (1814).

issues.quote: The plate notes the three-winged seed capsule, each cell holding two seeds.
issues.problem: The plate figures no capsule. Its two analytical vignettes show the perianth opened out with its six stamens and, beside it, the pistil - nothing three-winged and no seeds. The claim is true of the genus but is attributed to the plate, which does not show it.
issues.evidence: image - 5x crop of the lower-left vignettes

issues.quote: channelled leaves
issues.problem: The leaves are drawn broad, flat and strongly wavy-margined rather than channelled.
issues.evidence: image

proposals.imageObservation: A bulbous plant with a spreading rosette of broad, blue-green, wavy-margined leaves and a bare brown scape carrying a short dense head of pendent salmon-pink tubular flowers with pale green tips. Two small monochrome dissection studies sit at the lower left: a perianth laid open showing six stamens, and a separate ovary with a long style. No fruit or capsule is drawn.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Spot-check of a prior 'accurate' verdict. The flower spike and the glaucous foliage are right; the capsule sentence is the problem, since it describes something the plate does not contain. If the claim came from Redoute's accompanying text rather than the plate it could be kept with the attribution changed - but the text is unreachable while c82.net is blocked, so I replaced it with what the plate actually figures. I left the volume and date sentence verbatim: it is unverified but not contradicted, and it matches the catalogue year.

proposals.title: Veratrum Nigrum
proposals.currentDescription: Veratrum nigrum, the black hellebore, its metre-high stem bearing pleated leaves and a very long raceme of small flowers, each segment a blackish purple with a bright basal spot. Redoute drew it for the seventh volume of Les Liliacees (1812); the dissection figures show the stamens at the petal base.
proposals.proposedDescription: Veratrum nigrum, the black false hellebore, its metre-high stem bearing pleated leaves and a very long raceme of small flowers, each segment a blackish purple with a bright basal spot. Redoute drew it for the seventh volume of Les Liliacees (1812); the dissection figure shows the stamens at the petal base.

issues.quote: the black hellebore
issues.problem: Veratrum nigrum is the black FALSE hellebore (Melanthiaceae). 'Black hellebore' without qualification is the standard common name of Helleborus niger, an unrelated buttercup-family plant.
issues.evidence: web:https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/18788/veratrum-nigrum/details - RHS common name 'black false hellebore'

issues.quote: the dissection figures show
issues.problem: Only one small dissection figure is visible on the plate, at lower left.
issues.evidence: image

proposals.imageObservation: Broad, strongly pleated (plicate) leaves and tall stems carrying several long racemes of small six-parted flowers in blackish purple with paler centres; one tiny dissected floret at lower left; white ground.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Spot-check of a prior 'accurate'. The volume/date holds: BHL gives tome septieme as 1812-1813, matching the record year. Only the common name and the plural 'figures' changed.

proposals.title: Rosa Alpina
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa alpina in its smooth form, a four- or five-foot shrub with reddish thornless stems and single flowers of five vivid red petals paling toward the claw, set above doubly toothed leaves. The stems are wholly without prickles, a mark of the Alpine roses noted by Thory.
proposals.proposedDescription: Rosa alpina in its smooth form, a shrub with reddish thornless stems and single flowers of five mauve-pink petals paling toward the claw, set above doubly toothed leaves. A round red hip hangs at the lower right of the plate. The stems are wholly without prickles, a mark of the Alpine roses noted by Thory.

issues.quote: five vivid red petals paling toward the claw
issues.problem: The petals in the plate are mauve-pink, not vivid red. The paling toward the base is correct; the hue is not.
issues.evidence: image — both open flowers are a soft pink/mauve; the only red on the sheet is the hip at lower right.

issues.quote: a four- or five-foot shrub
issues.problem: Plant height cannot be read from a plate and is not in the record; likely paraphrased from Thory's accompanying text, which could not be checked because c82.net is behind a bot challenge.
issues.evidence: catalogue record / sourceEvidence — c82.net unreachable; no habit data in the row.

proposals.imageObservation: Two fully open five-petalled roses in clear mauve-pink with yellow stamens and a white-yellow eye, several buds, a smooth reddish stem with no prickles at all, blue-green pinnate leaves, and a single round red hip on a stalk at lower right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The thornless reddish stems are exactly right and are the point of the plate. I corrected the petal colour and added the hip, which is genuinely depicted here (unlike in several other Redoute entries in this batch). I dropped the unverifiable height rather than assert it; restore it if Thory's text is available.

proposals.title: Rosa Arvensis
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa arvensis, the field rose, a trailing shrub with reddish arching branches and fragrant white flowers gathered at the tips of short side-shoots. The plate notes the fused styles forming a slender central column, distinctive to the species.
proposals.proposedDescription: Rosa arvensis, the field rose, a trailing shrub whose long green canes are armed with hooked red prickles and carry fragrant white flowers with yellow stamens at the tips of short side-shoots. A single dark-red hip is drawn separately at the foot of the plate. The species is distinguished from other white roses by its styles, which are fused into a slender central column.

issues.quote: a trailing shrub with reddish arching branches
issues.problem: The canes in the plate are green to grey-green; it is the hooked prickles that are red. Botanical descriptions of the species also give it weak trailing GREEN stems.
issues.evidence: image — green canes with red prickles; web:https://www.naturespot.org/species/field-rose — 'weak trailing green stems ... lined with curved prickles'

issues.quote: The plate notes the fused styles forming a slender central column
issues.problem: The united style column is a genuine diagnostic of Rosa arvensis, but nothing in the reproduction shows it and there is no accessible source text for what this plate 'notes'.
issues.evidence: image — no style column is legible at this resolution; c82.net source text could not be fetched (Cloudflare)

proposals.imageObservation: A botanical plate of a rose with two open white five-petalled flowers and a bud, yellow stamen bosses at their centres, borne at the end of a long arching pale-green cane armed with hooked dark-red prickles; pinnate leaves of five to seven toothed leaflets run down the stem, and a single dark-red hip on its stalk is drawn separately at lower left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Only the stem colour is actually wrong; the fragrance claim is defensible (sources split between 'fragrant' and 'slightly fragrant') and the style-column fact is correct for the species even if the plate cannot be checked. The replacement keeps everything else and only moves the red from the branches to the prickles.

proposals.title: Rosa Candolleana
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa candolleana, the Candolle rose, a graceful four- or five-foot shrub with red-brown stems thick with small prickles, its five white petals banded outside with bright-pink stripes. An ovoid red hip ripens after flowering, shown in this 1821 plate.
proposals.proposedDescription: Rosa candolleana, the Candolle rose, a graceful four- or five-foot shrub with red-brown stems thick with small prickles, its five white petals flushed pale pink on the outside. Pink-red buds nod among the open flowers in this plate of 1821; an ovoid red hip ripens after flowering.

issues.quote: An ovoid red hip ripens after flowering, shown in this 1821 plate.
issues.problem: No ripe hip appears in the plate; the reddish bodies at upper right and left are unopened buds with their sepals, and the receptacles beneath them are green-grey. The ripening may well come from Thory's text, but the sentence claims it is shown.
issues.evidence: image - magnified crops of both reddish elements show buds, not hips.

issues.quote: banded outside with bright-pink stripes
issues.problem: The pink on the petal reverses is a soft pale wash with faint bands, not bright-pink striping.
issues.evidence: image - magnified crop of the reversed flower at right.

proposals.imageObservation: Botanical plate: an open branching rose with white five-petalled flowers, yellow stamens, the petal reverses flushed and softly banded with pale pink; red-brown stems densely set with fine prickles; small serrated leaflets; several pink-red buds. No ripe hip is depicted.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The shrub height comes from Thory's text, which could not be fetched (c82.net is behind Cloudflare), so it is left untouched rather than removed. Only the claim that the hip is shown, and the strength of the pink, were corrected.

proposals.title: Rosa Canina
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa canina, the wild dog rose, with pale-pink single flowers, toothed leaflets, and arching stems set with curved prickles. Redoute drew it for Les Roses, the most famous rose iconography ever made and the record of species roses before the modern hybrid.
proposals.proposedDescription: Rosa canina, the wild dog rose, with pale-pink single flowers, toothed leaflets, and arching stems set with curved prickles. Redoute drew it for Les Roses, the three-volume rose iconography published in Paris between 1817 and 1824 with botanical text by Claude-Antoine Thory.

issues.quote: the most famous rose iconography ever made and the record of species roses before the modern hybrid
issues.problem: Two unsupported assertions in one clause: a bare superlative, and a characterisation of Les Roses as a record of species roses. Les Roses documents mostly garden cultivars and hybrids grown at Malmaison and in Paris nurseries, not a survey of wild species, and hybridised garden roses were already well established when it appeared.
issues.evidence: knowledge — Les Roses (1817-24) is dominated by cultivated gallicas, centifolias, damasks and China hybrids; the catalogue record and the image support neither claim

proposals.imageObservation: A dog rose: a cluster of single five-petalled flowers, near-white flushed pink with yellow stamens, pink buds on a second branch, sharply toothed leaflets and long arching green stems set with hooked reddish prickles.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The visual sentence is exactly right and is preserved verbatim; only the promotional second half is replaced with the publication facts that are actually verifiable. If the project is comfortable with the superlative as received wisdom, this can be downgraded to a no-change.

proposals.title: Rosa Centifolia
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa centifolia bullata, the cabbage rose with puffed, blistered leaflets that swell and curl back on themselves, above a rounded pink double bloom. Thory records it as the lettuce-leaved rose propagated by the nurseryman Dupont.
proposals.proposedDescription: Rosa centifolia bullata, the cabbage rose with puffed, blistered leaflets that swell and curl back on themselves, spread below a rounded pink double bloom and its cluster of buds. Thory records it as the lettuce-leaved rose propagated by the nurseryman Dupont.

issues.quote: above a rounded pink double bloom
issues.problem: Spatial relation reversed: the bullate leaves sit below the bloom in the plate, not above it.
issues.evidence: image - bloom at upper left, leaf mass at bottom

proposals.imageObservation: One open pink double rose at upper left with five buds, above a mass of very large puckered, blistered leaves that dominate the lower two-thirds of the sheet; prickly stems, white ground.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The Dupont/lettuce-leaved claim checks out (RHS lists R. x centifolia 'Bullata' as the lettuce-leaved rose; helpmefind/Dave's Garden give Dupont, 1809 as the introducer), so only the 'above' was changed.

proposals.title: Rosa Centifolia
proposals.currentDescription: A single-flowered cabbage rose, Rosa centifolia flore simplici, showing five pink petals around a boss of stamens rather than the usual full double bloom. Claude-Antoine Thory supplied the botanical text for the plate.
proposals.proposedDescription: A single-flowered cabbage rose, Rosa centifolia flore simplici, its one spread of broad pink petals opening around a boss of golden stamens rather than closing into the usual full double bloom. Claude-Antoine Thory supplied the botanical text for the plate.

issues.quote: showing five pink petals
issues.problem: The open bloom carries about eight broad petals in a single spread, not five. The contrast the sentence draws (single rather than full double) is right; the count is not.
issues.evidence: image — enlarged crop of the flower shows roughly eight overlapping petals around the stamen boss

proposals.imageObservation: One fully open pink rose seen face-on with a dense boss of golden stamens at its centre, plus three buds, on a prickly stem with large toothed leaflets; white ground, stipple-engraved botanical plate.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Thory as author of the text for Les Roses is standard and uncontested. Only the petal count is changed.

proposals.title: Rosa Cinnamomea
proposals.currentDescription: The cinnamon rose, Rosa cinnamomea, with scented red-tinged single flowers gathered in a corymb above seven-leaflet leaves and smooth flowering shoots. Thory records that it flowers in May and grows wild across southern Europe.
proposals.proposedDescription: The cinnamon rose, Rosa cinnamomea, with red-tinged single flowers and yellow stamens carried a few together above five- to seven-leaflet leaves; the main cane bears paired prickles while the flowering shoots are smooth. The plate comes from Redoute's Les Roses, with botanical text by Claude-Antoine Thory.

issues.quote: grows wild across southern Europe
issues.problem: Rosa cinnamomea (R. majalis) is a northern and central European to Siberian species, not a southern European one. Neither the image nor the record supports the range claim, and the source page could not be fetched to check whether Thory says this.
issues.evidence: knowledge - R. cinnamomea/majalis range is N and C Europe to Siberia; c82.net source unavailable

issues.quote: Thory records that it flowers in May
issues.problem: Flowering-in-May is plausible for the 'May rose' but is attributed to a source text that could not be retrieved.
issues.evidence: c82.net blocked; no corroboration found in search

proposals.imageObservation: Botanical plate: a rose branch with two open single (five-petalled) deep-pink flowers with yellow stamens, one bud and one smaller flower, on seven- and five-leaflet leaves; the main cane carries paired prickles, the flowering shoots are unarmed.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The corymb and 5-7 leaflet points are supported by standard descriptions of R. cinnamomea, so I kept them. The only substantive change is dropping the 'southern Europe' range, which conflicts with the species' actual distribution; if someone can read Thory's text on c82.net and it really says 'midi de l'Europe', the original sentence could be restored as a quotation of Thory rather than as fact.

proposals.title: Rosa Clynophylla
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa clynophylla, a smooth climbing shrub whose alternate leaves droop in a marked way, bearing solitary white flowers with petals yellowish toward the claw. The stems and the entire calyx are covered in a short silky whitish down, per Thory's text.
proposals.proposedDescription: Rosa clynophylla, a climbing shrub whose alternate leaves droop in a marked way, its prickled stems bearing solitary white flowers with petals yellowish toward the claw. The stems and the entire calyx are covered in a short silky whitish down, per Thory's text.

issues.quote: a smooth climbing shrub
issues.problem: "Smooth" reads as unarmed, but the plate plainly draws several prickles along the main stem and side branches.
issues.evidence: image — at least four dark prickles are visible on the lower and middle stem

proposals.imageObservation: Botanical plate on a plain ground: a long arching rose branch with pinnate, grey-green, downward-hanging leaflets, two open five-petalled white flowers with dense yellow stamens and pale yellow-green petal bases, and one closed hairy bud; several straight-to-hooked prickles are clearly drawn on the main stem.
proposals.reviewerNotes: c82.net is behind a bot challenge, so Thory's wording could not be read. Thory published the species in Les Roses vol. 1 (1817) as "Rosier à feuilles penchées", which matches the drooping-leaf claim and the 1817 date; the down on stems and calyx is consistent with the hairy bud in the plate. My only real objection is the word "smooth", which may be a mistranslation of a botanical term in the original French — hence medium confidence. The minimal fix above changes only that phrase.

proposals.title: Rosa Collina Monsoniana
proposals.currentDescription: Lady Monson's rose, Rosa collina monsoniana, with clear-pink five-petalled flowers notched at the tip and slender stems set with strong hooked prickles. The hips ripen to an orange-red, and Claude-Antoine Thory wrote the accompanying text.
proposals.proposedDescription: Lady Monson's rose, Rosa collina monsoniana, with clear-pink semi-double flowers of about ten broad petals around a ring of yellow stamens, on slender stems set with strong hooked prickles. Claude-Antoine Thory wrote the accompanying text for the plate.

issues.quote: five-petalled flowers
issues.problem: The open flower carries roughly ten petals in two ranks (semi-double), not five.
issues.evidence: image — a 3x crop of the upper-left bloom shows about ten overlapping broad petals around the stamen boss.

issues.quote: The hips ripen to an orange-red
issues.problem: No hips appear in the plate, and I could not reach Thory's text to confirm the colour.
issues.evidence: image + c82.net bot-blocked.

proposals.imageObservation: Clear pink roses with a broad yellow ring of stamens - the fully open bloom at upper left has about ten broad petals, not five - plus two spent flowers reduced to their stamen discs, buds, toothed leaflets and a green stem armed with strong red hooked prickles. No hips are shown.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Petal count is judged from the image and is solid; the hips sentence is dropped only because nothing supports it, not because it is known to be wrong - restore it if Thory's text says so. Thory as author of the Les Roses text is well established and kept.

proposals.title: Rosa Damascena
proposals.currentDescription: The damask rose, Rosa damascena, its five notched petals white faintly washed with pink opening from a deep-red bud, the flowers two or three together in a loose panicle. Hairy glandular pedicels and an elongate pinnatifid calyx complete the sheet, drawn for Les Roses.
proposals.proposedDescription: The damask rose, Rosa damascena, its five notched petals white faintly washed with pink opening from a pink bud, the flowers two or three together in a loose panicle. Hairy glandular pedicels and an elongate pinnatifid calyx complete the sheet, drawn for Les Roses.

issues.quote: opening from a deep-red bud
issues.problem: The single coloured bud is clear pink with a slightly deeper rose centre, not deep red.
issues.evidence: image - 3x crop of the bud shows pale-to-mid pink with no red saturation

proposals.imageObservation: Three open single roses, five broad white petals faintly washed with pink around a ring of yellow stamens, with one pink bud and several green buds; the stem is heavily armed with red prickles, the pedicels bristly-glandular, and a detached red hip lies at lower left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Everything else checks against the image: five notched white-pink petals, three flowers on one stem, visibly glandular-bristly pedicels, sepals with lateral appendages. Only the bud colour is changed. The detached red hip at lower left goes unmentioned in both versions - a possible addition, left out to keep the edit minimal.

proposals.title: Rosa Damascena
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa damascena, the damask rose grown as the Rosier de Cels, its pink double flower set above grey-green foliage. The stipple engraving was printed in colour from a single plate and finished by hand, the method used across all three volumes.
proposals.proposedDescription: Rosa damascena, the damask rose grown as the Rosier de Cels, its cluster of double flowers running from pink to near-white above grey-green foliage. The stipple engraving was printed in colour from a single plate and finished by hand, the method used across all three volumes.

issues.quote: its pink double flower set above grey-green foliage
issues.problem: The plate shows a cluster of four or more open blooms, not one, and the dominant central bloom is white/blush rather than pink.
issues.evidence: image | four or more open flowers, the largest one white with a yellow centre

proposals.imageObservation: Botanical plate: a cluster of at least four open double roses - the largest and most prominent is white/blush with a yellow centre, the others pink - plus several red-pink buds, above grey-green foliage on a prickly stem.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Only the singular flower and its colour are off; the Celsiana identification, the damask species and the printing technique all hold. Colour ranges in these restorations can shift, but the white bloom here is unmistakably the central one.

proposals.title: Rosa Damascena
proposals.currentDescription: A damask rose grown as the Portland rose, its faintly scented flowers borne three or four to a branch tip in a loose umbel. The corolla holds two or three rows of deep purple petals notched at the apex, above five or seven oval leaflets. Claude-Antoine Thory supplied the botanical text for the plate.
proposals.proposedDescription: A damask rose grown as the Portland rose, its faintly scented flowers borne three or four to a branch tip in a loose umbel. The corolla holds two or three rows of deep carmine petals notched at the apex, above five or seven oval leaflets; two hips are drawn cut open at the right to show the seeds. Claude-Antoine Thory supplied the botanical text for the plate.

issues.quote: deep purple petals
issues.problem: The petals as drawn are crimson-carmine with a magenta cast, not purple; the varietal epithet 'coccinea' means scarlet.
issues.evidence: image — the open flower is a deep pinkish red with a yellow centre

issues.quote: borne three or four to a branch tip in a loose umbel
issues.problem: Not wrong, but the plate's most distinctive feature — the two hips cut open to show the seeds — goes unmentioned.
issues.evidence: image

proposals.imageObservation: A single large open crimson-carmine rose with a bright yellow boss of stamens at its centre, two side buds, a thorny stem with five-leaflet leaves, and two hips shown cut open at the right to reveal the seeds.
proposals.reviewerNotes: c82.net could not be fetched, so the botanical particulars (three or four flowers to a branch tip, two or three rows of petals, Portland rose) could not be checked against Thory's text; none of them is contradicted by the image, and the leaf counts and petal ranks match what is drawn. The only change I propose is the colour word. Thory's French may well have said 'purpurin', which would excuse 'purple' — treat this as a low-stakes nit.

proposals.title: Rosa Dumetorum
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa dumetorum, a wild rose of woods and hedges near Paris, its small five-petalled flowers of very pale pink clustered in a short tight corymb. A spherical hip ripens bright red. The shrub rises to six feet, the flower small for its vigour, with hooked prickles paired near the stipules.
proposals.proposedDescription: Rosa dumetorum, a wild rose of woods and hedges, its five-petalled flowers a clear pink with white eyes, borne singly or in pairs along a spreading branch. Slender hooked prickles are set in pairs near the stipules, and the leaflets are small and grey-green.

issues.quote: A spherical hip ripens bright red.
issues.problem: No hip is depicted. Standing as its own sentence between two descriptions of the plate, it reads as an account of something in the frame that is not there.
issues.evidence: image — the plate carries open flowers and buds only; nothing on it is a ripened fruit.

issues.quote: very pale pink
issues.problem: The flowers are a clear mid-pink with white eyes, not very pale pink.
issues.evidence: image.

issues.quote: clustered in a short tight corymb
issues.problem: Overstated: the flowers are borne singly or in pairs on widely separated branchlets across the sheet, not gathered into one tight corymb.
issues.evidence: image.

proposals.imageObservation: A branching spray with three open five-petalled roses in clear mid-pink with yellow centres, plus several buds, borne singly or in twos on separate branchlets; small grey-green leaflets and slender hooked red prickles along the stems. No fruit or hip appears anywhere on the sheet.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The species, habit of the spray and the paired hooked prickles all hold. I removed the hip sentence and the height, which cannot be grounded, and softened the corymb and colour claims. If the Thory text (c82.net, unreachable here) supports the height and the fruit, those sentences can be restored as species notes rather than as descriptions of the plate.

proposals.title: Rosa Eglanteria
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa eglanteria, a tall rose to twelve feet whose large single flowers carry five jonquil-yellow petals nearly two and a half inches across, the styles tipped with purple stigmas. The crushed leaves smell of ripe apple while the flowers are fetid. Redoute drew it for Les Roses, issued between 1817 and 1824.
proposals.proposedDescription: Rosa eglanteria, shown with two open flowers of five broad jonquil-yellow petals around a ring of stamens, a bud beside them, and pinnate grey-green leaflets on a prickly stem. Redoute drew it for Les Roses, issued between 1817 and 1824; the plate is a stipple engraving printed in colour and finished by hand.

issues.quote: The crushed leaves smell of ripe apple
issues.problem: Apple-scented foliage is the diagnostic character of the sweet briar (Rosa rubiginosa), not of the yellow rose shown here. The plate's yellow five-petalled flowers are the Austrian briar (Rosa foetida), whose name records the flowers' bad smell; the two species were historically conflated under the name Rosa eglanteria, so the sentence may be importing a character from the other one.
issues.evidence: image | the plate shows the yellow-flowered rose; web:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosa_foetida | R. foetida is the yellow Austrian briar named for its unpleasant flower scent, with R. eglanteria listed as a synonym, while sweet briar is the apple-scented one

issues.quote: a tall rose to twelve feet
issues.problem: Specific height with no backing in the image or record; Rosa foetida is usually given as roughly 1.5-3 m.
issues.evidence: knowledge | standard horticultural range for R. foetida

proposals.imageObservation: Botanical plate: two fully open single yellow roses, each with five broad petals and a ring of yellow stamens, plus one yellow bud and two small buds, on a prickly stem with pinnate grey-green leaflets.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The petal count, colour and single form are confirmed by the image, and the 1817-1824 span for Les Roses is right. I could not check the flower size, the purple stigmas or the leaf scent because c82.net (the source these captions appear to paraphrase, presumably Thory's text) is behind a bot challenge. If c82's transcription of Thory does state the apple-scented leaves, the original sentence is defensible and only needs a hedge; my replacement drops every unverified sensory and dimensional claim rather than guessing.

proposals.title: Rosa Eglanteria-Subrubra
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa eglanteria subrubra, the cherry eglantine, its solitary flowers showing five heart-notched petals pale cherry-red within and canary-yellow without. Seven small glaucous leaflets sit above a nearly thornless flowering branch. Redoute drew it for the third volume of Les Roses, published in 1824.
proposals.proposedDescription: Rosa eglanteria subrubra, the cherry eglantine, its solitary flowers showing five heart-notched petals of pale cherry-red, paler on the outer face, around a crown of yellow stamens. Seven small glaucous leaflets sit above a nearly thornless flowering branch. Redoute drew it for the third volume of Les Roses, published in 1824.

issues.quote: canary-yellow without
issues.problem: The outer face of the petals in this plate is pale pink; nothing yellow appears on the petal reverses. Red-within/yellow-without is the colouring of Rosa eglanteria punicea (the Austrian Copper), a different plate.
issues.evidence: image - the lower flower is turned to show the petal reverse, which is pale pink

proposals.imageObservation: Two single five-petalled roses, salmon-to-cherry pink with notched petal tips and yellow stamens; the lower flower shows the reverse of its petals, which are pale pink, not yellow. Small greyish leaflets in sevens on an almost thornless stem.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Volume/date check out (Les Roses vol. 3, 1824, matches the record year). Only the petal-reverse colour changed; the resemblance to the punicea description suggests the colour was imported from a sibling plate.

proposals.title: Rosa Gallica Agatha
proposals.currentDescription: An Agatha form of Rosa gallica grown as the Enfant de France, its many close-set petals of deep rose folded over one another like a military pompon, hiding the calyx lobes. A pear-shaped hip ripens red. Redoute drew it for the third volume of Les Roses, published in 1824.
proposals.proposedDescription: An Agatha form of Rosa gallica, its many close-set petals of deep rose folded over one another like a military pompon, hiding the calyx lobes. Redoute drew it for the third volume of Les Roses, published in 1824.

issues.quote: A pear-shaped hip ripens red.
issues.problem: Nothing resembling a hip is depicted. Placed in the middle of the visual description, the sentence reads as a description of the plate, and the plate shows only flowers, buds and leaves.
issues.evidence: image — no fruit is present

issues.quote: grown as the Enfant de France
issues.problem: A specific cultivar synonym that neither the image nor the catalogue record supports; c82.net (which would carry Thory's text) could not be fetched.
issues.evidence: catalogue record — silent; c82.net behind a bot challenge

proposals.imageObservation: A single deep rose-crimson pompon flower with dozens of tightly packed, rolled petals, two buds of the same colour, broad toothed leaflets and a smooth green stem. No fruit or hip appears anywhere on the plate.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The hip sentence may well come from Thory's botanical text rather than from the picture, so this is a placement/framing problem as much as a factual one — if the project wants to keep text-derived botany, it should be marked as such ('Thory's text notes...') as the other Redouté entries in this batch do. Volume 3 / 1824 is correct for Les Roses. The 'Enfant de France' synonym is unverified, not disproven.

proposals.title: Rosa Gallica Agatha
proposals.currentDescription: An Agatha variety of the Provins rose, its very double flower of dark violet-purple packed with tight rolled petals like a ranunculus. The shrub barely reaches a foot and a half, with pear-shaped hips that hold through much of winter. Claude-Antoine Thory supplied the botanical text for the plate.
proposals.proposedDescription: An Agatha variety of the Provins rose, its very double crimson flower packed with tight rolled petals like a ranunculus, shown with two buds on bristly stems. The plate is from Redoute's Les Roses, with botanical text by Claude-Antoine Thory.

issues.quote: dark violet-purple
issues.problem: The bloom reads crimson/deep carmine in the plate (sampled median hue ~346 degrees, well away from violet). The variety epithet 'violacea' is probably what prompted the wording.
issues.evidence: image - pixel-sampled hue of the flower

issues.quote: pear-shaped hips that hold through much of winter
issues.problem: No hips are shown in the plate; the claim (and the shrub's height) rests on a source text that could not be fetched.
issues.evidence: image; c82.net blocked

proposals.imageObservation: Botanical plate: one very double crimson rose (measured median hue ~346 degrees, i.e. crimson-red rather than violet) packed with tightly rolled petals, plus two buds; bristly stems and five-leaflet leaves. No hips shown.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The colour is the substantive fix. The height ('barely reaches a foot and a half') is plausible for a variety named parvula but unverifiable, so I left it out rather than restate it; a reader with Thory's text could put both the height and the hips back as attributed statements.

proposals.title: Rosa Gallica
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa gallica in a marbled form, its nearly scentless flowers above three inches wide carrying two or three rows of pale pink petals spotted with a deeper rose that reads as marbling. Numerous stamens surround a sessile half-globular head of stigmas. Claude-Antoine Thory supplied the botanical text for the plate.
proposals.proposedDescription: Rosa gallica in a marbled form: one open flower whose inner rows of petals are pale pink and whose outer ring is deep rose, the whole flecked with paler, almost white spots that read as marbling. Numerous stamens surround a low central head of stigmas, and two buds and one spent calyx share the prickly stem. Claude-Antoine Thory supplied the botanical text for the plate.

issues.quote: pale pink petals spotted with a deeper rose that reads as marbling
issues.problem: Inverted. In the plate the spots are paler than the ground - whitish flecks on both the pale pink inner petals and the deep rose outer ones. The deeper rose is the colour of the outer ring of petals, not of the marbling.
issues.evidence: image - a 4x crop of the flower head shows white flecks over a pink and a deep rose ground

issues.quote: nearly scentless flowers above three inches wide
issues.problem: Scent and measurement are Thory-style claims that cannot be checked while c82.net is blocked.
issues.evidence: no accessible source

proposals.imageObservation: A single large semi-double rose seen face-on: the inner rows of petals are pale pink and the outer, lower ring is deep rose, and every petal is flecked with small paler, almost white spots. Yellow stamens ring a low central head. Two buds and one spent flower with reflexed sepals are on the same prickly stem, with toothed leaflets below.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The colour inversion is the finding and it is clear at high zoom. I dropped the scent and size claims from the replacement because they cannot be grounded; if someone can read Thory's text they can be restored.

proposals.title: Rosa Gallica
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa gallica in a giant-flowered Provins form, its lightly scented corolla more than five inches across with several rows of fine rose petals, those at the centre rolled and crumpled over the spent stamens. A large nearly round hip ripens red. Redoute drew it for the third volume of Les Roses, published in 1824.
proposals.proposedDescription: Rosa gallica in a giant-flowered Provins form, its lightly scented corolla more than five inches across with several rows of fine rose petals, those at the centre rolled and crumpled over the spent stamens. Redoute drew it for the third volume of Les Roses, published in 1824.

issues.quote: A large nearly round hip ripens red.
issues.problem: No hip is drawn on this plate. Sitting between a description of the flower and the publication note, the sentence reads as if the hip were in the frame; if it comes from the plate's botanical text that is not stated.
issues.evidence: image — the sheet shows one open bloom, three buds, stem and leaves only

proposals.imageObservation: One very large, fully double rose-pink bloom with many rows of petals, the innermost crumpled and folded inward, flanked by three buds, on a prickly stem with big dark toothed leaflets. No hip appears anywhere on the sheet.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Only the hip sentence is dropped. The five-inch corolla is plausible against the plate (the bloom spans roughly half the 25 cm sheet width) and the 1824 third volume matches the record's year, so both are kept. If the hip statement can be sourced to Thory's text it could be restored with that attribution made explicit.

proposals.title: Rosa Gallica
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa gallica grown as the Rosier de France, a deep-toned French rose set above its coarsely toothed leaflets. The stipple plate was printed in colour from a single plate and finished by hand in watercolour, the method used across all three volumes of Les Roses.
proposals.proposedDescription: A double variety of Rosa gallica, the Rosier de France, its crowded soft-pink petals opening flat above coarsely toothed leaflets, with deeper-pink buds alongside. The stipple plate was printed in colour from a single plate and finished by hand in watercolour, the method used across all three volumes of Les Roses.

issues.quote: a deep-toned French rose
issues.problem: The open bloom is a soft mid-pink; only the unopened buds are deeper. 'Deep-toned' overstates it.
issues.evidence: image

issues.quote: grown as the Rosier de France
issues.problem: 'Rosier de France' is the standard French vernacular for Rosa gallica, so this is defensible, but the phrasing 'grown as' implies a source statement about this particular cultivar that cannot be checked.
issues.evidence: c82.net source text could not be fetched (Cloudflare); knowledge — Rosier de France is the ordinary French name for the species

proposals.imageObservation: A single large, fully double rose in soft-to-mid pink, its many petals crowded into a flat cupped head, with four deeper-pink buds around it on green stems; the leaflets below are broad, oval and coarsely toothed, blue-green above and lighter beneath; no prickles are conspicuous.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The technique sentence is correct and untouched. The plate number in the file URL (roses-107) matches Les Roses pl. 107, sold as 'Variety of French Rose', which supports the identification and also suggests the description should say 'variety' rather than the bare species. The doubleness of the flower is the most striking thing in the plate and the original description never mentions it.

proposals.title: Rosa Gallica Maheka
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa gallica maheka in a near-single form, a Provins variety carrying broad pink to crimson petals above toothed foliage. Redoute drew it for Les Roses, the most famous rose iconography ever made, which documented species roses and early garden cultivars before the modern hybrid.
proposals.proposedDescription: Rosa gallica maheka in a near-single form, a Provins variety whose broad deep-crimson petals open around a wide boss of yellow stamens above toothed foliage. Redoute drew it for Les Roses, which documented species roses and early garden cultivars before the modern hybrid.

issues.quote: broad pink to crimson petals
issues.problem: The bloom carries no pink: the petals are a uniform deep crimson to purple-maroon.
issues.evidence: image | single dark crimson-purple flower

issues.quote: the most famous rose iconography ever made
issues.problem: Unsupported superlative doing rhetorical work.
issues.evidence: knowledge | no source in the record supports a ranking claim

proposals.imageObservation: Botanical plate: a single large near-double rose of deep crimson-purple, its broad petals surrounding a wide boss of yellow stamens, one bud above left, and toothed green leaflets on a bristly stem.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Rosa gallica is the Provins rose, so that part stands, and the flower is indeed near-single (a single ring of broad petals with the stamens fully exposed). Only the colour range and the superlative needed changing.

proposals.title: Rosa Gallica
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa gallica purpurea velutina parva, a low Provins variety with trailing branches and medium flowers of three petal ranks, brilliant purple shading to a velvety violet over golden stamens. It was raised from seed by the nurseryman Van Eeden of Haarlem, who used it to plant the gardens of Malmaison in 1810.
proposals.proposedDescription: Rosa gallica purpurea velutina parva, the Van Eeden rose, a low Provins variety whose two blooms here run from brilliant crimson to a velvety near-black violet over golden stamens. It was raised from seed before 1810 by the Dutch nurseryman Van Eeden.

issues.quote: who used it to plant the gardens of Malmaison in 1810
issues.problem: Sources record only that the variety was raised by the nurseryman Van Eeden in the Netherlands before 1810. No source found supports Van Eeden planting, or being used to plant, the gardens of Malmaison, and 1810 appears to be the 'raised before 1810' date repurposed as a planting date.
issues.evidence: web:https://www.helpmefind.com/rose/l.php?l=2.2389.2 - 'Bred by Arie Cornelis Van Eeden (Netherlands, before 1810)'; Alamy/Meisterdrucke plate captions: 'Rosier de Van Eeden. Raised in the Netherlands by Van Eeden pre 1810'

proposals.imageObservation: Two open double flowers on one stem - one brilliant crimson-red, one almost black-violet - both showing golden stamens at the centre, with two buds and large green leaflets below.
proposals.reviewerNotes: 'Of Haarlem' is plausible - the van Eeden nursery family was based at Haarlem - but I dropped it because the sources I could reach say only 'Netherlands'. The 'three petal ranks' detail was also dropped: the flowers in the plate are fuller than three ranks, though the phrase may come from Thory's text, which I could not fetch (c82.net is behind a bot challenge).

proposals.title: Rosa Gallica
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa gallica purpuro-violacea magna, the rose called l'Eveque, an old Provins variety with broad purple-violet petals heart-notched at the tip and gathered around a central tuft of styles. Its leaves carry five firm ovate leaflets, hairless above and downy beneath. Claude-Antoine Thory supplied the botanical text for the plate.
proposals.proposedDescription: Rosa gallica purpuro-violacea magna, the rose called l'Eveque, an old Provins variety: two fully double blooms open on one stem, the larger deep purple-violet and the smaller a bright carmine, their broad petals heart-notched at the tip, with three buds above. Its leaves carry five firm ovate leaflets, hairless above and downy beneath. Claude-Antoine Thory supplied the botanical text for the plate.

issues.quote: gathered around a central tuft of styles
issues.problem: Both flowers on the plate are fully double with quartered, petal-packed centres; no tuft of styles is shown.
issues.evidence: image — the centres of both blooms are closed with petals

issues.quote: broad purple-violet petals
issues.problem: Only the larger bloom is purple-violet; the second, smaller flower on the same stem is bright carmine-red. The description reads as if there were one colour.
issues.evidence: image — two blooms, one purple-violet and one carmine

proposals.imageObservation: Two fully double blooms on one prickly stem — the larger a deep purple-violet, the smaller a bright carmine-red — with three buds above and five broad ovate leaflets below. The centres of both flowers are packed with petals; no styles or stamens are visible.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Low-stakes fix. 'L'Évêque' for this variety and Thory's authorship of the Les Roses text are both standard and left untouched. The leaflet underside ('downy beneath') is a Thory detail that cannot be checked from the plate; I kept it since it was already there, but a stricter pass could drop it.

proposals.title: Rosa Gallica
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa gallica stapeliae-flora, a Provins shrub with five large concave petals of fairly deep purple marked with many small tawny-yellow spots set in longitudinal lines. The numerous stamens surround a convex head of styles, and the fruit ripens from reddish to black. Claude-Antoine Thory wrote the descriptive text that accompanied the plate.
proposals.proposedDescription: Rosa gallica stapeliae-flora, a Provins shrub with five large concave petals of deep rose-carmine flecked with many small dark spots set in longitudinal lines. The numerous stamens surround a convex head of styles, and the fruit ripens from reddish to black. Claude-Antoine Thory wrote the descriptive text that accompanied the plate.

issues.quote: marked with many small tawny-yellow spots
issues.problem: Magnified, the spots are darker than the petal ground - deep red to maroon - not tawny-yellow.
issues.evidence: image - 7x crop of the petal surface.

issues.quote: of fairly deep purple
issues.problem: The petal ground reads as rose-carmine with a purple cast rather than deep purple.
issues.evidence: image.

proposals.imageObservation: Botanical plate: one large open rose with five broad concave petals of rose-carmine, finely speckled with small darker (maroon) dots arranged in radiating lines, a ring of yellow stamens around a convex green head of styles, two spent flowers above, bristly stem and serrated leaflets.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Thory's own wording for this plate could not be retrieved (c82.net blocked), so it is possible the 'tawny-yellow' spots come from the source text and the restored plate reads darker. Either way the description contradicts the image a reader is looking at. The fruit-colour sentence is unverifiable and was left alone.

proposals.title: Rosa Gallica
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa gallica versicolor, the striped rose of France, always semi-double and never full, its soft-pink petals streaked with brighter red. The leaves bear seven oblong leaflets downy beneath, and the fruit is round and reddish at maturity. Redoute drew it for Les Roses, which grew out of Empress Josephine's rose collection at Malmaison.
proposals.proposedDescription: Rosa gallica versicolor, the striped rose of France, shown semi-double, its white-pink petals streaked and flecked with deeper crimson above a yellow centre. The leaves bear five broad serrated leaflets, pale beneath, and crimson buds cluster around the open flower. Redoute drew it for Les Roses, which grew out of Empress Josephine's rose collection at Malmaison.

issues.quote: The leaves bear seven oblong leaflets
issues.problem: The compound leaves in the plate carry five leaflets (a terminal plus two pairs), not seven, and they are broadly ovate rather than oblong.
issues.evidence: image — the lower-left and right-hand leaves each resolve to five leaflets on magnification.

issues.quote: and the fruit is round and reddish at maturity
issues.problem: No fruit appears anywhere on the sheet; this is a species statement that neither the image nor the record supports.
issues.evidence: image — the plate shows one open flower and buds only.

issues.quote: always semi-double and never full
issues.problem: An absolute claim ('always', 'never') about the variety, stated as certainty with nothing behind it in the record.
issues.evidence: catalogue record / sourceEvidence — c82.net unreachable, so Thory's wording could not be checked.

proposals.imageObservation: One large open semi-double rose whose white-pink petals are boldly striped and flecked with deeper crimson, with a yellow centre; three or four crimson buds; broad ovate serrated leaflets, pale grey-green beneath; a green stem with a few small prickles. No fruit is shown.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The identification and the striped petals are unambiguous. The leaflet count is the substantive fix. The Malmaison sentence is the standard account of Les Roses and I left it verbatim. Flagging that the striping in the plate reads as crimson on white-pink rather than 'soft-pink petals streaked with brighter red', which is a shade off but not wrong enough to matter on its own.

proposals.title: Rosa Hispida
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa hispida argentea, a dense shrub reaching six or seven feet, its branches covered in stiff bristles and scattered straight prickles. The flowers carry six or seven ranks of concave silvery-white petals, and the round fruit is bristly and reddish when ripe. Redoute drew it for Les Roses, issued in three folio volumes between 1817 and 1824.
proposals.proposedDescription: Rosa hispida argentea, its branches covered in stiff bristles and scattered straight prickles, carrying one fully double flower of concave silvery-white petals above three bristly dark-red buds. A spent bloom at the left of the plate shows its ring of stamens. Redoute drew it for Les Roses, issued in three folio volumes between 1817 and 1824.

issues.quote: and the round fruit is bristly and reddish when ripe
issues.problem: No fruit is shown on the plate. Phrased as a species trait rather than as something depicted, so it is unsupported rather than flatly contradicted, but nothing in the record backs it.
issues.evidence: image — flower, buds and one spent bloom only.

issues.quote: a dense shrub reaching six or seven feet
issues.problem: Habit and height are not in the record and cannot be read from the plate; six or seven feet is on the high side for a Rosa pimpinellifolia-group form.
issues.evidence: sourceEvidence — c82.net unreachable; knowledge — Scots-rose relatives are usually cited at well under two metres.

proposals.imageObservation: One large fully double white rose with a few yellow stamens showing at its centre, three bristly dark-red buds, and a spent flower at left with its stamens exposed; the stems and receptacles are covered in fine stiff bristles, and the leaves are small with many little serrated leaflets. No ripe fruit is depicted.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The bristly stems and the silvery-white double flower are exactly as described and are the identifying features. Only the height and the fruit are unsupported; I removed both and added the spent flower, which is clearly drawn. The 1817-1824 three-volume publication fact is correct.

proposals.title: Rosa Hudsoniana
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa hudsoniana salicifolia, the willow-leaved Hudson rose, with smooth thornless green stems and narrow leaflets resembling those of the osier willow. Its flowers, gathered in a loose cyme, show five petals of a pretty deep pink, often pointed at the tip. The plate was printed in colour from a single stipple-engraved plate and finished by hand.
proposals.proposedDescription: Rosa hudsoniana salicifolia, the willow-leaved Hudson rose, with smooth thornless stems and narrow leaflets resembling those of the osier willow. Its flowers, gathered in a loose cyme, show five petals of a clear pink, often pointed at the tip, around a boss of yellow stamens. The plate was printed in colour from a single stipple-engraved plate and finished by hand.

issues.quote: smooth thornless green stems
issues.problem: The canes in the plate are brown-purple to grey, not green. 'Smooth' and 'thornless' do match the plate.
issues.evidence: image — no green stem is shown; the main cane is a dull purple-brown

issues.quote: five petals of a pretty deep pink
issues.problem: The flowers are a mid, slightly cool pink rather than a deep pink.
issues.evidence: image
