proposals.imageObservation: A grinning nude winged boy, arrows in his right hand, stands with one leg on a white-sheeted bed, above a violin, a lute, a sheet of music, a set square and compass, a celestial globe, a laurel branch and a suit of black armour; a crown and sceptre lie in shadow at the right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Every emblem the description groups as music, war, science and rule is visible in the picture. The Gemaldegalerie Berlin attribution is confirmed by the Commons imageDescription, and the record's 113.3 x 156.5 cm matches its 156 x 113 cm. The provenance sourceLink to museum-kunst-palast.de is only where the file was cropped from, not a collection claim, so it is not a conflict. 'Notorious among Roman collectors' is loose but consistent with the picture's documented reception in the Giustiniani circle.

proposals.title: Anisimov Alexander Ivanovich
proposals.currentDescription: Alexander Ivanovich Anisimov is shown in close-up against a luminous Russian landscape with domed church spires, rivers, and autumn foliage — a backdrop characteristic of Kustodiev's outdoor portraits. Boris Kustodiev painted the portrait in 1915; Anisimov was a leading scholar of medieval Russian icon painting.

issues.quote: rivers
issues.problem: One river winds through the background, not several.
issues.evidence: image

proposals.imageObservation: Close-up of a bearded man with a receding hairline in a light suit, white shirt and green tie, set against a Russian landscape: a white church with dark and green domes at the left, a curving river, autumn-yellow birches, green hills and a streaked evening sky. Signed at the lower right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Sitter, date and Kustodiev's authorship are all on the Commons record, which titles it 'Portrait of the art historian and restorer A. I. Anisimov' - so 'a leading scholar of medieval Russian icon painting' is supported. Only the plural 'rivers' is off, which is too small to rewrite for.

proposals.title: Self portrait of Antoine Coypel
proposals.currentDescription: Coypel turns toward the viewer in a large powdered wig and a voluminous dark velvet robe, holding an ornate bound volume — attributes befitting his role as First Painter to the King and director of the Académie royale. The self-portrait is dated 1715, seven years before his death in 1722.

issues.quote: a voluminous dark velvet robe
issues.problem: The robe is a deep red or maroon velvet, not simply dark; the colour is the most conspicuous thing in the picture.
issues.evidence: image

proposals.imageObservation: Half-length self-portrait of a man in a large grey powdered wig and a deep red velvet robe over a white cravat, his right hand resting on the fore-edge of a large gilt-tooled volume propped at the left and his left hand, in a white lace cuff, on a second book below.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Date 1715 and Coypel's death in 1722 are both right, and the Commons title itself styles him 'Ecuyer Premier Peintre du Roy', so the offices in the description are supported. One thing to watch: he was made director of the Academie royale in 1714 and Premier peintre du roi in 1715/1716 depending on the source, so at the moment of this portrait the title may have been very new. Also note the description says 'an ornate bound volume' where the picture shows two books. Neither is enough to rewrite for.

proposals.title: The Last Meeting between Jacopo Foscari and his Family Before Being Sent into Exile
proposals.currentDescription: The painting was commissioned in 1838 by Emperor Ferdinand I , who had arrived in Milan for his coronation as king of Lombardy and Veneto , and it was destined for the Belvedere Gallery in Vienna. On its completion in 1840 the work was valued at the extremely high price of five thousand florins by the Commissione Permanente di Pittura dell’Accademia di Brera , which thus recognized its exceptional quality.

issues.quote: The painting was commissioned in 1838 by Emperor Ferdinand I
issues.problem: The description is a verbatim copy of the Commons commission/valuation paragraph and never says what the picture shows - no doge, no family, no Venetian loggia.
issues.evidence: commons - imageDescription field begins with exactly this text

proposals.imageObservation: A crowded loggia of the Doge's Palace: the aged doge in gold brocade and horned cap at centre, women in period dress and children at left, a girl kneeling with clasped hands, and a young man at right being pulled away toward a balustrade with a view of Venice beyond.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Every factual claim is taken straight from the Commons imageDescription and is historically sound (Ferdinand I was crowned King of Lombardy-Venetia in Milan in September 1838), so no verdict downgrade. But this is scraped catalogue prose, not a description: it should be rewritten to open on the scene. Note also the record's collection (Gallerie d'Italia, Milan) is not in conflict - the Commons text goes on to describe the 1928 Milan auction, which the copied excerpt cuts off.

proposals.title: A Girl with a Watering Can
proposals.currentDescription: A small girl in a blue dress and lace-trimmed pinafore stands on a garden path holding a watering can, flowers scattered at her feet. Renoir painted the figure in 1876, oil on canvas, now in the National Gallery of Art, Washington (Chester Dale Collection).
proposals.imageObservation: A small blonde girl with a red bow in her hair stands on a pale garden path in a blue dress with white lace trim and buttons, a green watering can in her right hand and a few small white and pink flowers in her left; flowerbeds and a rose bush press in at the left, lawn and blossom behind. Signed and dated lower right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Figure, dress, lace, watering can and path all match; the date matches Commons and the National Gallery of Art / Chester Dale Collection is the standard published provenance (Commons: 'Google Art Project works in National Gallery of Art, Washington DC'). I checked 'flowers scattered at her feet' at full crop: the flowers are the rose bush and border immediately beside her boots rather than blooms lying on the path, which is loose phrasing but not a false statement. She also holds a small bunch of daisies the description does not mention.

proposals.title: Jeunes filles au piano
proposals.currentDescription: Two girls in white and pink dresses lean over an upright piano, one seated and playing while the other follows the score. Renoir painted this version in 1892 as the first of his works acquired by the French state, placed in the Musée du Luxembourg and now in the Musée d'Orsay. He made several oil and drawn repetitions of the composition for dealers and collectors.
proposals.imageObservation: Two girls at an upright piano: a blonde in a white dress with a blue sash sits playing, and a second girl in a pink-salmon dress with a white ruff leans over her shoulder pointing at the open score; a green curtain, a flowered vase on the piano and a framed picture at the left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The dresses, poses and the piano match. The state-acquisition story (bought by the French state in 1892 for the Musée du Luxembourg, Renoir's first work to enter a national collection, now Orsay) is standard and consistent with the Commons category placing the picture in the Musée d'Orsay; the existence of several painted and pastel repetitions is likewise well documented.

proposals.title: Selbstporträt mit Barett
proposals.currentDescription: The painter shown half-length in a soft beret and dark coat, turned slightly from the viewer with a guarded expression. Oil on canvas of about 1898 to 1900, in the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston. It is among the last of the roughly two dozen self-portraits Cézanne made across his career.
proposals.imageObservation: Half-length self-portrait of a balding, white-bearded man in a black beret and dark coat, seated in front of a red chair back against a mottled grey-tan wall, looking out at the viewer.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Commons gives 1898-1900 and categorises the picture with Cezanne's paintings in the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, matching the description. 'Roughly two dozen' self-portraits is a fair rounding of the usual count, and this is generally described as among his last.

proposals.title: Selbstporträt vor olivfarbener Tapete
proposals.currentDescription: A bearded self-portrait set against a dull olive-green wallpaper whose pattern Cézanne echoes in the modelling of the head. Painted in Paris around 1880 to 1881, oil on canvas, now in the National Gallery, London. The dome of the skull is built from short oblique patches of white, red and ochre, the ear and crown outlined in blue.
proposals.imageObservation: Head-and-shoulders self-portrait of a balding, bearded man in a dark coat, turned three-quarters; the ground is olive-brown wallpaper with a dark lozenge and cross-motif pattern, with a pale blue-grey strip of plain wall at the left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Wallpaper, palette of the skull and the National Gallery attribution all check out (Commons: 'Paintings by Paul Cezanne in the National Gallery, London'; date 1880-1881). The claim that the wallpaper pattern is echoed in the modelling of the head is interpretation rather than a checkable fact; I left it, since it is not contradicted.

proposals.title: Rainbow
proposals.currentDescription: A rainbow arches above a shipwreck and lifeboat tossed in heavy seas, survivors pulling at the oars while the sky breaks open behind them. Painted in 1873 and now in the State Tretyakov Gallery, the canvas is one of Aivazovsky's signature meditations on rescue at sea, salvation hinging on a sliver of coloured light.
proposals.imageObservation: A storm at sea: an overcrowded open boat of survivors, one man standing with a raised oar, rides a huge wave in the foreground while a dismasted ship founders in the spray behind; a rocky cliff rises at left and a faint pale rainbow arcs down through the golden-grey haze.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The rainbow is genuinely faint but present as a pale iridescent arc left of centre, and the title is 'Radiga/Rainbow'. 1873 and the State Tretyakov Gallery are both confirmed by the Commons credit line and categories ('Paintings by Ivan Aivazovsky in the Tretyakov Gallery', 'Paintings of ships in distress'). The closing clause is a flourish but is grounded in what the picture shows.

proposals.title: Back View of Fuji from Dream Mtn in Kai Province
proposals.currentDescription: Hiroshige reverses the conventional southern view of Fuji, glimpsing the sacred peak from Kai Province on the mountain's far side. Part of his first Thirty-six Views series, the design uses graduated bokashi printing to layer mist, peak, and foreground.
proposals.imageObservation: Horizontal woodblock print: a steep green mountain flank with wind-shaped pines fills the left two thirds, two tiny travellers with packs climbing a dotted path across it; Mount Fuji rises at the right in cream and white above a pale cloud bank, with temple roofs and dark conifers in the lower right corner. Deep blue bokashi grades down from the top of the sky; title cartouche upper right, artist's signature lower left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Both substantive claims hold: the Commons record describes this as No. 33 (or No. 6) of the first-version Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji (1852), matching "his first Thirty-six Views series", and the graded bokashi is plainly visible in the sky and the cloud band. "On the mountain's far side" is the literal sense of urafuji (裏富士) in the Japanese title. The two climbing figures and the temple roofs go unmentioned, which is an omission only.

proposals.title: Dinner
proposals.currentDescription: Bakst's 'Dinner' of 1902 shows an elegantly dressed woman in a black gown and wide-brimmed black hat seated at a white-clothed restaurant table, a bowl of oranges before her. The restrained palette and confidently simplified forms belong to his St Petersburg period, when he was closely associated with the World of Art circle in the years before his celebrated work for Diaghilev's Ballets Russes.

issues.quote: seated at a white-clothed restaurant table
issues.problem: Nothing in the image or the record establishes a restaurant; the setting is a table with bentwood chairs against a blank ground. It is a reasonable inference from the picture's title ('Ужин' / Supper) and from the way the work is usually discussed, but it is stated as fact.
issues.evidence: image — no interior detail beyond the chairs and a pale wall; commons record gives only the title and date

proposals.imageObservation: A woman in a long black dress with a low white-edged neckline and a large soft black hat sits in profile-to-three-quarters at a table under a white cloth; on the table are a footed glass dish of oranges, a single orange, a glass and a folded patterned fan. A dark bentwood chair stands at each side against a grey-cream ground. Signed at upper right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Kept at 'accurate' because the restaurant reading is a mild and conventional inference rather than a fabrication, and everything else holds: the black gown and hat, the oranges, the 1902 date (Commons: 24 January 1902), Bakst's Mir Iskusstva association and the fact that this precedes his Ballets Russes work by seven years. The description does not mention the fan or the glass; not worth a finding.

proposals.title: Landscape of Aigues-Mortes
proposals.currentDescription: The medieval ramparts of Aigues-Mortes seen across flat marshland under a wide sky. Oil on canvas, 46 by 55 cm, painted in 1867 and held by the Musée Fabre, Montpellier. Bazille made several views of the walled Camargue town during a summer in the region.
proposals.imageObservation: A low horizon of flat marsh and shallow pools in the foreground, the crenellated ramparts and towers of a walled town strung across the middle distance, under a wide blue sky with light cloud and two birds.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The Commons imageDescription (in Russian) gives 1867, oil on canvas, 46 x 55 cm, Musee Fabre, Montpellier — every specific in the description is backed there. Bazille did paint several Aigues-Mortes views in 1867.

proposals.title: Flowers
proposals.currentDescription: A dense bouquet rising from a vase set on a console table, catalogued as Vase de fleurs sur une console. Oil on canvas, 130 by 97 cm, painted between 1867 and 1868 and now in the Musée de Grenoble.
proposals.imageObservation: A tall blue-and-white decorated urn on a marble-topped rococo console holds a dense mixed bouquet; more cut flowers lie loose on the marble, a climbing plant with orange trumpet flowers spreads across the grey wall behind, and a dark embroidered footstool sits below at the left. Signed at the lower right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Every stated fact is carried by the Commons record itself: the Russian imageDescription gives "Vase de fleurs sur une console", 1867–1868, oil on canvas, 130 × 97 cm, Musée de Grenoble — exactly what the description says. The image confirms vase, console and bouquet.

proposals.title: Summer Scene
proposals.currentDescription: Young men in swimming costume resting and wrestling along the wooded bank of the Lez near Montpellier. Bazille drew the figures in his Paris studio before placing them in the open-air setting; the oil was shown at the Salon of 1870 and is now in the Harvard Art Museums (Fogg).
proposals.imageObservation: Young men in striped and coloured swimming trunks on a wooded riverbank: one leaning against a birch, one reclining on the grass, two wrestling in the sunlit meadow behind, one swimming toward the viewer and one being hauled from the water by a standing figure in trousers. Signed F. Bazille 1869 at lower left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The studio-drawing account and the Lez near Montpellier are both documented for this picture (Harvard Art Museums material: the figures were drawn in his Paris studio and then set into the outdoor scene; the setting is the bank of the Lez near Montpellier). The 1870 Salon showing of 'Scene d'ete' is well established, and Harvard Art Museums / Fogg is in the file title.

proposals.title: Bemberg Fondation Toulouse - Bateaux sur la plage à Etretat - Claude Monet - 1883 65x81 Inv.2077
proposals.currentDescription: Monet paints fishing boats hauled up beneath the chalk cliffs of Étretat, a Norman coast he returned to repeatedly in the 1880s. The pale beach and overcast sea are built from short, broken strokes that record shifting weather rather than narrative incident. The canvas now resides at the Bemberg Foundation in Toulouse.
proposals.imageObservation: Oil: fishing boats hauled up on the pebble beach at Etretat, several with masts and gear, the chalk cliff and the Porte d'Amont arch closing the view at the right, pale green-blue sea with small sails offshore, a few figures on the sand; signed lower right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Spot-check of a prior 'accurate' verdict; still accurate. Boats, cliffs and beach match; the Fondation Bemberg in Toulouse is in the record's own provenance block, and Monet worked repeatedly at Etretat in the 1880s. 'Overcast sea' slightly overstates a hazy, high-key sky, which is not enough to lower the verdict.

proposals.title: The lamentation over the dead Christ
proposals.currentDescription: The dead Christ lies stretched out on a white shroud over blue drapery, his head fallen back toward the Virgin, who throws her arms wide in grief while Saint John and weeping angels gather around the body beneath a darkened sky. Anthony van Dyck painted this horizontal Lamentation in oil on canvas around 1635, after his return to Antwerp from England. It hangs in the Royal Museum of Fine Arts Antwerp (KMSKA), inventory number 404.

issues.quote: after his return to Antwerp from England
issues.problem: Neither the image, the catalogue row nor the Commons metadata places the picture in van Dyck's 1634-35 Antwerp stay; it is a biographical inference.
issues.evidence: knowledge + web:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deposition_(van_Dyck,_1635) — the article confirms 1635, KMSKA, and a commission by Cesare Alessandro Scaglia for his tomb in the Recollects convent in Antwerp, but does not state where van Dyck painted it. Van Dyck's second Antwerp period (1634-35) makes the claim plausible.

proposals.imageObservation: A horizontal Lamentation: the dead Christ, crowned with thorns, laid out on a white shroud over blue drapery; the Virgin at left in white headcloth throws both arms open, a curly-haired young man in a red cloak leans in at centre, and two winged angels grieve at right beneath a stormy blue-grey sky.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Everything checkable holds: oil on canvas, 115 x 208 cm, KMSKA inv. 404, c.1635 (Commons: 'circa after 1635'; web confirms the same dimensions and inventory). The figure identifications (Virgin, St John, angels) match standard iconography and the image. Only the Antwerp/England sentence is inference rather than sourced fact; it is very likely right and I would leave it.

proposals.title: Coronation of the Virgin
proposals.currentDescription: A predella scene from the San Marco altarpiece, showing John the Evangelist receiving his vision on the rocky island of Patmos. The miniature format allowed Botticelli's workshop to compress dramatic landscape and visionary light into a narrow horizontal panel.

issues.quote: compress dramatic landscape and visionary light into a narrow horizontal panel
issues.problem: The panel is spare and evenly lit; 'dramatic' and 'visionary light' overstate what is a plain rocky shore under an even sky.
issues.evidence: image

proposals.imageObservation: A long, narrow horizontal panel: a bearded haloed man in a blue tunic and red mantle sits on the shore writing, wedged against a mass of grey broken rock at the left, with pale green ground and a flat expanse of sea and sky at the right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Spot-check of a prior 'accurate' verdict, and it holds: Commons gives 'Predella: St John on Patmos' from the San Marco Altarpiece, and the record's 56.8 x 21 cm matches the narrow horizontal format. Two soft points I would not act on alone — the attribution to 'Botticelli's workshop' (the San Marco predella is often given to Botticelli himself) and 'receiving his vision' (he is shown writing, with no apocalyptic imagery). Neither is contradicted by the evidence available.

proposals.title: Богоматерь с младенцем
proposals.currentDescription: The Virgin holds the Christ Child against a darkened ground, the academic Madonna type Bruni returned to across his career. He painted this oil in 1858, in the years when he directed the Imperial Hermitage picture gallery in St Petersburg.
proposals.imageObservation: The Virgin in a brilliant blue mantle over a white veil holds the naked, fair-haired Christ Child against her breast, both looking out at the viewer, set inside a painted oval against a dark brown ground.
proposals.reviewerNotes: No claim is contradicted. Date 1858 matches Commons; Bruni did head the Imperial Hermitage picture gallery from 1849, so 1858 falls inside that tenure. Purely as a style note (not affecting the verdict), the description passes over the two most striking things in the picture — the saturated blue mantle and the feigned oval — and no medium is stated in the source, so 'this oil' is an assumption, though a very safe one for a Russian academic Madonna of this date.

proposals.title: Buddhist Temple in Darjiling. Sikkim
proposals.currentDescription: A Buddhist temple at Darjeeling in the eastern Himalayas, its painted woodwork and prayer banners set against the mountains. Vereshchagin made the study during his Indian journey of 1874 to 1876, one of roughly 150 sketches from the trip, oil on canvas in the Tretyakov Gallery, Moscow.

issues.quote: one of roughly 150 sketches from the trip
issues.problem: A specific count with no backing in the record or the Commons metadata. It is a commonly repeated figure for Vereshchagin's Indian studies and is hedged with 'roughly', but it is not verifiable from anything supplied here.
issues.evidence: catalogue record and commons — neither mentions a number of studies

proposals.imageObservation: A small Himalayan temple with a thatched roof, whitewashed and red-banded walls and a painted, fringed valance over the porch, its finial against a deep blue sky; a row of tall poles carries white prayer flags, a snow range fills the distance at the right, and a few small figures sit and stand on the sunlit dirt forecourt.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The visual claims (painted woodwork, prayer banners, mountains behind), the 1874-76 Indian journey, and the Tretyakov Gallery all check out — the Tretyakov is in the record's own provenance and credit fields. The '150 sketches' figure is the only soft spot and is hedged, so I did not lower the verdict.

proposals.title: Буря над Евпаторией Айвазовский
proposals.currentDescription: A dramatic seascape by Russian marine painter Ivan Aivazovsky (1817–1900) depicting stormy weather over the port city of Yevpatoria on the Crimean coast. The work exemplifies Aivazovsky's mastery of turbulent seascapes and atmospheric effects. Housed in the Russian Museum collection.

issues.quote: exemplifies Aivazovsky's mastery of turbulent seascapes
issues.problem: Evaluative filler; the description never mentions the ships in distress, the red flag, the figures aboard or the burning sky, which are what the picture actually shows.
issues.evidence: image

proposals.imageObservation: A storm at the edge of a shore: a square-rigged ship heels hard over with a red flag streaming from its rigging and figures crowded on deck, other vessels founder in the spray behind it, breakers run up a pale beach in the right foreground, and the sky burns orange-red at the left and turns green-grey at the right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: All checkable claims hold: Aivazovsky's dates 1817-1900 are right, Yevpatoria is a Crimean port, and Commons files the work under 'Paintings by Ivan Aivazovsky in the Russian Museum'. Commons dates it 'before 1900' rather than 1900 exactly, which the description sensibly does not assert. Style rewrite would help; no accuracy defect.

proposals.title: Campo de trigo
proposals.currentDescription: A field of standing wheat under a broad sky, the grain laid in with quick yellow and green strokes and no incident to interrupt the view. Renoir painted the landscape in 1879, probably near Wargemont on the Bérard family estate in Normandy; it belongs to the Carmen Thyssen-Bornemisza Collection in Madrid.
proposals.imageObservation: A ripe wheat field filling the lower two-thirds of the canvas, a clump of slender trees at the left, a low wooded ridge behind and a white-clouded sky; no figures. Signed 'Renoir' and dated '79' at lower right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Verified: the Carmen Thyssen-Bornemisza / Museo Thyssen entry for this Wheatfield says it was probably painted around Wargemont, near Dieppe in Normandy, where Renoir spent the summer of 1879 on the Berard family estate, and notes the same absence of anecdote the description points to. The '79' in the signature corroborates the date.

proposals.title: The Entombment of Christ
proposals.currentDescription: Christ's lifeless body is lowered onto the anointing stone, his arm and shroud dropping toward the viewer. Painted for the Chiesa Nuova in Rome, the altarpiece compresses the mourners into a powerful diagonal lit by Caravaggio's signature raking shaft.
proposals.imageObservation: Large altarpiece: Christ's pale corpse is carried by a bearded man supporting his legs and a younger man taking his shoulders, lowered over the projecting corner of a stone slab; a white shroud spills over the edge toward the viewer and Christ's right arm hangs down. Three women behind - one veiled, one wiping her eyes, one with both arms flung upward - complete a diagonal against a black ground.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The hanging arm, the spilling shroud, the projecting anointing stone and the compressed diagonal of mourners are all in the frame. The altarpiece was painted for the Vittrice chapel in Santa Maria in Vallicella, the Chiesa Nuova, in Rome, matching the record's c. 1602 date. The description does not claim a present location, which is prudent: the original hangs in the Vatican Pinacoteca and a copy is in the church.

proposals.title: Der Bohnenesser.jpeg
proposals.currentDescription: A celebrated painting by Annibale Carracci created between 1584 and 1585, exemplifying the artist's naturalistic approach to genre scenes. The work depicts a humble figure eating beans, rendered with the careful attention to everyday life that characterized Carracci's innovative departure from Mannerist convention. This painting is now in the public domain and represents an important moment in the development of modern European art.

issues.quote: A celebrated painting by Annibale Carracci
issues.problem: Opens with an evaluative label rather than with what is in the frame; house style wants the first sentence to describe the picture.
issues.evidence: image — the description never mentions the straw hat, the table setting, the bread, wine or jug, or the sitter's outward gaze

issues.quote: represents an important moment in the development of modern European art
issues.problem: Empty superlative with no specific content; also 'This painting is now in the public domain' is licence boilerplate that belongs in the record, not the description.
issues.evidence: knowledge — no checkable assertion is made here

proposals.imageObservation: A peasant in a broad straw hat sits at a white-clothed table, spooning beans from a bowl and looking out at the viewer with his mouth open; bread rolls, spring onions, a pie or tart on a dish, a knife, a wine glass and a striped jug are laid out in front of him, with a barred window behind at left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Nothing factually wrong: the 1584-85 dating matches the Commons date field exactly, and the naturalistic-genre framing is standard Carracci art history. The description is however almost entirely generic and never describes the table, which is half the picture. A style-only rewrite would be an improvement but I did not classify it as an accuracy defect.

proposals.title: Solitary Tree
proposals.currentDescription: A weathered oak rises at the centre of a Bohemian valley at dawn, its dead crown set against luminous distant mountains. Friedrich uses the broken tree as a quiet emblem of endurance, paired with the morning panorama as one half of a meditation on the cycle of day and life.
proposals.imageObservation: Oil: a broad old oak stands alone at the centre of a green meadow above a pond, its upper branches bare and broken while the lower crown is still in leaf; a shepherd leans against the trunk with a flock of sheep beside him; yellow-green fields, a village and church spire in the middle distance, blue mountains and a bright morning sky behind.
proposals.reviewerNotes: 1822 and the title are confirmed by Commons; the picture's alternative German title (Dorflandschaft bei Morgenbeleuchtung, and the French label 'Paysage champetre, le matin' in the Commons metadata) supports 'at dawn', and the pairing with Moonrise by the Sea supports 'one half of a meditation on the cycle of day and life'. 'Bohemian valley' is the conventional identification of the Riesengebirge motif and I found nothing against it. The shepherd and sheep go unmentioned - an omission, not an error.

proposals.title: Le Printemps
proposals.currentDescription: A female personification of Spring stands with a garland of blossom, one of four season panels Cézanne signed 'Ingres'. He painted them about 1860 to 1861 for the salon alcove of the family estate, the Jas de Bouffan near Aix; the panels were later transferred to canvas and given to the Petit Palais, Paris.
proposals.imageObservation: Tall narrow panel: a barefoot woman in a red-orange gown, one shoulder bare, holds a long garland of flowers falling across her body; a stone pedestal with a leafy urn at upper right, hillside and blue sky behind; signed 'INGRES' in the lower right corner.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Checked the second sentence: the Four Seasons were painted on the plaster of the alcove in the grand salon of the Jas de Bouffan, later detached and mounted on canvas, and are at the Petit Palais (Paris Musees / Petit Palais pages; the panels came to the museum as a donation). The 'INGRES' signature is visible in the image.

proposals.title: The Sacrifice of Polyxena
proposals.currentDescription: Polyxena is led to the altar to appease the ghost of Achilles while her mother Hecuba reaches to restrain her and the soldier Neoptolemus lifts his sword. Le Brun painted the subject from Ovid's Metamorphoses in 1647, before his career as premier peintre to Louis XIV.
proposals.imageObservation: A young woman in white and blue with one breast bared is pulled forward by a helmeted soldier while an older woman in orange and green lunges after her from the right; a garlanded stone tomb-altar with a helmeted portrait relief stands at the left with a bearded priest beside it, a child holds a casket below, spears and a horse's head appear at the right, and a silver ewer and gilt stand fill the foreground corner.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Spot-check of a prior 'accurate' verdict. The Commons imageDescription independently gives the same reading (Ovid; Polyxena led to the altar to appease Achilles' ghost; her mother restraining her; Neoptolemus raising his sword; the infant with the incense chest and the priest). Date 1647 matches Commons; Le Brun became premier peintre to Louis XIV in 1664, so 'before his career as premier peintre' is right. The Met holds it per the Commons credit link, which the description does not claim either way.

proposals.title: Camille Monet sur son lit de mort
proposals.currentDescription: Monet painted his first wife within hours of her death from uterine cancer at age thirty-two, the brushwork dissolving her features into a veil of violet, grey and white. He later confessed unease at finding himself analysing her colour rather than mourning her.
proposals.imageObservation: A face barely emerges from a storm of violet, grey, blue and white brushstrokes; the head lies tilted on a pillow with what reads as a veil or sheet swept diagonally across the lower half of the canvas. Signed 'Claude Monet' at lower right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The Commons file lookup came back missing, so the source column is empty here and I judged this on the image, the record and established biography. Camille Doncieux died on 5 September 1879 at thirty-two, the cause usually given as uterine cancer, and Monet's own account to Clemenceau of catching himself registering the colours death laid on her face is the standard anecdote behind this canvas. The record's provenance (Musee d'Orsay, RF 1963 3) is not mentioned in the description but nothing stated is contradicted. Flagging the missing Commons record so a later pass knows the external check could not be run.

proposals.title: en
proposals.currentDescription: Boats crowd the harbour mouth of the Norman resort of Trouville, where Monet honeymooned with Camille in the summer of 1870. The pictures from that holiday — sand still embedded in some of the canvases — were the last he made before fleeing the war to London.

metadataIssues.proposed: Entrance to the Port of Trouville
metadataIssues.evidence: The title field has captured the language tag 'en' from the Commons objectName string; englishTitle already holds the real title.

proposals.imageObservation: A harbour mouth between two dark jetties under a grey-white sky: fishing boats with red-brown and white sails cluster in the channel, small figures walk along the right-hand jetty, and two anglers - one seated, one standing - fish from the near jetty in the foreground. Signed 'Claude Monet 70' lower left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Spot-check holds. Signed and dated 70 in the canvas itself; Monet married Camille in June 1870 and spent that summer at Trouville, and grains of sand embedded in the paint of the Trouville canvases are well documented. 'The last he made before fleeing the war to London' is the standard account and is phrased loosely enough to be safe. The description does not mention the Hungarian National Gallery, which the record's provenance block gives - an omission, not an error.

proposals.title: Google Art Project
proposals.currentDescription: Two young women in white summer dresses and straw hats sit in a small rowing boat, their figures reflected in the shimmering water beneath. Painted in 1887 and held by the National Museum of Western Art, Tokyo, the canvas presents its subjects from an elevated vantage point that flattens the scene into broad planes of colour, a compositional strategy Monet shared with contemporaries drawn to Japanese prints.

metadataIssues.evidence: commons | the file is 'Claude Monet - On the Boat - Google Art Project.jpg' and the objectName field gives the Japanese title 舟遊び; the stored title is a fragment of the filename

proposals.imageObservation: Two young women in white summer dresses and straw hats sit in a small green-and-white rowing boat seen steeply from above, one facing the viewer and one from behind holding an oar; the boat and figures are reflected in blue-violet water flecked with pink.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Everything checks: the 1887 date is signed in the picture and matches Commons, and the National Museum of Western Art, Tokyo, is in the record's own provenance block with inventory P.1959-0148. The high viewpoint and the Japanese-print connection are standard readings and not overstated. Only the catalogue title is broken.

proposals.title: Regnvær
proposals.currentDescription: Rain over Étretat: the Norman cliffs and arched rock recede behind a grey curtain of weather, the Channel rendered in broken slate strokes. Monet often returned to Étretat through the 1880s, attracted by its dramatic chalk geology under shifting marine light.
proposals.imageObservation: The Étretat cliff with its natural arch looms grey-violet through rain at the left, diagonal streaks of weather crossing the pale sky at the upper right, a choppy blue-green sea filling the middle and a strip of shingle beach across the foreground. Signed and dated 'Claude Monet 1886' at lower left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Re-checked as if fresh: the arched Falaise d'Aval, the rain and the 1886 date are all visible in the canvas itself, and Monet's repeated Étretat campaigns through the 1880s are uncontested. 'Broken slate strokes' is a slightly odd colour word for a sea painted in blue, green and white, but it describes the stroke character rather than making a factual claim, so I did not raise it as a finding. The description does not name the collection (National Museum, Oslo, NG.M.00368), which the record carries — an omission, not an error.

proposals.title: Tulip fields in Holland
proposals.currentDescription: Sweeping bands of red and violet tulips fill the foreground, with a windmill and farm buildings rising against a brisk cloudy sky. Monet visited the Dutch bulb fields in 1886 to paint these intensely saturated expanses of colour. The canvas, dated 1886, is held at the Musée d'Orsay, Paris.
proposals.imageObservation: Broad beds of scarlet, pink and violet tulips run across the foreground of a flat field; a windmill with dark sails and a cluster of red-roofed farm buildings stand along the horizon under a high sky of white and grey cloud; signed lower left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Colour bands, windmill, farm buildings and cloudy sky all match. Monet's 1886 trip to the Dutch bulb fields is well documented; the Musee d'Orsay attribution is supported by the file title and the 'Base Joconde' category, and realDimensions (81.5 x 65.5 cm, landscape) match the picture's format.

proposals.title: Vétheuil
proposals.currentDescription: A field of red poppies and summer grasses occupies the foreground, with tall poplars and cypresses framing the distant village of Vétheuil on the hillside. The Seine is glimpsed at the far right edge. Monet painted this sunlit meadow view in 1880, during his years living at Vétheuil; the canvas is in the Kelvingrove Art Gallery and Museum, Glasgow.
proposals.imageObservation: A foreground field of golden grasses shot through with red poppies; a tall poplar at the right and darker conifers left of centre; a wooded slope behind with a cluster of pale buildings on it; a patch of blue water visible at the right edge through the foliage; a broad sky of dappled blue and cream. Signed lower right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Spot-check of a prior 'fabricated-fixed'. I checked the two riskiest details by zooming: there is a distinct blue passage at the right edge that reads as water, and there is a cluster of buildings including a white structure on the hillside, so 'the Seine is glimpsed at the far right edge' and 'the distant village' are both defensible. Kelvingrove and 1880 come from the record's own provenance and Commons.

proposals.title: Correggio
proposals.currentDescription: A three-quarter-length portrait of a seated woman in a dark overmantle and white chemise, holding a small dish, set before an open landscape. The work is signed with the Latinised "Anton(ius) Laet(us)" and has traditionally been identified as either Veronica Gambara or Ginevra Rangoni. Painted between 1517 and 1518, it is held at the Hermitage in Saint Petersburg and represents Correggio's early mature manner.
proposals.imageObservation: A woman shown to below the waist, turned three-quarters, in a white chemise with full sleeves and a dark brown overmantle, a gold chain at her neck and a braided pale headdress; she holds a shallow bronze dish with an inscription round its rim; laurel and ivy behind at the left, an open landscape and blue sky at the right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Spot-check of a prior 'minor-fixed'. The Commons image description independently carries the signature ('Anton(ius) Laet(us)'), the Gambara/Rangoni identifications, the Hermitage location and the 1517-18 dating, and the record's 87.5 x 103 cm is consistent with the '102 x 86' quoted there.

proposals.title: Creación de Adán
proposals.currentDescription: One of the most iconic frescoes in the history of Western art, painted by Michelangelo on the Sistine Chapel ceiling in Vatican City. This scene depicts God breathing life into Adam, the first human, and is celebrated for its masterful depiction of human anatomy and the moment of divine creation. The work remains among the most recognized and studied paintings in existence.

issues.quote: One of the most iconic frescoes in the history of Western art
issues.problem: Empty superlative opening; house style asks the first sentence to say what is in the frame.
issues.evidence: knowledge — house style in the corpus is plain description first, no ranking language

issues.quote: celebrated for its masterful depiction of human anatomy
issues.problem: Evaluative boilerplate rather than a grounded observation.
issues.evidence: knowledge

issues.quote: This scene depicts God breathing life into Adam, the first human
issues.problem: The only visual statement is a title gloss; the picture's actual content (the two nearly touching hands, the red mantle full of figures, the reclining nude on the rock) is never described.
issues.evidence: image — the near-touching hands and the figure-filled mantle are the whole composition

proposals.imageObservation: A fresco panel on a vaulted ceiling: a reclining nude male on a rocky green ground at the left reaches his left hand toward the outstretched right hand of a white-bearded figure who floats at the right inside a billowing red-violet mantle crowded with nude figures; surrounding ceiling figures and painted architecture frame the scene, and the plaster shows visible cracks.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Every factual claim holds: Michelangelo, Sistine Chapel ceiling, Vatican, and the c.1511-12 date all match the record and the image. Verdict left at accurate because only style is at fault, per the rule that style does not move the verdict — but this one is a good candidate for a style-only rewrite that opens on the two hands and drops the three ranking phrases. Minor nit: the last sentence calls a fresco a 'painting'.

proposals.title: Portrait of the Comtesse Vilain XIIII and her Daughter Louise
proposals.currentDescription: The Comtesse Vilain XIIII, identified by the source as Sophie-Louise-Zoé de Feltz (1780–1853), sits in a deep navy velvet dress with white lace frills and a bold orange shawl, her young daughter Marie-Louise standing before her. David painted the double portrait in 1816 during his Belgian exile, one of the most intimate of his late commissions. The neutral interior background is characteristic of his Brussels portrait style.

issues.quote: one of the most intimate of his late commissions
issues.problem: An unsupported superlative; nothing in the record or the source ranks this against David's other Brussels portraits.
issues.evidence: catalogue record

proposals.imageObservation: A seated woman in a dark navy velvet dress with a wide white lace collar and an orange-red shawl draped over her arms and lap, a small red-haired girl in a white empire dress leaning against her knee; plain brown ground, signed and dated at the right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Sitter names and dates come straight from the Commons caption (Sophie-Louise-Zoé de Feltz, 1780-1853, with her daughter Marie-Louise Vilain, 1811-1883), and the description is careful to attribute them to the source. The signature in the picture reads 'L. David 1816 Brux.', which confirms both the date and the Brussels exile. Only the superlative overreaches, which is why I left the verdict at accurate rather than minor.

proposals.title: Death and the Maiden Baldung
proposals.currentDescription: A tempera painting on limewood by German Renaissance artist Hans Baldung Grien, depicting the allegorical encounter between personified Death and a young maiden. The work exemplifies the Northern Renaissance fascination with the danse macabre theme, exploring mortality and youthful vitality through an intimate compositional arrangement.

issues.quote: depicting the allegorical encounter between personified Death and a young maiden
issues.problem: The description never says what is literally in the frame - the nude weeping woman, Death gripping her hair, the painted inscription and date at the top edge - so the reader learns the theme but not the picture.
issues.evidence: image | the frame contains a nude woman, a corpse-figure pulling her hair by the handful, and a legible inscription HIE MVST DV YN 1517

issues.quote: The work exemplifies the Northern Renaissance fascination with the danse macabre theme
issues.problem: Catalogue boilerplate; 'exemplifies ... through an intimate compositional arrangement' asserts nothing checkable.
issues.evidence: knowledge | house style asks for plain description plus grounded context

proposals.imageObservation: Vertical panel: a nude young woman with tears on her cheeks stands frontally while a shrivelled corpse-figure of Death behind her seizes a hank of her long hair; a green cloth falls behind her; the top edge carries the painted inscription HIE MVST DV YN and the date 1517.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Every substantive claim holds: Commons categorises the file 'Tempera on lime', confirming tempera on limewood, and the artist and 1517 date match both the record and the painted inscription. Only style is weak - it is pure theme with no visual content. Left as accurate per the rule that style does not lower the verdict; a rewrite would be an improvement, not a correction. The panel is in the Kunstmuseum Basel (Commons category 'Museum Faesch'), which the description does not claim either way.

proposals.title: Portuguese Woman
proposals.currentDescription: A woman in embroidered folk dress stands amid a swirl of concentric chromatic discs, exotic plants, and stacked vessels, the figure and environment dissolving into interlocking arcs of colour. Robert Delaunay painted this large canvas in 1916, applying the Simultanism he had developed with Sonia Delaunay to a subject rooted in the couple's wartime stay in Portugal.
proposals.imageObservation: A woman in a patterned bodice and long red skirt leans forward over a large yellow bowl at the upper right, surrounded by concentric colour discs, broad-leaved plants, melons and stacked vessels; figure and setting alike dissolve into interlocking arcs of red, yellow, blue and green. Signed at lower right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: No claim is contradicted. The Columbus Museum of Art version measures about 53.5 × 61.4 in (roughly 136 × 156 cm), so 'large canvas' is fair; the record's own sourceLinks point at columbusmuseum.org and the Commons categories place it there. Simultanism, Sonia Delaunay and the couple's wartime years in Portugal and Spain are all standard. One nit I did not raise as a finding: the woman is bending forward and pouring — the picture is also known as 'Woman Pouring' — so 'stands amid' understates the central action; a future rewrite could say so.

proposals.title: Despair
proposals.currentDescription: This is a painting featuring a figure standing on a bridge, gazing down, seemingly lost in thought. The background consists of a dramatic, swirling sky with striking red, yellow, and blue colors. The figure is dressed in dark clothing, and their posture and the expression on their face convey a sense of melancholy or introspection.

issues.quote: This is a painting featuring a figure standing on a bridge
issues.problem: Style only: the text is copied verbatim from the Commons image description, opens with 'This is a painting featuring', and gives no date, medium or collection. Verdict unaffected - nothing in it is wrong.
issues.evidence: commons imageDescription is the same text, one sentence longer.

proposals.imageObservation: Oil: a dark-clad figure with a bowed head and a sallow yellow-green face fills the lower foreground beside a bridge railing; two smaller figures walk away up the bridge at the left; a fjord with a curving shoreline behind, and a sky banded in red, orange and yellow with green-blue at the top corners.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Two further figures on the bridge go unmentioned and the sky is banded rather than 'swirling', but neither is a false statement. Worth flagging to a style pass: this description is a copy of Commons boilerplate rather than house-style prose, and omits that the picture is in the Munch Museum and is a forerunner of The Scream.

proposals.title: Дети племени солонов
proposals.currentDescription: A painting by Russian artist Vasily Vereshchagin from his Turkestan series, depicting children from the Solon people. The work is part of Vereshchagin's ethnographic and orientalist documentation of Central Asian communities, currently housed in the Tretyakov Gallery, Moscow.

issues.quote: A painting by Russian artist Vasily Vereshchagin from his Turkestan series, depicting children from the Solon people.
issues.problem: The description never says what is in the frame - two children in a flowering meadow, one seen from behind with a long braid, the other in a blue jacket. It is catalogue boilerplate plus a series label.
issues.evidence: image; corpus house style asks the first sentence to describe the picture

proposals.imageObservation: Two children stand in a flowering summer meadow: one seen from behind, bare-torsoed with a long black braid, holding something small in his cupped hand; the other faces him in a blue jacket and pale trousers, head bowed. Low hills and pale sky behind.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Turkestan series and Tretyakov are both supported by the Commons categories. Nothing is false, so the verdict stays accurate, but this one would benefit from a house-style rewrite that actually describes the two children; I did not write one because the rules reserve replacements for minor/major/fabricated.

proposals.title: Deux jeunes amies qui s'embrassent
proposals.currentDescription: "Deux jeunes amies qui s'embrassent" ("Two Young Female Friends Kissing") Painting created by French artist Louis-Léopold Boilly circa 1789-1793. Wiltshire, The Ramsbury Manor Foundation

issues.quote: Painting created by French artist Louis-Léopold Boilly circa 1789-1793.
issues.problem: The whole description is the Commons caption plus a dangling credit fragment ('Wiltshire, The Ramsbury Manor Foundation'); it never describes the scene.
issues.evidence: commons — imageDescription is identical to the description text, including the trailing owner line.

proposals.imageObservation: Two young women embrace and kiss in a panelled interior, one in a white gown, the other in a pale green dress with a red ribbon in her hair; a small table at left carries a hat with a blue bow, a bottle and a red wrap, and an empty chair stands at right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: No false claim: the subject matches the title, the date range and the Ramsbury Manor Foundation ownership both come from the Commons record. The trailing credit fragment reads as a data-entry artefact rather than prose; worth a rewrite for style but not a factual correction.

proposals.title: Xiao and Xiang Rivers
proposals.currentDescription: A detail from a long handscroll associated with the Southern Tang master, depicting the misted reaches of the Xiao and Xiang rivers in Hunan. Dong Yuan's soft hemp-fibre brushstrokes and graded ink washes established the canonical southern landscape mode followed for centuries.
proposals.imageObservation: Ink on silk, browned with age: a river landscape with rounded hills built from long parallel texture strokes, a wooded spit with houses and a pavilion among trees, a small boat with two standing figures poling on open water, reeds across the foreground.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Spot-check of a prior 'accurate' verdict: still accurate. Commons confirms it is a detail of the Xiao and Xiang Rivers handscroll in the Palace Museum, Beijing; the Xiao and Xiang are in Hunan; Dong Yuan served the Southern Tang; and the hemp-fibre (pima cun) texture strokes the text names are plainly visible.

proposals.title: dürer seven headed dragon
proposals.currentDescription: A dramatic woodcut from Albrecht Dürer's Apocalypse series depicting the vision described in the Book of Revelation - a woman clothed in sunlight and standing on the moon confronted by a seven-headed dragon. This masterwork from 1497-1498 exemplifies Dürer's technical mastery of the woodcut medium and his ability to capture apocalyptic grandeur through intricate line work and bold composition.

issues.quote: This masterwork from 1497-1498 exemplifies Dürer's technical mastery of the woodcut medium and his ability to capture apocalyptic grandeur through intricate line work and bold composition.
issues.problem: Second sentence is hype and boilerplate ('masterwork', 'exemplifies... mastery', 'apocalyptic grandeur') and adds no grounded information; house style prefers plain factual context.
issues.evidence: house style / description text itself

proposals.imageObservation: Hand-coloured woodcut: a crowned, winged woman in a yellow robe standing on a crescent moon inside a sunburst, facing a seven-headed dragon whose crowned heads spout water; God the Father enthroned in clouds above with angels and putti carrying a child, a starry sky at upper right, the AD monogram on a tablet at bottom centre.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Medium, subject, series and date all check out (Commons dates the sheet 1497-1498, matching the record year 1497). The impression reproduced here is hand-coloured, which the description does not mention - an omission, not an error. Only the hype sentence is worth touching if someone rewrites.

proposals.title: East Cowes Castle
proposals.currentDescription: Racing yachts heel into the wind as they beat to windward through a choppy Solent, with the wooded shoreline of East Cowes Castle beyond. Turner painted this oil on canvas and a companion view for the architect John Nash after staying at the castle, Nash's residence on the Isle of Wight, during the Cowes regatta of 1827, and exhibited both at the Royal Academy in 1828. This canvas is in the Indianapolis Museum of Art; its pendant, showing the regatta boats starting for their moorings, is in the Victoria and Albert Museum.

issues.quote: with the wooded shoreline of East Cowes Castle beyond
issues.problem: The middle distance dissolves into haze, masts and what read as buildings; I cannot make out woods or the castle itself, so 'wooded' is an addition the reproduction does not support.
issues.evidence: image

proposals.imageObservation: A bright, high-keyed marine: yachts under tall cream sails heel over in a short green sea, a crowded open boat full of figures in the centre foreground, a red buoy bobbing at lower left, and a hazy line of shipping, masts and shore buildings across the middle distance under a large cloud-filled sky.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The whole factual apparatus checks out: Nash commissioned two oils from Turner after Turner stayed at East Cowes Castle for the 1827 regatta; both were shown at the Royal Academy in 1828; this one is in the Indianapolis Museum of Art and the pendant, 'the Regatta Starting for their Moorings', is in the V&A. Only the word 'wooded' is unsupported, which is not enough to lower the verdict.

proposals.title: le tub
proposals.currentDescription: A nude crouches in a shallow zinc tub sponging her neck, beside a marble-topped washstand whose pitcher and brushes are seen from a sharply tilted angle. Degas drew the pastel on heavy wove paper in 1886 and showed it at the Eighth Impressionist Exhibition that May; the sheet entered the Musee d'Orsay as one of his most accomplished bather compositions.

issues.quote: marble-topped washstand
issues.problem: The tilted surface at the right is a pale grey shelf or table top; whether it is marble is not something the reproduction settles, and no source I checked specifies it.
issues.evidence: image | web:https://www.musee-orsay.fr/en/artworks/le-tub-2086 - record gives pastel and support, not the furniture

issues.quote: as one of his most accomplished bather compositions
issues.problem: Evaluative filler tacked onto the acquisition clause; it also blurs the fact that the pastel came to the Louvre with the Camondo bequest and passed to the Musee d'Orsay in 1986.
issues.evidence: house style

proposals.imageObservation: A red-haired nude crouches in a shallow round zinc tub, one hand braced in the water, the other sponging the back of her neck; at the right a pale shelf seen from a steeply tilted angle carries a copper jug, a large pitcher, a hairbrush, a comb and a red cloth. Signed and dated Degas 86 at the lower right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Ledger says accurate and the substance holds: pastel, 1886, shown in the Eighth Impressionist Exhibition (opened 15 May 1886), Musee d'Orsay RF 4046, 60 x 83 cm as in the row. 'Heavy wove paper' matches the support given in English-language sources, though French records say 'carton' - worth knowing, not worth changing. No rewrite proposed; the two nits are low severity.

proposals.title: The Dead Christ with Angels
proposals.currentDescription: Two angels support the slumped body of the dead Christ, his pallid torso lit against shadow. Manet borrows a traditional Lamentation type but flattens modeling and exposes brushwork in a way that scandalized the 1864 Salon, where critics also faulted the placement of the side wound on the wrong flank.
proposals.imageObservation: The dead Christ sits slumped on a white winding sheet with his legs forward, supported by two winged angels - one in dark red at the left with grey wings, resting her head on her hand, one in orange with blue wings at the right. A wound is visible high on the torso, and stones and a snake lie on the ground below. Signed lower left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Spot-check of a prior 'accurate' verdict holds. Two angels, correct; the Salon of 1864 showing and the contemporary criticism of the wound's placement are both well documented, and the wound in the image is indeed on the figure's left side, opposite the traditional side. Met attribution matches the record's provenance block (accession 29.100.51).

proposals.title: Eduard Gaertner Berlin Bruederstrasse
proposals.currentDescription: The Brüderstraße on the Spreeinsel in Berlin-Mitte recedes between rows of plastered townhouses toward the tower of the Petrikirche. Gaertner painted the view in 1863, still working in the precise Berlin Biedermeier vedute mode he had practised since the 1820s.
proposals.imageObservation: A street view running back between rows of four- and five-storey plastered houses with shopfronts toward a tall brick neo-Gothic church spire; a mounted rider, a carriage, a two-horse team, children and pedestrians occupy the cobbled roadway. Signed and dated at lower right; the reproduction is a photograph taken through an arched frame, which darkens the upper corners.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The Commons imageDescription independently identifies the view as the Bruderstrasse on the Spreeinsel in Berlin-Mitte with the Petrikirche behind, matching the description exactly, and gives 1863. The spire in the picture is the neo-Gothic Petrikirche rebuilt in the 1850s, consistent with an 1863 date. Gaertner's Berlin vedute practice does go back to the 1820s. Note for a viewer, not a finding: the reproduction is a photograph of the framed painting, so the dark arch at the top belongs to the frame, not the picture.

proposals.title: The Colossus
proposals.currentDescription: A naked giant rises behind a mountain ridge as a panicked crowd and herds flee across the plain below. Long attributed to Goya and tied to the Peninsular War, the picture stages collective terror with the bituminous darkness of his late, troubled imagination.
proposals.imageObservation: Dark oil painting: a huge muscular nude male figure, seen from behind with fists raised, rises above a bank of cloud behind a dark ridge; on the plain below, crowds of tiny figures, horses, carts and cattle scatter in all directions.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The scene reads exactly as described, including the fleeing herds. The hedge 'Long attributed to Goya' is the right call and matches the Commons artist field 'Attributed to Francisco Goya'; the Prado reattributed the picture to Asensio Julia in 2008, so a later editor may want the description to go further than the hedge - as written, the trailing phrase 'his late, troubled imagination' quietly reasserts Goya after hedging. Not enough to downgrade. 'Bituminous' reads as a description of the tone, not a pigment analysis.

proposals.title: Eugène Murer
proposals.currentDescription: The pastry cook and collector Eugène Murer, born Hyacinthe-Eugène Meunier, shown bust-length in a dark coat. Renoir painted the portrait in 1877; Murer eventually gathered some 122 Impressionist works, including fifteen by Renoir, and the canvas is now in the Metropolitan Museum of Art.
proposals.imageObservation: A bust-length portrait of a young red-bearded man in a dark coat, white collar and loosely tied violet cravat, his left hand raised to the side of his head, against a mottled green-and-tan ground; signed 'Renoir' upper right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The '122 works ... including 15 by Renoir' figure matches the Met's own catalogue text for this portrait (by 1887 Murer had amassed some 122 works by his painter friends, 15 of them Renoirs) - web:metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/438011 via search. Description omits the raised hand, which is the picture's most distinctive gesture; worth adding in any future edit but not an error.

proposals.title: Portrait of Marguerite Khnopff
proposals.currentDescription: Khnopff portrays his sister Marguerite, a recurring presence in his work, with the cool, hieratic detachment that defines his Symbolist portraiture. The pale palette and flattened space distil her into an emblem of withdrawn, idealised femininity rather than likeness alone.

issues.quote: Khnopff portrays his sister Marguerite, a recurring presence in his work
issues.problem: Nothing in the description says what is in the frame — the white high-collared dress, the long gloves, the doorway and the near-empty grey wall are the picture, and all of it is replaced by interpretation.
issues.evidence: image

proposals.imageObservation: A full-length standing portrait of a young woman in a long white dress with a high buttoned collar and long pale gloves, her red-brown hair pinned up, standing in a doorway of a pale blue-grey panelled interior with a brown floor and a gold disc on the wall at the left; an inscription runs along the top edge.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The one checkable fact — that the sitter is the artist's sister Marguerite — is confirmed by Commons ('Portrait of the artist's sister'), and 1887 matches. The rest is interpretation, which cannot be contradicted but also cannot be verified; per the rule that style does not move the verdict I left it accurate. A rewrite opening on the white dress and the doorway would bring it into house style.

proposals.title: Flaming June
proposals.currentDescription: A young woman sleeps curled in a translucent orange-saffron gown, one arm thrown over her head, a sprig of oleander above her. Leighton painted the oil in 1895; after decades of neglect it was bought for the Museo de Arte de Ponce in Puerto Rico in the 1960s. The folded pose fills a square format, the fabric worked in deep orange against a marble parapet and sea.
proposals.imageObservation: A square canvas: a young woman sleeps curled up on a marble bench, knees drawn to her chest, her right arm bent above her head, wrapped in a translucent orange-saffron gown over gold and dark red drapery; behind her a marble parapet, a glittering sunlit sea, and a sprig of flowering oleander at the upper right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: All four visual claims (curled sleeping pose, translucent orange gown, arm over the head, oleander sprig above) match, as do the square format, the marble parapet and the sea. The Ponce acquisition in the 1960s after decades of neglect is the standard, well-documented history (bought by Luis A. Ferré for the Museo de Arte de Ponce in 1963) and Commons carries the 'Museo de Arte de Ponce' category. Date 1895 matches Commons.

proposals.title: Fourth muscle man
proposals.currentDescription: A woodcut from Andreas Vesalius's De humani corporis fabrica, the fourth in the famous sequence of muscle men that strip away the body's musculature layer by layer; here dissected muscles hang loose from the figure's arms as he stands in a landscape of hills and buildings that continues from plate to plate across the series. The blocks, cut for the book's first edition of 1543 and attributed to artists in Titian's circle, transformed anatomical illustration. This impression comes from the 1555 second edition and is in the Wellcome Collection, London.

metadataIssues.evidence: commons category 'De humani corporis fabrica 1555'; the printed page number 221 in Liber II is consistent with the enlarged second edition rather than the 1543 first

metadataIssues.proposed: After Andreas Vesalius (blocks attributed to the circle of Titian / Jan Stephan van Calcar)
metadataIssues.evidence: commons objectName 'Fourth muscle man, by Vesalius.'; the attribution of the blocks is traditional and should stay hedged

proposals.imageObservation: A woodcut écorché: a flayed male figure stands frontally in a landscape with a walled town and hills behind, superficial muscles cut and left hanging in long flaps from both arms and from the knees. Headline across the top reads 'HVMANI FABRICA LIBER II' with the page number 221 and 'QVARTA MVSCVLORVM TABVLA' at the upper right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The printed heading confirms this is the fourth muscle table of Book II, and the flayed muscles hanging from the arms and the continuous landscape are both visible. The 1555 second edition and the Wellcome Collection are both supported by the Commons record (category 'De humani corporis fabrica 1555'; Wellcome credit line). The attribution of the blocks to artists in Titian's circle is traditional and correctly hedged in the description.

proposals.title: Susanna at Her Bath
proposals.currentDescription: The biblical Susanna twists modestly at her bath, surprised by the elders whose presence is implied beyond the frame. Hayez handles the polished nude in the National Gallery, London, with a sculptural finish indebted to Canova and the warm tonalities of his Venetian training.
proposals.imageObservation: A nude woman seen from behind sits on white drapery at the edge of a dark pool, twisting to look back over her right shoulder, one hand drawn up to her breast; ivy trails down the warm ochre stone wall behind her and an evening sky glows through trees at the upper right. No other figure is shown.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Spot-check of an earlier 'accurate' verdict: it holds. The elders are indeed absent from the frame, which is what the description says. The National Gallery, London is confirmed by both the record's provenance (inventory L1009) and the Commons credit. Hayez trained at the Venice Accademia and worked in Rome under Canova's patronage, so both the Canova and the Venetian-training remarks are well-founded art history rather than invention.

proposals.title: Self-portrait
proposals.currentDescription: A direct self-portrait set against a dark ground, the painter holding his palette and brushes. Oil on canvas, 108.9 by 71.1 cm, executed in 1865 to 1866 and held by the Art Institute of Chicago, which purchased it in 1962. Bazille was in his mid-twenties when he painted it.

issues.quote: Bazille was in his mid-twenties when he painted it
issues.problem: Bazille was born in December 1841, so he was 23 turning 24 in 1865-66 - early rather than mid twenties. Borderline, not worth rewriting on its own.
issues.evidence: knowledge - Bazille b. 6 December 1841

proposals.imageObservation: A bearded young man in a white shirt and dark waistcoat stands turned in three-quarter view against a dark green ground, holding a loaded palette and brushes in his left hand and a brush in his right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Verified against the Art Institute of Chicago record: Self-Portrait, 1865-66, oil on canvas, 108.9 x 71.1 cm, accession 1962.336, acquired 1962 with restricted gift funds (artic.edu/artworks/110661). 'Purchased in 1962' is a fair summary of that credit line. No rewrite proposed.

proposals.title: L'atelier de Bazille
proposals.currentDescription: The painter's studio at 9 rue de la Condamine in the Batignolles quarter of Paris, hung with canvases and peopled by his circle, Bazille himself shown at the easel. Painted in 1870; Manet contributed the figure of Bazille, and the work has been in the Musée d'Orsay since 1986.
proposals.imageObservation: A grey-walled studio hung with framed canvases around a tall curtained window; a tall man holding a palette stands before an easel with two men beside him, another leans on the staircase at the left, a fifth sits below it, and a sixth plays an upright piano at the right beside a pink sofa and a lit stove. Signed 'F. Bazille 1870' at lower right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Address, date, Manet's contribution of the standing Bazille figure, and the Musée d'Orsay transfer in 1986 are all standard and uncontested; the signature in the image confirms 1870 and the Commons categories confirm the Orsay. No visual claim is contradicted.

proposals.title: Still Life with Fish
proposals.currentDescription: A still life of fish laid out on a kitchen table. Oil on canvas, painted in 1866 and held by the Detroit Institute of Arts. Bazille took up still life repeatedly in the mid-1860s, treating fish, game and a heron in turn.
proposals.imageObservation: A still life on a dark ground: a large carp and a smaller pike lie on a rumpled white cloth over a yellow-ochre table, with a basket of mussels or shellfish at the upper left. Signed 'F. Bazille' in red at lower right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Date, medium and the Detroit Institute of Arts are all confirmed by the Commons record (categories include 'French paintings in the Detroit Institute of Arts' and 'Still Life with Fish (1988.9)'). Bazille's mid-1860s still lifes of fish, game and a heron are well documented. The basket of shellfish goes unmentioned but nothing stated is wrong.

proposals.title: La Robe Rose
proposals.currentDescription: A young woman in a pink-and-white striped dress seen from behind, seated on a wall and looking out over the sunlit village of Castelnau near Montpellier. Oil on canvas, 147 by 110 cm, painted in 1864 and now in the Musée d'Orsay, Paris. The sitter is Bazille's cousin Thérèse des Hours.
proposals.imageObservation: A young woman in a pink-and-white striped dress sits on a low stone wall with her back to the viewer, head turned in profile, looking across to a sunlit hill village with a church tower; dark cypresses and a pine frame the view; signed F. Bazille at lower right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Everything holds: pose, dress, wall, village view; Commons carries the dimensions 147 x 110 cm and the Musée d'Orsay attribution, and the 1864 date matches the record. The sitter identification (the artist's cousin Thérèse des Hours) and the setting (Castelnau, near Montpellier) are the standard, long-established readings of this picture. Worth noting the record's realDimensions is null while Commons states 147 x 110 cm, if the project wants to backfill.

proposals.title: Young Woman with Peonies
proposals.currentDescription: A Black woman holding out a bouquet of pink-and-white peonies beside a basket of tulips, roses and lilac, posed as a flower seller. Oil on canvas, 60 by 75 cm, painted in 1870 and now in the National Gallery of Art, Washington; a related version is at the Musée Fabre.
proposals.imageObservation: A Black woman in a striped headscarf and pale blouse holds out a spray of pink-and-white peonies in her right hand; a broad basket of tulips, narcissi, roses and lilac fills the foreground and a second bank of flowers stands at the right. Signed and dated F. Bazille 1870 at the upper right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Subject, flowers and the 1870 date (inscribed on the canvas) all check out; NGA is confirmed by the Commons credit and the accession category 1983.1.6, and the second version at the Musee Fabre, Montpellier, is well documented. 'Beside a basket' is slightly off - the main basket is in front of her - but the baskets flanking her make it defensible.

proposals.title: Frederic Leighton
proposals.currentDescription: Frederic Leighton seated in his Academician's gown, left elbow hooked over the chair back, hands loosely clasped. Watts painted this oil from sittings in 1881, the year Leighton sat for the work now in the National Portrait Gallery, London (NPG 1049). It is one of three portraits Watts made of his friend across their long acquaintance.

issues.quote: from sittings in 1881
issues.problem: The date 1881 is confirmed, but 'from sittings' is an added specific that no source states.
issues.evidence: web:npg.org.uk - NPG's own entry gives the date and pose but says nothing about sittings

proposals.imageObservation: A bearded, grey-haired man sits in near profile facing right, in a loose brown gown over a white collar and dark red tie, against a plain brown ground; one hand rests on his lap or a chair arm at the lower right, a green upholstered chair back shows behind him, and a small table with white papers stands at the lower left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: I nearly filed this as a contradiction: at this reproduction size only one hand is legible and it looks unclasped. But the National Portrait Gallery's own entry for NPG 1049 describes the sitter 'wearing his Academician's gown, with his left elbow hooked over the back of the chair and hands loosely clasped upon his lap', and calls it 'one of three images of Leighton painted by George Frederic Watts'. The description is a close paraphrase of that entry, so all three of its distinctive claims - gown, pose, three portraits, NPG 1049 - are museum-sourced and correct. The second sentence is circular in phrasing ('painted this oil ... in 1881, the year Leighton sat for the work now in the NPG' - it is the same work), which is worth tidying but is not a factual fault.

proposals.title: Cimabue's Celebrated Madonna is carried in Procession through the Streets of Florence
proposals.currentDescription: A long procession bears Cimabue's altarpiece of the Madonna through Florence toward Santa Maria Novella, the painter Cimabue leading with the boy Giotto. Leighton painted this over two metres tall and more than five metres wide in Rome between 1853 and 1855; Queen Victoria bought it on the opening day of the 1855 Royal Academy exhibition for 600 guineas.
proposals.imageObservation: A very wide frieze-like procession moving left to right along a Florentine street: a laurel-crowned man in white robes leads a boy in dark hose by the hand, musicians and richly dressed onlookers crowd both sides, and the framed altarpiece is carried under a tall garlanded canopy at the right, with cypresses and a walled garden behind.
proposals.reviewerNotes: All four checkable claims hold: the scale (231.8 × 520.7 cm — over two metres tall, more than five metres wide), painting in Rome 1853–55, and Queen Victoria's purchase on the first day of the 1855 Royal Academy exhibition for 600 guineas are confirmed by the National Gallery record and the Wikipedia entry. The Santa Maria Novella destination is the traditional subject of the picture.

proposals.title: Portrait of May Sartoris
proposals.currentDescription: May Sartoris, about fifteen, stands in a dark riding habit with a red scarf and a wide black hat, a felled tree at her side. Leighton painted the portrait around 1860; the oil measures 152.1 by 90.2 cm and is held in the Kimbell Art Museum, Fort Worth.
proposals.imageObservation: A full-length portrait of a girl standing on a pale path: wide black plumed hat, black velvet jacket over a dark teal skirt, a long red scarf down her front, brown gloves and a riding crop; a felled tree with dried leaves lies at the left, a rock at the right, and a green hillside with a distant windmill behind.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Verified: the Kimbell Art Museum holds the picture, dated c. 1860, oil on canvas, 152.1 x 90.2 cm, and its catalogue says May was about fifteen; the felled tree is in the picture. Sources: kimbellart.org/collection/acf-196403 and the Commons category 'Google Art Project works in Kimbell Art Museum'.

proposals.title: The Garden of the Hesperides
proposals.currentDescription: Three nymphs recline beneath an apple tree, the serpent Ladon coiled around its trunk to guard the golden fruit that was Hera's gift. Leighton painted the tondo about 1892; it is held by the Lady Lever Art Gallery in Port Sunlight. The circular format sets the sleeping figures within the curve of the tree's foliage.
proposals.imageObservation: A circular painting: three women in orange, cream-pink and olive-green drapery sleep entwined beneath a tree hung with golden fruit, a large dark serpent coiling round the trunk and across them; one holds a lyre, a white heron stands among flowers at the lower left, and blue sea shows through on both sides.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Tondo format, three figures, serpent, golden fruit all match. The Lady Lever Art Gallery (Port Sunlight) attribution and the c.1892 date are confirmed by independent sources; the golden apples as Hera's gift is also what the Commons imageDescription says. The lyre goes unmentioned — an omission only.

proposals.title: The Return of Persephone
proposals.currentDescription: Hermes lifts Persephone up from the underworld toward her mother Demeter, who reaches down through a gap of light at the cave mouth. Leighton painted the oil in 1891 and it hangs in Leeds Art Gallery. The figures form a single rising diagonal from the dark earth into the bright opening above.
proposals.imageObservation: Hermes, in a winged cap and blue cloak and holding a gold caduceus, rises through a dark rock cleft carrying a pale, limp Persephone in yellow and pink drapery whose arms reach upward; above and to the left Demeter stands on a ledge in orange-red robes against a bright cloudy sky, one arm raised and the other reaching down.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Iconography, date and collection all check out: Commons categories include '1891 oil on canvas paintings' and 'Mythological paintings in Leeds City Art Gallery', plus 'paintings of Mercurius (Hermes)' and 'paintings of Ceres (Demeter)'. The rising-diagonal reading is a fair description of the composition.

proposals.title: Perseus and Andromeda
proposals.currentDescription: Andromeda is chained naked to the rocks while the dragon spreads dark wings over her and Perseus dives in from above on the winged horse Pegasus. Leighton painted the oil in 1891; it entered the Walker Art Gallery in Liverpool. The arched composition wraps the monster's body around the upper edge like a canopy.

issues.quote: Andromeda is chained naked to the rocks
issues.problem: She is partly draped — a substantial fall of white cloth covers her hips and legs — and I cannot make out a chain at this resolution. 'Chained naked' is the standard iconography of the subject but overstates what the reproduction shows.
issues.evidence: image
