proposals.imageObservation: A tall upright canvas: Andromeda crouches against a dark rock in a narrow sea inlet, her torso bare and white drapery slipping around her hips and legs, her red hair falling loose; the dragon's dark grey wings arch right across the top of the composition like a canopy and its clawed forelimb, breathing fire, grips the rock at right. High above, in a burst of pale light, Perseus rides Pegasus and draws his bow. Sea and cliffs at left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Everything else holds against the image and the Commons record: the dragon's canopy of wings, Perseus on Pegasus overhead, the 1891 date and the Walker Art Gallery, Liverpool (Commons category 'Perseus and Andromeda (Frederic Leighton - Walker Art Gallery)'). I left the verdict at accurate because 'chained naked' is conventional for the subject and I could not rule the chain out; a cautious editor might soften it to 'bound' and 'partly draped'.

proposals.title: Memories
proposals.currentDescription: A half-length young woman in a black and gold dress turns to one side, her head resting against her hand. The model was Edith Pullen, sister of Leighton's regular model Dorothy Dene; the picture dates to 1883. Leighton kept his contours smooth and his palette restrained in the manner of his classicising portraiture.

issues.quote: The model was Edith Pullen, sister of Leighton's regular model Dorothy Dene
issues.problem: The source record identifies the sitter as Dorothy Dene herself, not a sister. The name is also misspelled: Dorothy Dene was born Ada Alice Pullan, so her sisters were Pullan, not Pullen. No source I could find names Edith for this picture.
issues.evidence: commons - the file is categorised 'Dorothy Dene' and '19th-century paintings of women with identified models'; https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Frederick_Leighton_-_Memories.jpg | web:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorothy_Dene - born Ada Alice Pullan; sisters Edith Ellen, Henrietta and Isabell also sat to Leighton

issues.quote: a black and gold dress
issues.problem: What is visible is a black lace shawl or mantilla with gold sprigs drawn over the head and shoulders rather than a dress; only a scrap of white collar shows beneath it.
issues.evidence: image

proposals.imageObservation: Half-length portrait of a young woman in a black lace shawl or mantilla flecked with gold, drawn over her hair, her bare right forearm raised so her hand rests at her cheek; a brass vessel catches light at the lower left, against a plain grey-brown ground.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Medium confidence on the sitter: Commons categorisation is the only identification I could find, and Dene's sisters did sit to Leighton, so an 'Edith' version of the story is not impossible - but nothing supports it and the surname is spelled wrong. The 1883 date is supported by the Commons category '1883 paintings of women'. The catalogue row has year: null; 1883 could be filled in from Commons.

verifier.reason: The finding is refuted. The Leighton House / RBKC catalogue record for this picture (lordleightonsdrawings, workid 790, 'Memories', c.1883, oil on canvas) states that Edith Pullen, sister of Leighton's friend and favourite model Dorothy Dene, sat for it, and quotes the 1904 biography: 'It shows the half-length figure of a blonde in a black and gold dress.' The description's sitter claim and its 'black and gold dress' wording both trace to that museum record, not to invention — the first agent overturned a museum catalogue on the strength of a user-applied Commons category ('Dorothy Dene'), which is the weaker source and is exactly what one would expect for a picture of Dene's sister. The surname objection also fails: the National Portrait Gallery's own authority record spells her 'Dorothy Dene (Ada Alice Pullen)', so 'Pullen' is a standard spelling, not a misspelling. On the image, the garment reading is at best a toss-up: she wears black flecked with small gold sprigs over hair, shoulders and body, and whether that is one lace mantilla or a mantilla over a matching dress is not decidable at this resolution — the 1904 description calls it a dress. Applying this finding would replace a sourced sitter identification with a less-supported one.

proposals.title: Solitude
proposals.currentDescription: A single draped woman seated on a rock above still water in a deep mountain hollow. Oil on canvas painted around 1890; Leighton described the setting as a place worn so deep that absolute silence holds. The picture is now in the Maryhill Museum of Art, Washington State.
proposals.imageObservation: A single woman in a pale grey-white robe with a rose-pink head covering sits on a rock, knees drawn up, chin resting on her hand and eyes lowered, an apricot-coloured drapery spread beneath her; behind and above is a dark brown rock face, and at the bottom a strip of still dark water with reddish reflections.
proposals.reviewerNotes: I specifically chased the attributed remark, which had the shape of a hallucination, and it holds: Leighton drew the setting from the Lynn of Dee near Braemar and wrote to his sister of pools 'scooped and worn so deep' that no sound reaches you and 'the silent mystery of it all' possesses you — which is what he said he tried to put into Solitude. The Maryhill Museum of Art attribution is supported by the record's credit URL (maryhillmuseum.org). Source: https://shop.maryhillmuseum.org/products/solitude-by-leighton-post-card

proposals.title: 冨嶽三十六景 武州玉川-Fuji—The Tama River
proposals.currentDescription: A woodblock print from Katsushika Hokusai's acclaimed series Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, depicting the Tama River flowing through Musashi Province with Mount Fuji visible in the distance. Created circa 1830-32, this work exemplifies the ukiyo-e style's masterful composition of landscape and water. Part of the Metropolitan Museum of Art's open access collection.

issues.quote: this work exemplifies the ukiyo-e style's masterful composition of landscape and water
issues.problem: Empty praise standing in for description; the boat, the packhorse and drover, and the print's near-monochrome blue palette all go unmentioned.
issues.evidence: image

proposals.imageObservation: A horizontal colour woodblock print in blues and buff: a broad river with a laden ferry-boat, a snow-capped Mount Fuji beyond the far bank, a man leading a packhorse along a sandbar in the foreground, and the series cartouche and signature at the upper left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Subject, series, date range (circa 1830-32 per Commons) and the Met open-access provenance are all correct — no factual finding. Only the middle sentence is boilerplate; per the brief, style does not change the verdict.

proposals.title: Fujiwara no Yasumasa Playing the Flute by Moonlight
proposals.currentDescription: A late triptych by Yoshitoshi shows the Heian courtier Fujiwara no Yasumasa playing his flute on a moonlit moor while the bandit Hakamadare, disarmed by the music, looks on. Long stretches of muted ground and the cool autumnal palette demonstrate Yoshitoshi's reformed late style for the Meiji woodblock market.
proposals.imageObservation: A woodblock triptych: a courtier in an orange patterned robe and black cap walks through moonlit pampas grass playing a transverse flute, a full moon low at the upper left; at the right a barefoot man in a blue robe crouches among the grasses with a sword, watching him. Long inscription and seals in the lower left panel.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Spot-check holds: triptych format, moonlit moor, flute, and the watching figure are all in the image, and the Yasumasa/Hakamadare story is the standard subject of this design. LACMA and 1883 come from the record and Commons. One observation for the record, not a description fault: the inscription in the print reads 明治十五壬午年秋 - autumn of Meiji 15, that is 1882 - while LACMA dates the print 1883; the description wisely states no year.

proposals.title: Gathering Bamboo Shoots
proposals.currentDescription: A color woodblock print by Suzuki Harunobu of a young woman in a wide straw hat digging in deep snow with a hoe, where a single bamboo shoot has broken the surface beneath snow-laden bamboo. The unseasonable subject evokes the Chinese filial-piety tale of Meng Zong, who dug for bamboo shoots in midwinter to feed his ailing mother, recast in Harunobu's fashion as a scene with an elegant contemporary beauty. The print, from about 1765, is in the Art Institute of Chicago.
proposals.imageObservation: Colour woodblock print: a young woman in a wide conical straw hat and patterned pale-yellow robes bends forward in deep snow, pushing a long-handled hoe/spade toward a single reddish bamboo shoot emerging from the snow; snow-laden bamboo canes and foliage fill the top and left of the sheet.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Every element checks out against the image (hat, hoe, snow, single shoot, snow-laden bamboo). Commons credit links to artic.edu/artworks/20801, confirming the Art Institute of Chicago and the c.1765 date. The Meng Zong filial-piety reading is the standard interpretation of this design and is presented as an allusion ("evokes"), not as a documented statement, so it is fairly hedged.

proposals.title: Selfportrait
proposals.currentDescription: Gauguin portrays himself in strict profile against a deep reddish-brown ground, the face lit with warm, ruddy tones while the brushwork is reduced to its essentials. An inscription on the canvas reads 'à l'ami Daniel', identifying the work as a gift to Georges-Daniel de Monfreid, who supported the artist during his Tahitian years. The self-portrait is dated 1896.
proposals.imageObservation: A head-and-shoulders self-portrait in strict left profile against a mottled red-brown ground: dark hair, heavy moustache, ruddy modelled face, a yellow-green coat with a dark collar, and a cursive inscription in dark paint at lower right that reads as 'à l'ami Daniel' with a signature and date beneath.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The profile, the reddish-brown ground and the inscription are all visible in the image, and the Commons title 'Autoportrait à l'ami Daniel / Selfportrait, dedicated to his friend Daniel' with date 1896 confirms both the dedication and the year. Georges-Daniel de Monfreid as the 'Daniel' of the dedication and as Gauguin's supporter during the Tahitian years is standard, well-documented Gauguin biography.

proposals.title: Orlando Pursuing the Fata Morgana
proposals.currentDescription: Orlando lunges after the fleeing sorceress Fata Morgana, a scene drawn from Boiardo's epic 'Orlando Innamorato'. Watts began the canvas in Italy in 1846 and finished it in London by 1848; the oil, 165 by 120 cm, was given by the artist to the Leicester Museum and Art Gallery in 1888.
proposals.imageObservation: A dark oil: a nude female figure sweeps diagonally across the canvas, one arm flung up, drapery of white and gold beneath her, while at the right a helmeted, armoured figure in a red cloak lunges after her and grasps at her arm.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Every checkable claim held up: subject from Boiardo's Orlando Innamorato, begun 1846 in Italy and finished on his return to London (Commons date 'between 1846 and 1848'), oil 165 x 120 cm, given by the artist to Leicester in 1888. The accession number L.F5.1889.0.0 refers to the 1889 accessioning, which is not a contradiction. Source: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Pursuing_the_Fata_Morgana.

proposals.title: The Minotaur
proposals.currentDescription: The Minotaur leaning on a parapet and gazing out to sea, a small bird crushed in his fist. Watts painted the oil in 1885 as a protest against the child prostitution exposed that summer by W. T. Stead in the Pall Mall Gazette. It entered the Tate in 1897 (N01634).
proposals.imageObservation: The Minotaur seen from behind, a heavy ochre-brown bull-headed man leaning both arms on a stone parapet and gazing out over a pale sea toward the horizon; beneath his clenched left fist a small crushed bird is visible, its wing and feathers protruding.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Pose, parapet, sea and the crushed bird under the fist are all in the image. Tate accession N01634 and the 1885 date are on the Commons record; the picture's connection to W. T. Stead's July 1885 'Maiden Tribute of Modern Babylon' in the Pall Mall Gazette is the standard, well-established account of the painting. Watts presented it to the nation in 1897, which matches the description's 'entered the Tate in 1897'; the Commons record does not itself carry that year, so it rests on established fact rather than the source metadata.

proposals.title: George Meredith
proposals.currentDescription: George Meredith , by George Frederic Watts (died 1904), given to the National Portrait Gallery, London in 1909. See source website for additional information. This set of images was gathered by User:Dcoetzee from the National Portrait Gallery, London website using a special tool.

issues.quote: This set of images was gathered by User:Dcoetzee from the National Portrait Gallery, London website using a special tool.
issues.problem: Wikimedia housekeeping text about how the file was uploaded, sitting in the catalogue where a description of the picture should be; the text never says what the portrait shows.
issues.evidence: commons | the sentence is copied verbatim from the Commons imageDescription batch boilerplate

proposals.imageObservation: Half-length portrait of an elderly man with white hair and a full white beard, turned three-quarters right, in a grey coat with a white shirt and red-brown cravat, against a warm red-brown ground.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Nothing here is false - Watts did die in 1904 and the Commons record does say the portrait was given to the National Portrait Gallery in 1909 - so I left the verdict accurate, but the text is a metadata dump and its last sentence is about the upload batch rather than the artwork. A rewrite could keep the NPG facts and add the sitter's appearance.

proposals.title: Lute Player
proposals.currentDescription: A young woman in a yellow-gold drape and a feathered cap holds a small stringed instrument, glancing to the side with a broad smile. The half-length single-figure format belongs to the series of Utrecht musician pictures Honthorst produced for the open market in the early 1620s, deriving from his study of Caravaggio's followers in Rome. The work is dated 1624.
proposals.imageObservation: A smiling young woman in a gold-yellow drape over a white chemise, a plumed headdress in her hair, turns half away and holds up the pegbox of a lute in her right hand; the body of the instrument is out of frame. Half-length, against a dark ground, with a faint inscription at the upper left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Ledger says fabricated-fixed and the current text holds up: the yellow drape, plumed cap, broad smile and sideways glance are all in the picture, and the 1624 date is on the Commons record. 'A small stringed instrument' is a hedge - only the lute's pegbox is visible, so nothing in the frame settles the size - but it is not wrong. The Utrecht Caravaggist half-length musician type and Honthorst's Roman years (1616-20) are standard art history. The Commons categories place the painting in the Hermitage; the description does not name a collection, which is a gap rather than an error.

proposals.title: Merry Violinist
proposals.currentDescription: A grinning young man in a feathered hat raises a wine glass while cradling a violin against his body, his expression caught in a moment of convivial pleasure. Painted circa 1624, this half-length belongs to the series of merry musicians that Honthorst's Utrecht workshop produced for the bourgeois market, each varied by costume and instrument.
proposals.imageObservation: Half-length: a grinning moustached young man in a plumed black beret raises a large wine glass in his right hand while his left hand holds a violin and bow against his chest; loose white shirt slipping off one shoulder, plain brown ground, signature at the upper right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Figure, glass, violin, hat and half-length format all match; circa 1624 is the Commons date. The claim about a workshop series of merry musicians made for the bourgeois market is a general characterisation of Honthorst's Utrecht production in the 1620s rather than a documented fact about this canvas — true in outline, but it is the one sentence a stricter pass might want softened. Commons identifies the work as 'The Happy Violinist with a Glass of Wine'; the description names no collection, so nothing to contradict.

proposals.title: Major-General Henry Dearborn
proposals.currentDescription: Henry Dearborn, the Jefferson-era Secretary of War newly returned to active command at the outbreak of the War of 1812, sits in dark blue uniform with gold epaulets. Stuart painted him in 1812; the canvas entered the Art Institute of Chicago as accession 1913.793.
proposals.imageObservation: A bust-length portrait of a white-haired, ruddy-faced man in a dark blue uniform coat with gold oak-leaf embroidery on the collar and lapels, two gold bullion epaulettes, a white ruffled shirt and stock, a red sash across the chest with a gold medallion, and a small silver eagle badge on a pale blue ribbon; warm dark ground.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Uniform, epaulettes and blue-and-gold match the image; Dearborn was Jefferson's Secretary of War (1801-09) and became senior major general at the outbreak of the War of 1812; the accession 1913.793 and the Art Institute of Chicago are in the file name and the Commons credit URL. 'Sits' is a fair reading of a bust-length pose. Prior ledger status 'accurate' holds.

proposals.title: Giovanna Baccelli
proposals.currentDescription: Full-length portrait of the Italian dancer Giovanna Baccelli (c. 1753–1801), painted by Thomas Gainsborough around 1782. The work depicts her in elegant 18th-century attire against a natural background, capturing the grace and poise of one of the era's most celebrated performers.
proposals.imageObservation: Full-length portrait of a woman in a pale pink and cream gown with blue ribbons and a wide feathered hat, caught mid-dance step with a gauzy shawl raised in her right hand; a tambourine and scattered flowers lie on the ground at lower left, before a landscape and sunset sky.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Sitter dates (c.1753-1801), artist, and the c.1782 date all match the Commons record exactly; 'natural background' matches both the image and the Commons category 'Portrait paintings with natural background'. The description is thinner than house style - it never mentions the dance step, the tambourine or the raised shawl, which are the most distinctive things in the frame - but nothing in it is wrong, so it stays accurate.

proposals.title: Girl in the Sunlight
proposals.currentDescription: Maria Simonovich, Serov's cousin, sits leaning against a large tree at Domotkanovo, dappled summer light falling across her white blouse and dark skirt. Painted in 1888 and acquired by the Tretyakov Gallery, Moscow, the portrait is paired with Girl with Peaches as the second of the two early canvases that established Serov's reputation as a colourist.
proposals.imageObservation: Oil portrait: a young woman sits at the foot of a massive tree trunk, hands loosely clasped in her lap, in a cream blouse with lace at the collar and cuffs and a dark blue skirt, dappled sunlight falling across her; behind her a sunlit clearing and dark trees.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Pose, tree, dappled light and the cream blouse/dark skirt all match. Maria Simonovich was Serov's cousin, the picture was painted at the Derviz estate at Domotkanovo in 1888, and the Tretyakov holding is supported by the Commons categories ('19th-century portrait paintings in the Tretyakov Gallery'). The pairing with Girl with Peaches (1887) as the two works that made his name is the standard account.

proposals.title: Girl with a hoop
proposals.currentDescription: Marie Goujon, aged nine, in a blue dress and sash holding a hoop against a screen of foliage. Oil on canvas painted in 1885 and commissioned by her father, the physician Étienne Goujon, now in the National Gallery of Art, Washington, from the Chester Dale Collection.
proposals.imageObservation: A full-length portrait of a girl of about nine standing in a garden, in a pale bluish-white dress with a wide blue sash, a blue ribbon in her long brown hair and black buckled shoes, holding a wooden hoop in her right hand and a stick in her left, with flowering shrubs and dappled grass behind. Signed and dated lower left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: All specifics verified: the National Gallery of Art records the sitter as the nine-year-old Marie Goujon, the commission as coming from her father Senateur Etienne Goujon, and the picture as 1885, Chester Dale Collection. Etienne Goujon (1839-1907) was indeed a physician who ran a maison de sante in Paris before entering the Senate, so 'the physician Etienne Goujon' is correct. The dress reads as white with blue flecks rather than solidly blue, but the sash is unambiguously blue and the overall impression is bluish, so I did not treat 'a blue dress and sash' as an error.

proposals.title: Golden Autumn. Золотая осень
proposals.currentDescription: A sunlit forest interior with large broadleaf trees bearing golden-yellow autumn foliage, their trunks casting deep shadows across a carpet of fallen leaves. Isaac Levitan's 1895 canvas, signed at the lower right and exhibited at the Munich Secession in 1896, captures the mood of a Russian autumn woodland in a 58 × 68 cm oil on canvas.
proposals.imageObservation: Oil: a forest interior with several heavy trunks, a canopy of gold and yellow autumn leaves with some green still in it, blue-grey light between the trunks and a rust-brown carpet of fallen leaves; a faint signature at the lower right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Spot-check of a prior 'fabricated-fixed' verdict; the rewrite now matches both the image and the Commons file description, which gives oil on canvas, 58 x 68 cm, signed lower right, and 'Exhibited: Munchen Seccession 1896 #233'. Caveat for a later pass: those facts, the 1895 date and the Levitan attribution all rest on a single uploader credit ('Russian Art Masterpieces') - this is not the famous Tretyakov 'Golden Autumn' birch-grove picture, and no museum record backs it.

proposals.title: Goltzius's right Hand
proposals.currentDescription: A virtuoso pen-and-ink study of the artist's own drawing hand, deformed since childhood by a burn. Goltzius turns the disability into a manifesto of skill, building the form from his signature swelling-and-tapering parallel hatchings copied across Europe.
proposals.imageObservation: A pen-and-brown-ink drawing on cream paper of a right hand seen from the back, fingers splayed, the wrist emerging from a cuff at the left; the form is built entirely from swelling-and-tapering parallel hatching and cross-hatching, and the sheet is inscribed 'HGoltzius fecit Anno 1588' with a calligraphic flourish beneath.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Medium, date and technique are confirmed by the sheet's own inscription and by the Commons record (pen and brown ink, 23 x 32.2 cm, Teylers Museum, Haarlem; the record's realDimensions 32.7 x 23 agree within rounding). The childhood burn that maimed Goltzius's right hand is standard biography. The 'copied across Europe' claim about his hatching is a fair summary of his engraving style's influence and did not seem worth a finding.

proposals.title: American Gothic
proposals.currentDescription: A stern Iowa farmer and his daughter stand before a white frame house with a Carpenter Gothic window, the pitchfork echoing the seams of his overalls. Wood used his sister Nan and his dentist as models, fashioning a dry, hard-edged image that became shorthand for rural America.
proposals.imageObservation: A bald bespectacled man in a black jacket over a denim bib overall holds a three-tined pitchfork upright; a woman in a dark apron-front dress with a white collar and cameo brooch stands slightly behind him at his left, both unsmiling; behind them a white frame house with a pointed gable and a tall arched Gothic window, a red barn and trees at right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Re-checked as if fresh. The models were Wood's sister Nan Wood Graham and his dentist Byron McKeeby — documented and correct; Wood himself described the pair as a farmer and his daughter; the house is the Carpenter Gothic cottage in Eldon, Iowa; the vertical seams of the overalls and shirt do echo the fork's tines. Nothing overreaches.

proposals.title: Harlech Castle
proposals.currentDescription: An early oil painting by J. M. W. Turner of Harlech Castle on its crag above the Welsh coast, seen across the estuary from Tygwyn Ferry in the fading light of a summer evening. Turner exhibited the picture at the Royal Academy in 1799, the year he was elected an Associate of the Academy, translating his watercolour studies of Welsh castles into the atmospheric oil manner of his early maturity. The painting is in the Yale Center for British Art.
proposals.imageObservation: A wide estuary at twilight under a pink-gold sky: a small castle sits on a low hill in the left middle distance, moored ships and a timber shipyard frame occupy the right bank, and three small figures stand on rocks in the left foreground beside still water.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Every checkable claim holds. Yale Center for British Art confirmed by the Commons categories and by the YCBA's own page (interactive.britishart.yale.edu, the credited source). Exhibition at the Royal Academy in 1799 confirmed by web search; Turner was elected ARA in November 1799, so 'the year he was elected an Associate' is right. A watercolour study of the composition survives in Turner's North Wales sketchbook (Tate D01459), which supports the 'translating his watercolour studies' line. One completeness note, not a finding: the YCBA entry observes that the shipyard takes centre stage and the castle sits far back, so the first sentence gives the castle more prominence than the picture does.

proposals.title: Evening at Tagonoura
proposals.currentDescription: A shin-hanga woodblock print by Kawase Hasui from 1940. Mount Fuji rises with rose-colored evening light on its snows, framed between the dark trunks and boughs of pines, while a farmer leads a loaded horse cart across the fields of Tagonoura below, a stretch of coast whose views of Fuji have been celebrated since classical poetry. An impression is held by the Aichi Prefectural Museum of Art.
proposals.imageObservation: A colour woodblock print: snow-covered Mount Fuji glows pink in evening light between the trunks and dark boughs of foreground pines, while a small figure leads a horse drawing a high-piled cart along a ridge of dry grassland below; the artist's signature and red seal appear at lower right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Every visual claim checks out, including the rose light on the snow, the pine framing and the loaded horse cart. The Aichi Prefectural Museum of Art impression is the record's own credit field. Tago-no-ura's poetic fame (the Man'yōshū poem by Yamabe no Akahito) is well established; the print itself shows no sea, but the description only says the coast is celebrated, not that it is visible.

proposals.title: Heirin-ji
proposals.currentDescription: A late woodblock print by Kawase Hasui, published in 1952, of Heirin-ji, a Rinzai Zen temple at Nobidome in Saitama prefecture. The temple's dark timber gate stands in deep shadow while sunlight breaks through the foliage in bright patches across the flagstone path, autumn maples burning orange in the middle distance. An impression is held by the Aichi Prefectural Museum of Art.
proposals.imageObservation: A woodblock print looking out from under a dark temple gate: heavy timber posts and a shadowed upper storey at left, a flagstone path in the foreground broken by bright patches of sunlight, and burning orange-red maples with a smaller roof beyond.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Every element of the description is visible in the print, and the 1952 date, the Nobidome/Heirin-ji subject and the Aichi Prefectural Museum of Art impression all come from the Commons record and the credit field. Heirin-ji at Nobidome (Niiza, Saitama) is a Rinzai Zen temple.

proposals.title: Mr and Mrs Edwin Edwards
proposals.currentDescription: Edwin Edwards and his wife Ruth are portrayed together, he seated among papers and prints, she standing beside him, both in Fantin-Latour's habitual sober blacks. The Edwardses were the artist's closest English patrons, channelling his still lifes into the London market; this 1875 double portrait, held at Tate, London, is among the most intimate records of that long friendship.
proposals.imageObservation: A double portrait in a brown-olive interior: a woman in black with a lace collar stands at left, arms folded, looking out at the viewer; a bearded man in dark clothes sits at right, leaning on a large portfolio of sheets on a cloth-covered table, looking down and away.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The wife's name checks out (Elizabeth Ruth Escombe, known as Ruth), as does Tate ownership (N01952, exhibited Salon of 1875 - currently on loan to the National Gallery, London, which is worth knowing but does not make 'held at Tate' wrong). Edwin Edwards's role as Fantin-Latour's promoter and agent in England is well documented; 'closest English patrons' and 'among the most intimate records' are soft, subjective phrasings but not assertions of fact I can falsify.

proposals.title: Henri Meunier04
proposals.currentDescription: A poster, L'Heure du Silence, by the Belgian Art Nouveau designer Henri Meunier, lithographed in the flat planes and sinuous contour the Brussels school adopted from Japanese prints. Meunier worked extensively in advertising, treating commercial commissions with the same graphic refinement as his fine-art prints.

issues.quote: A poster, L'Heure du Silence, by the Belgian Art Nouveau designer Henri Meunier
issues.problem: The description never says what the sheet depicts - the woman's finger-to-lips gesture that literally illustrates the title, the setting sun, the green robe. It describes a manner, not an image.
issues.evidence: image; house style asks the first sentence to describe the frame

proposals.imageObservation: A flat-colour lithographic poster: a dark-haired woman seen in profile raises one finger to her lips in a hushing gesture, wrapped in a green robe, before an orange sun setting into banded cloud on a cream ground; signed 'Henri Meunier 97' lower right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Title and authorship confirmed by the Commons file description ('L'Heure du Silence', Poster by Henri Meunier). The date 1897 matches the '97 in the signature. Ledger says 'accurate' and no claim is false, so I left the verdict there, but the entry would be much better if it named the hushing gesture. One thing a later pass could check: the file is categorised under 'L'Estampe Moderne', which would make this a print for that portfolio rather than a commercial poster; I could not resolve which.

proposals.title: Hércules lucha con la hidra de Lerna
proposals.currentDescription: Hercules grapples with the many-headed Hydra of Lerna, his muscular body twisting against the dark serpentine coils. The canvas belongs to a series of ten Labours of Hercules painted for the Hall of Realms in the Buen Retiro Palace, where Zurbarán's stark tenebrism set the hero against an almost theatrical void.

issues.quote: his muscular body twisting against the dark serpentine coils
issues.problem: Slight overstatement of contact: Hercules is not entangled with the hydra but stands clear of it, striking with a club, and the description omits the second figure (Iolaus) cauterising the necks with a torch, who is a third of the composition.
issues.evidence: image — the two figures are separated by the width of the canvas and Hercules' body is braced, not entwined

proposals.imageObservation: A nude, muscular Hercules seen from behind, a lion skin knotted at his waist, swings a club two-handed at a scaly many-headed serpent that rears in the shadows at the left; at the right a second young man leans in from behind a rock holding a burning brand. Dark, nearly monochrome ground with a strip of sky at the upper right; '536' painted at the lower left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Nothing false: the Prado provenance (P001249), the 1634 date and the series of ten Hercules canvases for the Hall of Realms of the Buen Retiro are all supported by the record and the Prado text in the source evidence. The only thing I would change is adding Iolaus with the torch, which is a real presence in the frame — a content gap rather than an error, so the verdict stays accurate.

proposals.title: Hieronymous Bosch The Last Judgement
proposals.currentDescription: A monumental triptych depicting the Day of Judgment, with divine judgment of humanity set against a complex landscape of heaven, earth, and damnation. Executed in oil on panel, this iconic work by Hieronymus Bosch synthesizes medieval eschatological imagery with his characteristically imaginative grotesque details, now housed in Vienna's Academy of Fine Arts.

issues.quote: iconic work
issues.problem: Empty evaluative adjective; house style is plain and factual.
issues.evidence: style guideline

proposals.imageObservation: A three-panel triptych: left wing shows Eden with the creation of Eve, the Fall and the expulsion; the centre panel has Christ enthroned in a light-filled mandorla above a vast brown landscape swarming with grotesque torments; the right wing is a dark burning hell.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Triptych form, oil on panel, Vienna Academy of Fine Arts holding and the heaven/earth/hell structure all match the image and the Commons category 'The Last Judgment by Hieronymus Bosch (Vienna)'. The Commons date field reads '1450', which is Bosch's approximate birth year and not a date for this work; the catalogue's 1504 is within the usual range given for the Vienna triptych. The left wing is strictly Paradise/Eden rather than heaven, a nuance not worth a rewrite.

proposals.title: Hieronymous Bosch Tondals Visions
proposals.currentDescription: A visionary narrative painting depicting Tondal's Vision, a medieval tale of spiritual otherworldly journey. This work is attributed to a follower of the Flemish master Hieronymus Bosch and exemplifies the Northern Renaissance fascination with intricate allegorical and fantastical imagery. The painting is housed in the Museo Lázaro Galdiano in Madrid.

issues.quote: exemplifies the Northern Renaissance fascination with intricate allegorical and fantastical imagery
issues.problem: Boilerplate appraisal; the description also spends no words on the extraordinary content actually in the frame.
issues.evidence: house style / image

metadataIssues.evidence: commons artist field 'Follower of Hieronymus Bosch', file title 'Follower of Jheronimus Bosch 037.jpg', category 'Followers of Jheronimus Bosch' - the description itself already says 'attributed to a follower'
commons date field 'mid 16th century date QS:P571,+1550-00-00T00:00:00Z/7'

proposals.imageObservation: Oil on panel: a giant disembodied head spewing coins into a large wooden tub of nude bathers; Tondal asleep at lower left with a guardian angel, a burning city at upper right, a figure in a red bed inside a giant vessel at right, and grotesque hybrid creatures throughout; the inscription 'visio tundali' at lower left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Subject, follower attribution and the Museo Lazaro Galdiano holding all check out against Commons (categories '16th-century paintings in the Museo Lazaro Galdiano', 'Visio Tnugdali (followers of Jheronimus Bosch)'). Note the record's artist field says Bosch outright while the description correctly hedges - that internal mismatch is the thing to fix, not the prose.

proposals.title: Kumoi-Zakura (Kumoi Cherry Trees)
proposals.currentDescription: Two figures stand beneath a weeping cherry tree at night, its blossoming branches silhouetted against a deep teal sky and a luminous full moon. The woodblock print, dated 1926 and held at the Toledo Museum of Art, exemplifies Yoshida's ability to capture atmospheric nocturnal effects through delicate gradations of colour.
proposals.imageObservation: Two women in patterned kimono stand at the foot of a large weeping cherry in full blossom at night; the trailing branches spread across a deep teal sky and a pale full moon glows through them above a dark slope. Japanese inscriptions and a red seal in the margins, pencil signature below.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Everything in the text is in the image - two figures, weeping cherry, teal sky, full moon - and the 1926 date and Toledo Museum of Art holding come from the Commons record and the provenance block (Q113487261, inv. 1939.381). The earlier 'fabricated-fixed' rewrite looks sound.

proposals.title: Yomei Gate
proposals.currentDescription: A color woodblock print by Hiroshi Yoshida of the Yomeimon, the lavishly carved and gilded gate of the Tosho-gu shrine at Nikko, with small figures on the steps below and towering cedars closing in behind. Yoshida renders the gate's dense ornament in a subdued harmony of golds and greys, capturing the gleam of gilding in deep forest shade. The print was made in 1937.
proposals.imageObservation: A colour woodblock print of the Yomeimon at Nikko: the heavily carved and gilded gate rises above a broad flight of stone steps with a single white-and-blue-robed figure on them and two small seated figures under the gate, cedars pressing in behind, a stone lantern at the right. Pencil signature and title below the image.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Everything checks against the sheet: the gate, the steps and figures, the cedars, the muted gold-and-grey harmony. Date 1937 is on the Commons record and in the Japanese inscription at the left margin. Only quibble is 'figures' plural on the steps where one figure is on the steps and the others are at the top under the gate.

proposals.title: Hiroshige-53-Stations-Hoeido-37-Akasaka-MFA-01
proposals.currentDescription: The Akasaka inn is shown in a tilted cross-section view: on one side, a traveller is attended to while a companion waits; on the other, maids prepare for guests, the two halves separated by a palm in the courtyard. Hiroshige's elevated vantage and interior detail make this one of the most architecturally observed scenes in the Hōeidō Tōkaidō (c. 1833–35).
proposals.imageObservation: An inn seen from above in cutaway: on the left wing a bath-side room where a man in a blue robe stoops with a towel, a seated guest is attended by a masseur and a servant carries a tray; on the right wing women do their hair and make-up before a mirror and prepare to serve; a large sago palm and a stone lantern stand in the courtyard between the two wings, with the title cartouche upper right and Hiroshige's signature and publisher seal lower right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Matches the print closely, including the split composition, the palm in the courtyard and the elevated viewpoint. The 'c. 1833-35' dating matches the Commons date 'circa 1833/35' exactly, and the Hoeido publisher seal is named in the Commons imageDescription. The prior 'minor-fixed' pass looks sound; the only quibble is that the courtyard tree is a sago palm (a cycad) rather than a true palm, which is how it is usually described anyway.

proposals.title: Hiroshige Fudo Falls
proposals.currentDescription: A woodblock print from Utagawa Hiroshige's famous series One Hundred Famous Views of Edo (no. 49), depicting the sacred Fudo Falls at the Shoju-in temple in Oji. The composition captures the cascading waterfall in Hiroshige's characteristic style with bold perspectives and atmospheric depth, exemplifying the ukiyo-e tradition of landscape prints.

issues.quote: The composition captures the cascading waterfall in Hiroshige's characteristic style with bold perspectives and atmospheric depth, exemplifying the ukiyo-e tradition of landscape prints.
issues.problem: Pure catalogue boilerplate. It asserts nothing checkable and describes nothing actually in the frame - the bather, the sacred rope and streamers, the tea benches and the onlookers all go unmentioned.
issues.evidence: image - the print's staffage is its whole lower third

issues.quote: famous series
issues.problem: Empty intensifier of the kind house style avoids.
issues.evidence: house style

proposals.imageObservation: A vertical woodblock print: a narrow white-blue waterfall drops through a dark rock cleft hung with a shimenawa rope and paper streamers; below, a naked bather stands in the pool, two women in kimono look on, and an attendant serves at low benches beside a bucket and tub. Title and artist cartouches upper right and left; pencilled '47' and 'Oji' on the top margin.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Facts all check out: the print is No. 49 of One Hundred Famous Views of Edo (Brooklyn Museum and Art Institute of Chicago both catalogue it as No. 49; the Commons filename '047' is a scan-sequence number, not the series number), and visitors approached the falls through the precincts of Shojuin temple. Verdict stays accurate because nothing is wrong - but this is a candidate for a rewrite on style grounds alone, since the second sentence is filler and the description never says what is in the picture.

proposals.title: Hiroshige View from massaki
proposals.currentDescription: Print no. 36 from Utagawa Hiroshige's One Hundred Famous Views of Edo series, part 1: Spring. This woodblock print depicts a view across Suijin Shrine's sacred grove toward the Uchigawa inlet and the village of Sekiya, exemplifying Hiroshige's mastery of landscape perspective and atmospheric detail.

issues.quote: exemplifying Hiroshige's mastery of landscape perspective and atmospheric detail
issues.problem: Boilerplate; also the print's defining device - the view seen through a huge circular window with a plum branch across it - is never mentioned.
issues.evidence: image

proposals.imageObservation: A vertical print framed by a large round window cut into a dark grey wall: through it, a plum branch in white blossom, boats on a broad river, a low wooded shore, geese in flight and a red sunset band on the horizon. Title cartouche and number 36 at top right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Series, part and print number ('no. 036, part 1: Spring') are confirmed by the Commons record and by the '36' inked at the top right of the sheet. Content claims are correct; only the framing device is missing.

proposals.title: Chôshi in Shimôsa Province
proposals.currentDescription: Chōshi in Shimōsa Province, from Hokusai's Oceans of Wisdom series (c. 1833), places two fishing boats amid churning open seas, their crews bracing against the swell as a rocky headland rises in the background. The forceful wave patterns and restricted blue-and-white palette recall the graphic intensity Hokusai had brought to the Great Wave in the Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji. The work is held in the Art Institute of Chicago.
proposals.imageObservation: Colour woodblock print: two long fishing boats with crews ride steep dark-blue waves crested in white; a sandy-ochre headland with scattered vegetation runs down the right side; red title cartouche at upper right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Two boats, crews braced, headland at the right — all as described. The Chie no Umi ('Oceans of Wisdom') series and the 1833 date are confirmed by the Commons category and date; the Art Institute of Chicago holding comes from the record's provenance block (inv. EO1852). 'restricted blue-and-white palette' slightly undersells the ochre of the boats and headland, but the print is genuinely dominated by blue and white.

proposals.title: Holbein Danse Macabre 34
proposals.currentDescription: Part of Holbein's Imagines Mortis, the small woodcut sets a skeleton against a figure of social rank, a formula the artist varies with inexhaustible invention across the series.

metadataIssues.evidence: Commons categorises the file under 'Danse Macabre (Holbein)'; the description already attributes the series to Holbein, so the null artist field is a gap rather than a conflict. Note the blocks were cut by Hans Lutzelburger, so 'designer' is the accurate role.

proposals.imageObservation: A small upright woodcut of a panelled interior: a richly dressed woman stands at her toilet while a skeleton at the left presses close behind her shoulder and reaches around her; a maidservant in a headdress attends at the right and a further figure holds a garment or chain at the centre. An hourglass and other objects stand on a carved chest at the lower left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Nothing here is contradicted: there is a skeleton, there is a richly dressed figure, and the sheet is a small woodcut from the Holbein Dance of Death. 'Imagines Mortis' is a legitimate name for the series (the Latin editions from 1542), though the first edition of 1538 was 'Les simulachres & historiees faces de la mort'. Style only, and not counted against the verdict: the description is generic enough to fit any plate in the series and never says that this one shows a woman at her toilet with an hourglass on the chest beside her. The Commons record is almost empty (no author, no date, no description), so I could not confirm which plate number in which edition this is.

proposals.title: The Apotheosis of Homer
proposals.currentDescription: Commissioned for a ceiling in the Louvre, this strictly symmetrical tableau enthrones the blind poet beneath a winged Victory while artists and writers from antiquity to the modern age gather as witnesses. Ingres treats the canvas almost as a bas-relief, marshalling Neoclassical contour and frieze-like balance to assert Homer's status as the wellspring of Western art.
proposals.imageObservation: A strictly symmetrical composition: Homer sits enthroned on the steps of a Greek temple while a winged, laurel-crowned Victory holds a wreath above his head; two allegorical women in red and green sit on the steps below, and dense ranks of poets, philosophers and artists in antique and modern dress crowd in from both sides. Greek inscriptions run across the temple and the steps; 'INGRES PINX' and 'ANNO 1827' are lettered on the plinths at bottom left and right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Spot-check of an earlier 'accurate' verdict: it holds. The ceiling commission for the Musee Charles X in the Louvre is standard, the 1827 date is lettered in the painting itself and matches both the record and Commons, and the record's provenance gives the Louvre's Department of Paintings, INV 5417, Room 702. The two seated allegories are the Iliad and the Odyssey; the description does not name them but says nothing wrong.

proposals.title: Horatio Gates
proposals.currentDescription: General Horatio Gates is shown in three-quarter length, wearing his dark blue Continental Army uniform with gold epaulettes and a large gold medal suspended from a blue ribbon sash — the Congressional Gold Medal awarded for his victory at Saratoga. Stuart painted the portrait between 1793 and 1794 and it is now in the collection of the Metropolitan Museum of Art.
proposals.imageObservation: A portrait of an elderly officer with white hair, shown to the hips: dark blue coat with buff facings and gold epaulettes on both shoulders, a large gold medal on a pale blue ribbon at his chest, a paper in his right hand and his left on a sword hilt, with a stormy sky and distant landscape behind.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Commons gives 'between 1793 and 1794' and the credit line says the original is at the Metropolitan Museum of Art, both matching. The uniform, epaulettes and the large gold medal on a blue ribbon are all visible; Gates's Congressional gold medal for Saratoga is well established. 'Three-quarter length' is generous - the figure is cut at the hips - but is within normal catalogue usage.

proposals.title: The Rainbow
proposals.currentDescription: A rainbow descends through parting storm clouds over a pastoral meadow, where cattle rest and graze in the foreground and a farmstead sits to the left. George Inness painted this canvas around 1878, combining dramatic meteorological observation with the Swedenborgian spiritual symbolism that pervades his later work.
proposals.imageObservation: A rainbow arcs down out of a dark, breaking storm sky onto a sunlit green meadow; a brown cow lies in the grass in the foreground with a white and a dark cow standing behind it and more cattle grazing at the right, a line of trees crosses the middle distance, white farm buildings sit among trees at the left, and a few birds fly at the upper right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Rainbow, parting storm clouds, resting and grazing cattle and the farmstead at left are all exactly as described. Circa 1878 matches the Commons date ("circa 1878-1879") and the record year. Inness's Swedenborgianism is well documented and the sentence attributes only a general influence, so I did not treat it as an unsupported specific. Collection (Indianapolis Museum of Art, per Commons categories) is not claimed in the text, so there is nothing to check there.

proposals.title: From Mleta to Gudauri
proposals.currentDescription: A caravan of travellers and pack animals working along the precipitous mountain road that climbs from Mleta to Gudauri in the Caucasus, snow-capped peaks behind. Aivazovsky painted the oil in 1868, applying the atmospheric handling of mist and distance he is better known for in his sea pieces.
proposals.imageObservation: A road cut into a sheer cliff face winds around a Caucasus gorge filled with mist; horse-drawn carriages, oxen and figures on foot move along it at the right, a snow-covered peak rises in the blue distance, birds wheel over the void at the left. Signed and dated at lower right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The subject, the road, the pack and draught animals, the snow peaks and the mist are all in the frame, the oil medium and 1868 date are confirmed by the Commons categories ('1868 oil on canvas paintings'), and the Mleta–Gudauri stretch of the Georgian Military Road is the picture's documented subject. The description omits the collection, which is not an error.

proposals.title: The Great Pyramid at Giza
proposals.currentDescription: The Great Pyramid of Giza rising over the Egyptian desert under low warm light, with small figures at its base. Aivazovsky, better known for marine subjects, painted the oil in 1871; the canvas later passed through Christie's, London.
proposals.imageObservation: A large pyramid stands in silhouette against a glowing orange sunset sky, the tip of a second pyramid at the right edge; a caravan with camels and small figures crosses the sand at lower left, with a pale distant plain and settlement behind.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Subject, light and the small figures at the base are all in the frame. The 1871 date, the oil medium and the Christie's London provenance are carried by the Commons date and credit fields (LotFinder entry, sale 7905, London, 29 November 2010), and 'better known for marine subjects' is uncontroversial for Aivazovsky.

proposals.title: Night at Gurzof
proposals.currentDescription: A moonlit coastal scene at Gurzuf on the Crimean shore, with a glowing disc of moon laid across the water and dark vessels near the foreground rocks. Aivazovsky painted the marine view in 1891; the canvas later passed through Heritage Auctions in Dallas. The Armenian-Russian painter produced thousands of seascapes from his studio at Feodosia on the Black Sea.
proposals.imageObservation: A night seascape under heavy cloud: a broad silver path of moonlight lies across the bay (the moon itself is hidden behind the clouds), a two-masted ship and a small boat sit on the water at the right, beached boats and a lit hut stand on the shore at the left with a rider silhouetted on the headland, and dark mountains close the far side of the bay.
proposals.reviewerNotes: 1891, the Heritage Auctions Dallas provenance and Aivazovsky's Feodosia studio and enormous seascape output are all supported (the auction line is verbatim the record's credit field). One wording caution for a later editor: 'a glowing disc of moon laid across the water' reads correctly as the reflected moonlight on the water — which is what the picture shows — but a reader could take it as a visible moon in the sky, and there is none. Not a factual error as written, so I did not lower the verdict.

proposals.title: Иван Константинович Айвазовский - Широкий пейзаж с поселенцами
proposals.currentDescription: A panoramic Ukrainian steppe landscape depicting salt farmers in transit from Crimea to interior Russia. Aivazovsky captures the Izumskaya steppe with his characteristic atmospheric rendering, illustrating the vast and harsh terrain through which the caravan moves. Oil on canvas, 1856.

issues.quote: the vast and harsh terrain
issues.problem: The picture shows green pasture in warm evening light; 'harsh' is an editorial addition that the image does not support.
issues.evidence: image

issues.quote: Oil on canvas, 1856.
issues.problem: The date is confirmed by Commons, but the medium is not stated anywhere in the record or the Commons metadata. It is very likely correct for Aivazovsky at this scale; flagged only for completeness.
issues.evidence: catalogue record — no medium field; commons — date 1856 confirmed, medium not given

proposals.imageObservation: A very wide, low-horizon steppe under an enormous sky at sunset; a line of ox-drawn covered wagons recedes to the right along a green rise, a driver sits on the leading load, three or four figures stand and sit on the grass at centre right, geese are scattered in the foreground, and the sun sits low in an orange haze.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The unusual specifics — salt farmers, Crimea to the Russian interior, the Izumskaya steppe — are lifted almost verbatim from the Commons imageDescription, so they are sourced rather than invented. The description never mentions the sunset or the sky, which dominate the canvas; a style rewrite would help but there is no accuracy defect worth the label.

proposals.title: Portrait of the Comte de Turenne
proposals.currentDescription: The Comte de Turenne sits in a black fur-trimmed coat, a small medal ribbon at his lapel, his gaze directed at the viewer, one hand resting on his knee and the other holding gloves. A letter addressed to Brussels lies on the table beside him, suggesting David's exile context. Painted in 1816, the portrait is a characteristic product of David's Brussels years, calm and direct in its characterisation.
proposals.imageObservation: A three-quarter-length seated portrait: a curly-haired man in a black fur-trimmed coat over a pale waistcoat and white cravat, a small ribbon decoration on his chest, looking out at the viewer; his left hand rests on his knee, his right holds green gloves, a top hat is tucked under his arm, and a folded letter lies on a blue-draped table at the lower left. A stone pier and steps fill the right background.
proposals.reviewerNotes: I magnified the letter: the address reads as three lines ending 'Bruxelles', which confirms the description's 'letter addressed to Brussels' — this was the claim most at risk and it holds. Pose, gloves, fur coat and ribbon all match, and the 1816 date matches Commons. Commons categories place the painting in the Ny Carlsberg Glyptotek; the description makes no collection claim, so there is nothing to correct.

proposals.title: The Battle of Nördlingen
proposals.currentDescription: Two armoured commanders on horseback dominate the foreground, surveying the sprawling engagement below as troops and banners mass toward the right and smoke rises over the distant plain. Jan van der Hoecke's large canvas, painted in 1634 and now in the Royal Collection at Windsor Castle (RCIN 400100), commemorates the Habsburg victory at Nördlingen — one of the decisive engagements of the Thirty Years' War — in the grand battle-piece manner Rubens established for court patronage.

metadataIssues.evidence: Royal Collection Trust catalogues RCIN 400100 as by 'Jan van der Hoecke (Antwerp 1611 - Antwerp or Brussels 1651)'; Commons lists 'Jan van den Hoecke / Jacob Jordaens / Peter Paul Rubens' and categorises it 'History paintings by Jan van den Hoecke'. The record's flat attribution to Rubens contradicts the description's own opening and the source.

proposals.imageObservation: Two mounted commanders in the left foreground - one in gleaming armour with a red sash and plumed black hat, one in a fur-trimmed cloak - look right across a battlefield of massed pikes, red banners and armoured infantry, with smoke rising over the plain.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Verified RCIN 400100: oil on canvas, 242.0 x 339.6 cm, Windsor Castle, depicting the Cardinal-Infante Ferdinand's victory over the Swedes on 2 September 1634 (web:rct.uk/collection/400100). Dimensions match realDimensions exactly and the Windsor location checks out. The description is sound; the catalogue's artist field is the thing that needs fixing.

proposals.title: Bringing home the calf born in the fields
proposals.currentDescription: Two men carry a newborn calf on a litter toward a farmhouse, the cow following at their heels. Millet painted this oil about 1860, a study of farm routine from his Barbizon years; the canvas is in the Princeton University Art Museum.
proposals.imageObservation: Two men in hats carry a calf lying on a stretcher along a farm track; a red-brown cow follows immediately behind with a woman in a white cap beside it; a whitewashed farmhouse with a red roof stands at the right and trees fill the left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Subject, date (circa 1860 on Commons) and the Princeton University Art Museum credit all check out; Commons even categorises it under 'French paintings in the Princeton University Art Museum'. The woman leading the cow goes unmentioned, which is an omission, not an error.

proposals.title: The Angelus
proposals.currentDescription: A peasant couple pause over a basket of potatoes to pray as the Angelus bell sounds from a distant church spire. Millet painted the oil between 1857 and 1859; it measures 55.5 by 66 cm and hangs in the Musée d'Orsay, Paris.
proposals.imageObservation: Two peasants stand with bowed heads in a flat dusk field — a man holding his hat, a woman with hands clasped in prayer — a basket of potatoes on the ground between them, a pitchfork stuck in the earth at the left and a wheelbarrow at the right; a church spire breaks the horizon in the distance.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Every claim checks: the basket, the praying couple, the distant spire, the 1857-1859 date, 55.5 x 66 cm and the Musée d'Orsay are all confirmed by the image and the Commons record (the file name itself carries the dimensions and museum).

proposals.title: The Gleaners
proposals.currentDescription: Three women stoop across a stubble field gathering fallen grain, a loaded harvest cart and stacks behind them. Millet painted 'Des glaneuses' in 1857; the canvas entered the Musée d'Orsay, Paris, where it remains.
proposals.imageObservation: Three women stoop across a cut stubble field gathering stalks of grain; behind them a loaded harvest cart, stacked sheaves, a mounted figure and distant farm buildings under a pale sky.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Everything checks: three figures, cart and stacks in the image; 'Des glaneuses' 1857 in the Commons title data; the Musee d'Orsay holding is well established (Commons category 'Google Art Project works in Musee d'Orsay, Paris').

proposals.title: A woman baking bread
proposals.currentDescription: A woman slides a loaf into an oven, sleeves pushed back, the dough and peel close to hand. Millet painted this domestic labour in 1854, one of the Barbizon peasant subjects that defined his mature work.
proposals.imageObservation: A woman seen from behind in a dim stone-walled kitchen slides a loaf into a glowing brick oven on a long-handled peel; her sleeves are pushed up, a red sash hangs from her waist, a basket of dough sits on the table at right and a straw hat lies on the floor. Signed J. F. Millet at lower right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Every element of the description is visible: the loaf going in, the peel, the pushed-back sleeves, the dough in the basket. Commons dates the painting 1854, matching the record. Commons also places it in the Kroller-Muller Museum, which neither the description nor the record mentions - an optional addition, not a defect.

proposals.title: Young Girl Guarding her Sheep
proposals.currentDescription: A young shepherdess stands knitting beside her flock in an open field, her back to the grazing sheep. Millet painted this oil about 1860 to 1862; it belongs to the Sterling and Francine Clark Art Institute in Williamstown.
proposals.imageObservation: A young shepherdess in a red headscarf, hooded cape and pink skirt stands facing the viewer, knitting with needles in her hands and a staff leaning against her arm; a flock of sheep grazes behind her and a shaggy black dog stands at the right. Signed lower right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Knitting, standing pose, back to the flock, and the Clark Art Institute in Williamstown all confirmed - the Commons categories include 'Paintings of knitting women' and 'Paintings in the Sterling and Francine Clark Art Institute', and the credit field names the Clark. Date circa 1860-1862 matches. Only omission is the dog, which is not an error.

proposals.title: Potato Planters
proposals.currentDescription: A man and woman work a field together, he breaking the soil with a hoe while she drops seed potatoes, a basket and a donkey under a tree behind them. Millet painted this oil about 1861, pairing the two figures in the field labour central to his Barbizon work.
proposals.imageObservation: A man in a smock and cap bends to break the earth with a long-handled hoe while a woman opposite him drops potatoes from her apron into the furrow; behind them a grey donkey with panniers stands in the shade of a small tree, a basket at its feet, with fields and a hazy horizon beyond.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Every element the description names — hoe, seed potatoes, basket, donkey, tree — is in the frame and correctly assigned. 'About 1861' matches the Commons date exactly. The description makes no collection claim, so nothing to check there (Commons categories place it in the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston).

proposals.title: Shepherd Tending His Flock
proposals.currentDescription: A shepherd stands wrapped in a cloak as his flock spreads across a flat plain under a wide, luminous sky. Painted in the early 1860s, oil on canvas, now in the Brooklyn Museum. Millet drew his rural subjects from life around Barbizon, where he settled in 1849.

metadataIssues.evidence: commons date field reads 'early 1860s' and the categories include '1860s paintings in the Brooklyn Museum'. The row currently has no year at all, which is why the description had to hedge.

proposals.imageObservation: A shepherd in a broad hat and a heavy dark cloak stands facing right, leaning on a staff, on a flat stubbled plain; sheep graze in a loose band behind and beside him under a wide grey-white clouded sky, with a low line of trees on the far horizon.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The description matches the image closely and every claim is backed: 'early 1860s' is the Commons date verbatim, 'oil on canvas' and the Brooklyn Museum come from the Commons categories ('Oil paintings in the Brooklyn Museum', 'French paintings in the Brooklyn Museum'), and Millet's move to Barbizon in 1849 is standard. Note the record id in the batch file is the full Google Art Project slug; I have shortened nothing else.

proposals.title: The Goose Girl
proposals.currentDescription: A young girl, identifiable as a peasant by her kerchief and her work-roughened hands and feet, extends her leg to dip a heel into the stream. In this painting, Millet refers to a long tradition in European art of depicting the idealized female nude in a natural setting, often in the guise of a mythological figure. The artist reworks this convention from a Realist perspective, emphasizing the goose girl's working-class status, adolescent body, and vulnerable pose.
proposals.imageObservation: A nude adolescent girl wearing a blue kerchief sits on a wooded bank and stretches one leg to dip her foot into a stream; a flock of white geese swims and stands at the left, her clothes and a staff lie at the right beneath dark trees; signed lower left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The description is the Walters Art Museum's own catalogue text, reproduced verbatim from the Commons imageDescription (minus its final sentence about seven years of studies), and it matches the image point for point.

proposals.title: The Potato Harvest
proposals.currentDescription: After moving from Paris to the village of Barbizon on the edge of the Fontainebleau forest in 1851, Millet devoted himself to portraying the lives of his neighbors. Some critics interpreted his paintings of working farmers as a critique of the injustices inherent in the social conditions of his time. Others have seen his work as a representation of man's harmonious union with nature.

issues.quote: After moving from Paris to the village of Barbizon on the edge of the Fontainebleau forest in 1851
issues.problem: The whole description is biography and reception; it never says what the picture shows - the two figures filling a sack, the diggers behind, the sacks and cart at the right.
issues.evidence: image | none of the depicted action appears in the text

proposals.imageObservation: Dusk field under a heavy sky: a man and a woman in the right foreground hold open a sack while filling it, two more figures stoop to dig potatoes behind them, and full pale sacks and a large basket-sided cart stand at the right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The text is a verbatim copy of the Walters Art Museum label as carried in the Commons imageDescription, so every factual claim in it is sourced; Millet did move to Barbizon in 1851. No verdict change. If the corpus is being brought to house style, this one needs a first sentence about the frame, not a correction.

proposals.title: The Sheepfold
proposals.currentDescription: A shepherd folds his flock into a hurdle pen under a low moon, the sheep crowding through the gap. Millet worked this nocturne between 1856 and 1860, the kind of dusk pastoral he favoured at Barbizon.
proposals.imageObservation: A nocturne: a shepherd in a cloak, staff raised, stands at the open end of a hurdle enclosure while a dense flock of pale sheep presses through and fills the foreground; a dog waits at the far left, a low orange moon hangs just above the horizon, and a dark shed stands at the right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Shepherd, hurdle pen, crowding flock and low moon are all in the picture, and the 1856-1860 working span is exactly the Commons date qualifier. The Walters Art Museum holds it (Commons category 'Google Art Project works in The Walters Art Museum') — not mentioned, but omission is not an error. The dog at the left is also unmentioned.

proposals.title: Jean Frédéric Bazille - Reclining Nude - 1864
proposals.currentDescription: A female nude stretched full-length across the canvas, set against a dark ground. Oil on canvas, 70.5 by 190.5 cm, painted in 1864 and held by the Musée Fabre in Montpellier, Bazille's home city. The elongated horizontal format follows the academic odalisque tradition Bazille studied in Gleyre's Paris atelier.

metadataIssues.evidence: Commons title and categories ('Paintings by Frederic Bazille in the Musee Fabre'); the record's own title string already names him, and the description does too, so the null artist field is a data gap, not a description error.

proposals.imageObservation: Oil on canvas, strongly horizontal: a female nude lies full-length on her back on a red patterned rug, one arm bent over her head, a cream shawl with coloured patterning draped across her hips and thighs, against a dark indistinct ground.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Dimensions (70.5 x 190.5 cm), 1864 and Musee Fabre all come straight from the Commons image description. Bazille was born in Montpellier and did study under Gleyre; both hold. The odalisque-tradition sentence is interpretation but a conventional one.

proposals.title: Jean-Léon Gérôme - Riders Crossing The Desert
proposals.currentDescription: A substantial group of mounted and on-foot travellers crosses a sun-bleached desert plain, rust-coloured hills rising in the distance and a larger caravan trailing behind them in a haze of dust. Gérôme, painting after his 1868 Sinai expedition, deploys an oil-on-panel surface of great smoothness to convey the dazzling midday light. The 1870 work — 41 × 56 cm — exemplifies his frieze-like arrangement of colourful figures against an expansive desert landscape.
proposals.imageObservation: A sunlit desert plain: three or four riders in the foreground on white, chestnut and grey horses, in a red hooded cloak, a yellow robe with green drape and a dark robe with turban, one shouldering a long lance; two figures walk behind them and camels with more figures trail off to the left, with ochre hills at the right under a clear blue sky. Signed J L GEROME at the lower left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Verified against the Sotheby's catalogue text carried in the Commons imageDescription and the auction record: oil on panel, 41 x 56 cm, 1870, signed lower left, and the 1868 Sinai expedition with Goupil, Lenoir, Bonnat and About. The 'oil-on-panel' claim - the one thing a reproduction cannot settle - checks out.

proposals.title: Mädchen am Klavier
proposals.currentDescription: A young woman seated at an upright piano with a second woman sewing on a sofa behind her, in a domestic interior. Oil on canvas, about 57 by 92 cm, held by the Hermitage Museum in Saint Petersburg under accession ГЭ-9166. The work carries the subtitle Overture to Tannhäuser, after the Wagner prelude.

metadataIssues.evidence: web:https://hermitagemuseum.org/digital-collection/28717 (via search summary) — the Hermitage dates the canvas circa 1868 and gives 57.8 x 92.5 cm; other literature dates it 1869. Commons carries 'circa 1866', which is presumably where the catalogue value came from, so this is a low-priority discrepancy between sources rather than a clear error.

proposals.imageObservation: A young woman in a white dress sits playing an upright piano at the left, sheet music open above the keys; a second woman in black, seated on a red sofa at the right, works at a piece of white needlework. Patterned wallpaper and a floral-covered armchair fill the background.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Checked the two hard claims: inventory ГЭ-9166 and the dimensions are both confirmed for this painting at the Hermitage (57.8 x 92.5 cm; the description's 'about 57 by 92 cm' is properly hedged), and the 'Overture to Tannhäuser' subtitle is the standard one. The description asserts no date, so the 1866/1868 divergence is a metadata question only.

proposals.title: Self-portrait
proposals.currentDescription: The painter looks out in a white millstone ruff and black costume, holding his palette, brushes, and a maulstick as emblems of his craft. A coat of arms carved in relief is visible in the background. Signed and dated 1601, the panel is understood to be a pendant to the portrait of his wife Christina van Halen, both associated with the Centraal Museum in Utrecht.
proposals.imageObservation: Three-quarter-length oil portrait of a seated bearded man in a large white millstone ruff and black costume, turned toward the viewer; his right hand holds a palette loaded with colour, a sheaf of brushes and a long stick, his left hand a single brush. A carved relief coat of arms and an inscribed tablet, legible as AETATIS SVAE / ANNO 1601 / NON GLORIA SED..., occupy the upper left behind him.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Everything checks: the ruff, black costume, palette, brushes, maulstick and the relief coat of arms are all visible, and the inscription carries the 1601 date matching the record. The support is oil on panel (98 x 73.6 cm), and the picture is in the Centraal Museum, Utrecht, where its pendant is Wtewael's 1601 portrait of his wife Christina Wtewael van Halen - the two carry the same motto, 'Non gloria, sed memoria', of which the tablet's visible 'NON GLORIA SED' is the start. 'Signed and dated' is very slightly generous - the tablet is dated, and a signature is not legible in this reproduction - but the date claim itself is sound.

proposals.title: The Astronomer
proposals.currentDescription: A scholar in a long robe leans over a celestial globe, his hand brushing its surface as if to set the cosmos turning. Painted as a pendant to The Geographer, the picture reflects Delft's culture of empirical inquiry, its still light and book-strewn study tuned to quiet concentration.
proposals.imageObservation: A scholar in a long blue-grey robe leans across a table towards a celestial globe, his right hand on its surface and his left resting on the table beside an open book; a leaded window at the left, a cupboard with books and a framed picture behind, and a tapestry-like patterned cloth over the table.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Everything visible matches. The Geographer pendant relationship is the standard reading — same model, near-identical size, same date range, the two recorded together in early sales — and is stated without overclaiming. The Louvre is in the record's provenance, though the description does not name it.

proposals.title: Roman Pilgrims
proposals.currentDescription: A group of pilgrims is gathered inside a richly decorated basilica interior, its walls hung with devotional images and draped textiles, the floor spread with carpets. Women and children in regional Italian costume rest and pray amid the architectural splendour of the sacred space. Painted in 1854 and held at the Yale Center for British Art, the work applies the ethnographic precision Lewis would become famous for in his Orientalist pictures to the religious folk culture of Italy.

issues.quote: Women and children in regional Italian costume rest and pray
issues.problem: The most prominent figure in the group is an elderly male pilgrim with a staff and gourd at the centre; the description accounts only for women and children.
issues.evidence: image — a bearded man in a green cloak occupies the centre of the composition

proposals.imageObservation: A church interior with frescoed walls, mosaic inlay, a marble column and a heavy red hanging: an old bearded pilgrim in a green cloak with a staff and a gourd sits on the carpeted floor, a young girl leaning on him, while several women and children in Italian regional costume kneel, pray and rest around him; a child eats at a bench at the right and bundles lie on the carpets.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Setting, costume and the Yale Center for British Art all check out (the record's provenance names the YCBA and the Commons categories confirm 1854 and the Ciociaro costume). The omission of the central male pilgrim is an incompleteness rather than a false claim, so the verdict stays accurate. Worth knowing for any future edit: the Commons categories list this as a 1854 watercolour, so do not add 'oil' to this description.

proposals.title: John Hancock
proposals.currentDescription: John Hancock sits at a writing table in a blue coat with his ledger open before him, the merchant and future signer of the Declaration of Independence painted at twenty-eight. Copley made the portrait in 1765 for the Hancock family in Boston, and it now hangs in the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.
proposals.imageObservation: A seated three-quarter view of a young man in a powdered wig and a dark blue coat with gold braid and brass buttons, a quill in his right hand, his left resting on a large open ledger on a red-draped table; more books and an inkstand sit beyond, and he sits in a carved mahogany chair.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Spot-check of a prior 'accurate' verdict, and it survives: blue coat, open ledger, writing table all present; the Commons credit link is the MFA Boston object page; the 1765 date matches Commons; Hancock was born in January 1737, so 'painted at twenty-eight' is right. 'For the Hancock family in Boston' is the conventional account and is not contradicted by anything available.

proposals.title: Portrait of John Jay
proposals.currentDescription: John Jay is seated in the distinctive black and orange judicial robes of the first Chief Justice of the United States, one hand resting against an upright book or document beside him. Gilbert Stuart painted Jay in 1794, the year he travelled to Britain to negotiate the commercial treaty that bears his name; the portrait is now in the National Gallery of Art, Washington. The handling is Stuart's characteristic blend of assured brushwork and dignified Neoclassical restraint.
proposals.imageObservation: Three-quarter-length seated portrait of a balding man in black robes faced with salmon-orange and edged in white, a white stock and jabot at his throat; his far hand rests on the upright edge of a book on a red-draped table, his near hand holds a dark object in his lap, and heavy drapery hangs behind at the left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Spot-check of the 'minor-fixed' pass holds. Robes, pose and the hand on the upright book match the image (Commons even categorises it under 'Black and orange clothing'). Confirmed that the 1794 NGA portrait shows Jay as first Chief Justice in judicial robes and that Jay sailed for London that year to negotiate the treaty later called Jay's Treaty (web:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portrait_of_John_Jay and the NGA object page). The 'Neoclassical restraint' clause is an interpretive flourish, not a checkable claim.

proposals.title: Ezekiel Goldthwait
proposals.currentDescription: The Boston merchant and town clerk Ezekiel Goldthwait is shown three-quarter length in a dark red coat, holding a quill pen in one hand and a folded document in the other, with papers and an inkstand on the table beside him. Painted in oil on canvas in 1771, it is paired at the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston (accession 41.85) with Copley's companion portrait of his wife Elizabeth.
proposals.imageObservation: An elderly man in a powdered wig and a dark red coat and waistcoat sits three-quarter length behind a table, a quill in his right hand and a rolled or folded paper in his left, white lace cuffs at both wrists; papers and a dark inkstand on the table at the left, a heavy green-grey curtain behind, a brass-studded chair back below.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Everything checks: the dark red coat, the quill, the folded document, the papers and inkstand on the table are all in the image; the MFA Boston accession 41.85 is in the file name and the Commons credit links the MFA object page. The companion portrait of Elizabeth Goldthwait at the MFA is well established. Prior ledger status 'minor-fixed' looks sound.

proposals.title: Hugh Montgomerie
proposals.currentDescription: Hugh Montgomerie, later 12th Earl of Eglinton, stands in the full Highland dress of a British officer — red coat, tartan kilt, and feathered bonnet — his sword at his side and a battle in smoke behind him. Copley painted the full-length portrait in London in 1780 to mark Montgomerie's military service, including his years with the 77th (Highland) Regiment during the Seven Years' War.
