proposals.imageObservation: A full-length portrait of an officer in Highland dress - scarlet coat, dark green and blue tartan kilt and plaid, sporran, red-and-white diced hose, tall black feather bonnet - pointing with his right hand, a basket-hilted broadsword held point down at his left side; behind him a smoky skirmish with soldiers and figures in a rocky landscape. Inscribed 'Hugh 12th Earl of Eglinton' at lower right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Dress, sword, and the battle in smoke all match the image; Copley was working in London in 1780 and Montgomerie served with the 77th (Montgomerie's Highlanders) in North America during the Seven Years' War, which the background action is generally taken to depict. The one soft point is the purpose clause 'to mark Montgomerie's military service' - a reasonable reading of the picture rather than a documented commission term. The description does not name a collection; Commons places the picture in the National Galleries of Scotland, which could be added.

proposals.title: JohnMontresorByCopley
proposals.currentDescription: Captain John Montresor, the British military engineer who surveyed Quebec and Detroit, sits in three-quarter view in his red officer's coat. Copley painted the portrait in oil on canvas around 1771, during his Boston practice before he left for London on the eve of the Revolution. The Detroit Institute of Arts holds the canvas.
proposals.imageObservation: Half-length portrait of a man in a black tricorn hat with a gold cockade and tassel, a scarlet coat with black facings and gold buttons, white ruffled shirt cuffs; he rests his arm on a tree stump and holds a brown leather-bound book, his head turned in near profile to the left, with a patch of blue sky in a dark landscape behind.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Sitter, red officer's coat, oil on canvas, the c.1771 date and the Detroit Institute of Arts all come straight from the Commons record and credit line. Copley left Boston for Europe in 1774, so "during his Boston practice before he left for London on the eve of the Revolution" is sound. Montresor's engineering service in North America (including Quebec-route survey work and duty at Detroit) is well documented; I did not find grounds to challenge it, though "surveyed Quebec and Detroit" is a compression of a longer career. "Sits" is not quite verifiable — he leans on a stump and the lower body is cropped — but it is the conventional reading of the pose.

proposals.title: Head of a Person Asleep
proposals.currentDescription: A small, intimate study of a figure asleep, head sunk against bedding, kept in Turner's studio and bequeathed to the nation. The looseness of touch is closer to the colour-beginnings of his late watercolours than to anything he exhibited. It belongs to a private corpus of figurative sketches now in the Tate's Turner Bequest.
proposals.imageObservation: A small, badly abraded oil sketch: a head seen at an angle, eyes closed, resting on something pale at the lower left, painted in browns and ochres with a broad dark red vertical band down the right side; paint loss across the surface.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Spot-check of a prior 'accurate' verdict. Nothing checkable is asserted beyond the Turner Bequest / Tate holding, which the record's own provenance (inventory N05494, location Tate) supports. The comparison with the late colour beginnings is interpretation, not a factual claim about medium. Note the record's collection field says National Gallery while location says Tate - that is the normal Turner Bequest split, not an error.

proposals.title: Waves Breaking against the Wind
proposals.currentDescription: A pure marine, the canvas is given entirely to a churning sea raked by spray. Turner reportedly had himself lashed to a mast in storms; the picture's loose, scumbled paint claims that immediacy.

metadataIssues.evidence: the same provenance block gives location 'Tate' and describedAt tate.org.uk/art/artworks/turner-waves-breaking-against-the-wind-n02881; N02881 is a Tate (Turner Bequest) number

proposals.imageObservation: An almost abstract marine: grey-green breakers with white spray across the middle of the canvas, a pale yellow-lit sky at the upper right, dark storm cloud at the left, and a brown-ochre wedge of shore or shoal at the lower right. No vessels or figures.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The lashed-to-the-mast story is properly hedged with 'reportedly' - it is Turner's own much-repeated (and much-doubted) account attached to Snow Storm, not to this canvas, and the description does not claim otherwise. Minor overstatement in 'given entirely to a churning sea': there is a brown foreshore at lower right. Not enough to downgrade.

proposals.title: Linlithgow Palace
proposals.currentDescription: Linlithgow Palace rises through a warm golden haze above a wooded landscape, with bathers in the foreground pool and figures resting on the bank. The oil painting, dated circa 1806, translates a motif Turner drew on his Scottish tours into a richly atmospheric composition. It is held at the Walker Art Gallery, Liverpool.
proposals.imageObservation: A wide golden-hazed landscape: the long ruined block of Linlithgow Palace and a church tower stand on a wooded rise in the middle distance, with a dark still pool across the foreground where several nude bathers stand in the shallows and clothed figures sit on the sandy bank at the left, framed by trees on both sides.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Everything named — the palace above the haze, bathers in the foreground pool, figures on the bank — is in the frame. 'Circa 1806' matches the Commons date exactly, and the Walker Art Gallery, Liverpool, is confirmed by the record's own provenance block (WAG 2583) and by the Commons categories. The Scottish-tour sketch origin is properly hedged as a translation of a drawn motif.

proposals.title: Junks in Inatori Bay
proposals.currentDescription: A woodblock print by Japanese artist Takahashi Shōtei depicting traditional junks moored in Inatori Bay in the Izu region. Published in 1926, this work exemplifies the beauty of Japanese maritime scenes and traditional sailing vessels. The print measures 392mm by 268mm and is held in the collection of Te Papa Tongarewa, the Museum of New Zealand.

issues.quote: exemplifies the beauty of Japanese maritime scenes and traditional sailing vessels
issues.problem: Empty praise standing where a fact should be; it says nothing the reader could not guess from the title. It also leaves the description with no account of what actually makes the print distinctive — the dusk sky, the crescent moon and the lantern reflections.
issues.evidence: image — none of the print's actual visual content is described

proposals.imageObservation: A landscape-format woodblock print at dusk: three large wooden junks with tall bare masts lie moored close together in a bay, one with a partly furled pale sail, their cabin lanterns casting long reflections on grey-blue water; a crescent moon hangs in a deep blue sky above an orange horizon, a wooded headland and a lit village sit at the right, and a man sculls a small boat. Inscription and red seal at lower right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Every factual claim holds: 1926 corresponds to Taisho 15 as given on Commons, the 392 x 268 mm measurement is quoted verbatim from the Commons imageDescription, and Te Papa is the crediting institution (collections.tepapa.govt.nz). Verdict stays 'accurate' because the only defect is style, per the brief. If the corpus is being tidied for house style, this one is a good candidate for a rewrite that opens on the dusk harbour scene.

proposals.title: Jupiter and Juno Annibale Carracci fragment
proposals.currentDescription: A section of Annibale Carracci's fresco decoration of the Farnese Gallery in Rome, painted for Cardinal Odoardo Farnese and completed around 1602. The panel shows Juno, half-draped, coming to Jupiter on his couch, his eagle gripping a thunderbolt at the bedside and her peacock looking on; the scene is framed like an easel picture within an illusionistic surround of nude youths and feigned stone atlantes. The cycle of the Loves of the Gods made the gallery one of the founding monuments of Baroque ceiling painting.
proposals.imageObservation: A framed fresco panel showing a half-draped Juno leaning toward a bearded Jupiter reclining on a couch; a peacock stands behind her, an eagle grips a golden thunderbolt at the foot of the bed (confirmed by crop), and the whole is set inside a painted surround of grey stone atlantes, a green monochrome medallion and a nude youth in flesh tones.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Every visual claim checks out, including the eagle-with-thunderbolt, which I verified by cropping and enlarging the lower right of the quadro riportato. Odoardo Farnese as patron and the Farnese Gallery date of c.1600-1602 are standard art history; Commons' imageDescription independently gives 'Jupiter and Juno (1602), Palazzo Farnese'.

proposals.title: Kagurazaka Street at Night after Rain
proposals.currentDescription: A woodblock print from Hiroshi Yoshida's "Twelve Scenes of Tokyo" series (shin hanga). Completed in 1929, this composition captures a wet Kagurazaka street at night, rendered with the artist's characteristic approach to modern Japanese printmaking. Part of the Tokyo Fuji Art Museum collection.

issues.quote: rendered with the artist's characteristic approach to modern Japanese printmaking
issues.problem: Boilerplate; the description does not describe the lit shopfronts, fruit stall, umbrellas or the reflections that carry the picture.
issues.evidence: style

proposals.imageObservation: Colour woodblock print of a night street: a two-storey wooden building with lit paper lanterns and glowing upper windows, a street lamp, a fruit stall heaped with produce under an awning at the right, a few figures with umbrellas, and long yellow reflections in the wet roadway; Japanese inscriptions down the left margin, pencil-style title and signature below.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Date 1929, series and the Tokyo Fuji Art Museum credit are all in the Commons metadata. Style candidate only.

proposals.title: Kanae Yamamoto
proposals.currentDescription: An oil painting of Mount Fuji seen from Kami-Ide, a village at the foot of the mountain, painted by Yamamoto Kanae in 1938. The snow-streaked cone rises under drifting clouds beyond a foreground of plowed fields and autumn-red trees. Yamamoto, a pioneer of the sosaku-hanga creative print movement, devoted much of his later career to oil painting; the work is held by the Kanae Yamamoto museum in Ueda, Nagano.

metadataIssues.evidence: Yamamoto Kanae is the founding figure of the sosaku-hanga (creative print) movement, the rival tendency to shin-hanga - the description itself says so, contradicting the record. The work is also an oil painting rather than a print, so a print-movement tag fits it poorly either way.

proposals.imageObservation: An oil painting of Mount Fuji: the snow-streaked cone rises in blue-violet and white beneath pink-tinged clouds in a blue sky, above a foreground of ochre furrowed fields, bare and rust-red trees, and a dark green treeline. A red seal-like signature sits at lower right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Everything in the description matches the image (snow-streaked cone, drifting clouds, plowed fields, autumn-red trees) and the Commons record ('Oil painting by Japanese artist Kanae Yamamoto', 1938, credit 'Municipal Museum Kanae Yamamoto, Ueda'). Ueda is in Nagano prefecture and Kamiide lies at the southwest foot of Fuji in what is now Fujinomiya, so both place claims hold. The only defect is in the catalogue row, not the text.

proposals.title: Dutch girl in landscape
proposals.currentDescription: A color woodcut by Yamamoto Kanae of a girl in Dutch folk dress standing on a sandy path before a flat river landscape of fields, trees and a distant cottage, the scene built from broad, simplified planes of green and ochre. Yamamoto, the founding figure of Japan's sosaku-hanga movement of self-carved, self-printed artist's prints, took up European subjects of this kind in connection with his years of study in Europe from 1912 to 1916. The print is in the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.

metadataIssues.evidence: commons date field is 'before 1946', a copyright-derived upper bound, not a date of execution; Yamamoto died in 1946
Yamamoto Kanae is the founding figure of sosaku-hanga (creative prints), the movement usually set in opposition to shin-hanga; the description itself says so

proposals.imageObservation: A colour woodcut: a woman in Dutch dress - white cap, white shoulder cape, dark bodice and green skirt - stands on a broad sandy path in the foreground; behind her a flat river, green fields divided into planes, two slender trees, and a small white cottage with a red roof in the middle distance. Artist's seal at lower left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Everything visual matches, and Yamamoto's European study years (1912-16) and the MFA Boston credit are both supported. The record's year (1946) is a Commons copyright date rather than a date of execution and contradicts the description's own account of the European period - flagged as metadata, not as a description error.

proposals.title: Katsushika Hokusai
proposals.currentDescription: A polychrome woodblock print from Hokusai's series Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, published around 1830-32, known as Rainstorm Beneath the Summit (Sanka haku-u). While the peak of Fuji stands clear against drifting clouds, a storm breaks over the lower slopes and a jagged bolt of red lightning flashes across the darkened base of the mountain. The design is the stormy counterpart to the serene Fine Wind, Clear Morning, and ranks with the Great Wave among the most celebrated images of the series.

issues.quote: ranks with the Great Wave among the most celebrated images of the series
issues.problem: Ranking language; true enough as received opinion but it is the kind of superlative the house style avoids.
issues.evidence: knowledge

metadataIssues.evidence: The title field currently repeats the artist's name (it is the Commons file name); englishTitle already carries 'Rainstorm Beneath the Summit, from Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji'.

proposals.imageObservation: A framed colour woodblock print: Mount Fuji with a white snowcap and red-brown flanks rises against a graded blue sky with white cloud banks; the base of the mountain is almost black, and a branching red-orange lightning bolt runs across it. A title cartouche and signature sit at the upper left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The clear peak against clouds, the darkened base and the red lightning are all in the image; the identification as Sanka hakuu and the pairing with Gaifu kaisei (Fine Wind, Clear Morning) are standard. Note the reproduction is a photograph of a framed impression (Sailko's photo, Sumida Hokusai Museum category on Commons) — the description does not claim otherwise.

proposals.title: Snow in Mukojima
proposals.currentDescription: Thick snow falls through a darkening sky onto a boat landing at Mukojima, on the bank of Tokyo's Sumida River: moored boats lie blanketed in white, a stilt-built boathouse glows from within, and a lone ferryman crosses the still water. The 1931 color woodblock print shows Hasui's shin-hanga manner at its most atmospheric, using graded blues and untouched white paper to carry the weight of the snowfall. Snow scenes such as this became the works for which he is best remembered.

issues.quote: untouched white paper
issues.problem: A technique claim about how the snow was produced. The falling snow could equally be printed in white pigment or spattered; it cannot be settled from a reproduction.
issues.evidence: image — the flakes read as opaque white dots over the printed blues, which is at least as consistent with printed white as with reserved paper.

proposals.imageObservation: A vertical colour woodblock print in deep blues and greys: heavy snow falls over a river landing where several roofed boats lie under thick snow in the foreground, a dark timber building at the left shows a warm glow at one opening, a boatman poles a craft carrying a white paper lantern across the middle distance, and a second boat and a low far shore sit under a dark sky. Pencil titles 'Snow in Mukojima' and 'Hasui Kawase' below the image.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Site, river, date (昭和6年 = 1931), medium, the snow-laden moored boats, the lit building and the lone boatman are all confirmed by the image and the Commons record. Only the 'untouched white paper' technique detail and 'stilt-built' are shakier than the rest; neither is worth a rewrite, but a later pass could hedge the technique clause.

proposals.title: Kawase Hasui-No Series-Konjikido in Snow Hiraizumi
proposals.currentDescription: Kawase Hasui's final print design, published in 1957, the year of his death. Snow-covered stone steps climb between snow-laden cedars toward the hall sheltering the Konjikido, the famed Golden Hall of Chuson-ji temple at Hiraizumi, while a lone figure ascends under an umbrella through the falling snow. The design is traditionally honored as the artist's zeppitsu, or last work.
proposals.imageObservation: Colour woodblock print: broad snow-covered stone steps climbing between snow-laden conifers toward a wooden hall with a snow-covered roof; a single small figure with an umbrella partway up; snowflakes falling against a dark blue-grey sky. Title, seal and date inscriptions at the left and right margins.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Commons' own image description says 'Konjikido in Snow, Hiraizumi, final work' and dates it Showa 32 (1957), the year Hasui died; the covering hall (Oido) over the Konjikido is confirmed by the category 'Konjikido Ooido (Chusonji)'. 'Cedars' for the conifers is the one loose detail and is plausible for Chuson-ji, so I left it.

proposals.title: Киргизские кибитки на реке Чу
proposals.currentDescription: Kyrgyz felt tents (kibitki) pitched along the Chu river, which marks the border between present-day Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan. Vereshchagin recorded the encampment on his Central Asian travels of 1869 to 1870, the source material for his Turkestan series.
proposals.imageObservation: A large felt yurt with a red-and-ochre patterned door hanging stands on a golden steppe, a second yurt to the right, two riders and small standing figures nearby, a river at the left and a long snow-capped range under a pale sky; signed at lower centre right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Commons dates the work 'between 1869 and 1870' and files it under the Turkestan series, which supports both the travel dates and the series claim. The Chu does run along part of the Kazakhstan-Kyrgyzstan border, so that gloss is sound. The description omits the mountains, riders and river that dominate the picture, but asserts nothing false.

proposals.title: Китайская палатка
proposals.currentDescription: A Chinese tent standing in a Central Asian landscape, recorded as Kitayskaya palatka. The study comes from Vereshchagin's Turkestan travels of 1869 to 1870 across the Russian Empire's newly conquered frontier in Central Asia.
proposals.imageObservation: An oil study: a large blue tent with a white patterned border and a red inner panel is pitched on dry yellow steppe below low hills; a man in a white coat and cap stands at the left, a domed yurt with a smoking roof sits at the right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Commons dates it 'between 1869 and 1870' and files it under 'Turkestan series by Vasily Vereshchagin', which supports the description's travel dates and framing. The text is thin - it never mentions the tent's colour, the standing figure or the yurt - but nothing in it is wrong. Commons also categorises the painting under the Tretyakov Gallery, which the record's null provenance does not capture.

proposals.title: Крещение Руси
proposals.currentDescription: Viktor Vasnetsov's grand historical oil painting depicting the moment of the Christianization of Kievan Rus in 988 CE. The massive composition (214 × 187 cm) features multitudes gathered at a river for baptism, rendered in Vasnetsov's signature late-19th-century Romantic-realist style. A seminal work in Russian art celebrating the pivotal religious and cultural transformation.

issues.quote: A seminal work in Russian art celebrating the pivotal religious and cultural transformation.
issues.problem: Pure appreciation with no checkable content; 'seminal' and 'pivotal' are the kind of filler the house style excludes.
issues.evidence: house style

issues.quote: features multitudes gathered at a river for baptism
issues.problem: The one visual clause is vague and misses the central figure (Vladimir with raised arms), the clergy, and the distinctive arched top that marks it as a church design.
issues.evidence: image

metadataIssues.proposed: 187 x 214 cm (w x h), oil on canvas
metadataIssues.evidence: Russian sources for the 1890 Tretyakov Gallery canvas give 214 x 187 cm, matching the figure already quoted in the description

proposals.imageObservation: An arch-topped composition: Prince Vladimir stands on a carpeted dais with arms raised beneath a tall processional cross, flanked by clergy and boyars in gold and white vestments, crowds banked up on both sides, and naked figures entering the water across the foreground; angels and a cross in the clouds above.
proposals.reviewerNotes: I checked the dimension claim rather than assuming it was invented: Russian catalogue sources give 1890, oil on canvas, 214 x 187 cm, State Tretyakov Gallery, described as the preparatory composition (cartoon) for the west-wall mural of St Volodymyr's Cathedral in Kyiv (web search, veryimportantlot.com / rusmuseumvrm.ru). So the numbers are right and the record's year 1890 is right. Only hype and thin visual content remain, so the verdict stays accurate - but a rewrite could usefully name the Tretyakov and the cathedral commission.

proposals.title: Кронштадтский рейд Айвазовского
proposals.currentDescription: A marine painting by Russian seascape master Ivan Aivazovsky depicting the crowded anchorage at Kronstadt. Oil on canvas, 124 × 199 cm. Housed in the Central Naval Museum in Saint Petersburg.

issues.quote: Russian seascape master
issues.problem: Mild honorific; house style is plain and factual.
issues.evidence: house style.

proposals.imageObservation: A large ship of the line seen from astern rides at anchor in choppy golden-brown water under a broken storm sky, with two more sailing vessels and small craft to the right, a low fort at left, and two rowing boats of uniformed sailors in the foreground.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Medium, dimensions (124 x 199 cm) and the Central Naval Museum in Saint Petersburg all come straight from the Commons image description ('Kronshtadtsky reid. 1840. Kholst, maslo. 124h199sm. Tsentralny voenno-morskoy muzey'). The description is thin on what is actually in the frame but asserts nothing false.

proposals.title: Lakeside
proposals.currentDescription: A woman in a striped kimono sits by a calm lake, a round paper fan held loosely in her hands, with wooded hills visible across the water. Painted in 1897, Lakeside is among Kuroda Seiki's best-known canvases; trained in Paris under Raphaël Collin, he brought plein-air colour and a high-key palette to Meiji Japan. The work is held at the Tokyo National Museum.

metadataIssues.evidence: image | knowledge — this is an oil on canvas in a plein-air European manner, and Kuroda Seiki is the central figure of Yōga, the Western-style school, which is defined in opposition to Nihonga. The description's own 'plein-air colour' and Paris training point the same way.

proposals.imageObservation: An oil painting in a high-keyed blue-grey palette: a woman in a pale blue striped kimono sits on rocks by still water, holding a round white uchiwa fan in her lap and looking off to the right, with wooded shores and green hills across the lake behind her; signed 'SEIKI KURODA' and dated 1897 at the lower left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Description checks out entirely: striped kimono, round fan, calm lake and wooded hills are all in the frame; the 1897 date is signed on the canvas; the Tokyo National Museum holding comes from the record's provenance block. Kuroda's training under Raphaël Collin in France is well established. The only issue is the catalogue's movement field, which is the opposite of what this painting is.

proposals.title: Kustodiev Renee Notgaft
proposals.currentDescription: Renée Ivanovna Notgaft is shown in three-quarter length, seated in a green armchair in a black dress with a white neckline, a large bouquet of pink hydrangeas filling the background behind her. Kustodiev painted the portrait in 1914, in a mood of quiet elegance that contrasts with the vivid provincial festival scenes he would concentrate on in later years.
proposals.imageObservation: Three-quarter-length portrait: a woman with dark upswept hair sits in a pale green upholstered armchair with a dark red-brown frame, in a black dress with a white scoop-necked insert, right hand raised to her cheek showing a ring, left arm along the chair arm; hydrangeas in pink, white and lilac fill the upper left behind her against a plain green ground.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Sitter, pose, dress, chair, hydrangeas, 1914 date and Kustodiev's authorship all check out against image and Commons (the Russian title is 'Portret R.I. Notgaft'). Two small looseness points a rewrite could tighten but which do not amount to errors: the hydrangeas are pink, white and lilac rather than simply pink, and they occupy the left of the background rather than filling it — the right side is plain green. The closing claim about later provincial festival scenes is a soft generalisation; Kustodiev had already painted fair subjects before 1914, though the merchant-town series does belong mainly to 1915 onward.

proposals.title: The Night Watch
proposals.currentDescription: Captain Frans Banning Cocq in black with red sash steps forward giving the order to march, Lieutenant Willem van Ruytenburch in pale yellow strides beside him, and the company tumbles into motion behind. Signed and dated 1642, the canvas of 363 by 437 cm in the Rijksmuseum is the largest of the Amsterdam civic-guard group portraits.
proposals.imageObservation: A large militia group portrait: a captain in black with a broad white collar and a red sash strides forward at the centre, his hand extended, beside a lieutenant in pale yellow-buff with a wide hat and a partisan; behind them musketeers load and fire, a drummer beats at the right, pikes and a banner rise into the dark arch, and a small girl in gold catches the light at the left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Costumes, colours and action all match. The Rijksmuseum (SK-C-5) and the 1642 signature are supported by the Commons record. The 363 x 437 cm figure is the standard post-1715 measurement widely cited (the Rijksmuseum also quotes 379.5 x 453.5 cm including the strips restored in 2021), and the record carries no realDimensions to conflict with it — worth a second look only if the project wants the museum's current figure. 'Largest of the Amsterdam civic-guard group portraits' holds by area against the other big militia pieces.

proposals.title: Stilleben mit Früchtekorb
proposals.currentDescription: A kitchen table crowded with a fruit basket, pots and a folded cloth, the tabletop tipped sharply toward the viewer. Oil on canvas worked between 1888 and 1890, now in the Musée d'Orsay, Paris. Cézanne tilts the planes and crops the cloth at the lower edge to make geometric form, not accurate space, the subject.
proposals.imageObservation: A still life: a wicker basket of pears, apples and other fruit on a kitchen table, a lidded sugar bowl, a ginger jar and a small white teapot in front of it, a heavy white cloth draped across the table and running off the bottom edge; a chair and a second table behind; signed lower right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Objects, tipped tabletop and the cloth cropped at the lower edge all match. Commons gives 1888-1890 and the Musée d'Orsay categories, both as stated. 'Folded cloth' is loose for what is really a draped cloth, but not worth a downgrade.

proposals.title: The Last Judgment
proposals.currentDescription: Christ presides at the centre of a roiling vortex of saints, the resurrected, and the damned dragged toward Charon's boat, the entire altar wall of the Sistine Chapel given to a single muscular composition. Commissioned by Pope Paul III and painted in fresco between 1536 and 1541, the work was later partly draped by Daniele da Volterra under the censorship of the Council of Trent.
proposals.imageObservation: The full Sistine altar wall: Christ raising his arm at the centre of a ring of saints and martyrs, the blessed rising at the left, the damned dragged down at the right, Charon's boat and the trumpeting angels below, the lunettes above carrying the instruments of the Passion.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Christ at the centre, Charon's boat and the whole-altar-wall format are all visible. The Commons date field gives 1536-1541, matching the description and the record's year. Daniele da Volterra's added draperies following the Council of Trent are well established. One nuance not worth flagging: the commission was first given by Clement VII in 1533 and renewed by Paul III, so 'commissioned by Pope Paul III' is the common shorthand rather than the full story.

proposals.title: Le Bassin du Jas de Bouffan
proposals.currentDescription: The pond in the grounds of the Jas de Bouffan, the Cézanne family estate near Aix-en-Provence, ringed by trees with a sculpted lion spout at the water's edge. Cézanne painted the bastide and its garden in some thirty-six oils across forty years; this view, dated about 1876, is in the Hermitage Museum, Saint Petersburg.
proposals.imageObservation: A rectangular pond in the foreground reflects trees and yellow flowers; behind its stone rim run a low wall and a blue railing banked with yellow and pink flowers in pots, a gate with square piers at the centre, a pale outbuilding at the left, tall poplars and a dark chestnut canopy above. An ochre recumbent stone lion sits beside the gate and a dark carved spout pours water into the basin at the right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The specific-sounding number checks out: multiple sources on the Musée Granet's Jas de Bouffan exhibition give 36 oils (plus 17 watercolours) made at the estate over roughly four decades, so "some thirty-six oils across forty years" is grounded, not invented. The Hermitage is supported by the Commons category "Paintings by Paul Cézanne in the Hermitage" and by the credit line. One thing I looked at hard and decided not to raise: "a sculpted lion spout at the water's edge" compresses two features — there is a recumbent lion beside the gate and there are separate dark spouts discharging into the pond — but the lion is at the water's edge and the phrase is not demonstrably false.

proposals.title: Still Life with Bread and Eggs
proposals.currentDescription: A baguette, eggs, red onions, a pewter tankard, a knife and a wine glass arranged on a cloth-draped table. Oil on canvas, painted in 1865 and held by the Cincinnati Art Museum, one of Cézanne's earliest dated still lifes. X-ray scanning in 2022 revealed an earlier portrait beneath the surface.
proposals.imageObservation: Still life on a dark ground: a long pale loaf lying on a table, two white eggs, a red onion, a tall pewter tankard at left, a knife with a dark handle, a stemmed wine glass, and a heavy white cloth falling over the table edge. Signed and dated P. Cezanne 1865 at lower left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Every object listed is in the picture, and the canvas carries the date 1865 in the signature. Cincinnati Art Museum ownership is confirmed by the Commons credit link. The 2022 X-ray discovery is confirmed by multiple press reports from December 2022 (CNN, Smithsonian, The Art Newspaper): chief conservator Serena Urry's X-rays revealed a hidden portrait, widely thought to be a self-portrait. The description's careful phrasing ('an earlier portrait') is right not to assert the self-portrait identification.

proposals.title: The Artist's Father
proposals.currentDescription: The painter's father, the banker Louis-Auguste Cézanne, seated frontally in a large armchair and reading the newspaper L'Événement. Oil on canvas, 198.5 by 119.3 cm, painted in 1866 and held by the National Gallery of Art, Washington. It is the second of three portraits Cézanne made of his father.
proposals.imageObservation: A dark-suited older man in a cap sits frontally in a large floral-upholstered armchair reading a newspaper whose masthead reads L'EVENEMENT; a small still life of fruit hangs on the wall behind him, a brown door at right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Dimensions (198.5 x 119.3 cm), date, sitter, newspaper and the National Gallery of Art, Washington (Mellon Collection) all check out, and the 'second of three portraits of his father' claim is supported: the National Gallery, London canvas of c.1865 precedes it and a further portrait of c.1870-71 follows. The still life on the wall behind - an early Cezanne - is the one notable feature left out.

proposals.title: Captive Andromache
proposals.currentDescription: A long procession of women in flowing drapery filing toward a well, the widowed Andromache in black at the centre near a family group. Oil on canvas of about 1886 to 1888, the subject taken from a passage in Homer's Iliad. Manchester City Council bought the picture from Leighton for £4,000 in 1889; it hangs in Manchester Art Gallery.
proposals.imageObservation: A wide frieze-like composition: a long line of women in coloured drapery moves toward a fountain or well, water jars on heads and hips; a woman in a black hooded cloak stands alone at the centre; a seated family group with a baby at the right, men resting at the lower left; classical buildings and a mountain landscape behind.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Checked the purchase claim: multiple sources (Wikipedia's Captive Andromache article, Art UK / Manchester Art Gallery) give Manchester's purchase from Leighton in 1889 for GBP 4,000; one outlier says GBP 6,000. Date range 'about 1886 to 1888' matches Commons' 'circa 1886-1888'. Iliad source is correct.

proposals.title: Leighton Moses views the Promised Land
proposals.currentDescription: Moses views the Promised Land, by Lord Frederic Leighton , wood-engraving from Illustrations for “Dalziels' Bible Gallery” , engraved by the Dalziel Brothers and published 1881

issues.quote: Moses views the Promised Land, by Lord Frederic Leighton , wood-engraving from Illustrations for “Dalziels' Bible Gallery” , engraved by the Dalziel Brothers and published 1881
issues.problem: The text is the Commons caption verbatim, including its stray spacing and curly quotes; it never describes the figure, the summit or the sky, and it is not written as a sentence in house style.
issues.evidence: commons imageDescription is identical to the description

proposals.imageObservation: A wood-engraving: a bearded old man in a headcloth and heavy cloak stands barefoot on a rocky summit, gazing out; hatched clouds and distant mountains behind him.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Everything asserted is correct and matches both the image and the Commons record (Leighton, wood engraving, Dalziels' Bible Gallery, 1881). The only fault is that it is a pasted caption rather than a description; that is a style issue, so the verdict stays accurate and I wrote no replacement. A rewrite would simply add the standing figure on the rock.

proposals.title: Léopold Boilly Les conscrits de 1807 défilant devant la porte Saint-Denis
proposals.currentDescription: Young conscripts of the 1807 class marching past the Porte Saint-Denis as families crowd to bid them farewell. Oil on canvas, 84.5 by 138 cm, in the Musée Carnavalet, Paris, since 1888 and first shown at the Salon of 1808. The triumphal arch anchors the deep boulevard view behind the column of recruits.
proposals.imageObservation: A crowded Paris street scene: a column of young men in civilian dress moves left to right past the Porte Saint-Denis, embraced and watched by families, with a mounted officer and well-dressed onlookers at the right, dogs in the foreground and the boulevard receding to the left under a pale sky.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Verified: oil on canvas, 84.5 x 138 cm, Musee Carnavalet since 1888, exhibited Salon of 1808 (Wikipedia 'Departure of the Conscripts'; Paris Musees record; Commons categories 'Salon of 1808' and 'Paintings in Musee Carnavalet'). 'The triumphal arch anchors the deep boulevard view behind the column of recruits' is slightly loose - the arch is to the right of the marchers rather than behind them - but not worth a downgrade.

proposals.title: Life-Boat and Manby Apparatus Going Off to a Stranded Vessel Making Signal
proposals.currentDescription: Oil painting by Joseph Mallord William Turner depicting a dramatic maritime rescue scene, with a lifeboat and the innovative Manby apparatus being deployed to save a vessel in distress. The work showcases Turner's characteristic dynamic composition and atmospheric effects, capturing the tension and urgency of the emergency response at sea.

issues.quote: The work showcases Turner's characteristic dynamic composition and atmospheric effects
issues.problem: Empty appreciation ('showcases', 'capturing the tension and urgency') in place of what the picture actually contains - the breaking surf, the blue distress light, the wreck timbers, the figures on the beach.
issues.evidence: image | none of the visible incident is described

issues.quote: depicting a dramatic maritime rescue scene
issues.problem: The description restates the title rather than the frame, and omits the Victoria and Albert Museum, which the source evidence supplies.
issues.evidence: commons | imageDescription: 'oil on canvas by Joseph M. W. Turner at the Victoria and Albert Museum'

proposals.imageObservation: Stormy shore in oils: a huge breaking wave fills the left and centre, a boat with a mast and a bluish flare glows in the surf at left, timber wreckage lies on the wet sand in the foreground, two small standing figures at right, and a pier with masts and shipping in the hazy distance.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Nothing is contradicted: Commons confirms oil on canvas by Turner, 1831, and the Manby apparatus (Captain George Manby's line-throwing mortar, introduced 1808) is named in the work's own title. Verdict left accurate because the failings are stylistic, but this is a candidate for rewriting: it is generic, and the V&A location is available in the source and unused.

proposals.title: Lilium superbum
proposals.currentDescription: A Turk's cap lily (Lilium superbum) with downward-facing orange flowers spotted maroon, the petals sharply reflexed and curving back toward the stem. Plate from Redouté's Les Liliacées, published in Paris by Didot Jeune between 1802 and 1816. The print is a colour stipple engraving after Redouté, finished by hand.
proposals.imageObservation: A Turk's-cap lily: four nodding flowers and one closed bud on a stem with whorled lance-shaped leaves, the petals strongly reflexed, red-crimson at the tips shading to an orange-yellow throat spotted dark maroon. Two dissection vignettes — an ovary and a group of stamens — float at left and right, and the plate is lettered 'Lilium Superbum' / 'Lis Superbe' below.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The description matches the plate: nodding flowers, sharply reflexed petals curving back toward the stem, maroon spotting on an orange throat. The publication line comes straight from the record's own credit field ('Les Liliacees. Paris: Didot Jeune, 1802-1816') and the Commons category places it in Les Liliacées vol. 2. One conflict worth noting: the Commons file title and imageDescription call it a 'Lithographie', while the description calls it a colour stipple engraving finished by hand. Les Liliacées was produced by the colour stipple-engraving process, so I believe the description is right and the Commons title is wrong — but a human may want to settle it. The record's `year` is null and could reasonably be set to the 1802–1816 range.

proposals.title: Cymon and Iphigenia
proposals.currentDescription: Iphigenia asleep on the ground at evening, the herdsman Cymon halted at the right as he comes upon her. The subject is from a tale in Boccaccio's Decameron; Leighton exhibited the oil at the Royal Academy in 1884. The painting is now in the Art Gallery of New South Wales, Sydney, which acquired it in 1976.
proposals.imageObservation: A wide horizontal canvas: Iphigenia asleep on the ground in pale gold drapery beneath a dark tree, two further sleeping women at left and lower right, and a standing youth in a red cloak at the right looking down at her; a low sun or moon sits on the sea horizon behind, bathing the scene in warm orange-red.
proposals.reviewerNotes: All four checkable claims hold: the Decameron source (Day 5, story 1), the 1884 Royal Academy exhibition, the Art Gallery of New South Wales, and the 1976 acquisition — AGNSW's own accession number is 210.1976 and the gallery bought it at Christie's in London that year (web:https://www.artgallery.nsw.gov.au/collection/works/210.1976/).

proposals.title: Icarus and Daedalus
proposals.currentDescription: Daedalus fastening the wax-and-feather wings onto his son Icarus before flight, a subject from Ovid's Metamorphoses. Leighton painted the oil around 1869; it measures roughly 138 by 106 cm and belongs to the Faringdon Collection at Buscot Park, Oxfordshire.
proposals.imageObservation: On a white terrace above a bay, a nude fair-haired youth stands looking out to sea while a bearded older man in a gold skullcap and dark drapery stoops beside him, fastening a red sash or harness at his waist; a large white feathered wing rises behind them at left and a mass of dark drapery or a second wing at right, with a bronze statue on a column at far left and red drapery on the ground.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Checked the two specific assertions. The dimensions and collection hold: the painting is recorded as 138.2 x 106.5 cm, oil on canvas, Faringdon Collection Trust, Buscot Park, Oxfordshire, dated c.1869 — the description's 'roughly 138 by 106 cm' and 1869 are both right. Ovid's Metamorphoses is a correct source for the myth. Note that Commons files this under '1869 paintings in unidentified private collections', which conflicts with the Buscot Park attribution; the external sources are more specific and I trust them over the Commons category.

proposals.title: Lot and his Daughters
proposals.currentDescription: Beneath a tree the daughters press wine on their father while Sodom burns in the distance, a small dog and a still life of bread and cheese anchoring the foreground. Goltzius, the great Haarlem engraver turned painter, sets the nudes in cool, sculptural light typical of his late Mannerist style.

issues.quote: sets the nudes in cool, sculptural light
issues.problem: The modelling is sculptural, but the light is warm — golden and pinkish on the flesh, with a hot orange glow from the burning city. 'Cool' is off.
issues.evidence: image

proposals.imageObservation: Under a large tree, a bald bearded old man sits between two nude young women; he holds a decorated bowl which the daughter at right reaches toward, while the daughter at left leans back beside a red wine jug. A white-clothed table at lower left carries bread, cheese and grapes, a small brown dog sits below it, a fox looks out from behind the tree, and at the right a city burns orange on the horizon.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Re-checked as if fresh. Every element the description names is in the picture and in the Commons imageDescription: the tree, the wine, the bread and cheese, the little dog, burning Sodom in the distance. Goltzius as the Haarlem engraver who turned to painting late is standard and correct. The only quibble is the word 'cool' for what is a warm-lit picture; not enough to lower the verdict.

proposals.title: Game of Billiards
proposals.currentDescription: A billiard room crowded with players and spectators, a woman taking her shot at the centre of the table. Oil on canvas, 56 by 81 cm, in the Hermitage Museum, Saint Petersburg, dated 1807. The presence of women at the game reflects the looser social manners of the First Empire.
proposals.imageObservation: A crowded, skylit billiard room: a woman in a white Empire gown leans over the table to play her shot, another woman chalks at the far side, men in dark coats watch, and children, dogs and seated women fill the foreground; signed lower right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Every checkable claim holds: 1807, oil on canvas, 56 x 81 cm, Hermitage (Wikipedia 'A Game of Billiards' and the Commons categories 'Collections of the Hermitage Museum', 'Yusupov art collection'). The woman playing is just left of centre rather than dead centre - not worth a finding. The closing sentence about looser Empire manners is interpretive but matches the standard reading (mixed-sex play is what the picture is noted for).

proposals.title: The Barrel Game
proposals.currentDescription: Figures gathered around a tonneau game of skill, tossing discs toward the scoring holes of the cabinet. Oil on canvas, 37.8 by 46.8 cm, dated about 1828, in the Ramsbury Manor Foundation. Boilly drew the players in the tight finish he used for his late genre scenes of Parisian amusement.
proposals.imageObservation: A crowded outdoor courtyard beside a cafe: a wooden tonneau cabinet with scoring holes and drawers stands at centre-right, a man in a broad hat prepares to throw a disc while another bends to pick one up, and a large crowd of men, women and children watches; a battledore racket and shuttlecock lie on the ground and two dogs move through the scene.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Every hard fact in the description is a verbatim match to the Commons imageDescription: 'about 1828. Oil on canvas, 37.8 x 46.8 cm, The Ramsbury Manor Foundation.' The game shown is indeed jeu de tonneau.

proposals.title: The Geography Lesson
proposals.currentDescription: The paymaster Monsieur Gaudry instructing his daughter at a globe and map, the cartouche of which carries a sphinx and pyramid recalling Napoleon's Egyptian campaign. Oil on canvas, 73.6 by 59 cm, in the Kimbell Art Museum, Fort Worth, shown at the Salons of 1812 and 1814. The fine interior detail draws on the seventeenth-century Dutch genre pictures Boilly collected.

issues.quote: The paymaster Monsieur Gaudry
issues.problem: States the sitter's identity and profession as settled. Boilly exhibited the picture as 'M. G***'; the Kimbell titles it 'Portrait of Monsieur G.' and the identification as Gaudry, a paymaster, is traditional rather than documented.
issues.evidence: web:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Geography_Lesson — the sitter's identity remains uncertain; the catalogue record and Commons objectName do use 'Monsieur Gaudry'

proposals.imageObservation: A man in a brown coat, white stockings and red slippers sits at a table strewn with maps, loose sheets and books, a quill in his hand; a young girl in a white empire dress leans on his arm; a large terrestrial globe stands at the left, a marble chimneypiece with a candlestick at the right, a shaggy small dog on the patterned carpet at lower right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Dimensions (73.6 x 59 cm), the Kimbell Art Museum, and the Salons of 1812 and 1814 all check out (Commons carries 'Salon of 1812' and 'Salon of 1814' categories; the Kimbell/Wikipedia entry gives the dimensions). The sphinx-and-pyramid cartouche referring to the Egyptian campaign is stated by the Wikipedia entry on the painting; the map vignette is too small in this reproduction to confirm by eye, so I am taking that on the source rather than the image. Boilly's collecting of Dutch genre pictures is well attested. The dog goes unmentioned, which is fine.

proposals.title: The Reading of the Bulletin of the Grand...
proposals.currentDescription: A family gathered around a printed Napoleonic bulletin, tracing the army's progress on a map. Oil on canvas, 44 by 59 cm, in the Saint Louis Art Museum, shown at the Salon of 1808. The scene follows the campaign of the War of the Fourth Coalition against Prussia.
proposals.imageObservation: A dim interior crowded with figures of several generations gathered around a table on which a large printed sheet and a map are spread; an older man points at the map while a man in shirtsleeves leans over it. A woman nurses an infant at the left, children and dogs and cats occupy the foreground, and a violin and hat lie on a chair at the right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Every checkable claim holds: oil on canvas 44 × 59 cm and the Salon of 1808 are confirmed by the Wikipedia entry and the SLAM record, the Saint Louis Art Museum ownership by the Commons credit, and the War of the Fourth Coalition framing by the Wikipedia article. The description omits several vivid things in the frame (the nursing mother, the animals) but that is not an error.

proposals.title: The Young Harpist
proposals.currentDescription: A young woman seated at a pedal harp, her gaze turned toward the viewer. Oil on canvas catalogued 1977.152 at the Yale University Art Gallery and dated about 1804 to 1806. The harp signals the musical accomplishment expected of women in this period.
proposals.imageObservation: A young woman in a white empire-waist dress with an orange sash sits at a large gilt pedal harp, both hands at the strings, her head turned to meet the viewer's gaze; a chair and a blue object behind her, plain brown ground, visible craquelure.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Pose, harp, gaze and dress all match. Commons gives 'between circa 1804 and circa 1806', the Yale credit link and the accession number 1977.152 in the filename, and categories confirm oil on canvas at the Yale University Art Gallery. Final sentence is period-context interpretation, not a checkable assertion.

proposals.title: Woman Showing Her Portrait
proposals.currentDescription: A woman presents an oval portrait of herself to a small company while a gentleman peers at her through a magnifying glass. She appears twice, as both the living sitter and her painted likeness. Painted about 1790, oil on canvas, roughly 46 by 56 cm, in the Dallas Museum of Art.
proposals.imageObservation: An interior: a young woman in a white dress with a blue sash stands centre; behind her an oval gilt-framed portrait of a woman rests on a red chair, being uncovered by a boy holding a cloth. A man in a red-brown coat leans in holding a small lens to his eye; at left an older woman and a child in a green hat, with a dog on the floor.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Dimensions verified: DMA gives 46.36 x 55.56 cm, which matches 'roughly 46 by 56 cm'. Artist, date (1790) and collection all confirmed by Commons. Two soft points I chose not to flag: the lens the man holds is a quizzing glass rather than a hand magnifier (functionally the same thing), and his gaze may be directed past the sitter at the portrait rather than at her. Neither changes the sense of the sentence.

proposals.title: Love and Life
proposals.currentDescription: A winged male figure of Love guiding the slight nude figure of Life up a steep rocky path, violets springing where they tread. Watts called the picture a painted parable and first showed it at the Grosvenor Gallery in 1885. He gave a version to the United States; the work seen here is the one in the Tate (N01641).
proposals.imageObservation: A tall canvas in muted browns and greys: a large winged male figure supports a slender pale nude female by the hand and shoulder as she climbs a bare rocky slope; small dark flecks are scattered on the rock at her feet, and the background dissolves into pale mist.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Checked the three hard claims. Tate N01641 is confirmed as Watts's 'Love and Life', c.1884-5, presented by the artist in 1897 (web:https://www.tate.org.uk/art/artworks/watts-love-and-life-n01641). First exhibition at the Grosvenor Gallery in 1885 and the 1893 gift of a version to the United States (accepted by Congress in 1894, sent to the Corcoran after objections to the nudity) are both confirmed (web:https://victorianweb.org/painting/watts/paintings/7.html). 'Watts called the picture a painted parable' is the softest claim — the phrase is routinely attached to Watts's allegories but I could not source him applying it to this picture specifically; it is a plausible attribution rather than a verified quote. The violets are consistent with faint dark marks at the figures' feet but are not legible as violets at this resolution.

proposals.title: 冨嶽三十六景 下目黒-Lower Meguro
proposals.currentDescription: A woodblock print from Hokusai's celebrated 36 Views of Mount Fuji series, depicting the view of Mount Fuji from Lower Meguro in Edo-period Japan. Created circa 1830–32, this iconic work exemplifies the ukiyo-e tradition of landscape prints. The image is part of the Metropolitan Museum of Art's collection and is available in the public domain via Creative Commons CC0.

issues.quote: this iconic work exemplifies the ukiyo-e tradition of landscape prints
issues.problem: Hype plus boilerplate; the description never says what is in the frame (hamlet, thatched roofs, porters, pines, Fuji reduced to a distant white cone).
issues.evidence: style — house style asks the first sentence to describe the image

proposals.imageObservation: Colour woodblock print: a farming hamlet on rolling yellow-green hills with thatched roofs and straw stacks, a porter with a large round bundle on the path at left, travellers on steps at centre right, tall pines, and a small snow-capped Fuji far off between the hills; title cartouche and signature at upper left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: No factual problem: circa 1830-32, Met collection and CC0 are all in the Commons metadata. Purely a style candidate if the project rewrites content-free descriptions.

proposals.title: Male Nude
proposals.currentDescription: An academic study in oil on canvas of a reclining male nude, painted by Edgar Degas around 1856 during his years as a young art student in Paris. The canvas was reused, and traces of an earlier figure study, including toes and a bearded face, remain visible beneath the present nude. The painting is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York, a gift of Philip and Catherine Korsant in 2007.
proposals.imageObservation: A horizontal oil study of a male nude lying on his back on a brown cloth over a teal-green drape, head at the left with eyes closed, one arm flung above the head and the other extended toward the lower right; broad dark unfinished ground around the figure.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Every claim matches the Met catalogue text carried in the Commons imageDescription: 1856, oil on canvas, an unfinished student picture painted over an earlier figure study whose toes and bearded face show through, Gift of Philip and Catherine Korsant, 2007. The realDimensions in the row (34.9 x 61.6 cm) match the Met's measurements too.

proposals.title: Market at Jaffa
proposals.currentDescription: A bustling market square in Ottoman Jaffa rendered with Bauernfeind's near-photographic precision, every robe, awning and stone of the citadel sharply observed. A trained architect turned Orientalist painter, he based such scenes on extensive study trips and on-site sketches in the Levant.

metadataIssues.evidence: The Commons filename ('MarktJaffaGustavBauernfeind1887'), WikiArt and other Commons copies date it 1887, while this file's extmetadata says 1877. Bauernfeind's first journey to the Levant was 1880-82, so an 1877 date would put a studied Jaffa street scene before he ever saw the place. Medium confidence - the Commons text field for this file does say 1877.

proposals.imageObservation: Oil: a crowded market street in a Levantine town - massive banded stone masonry and a green-domed fountain house at the left, cloth awnings over stalls, a domed bazaar roofline, vendors seated on the ground with wares, a water pipe, a dog, a donkey, veiled women on steps, and low hills and sky at the right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Description makes no date claim, so the year problem is a metadata issue only. One soft spot worth knowing about: 'every robe, awning and stone of the citadel' - there is fortified-looking masonry in the background, but nothing identifies a citadel; it reads as a flourish rather than a fact. Not enough to lower the verdict.

proposals.title: Hunting Birds at Night
proposals.currentDescription: Peasants club pigeons flushed from the trees by torchlight, the flock caught in a burst of flame against the night. The subject came from Millet's own childhood memories near Gréville, and the canvas was his last completed painting before his death in 1875, now in the Philadelphia Museum of Art.
proposals.imageObservation: Two men swing clubs at a swirling mass of birds caught in a blaze of torchlight against a black night; more figures crouch over the ground in the foreground gathering the fallen. Signed at lower right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Sources describe the picture as drawn from Millet's childhood memories of hunters blinding flocks of pigeons with torchlight and clubbing them, and as his last work, painted at the very end of his life; the Philadelphia Museum of Art holding is in the credit field and Commons categories (William L. Elkins Collection, 1924). 'Near Greville' is right in substance - Millet was born at Gruchy in the commune of Greville. 'Last completed painting' is the strongest claim in the text; it is the standard characterisation but is a superlative, so treat it as supported-but-not-provable.

proposals.title: Miss May Prinsep by George Frederic Watts
proposals.currentDescription: Portrait of Miss May Prinsep by the English painter George Frederic Watts. Date painted: 1867-1869. Oil on canvas.

issues.quote: Portrait of Miss May Prinsep by the English painter George Frederic Watts. Date painted: 1867-1869. Oil on canvas.
issues.problem: A scraped catalogue stub in sentence fragments; it never says what the picture shows (a strict profile, the pale blouse, the plain brown ground).
issues.evidence: commons | the text is the Commons imageDescription field, truncated before the dimensions and the Watts Gallery credit

proposals.imageObservation: Bust-length portrait of a young woman in profile facing left, auburn hair pinned up, wearing a pale grey-white blouse with a lace collar and a dark ribbon, against a plain brown ground.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Nothing asserted is false: the Commons record gives exactly '1867-1869. Oil on canvas.' and adds '66 cm x 53.3 cm. Courtesy of the collection of the Watts Gallery', which a rewrite could safely use. The record's year of 1867 is the start of that range and does not contradict it.

proposals.title: La Porte d'Amont
proposals.currentDescription: An early seascape by Claude Monet showing the Porte d'Amont, one of the natural chalk arches in the cliffs at Etretat on the Normandy coast, painted about 1868-69. The evening sky glows through the opening of the arch while broken touches of sunset light flicker across the water below, an early statement of the coastal motifs Monet would return to at Etretat throughout the 1880s. The painting is in the Harvard Art Museums (Fogg Museum), Cambridge, Massachusetts.
proposals.imageObservation: A chalk cliff arch at Etretat seen close up, the sunset sky glowing pink through its opening with a needle rock beyond, dark seaweed-covered rock in shadow, and reflected light broken across shallow green water. Signed at the lower left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Subject, motif and the sunset through the arch are all visible in the picture; the Harvard Art Museums / Fogg attribution is in the catalogue's own provenance block (inv. 1957.163) and in the Commons credit link. The 1880s Etretat campaigns are well documented. Nothing to fix.

proposals.title: Morning on the Seine
proposals.currentDescription: One of the Mornings on the Seine series that Claude Monet painted at dawn from a moored studio boat where the river winds past Giverny. Trees and sky dissolve into their own reflections on the still water, the whole canvas given over to a single veiled harmony of early morning light. Painted in 1897, the picture is in the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.
proposals.imageObservation: A blue-green river scene: dense trees on the left bank and a further bank behind, all dissolving into their reflections in still water, with a pale lilac sky and its reflection running down the centre; signed 'Claude Monet 97' at lower left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The MFA Boston attribution is confirmed by the provenance field (inv. 11.1261) and the Commons credit URL; the 1897 date is in the signature. The Mornings on the Seine series painted at dawn from Monet's moored studio boat near Giverny is standard.

proposals.title: The Turkeys
proposals.currentDescription: White turkeys feeding across a grassy slope before the Château de Rottembourg, the birds cropped by the lower edge of the canvas. Monet painted the large panel in 1877 for his patron Ernest Hoschedé at Montgeron and showed it at the third Impressionist exhibition; it is now in the Musée d'Orsay.

issues.quote: the large panel
issues.problem: The work is oil on canvas, so 'panel' is loose if read as a support. It is defensible as the usual term for one of the four decorative panels made for Montgeron, which is clearly what is meant.
issues.evidence: commons categories — '1876 oil on canvas paintings in France'.

metadataIssues.evidence: commons categories date it 1876 ('1876 paintings from France', '1876 oil on canvas paintings in France') while the picture is signed and usually catalogued 1877; both are in circulation.

proposals.imageObservation: White turkeys with red heads and wattles scattered across a green lawn that slopes up toward a red-brick house with a grey roof among dark trees, under a yellow-and-grey evening sky; the bird at the bottom of the canvas is cut off by the lower edge.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Chateau de Rottembourg, Ernest Hoschede, Montgeron, the third Impressionist exhibition (1877) and the Musee d'Orsay are all confirmed by the Commons categories or by standard accounts, and the cropped bird is exactly as described. The only wobbles are the 1876/1877 dating and the word 'panel'; neither is worth a rewrite.

proposals.title: Monet w109
proposals.currentDescription: Heavy seas breaking against the pier at Le Havre, with the harbour lighthouse beyond, painted in 1868. At 147 × 226 cm it is one of the very large marine compositions of Monet's Salon-ambitious early years. Private collection.
proposals.imageObservation: A stone jetty with iron lamp standards runs into a heavy sea; waves break in white foam over the pier wall, a crowd of small dark figures walks along it, a lighthouse with a gallery stands at the far end, and a faint rainbow arcs at the right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: W109 checks out: La Jetee du Havre, 1868, oil on canvas 147 x 226 cm, refused by the Salon jury, private collection (Wildenstein W109 records surfaced by search agree on all four). Subject, lighthouse and heavy seas match the image. The rainbow goes unmentioned — an omission only.

proposals.title: The Studio Boat
proposals.currentDescription: Monet's floating studio, a converted boat moored on the Seine that let him paint from the water itself. Manet had recorded him at work in it; here the vessel becomes the subject, half-shaded under a bank of trees.

issues.quote: half-shaded under a bank of trees
issues.problem: The boat sits in front of a pale mass of trees rather than under them, and it reads as brightly lit, not shaded.
issues.evidence: image - the cabin is among the lightest passages in the canvas

proposals.imageObservation: A river scene in high-keyed pinks, creams and pale greens: Monet's studio boat with its pale cabin lies at the left bank, two small figures aboard - one seated at the stern, one standing beside the cabin - with a broad band of yellow-green reeds across the foreground and a mass of pink and russet trees at right. Signed 'Claude Monet' at lower left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Spot-check of an earlier 'accurate' verdict: substantively it holds. The Seine setting is confirmed by the Commons categories ('Paintings of the Seine by Claude Monet', "Monet's atelier-boat"), and Manet's Monet Painting on His Studio Boat (1874) does predate this 1875 canvas, so 'Manet had recorded him at work in it' is correct. Only the lighting clause is loose; not enough to warrant a rewrite, and the description otherwise omits the two figures aboard.

proposals.title: Hunting
proposals.currentDescription: A hunting scene from 1876, an unusual subject for Monet, who almost never painted narrative motifs. It belongs to the decorative panels commissioned by Ernest Hoschede for the chateau de Rottembourg at Montgeron.

issues.quote: A hunting scene from 1876, an unusual subject for Monet, who almost never painted narrative motifs.
issues.problem: The description never says what is in the frame — the leaf-covered path, the hunter with his gun, the game in the foreground.
issues.evidence: image vs description

proposals.imageObservation: A tall canvas: a path through an autumn wood carpeted in orange and yellow fallen leaves, a hunter in a blue smock and cap shouldering a gun in the right foreground, two or three further figures on the path beyond, and dead game lying at the lower right; signed lower left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: La Chasse (W433), 1876, is one of the decorative panels Monet made for Ernest Hoschede's Chateau de Rottembourg at Montgeron; the Commons category 'La chasse by Claude Monet' and the 1876 date support the record. The claims are true, so the verdict stands at accurate despite the missing visual content. Prior ledger status 'accurate' holds.

proposals.title: Monet w653
proposals.currentDescription: The chalk cliff at Grainval, just south-west of Fécamp on the Normandy coast, painted in 1881 during Monet's spring campaign there. Private collection (61 × 80 cm).
proposals.imageObservation: A grassy chalk headland fills the right foreground and drops to the sea; a pale green and blue sea occupies the left with three small sailing boats, and a further cliff headland recedes into haze at the centre right under a high overcast sky. Signed at the lower right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: I checked the one specific claim that had no backing in the record: Wildenstein 653 is catalogued as 'Falaise à Grainval près de Fécamp', 1881, 61 x 80 cm, private collection — matching the description exactly (web:https://www.impressionism.nl/monet-catalogue-raisonne/ and impressionism.nl's Normandy coast page). Grainval is in Saint-Léonard just south-west of Fécamp, which the Commons categories corroborate. Note the Commons 'date' field on this file is 14 November 1840, Monet's birth date, and is junk; the record's 1881 is right.

proposals.title: Monet w787
proposals.currentDescription: The beach and cliffs at Pourville in morning light, painted in 1882. The painting (French title 'Bord de mer et falaises de Pourville le matin') is held by the Tokyo Fuji Art Museum.
proposals.imageObservation: A beach at low tide filling most of the canvas, its wet sand broken by green weed-covered rocks and shallow pools reflecting blue and pink; white chalk cliffs rise at the left under a wide pale-blue sky. Signed at lower right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Wildenstein W787 is 'Bord de mer et falaises de Pourville le matin' (also given as 'Plage et falaise de Pourville, effet du matin'), 1882, Tokyo Fuji Art Museum, inv. 00128 — the French title, the year and the collection in the description all check out. Note that the Commons date field for this file is corrupt ('1840-11-14', Monet's birth date); the catalogue's year of 1882 is right and should not be 'corrected' to match the source metadata. Style only: the description is thin and never mentions the low tide and weed-covered rocks that occupy most of the picture.

proposals.title: Monet w849
proposals.currentDescription: A tall still life of poppies in a porcelain vase, painted in 1883, the year Monet moved to Giverny. The painting (W.849) is in a private collection.

metadataIssues.evidence: web:https://www.phillips.com/detail/claude-monet/HK010321/31 — 'Pavots dans un vase de Chine', painted in 1883, oil on canvas 100 x 61 cm, matching the record's realDimensions of 61 x 100 cm

proposals.imageObservation: A tall, narrow still life: five or six poppies — red, orange-white and pink — on long stems rising from a mass of blue-green foliage in a slim cylindrical vase decorated with pale flowers, against a mottled tan wall.
proposals.reviewerNotes: W.849 is 'Pavots dans un vase de Chine', 100 x 61 cm, dated 1883 — matching the record's dimensions and the description. Monet moved to Giverny in 1883, so that clause is right. 'In a private collection' is consistent with its appearance at Phillips Hong Kong in 2021 but is not independently confirmed for the present day; some sources place the work among the thirty-six panels made to decorate the doors of Durand-Ruel's drawing room, which would be worth adding if the parent wants more context. The record's year field is null and should be 1883.

proposals.title: Water Lilies
proposals.currentDescription: A nearly square oil on canvas from the group of water-lily paintings Claude Monet completed in 1907, depicting the lily pond of his garden at Giverny. The water surface fills the entire field of view: rafts of lily pads bearing pink blossoms drift across reflections of sky and trees rendered in veils of lavender, green and rose. The painting is in the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, accession number 19.170.
proposals.imageObservation: A nearly square canvas filled edge to edge with water: horizontal rafts of green lily pads carrying small pink and white blossoms drift across a surface of lavender, blue-grey, green and rose reflections, with no bank or horizon. Signed and dated "Claude Monet 1907" at the lower right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Format, subject, palette and the absence of a horizon all match the text exactly; the signature reads 1907. MFA Boston and accession 19.170 are in the record's own provenance block (Wikidata Q20538824) and in the Commons credit link.

proposals.title: Waterlilies Pond
proposals.currentDescription: A monumental canvas, two meters high and more than four meters wide, from the water-landscape decorations Claude Monet painted at Giverny between 1920 and 1926, in the orbit of the Grandes Decorations he ultimately gave to the French state. Known as Le Bassin aux nympheas, reflets verts (Waterlily Pond, Green Reflections), it stretches the pond's surface into a continuous field of deep green reflection scattered with lily pads. The painting belongs to the Foundation E. G. Buhrle Collection and is shown at the Kunsthaus Zurich.
proposals.imageObservation: A wide horizontal canvas of a pond surface with no horizon: blue-green and mauve vertical reflections run through the water, with clusters of pale lily pads and pink-red blossoms scattered across the lower and upper areas.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Dimensions in the text (two metres by more than four) match realDimensions 200 x 425 cm; the French title, the Bührle Foundation ownership and the Kunsthaus Zürich display are all in the record's provenance and the Commons credit. The 'deep green reflection' phrasing follows the work's own title (reflets verts) even though the surface reads as blue-green and mauve — not enough to call an error.

proposals.title: Wildenstein 1996
proposals.currentDescription: A close-up mass of chrysanthemums fills the entire canvas, their rounded heads in purple, yellow, red, and white packed so tightly that no background is visible. Monet produced a series of chrysanthemum studies in the 1890s at Giverny, treating the flower garden as a sustained subject in the same way he approached his series paintings. The paint is applied in short, looping strokes that follow each petal, building a dense decorative surface.

metadataIssues.evidence: the title is the Wildenstein catalogue number 1497; Monet painted his four Giverny chrysanthemum canvases in 1897, which is the group this close-up flower-bed composition belongs to. Worth confirming against the Wildenstein catalogue before applying.

proposals.imageObservation: Oil painting, vertical format: a dense mass of chrysanthemum heads filling the whole picture surface - mauve, violet, ochre-yellow, dark red and pale pink blooms - with no background, sky or ground visible, worked in short curling strokes.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The colours named (purple, yellow, red, white) are all present, the canvas is indeed filled edge to edge with no background, and the 1890s Giverny chrysanthemum series is documented. This entry is marked fabricated-fixed in the ledger; the current text is grounded. The only gap is the missing year in the record, flagged above as a suggestion rather than a certainty.

proposals.title: Montagne Sainte-Victoire
proposals.currentDescription: The limestone ridge of Mont Sainte-Victoire rises beyond a patchwork of fields and trees east of Aix-en-Provence. Oil on canvas of 1904, one of the last in the long series Cézanne painted of the mountain. He built the foreground from overlapping facets of green, ochre and blue that blur the line between plain and sky.
proposals.imageObservation: Oil landscape built from blocky parallel strokes: a blue-grey limestone ridge across the upper third under a blue and white sky, and below it a plain of green, ochre and blue patches with a few orange roofs.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Date (1904) and subject match the record and Commons. Mont Sainte-Victoire does lie east of Aix. The closing clause about the facets blurring 'the line between plain and sky' is loose — in the picture it is the plain/mountain junction that dissolves, the sky is above the ridge — but it reads as interpretation rather than a factual claim, so it does not move the verdict.

proposals.title: Morning Mist in Taj Mahal
proposals.currentDescription: A color woodblock print by Hiroshi Yoshida of the Taj Mahal looming through early-morning mist, its marble silhouette dissolving in pale light above the reflecting garden. The design, Morning Mist in Taj Mahal No. 5, belongs to the India and Southeast Asia series Yoshida produced after travelling across the subcontinent in 1930-31, returning to the monument at different hours in companion prints. It was published in 1932.
proposals.imageObservation: A colour woodblock print of the Taj Mahal seen head-on across its reflecting canal, pale marble against a cream-to-blue dawn sky, flanked by dark cypresses; eight small figures in orange, yellow and red robes stand on the near terrace, reflected in the water. Pencil title, number and signature in the lower margin.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The title, number 5 and 1932 date match both the pencil inscription in the margin and the Commons record. Yoshida's Indian journey of 1930-31 and the six Taj Mahal designs taken at different times of day are well established. The description does not mention the foreground figures, which are prominent, but nothing it says is wrong.

proposals.title: Mt. Heng, after Juran, from the Mustard Seed Garden Manual of Painting
proposals.currentDescription: Woodblock print from the influential Mustard Seed Garden Manual of Painting, designed by Wang Gai and published by Li Yu. This landscape depicts Mount Heng, rendered in the style of Northern Song painter Juran (active ca. 960–965).

issues.quote: This landscape depicts Mount Heng
issues.problem: House style asks the first sentence to say what is literally in the frame; nothing here describes the pines, houses, bridge, figure, seal or the printed double-page format.
issues.evidence: image | the printed opening shows a specific scene the text never mentions

proposals.imageObservation: A double-page woodblock book opening: an ink landscape of layered hills with tall pines at the left, a cluster of tiled houses, a figure crossing a bridge and a waterfall at the right; a four-character title inscription and a red seal occupy the blank sky at the upper right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Wang Gai as designer and Li Yu as publisher of the Jieziyuan huazhuan are standard and correct; the Juran attribution and the dates 'active ca. 960-965' are lifted from the Met's own title, as is 'Mt. Heng' (the inscription reads Ju Ran heng shan tu, and 'heng' here is the character for 'horizontal', so the Met's rendering may itself be loose). Calling Juran a 'Northern Song painter' sits oddly beside dates of 960-965, when he was still working under the Southern Tang; 'Five Dynasties to early Northern Song' would be safer. No claim is contradicted, so I left the verdict accurate, but a rewrite that opens on the picture would be an improvement.

evidence.sourceUrl: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:清_王槩_設計，李漁出版_芥子園畫傳_版本-Mt._Heng,_after_Juran_(active_ca._960–965),_from_the_Mustard_Seed_Garden_Manual_of_Painting_MET_DP-14004-001.jpg
evidence.fileUrl: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/7/7a/清_王槩_設計，李漁出版_芥子園畫傳_版本-Mt._Heng,_after_Juran_(active_ca._960–965),_from_the_Mustard_Seed_Garden_Manual_of_Painting_MET_DP-14004-001.jpg
evidence.objectKey: collection-of-beauty/清_王槩_設計，李漁出版_芥子園畫傳_版本-Mt._Heng,_after_Juran_(active_ca._960–965),_from_the_Mustard_Seed_Garden_Manual_of_Painting_MET_DP-14004-001.jpg

proposals.title: Мулла Рахим и мулла Керим по дороге на базар ссорятся
proposals.currentDescription: Vasily Vereshchagin's 1873 orientalist painting depicting two mullahs quarreling on the way to the bazaar. Part of his Turkestan series, exemplifying his ethnographic visual documentation of Central Asia.

issues.quote: exemplifying his ethnographic visual documentation of Central Asia
issues.problem: Generic closing clause; the description also never mentions that the men are mounted on donkeys, which is the picture's most concrete detail.
issues.evidence: image

proposals.imageObservation: Two men in striped robes and turbans (one red, one white) sit on donkeys facing each other on a dusty road, one pointing at the other in argument; a third robed rider follows behind and two small figures walk further off, under a pale blue sky over flat scrub.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Subject, date (1873, per Commons and Wikidata) and the Turkestan series membership are all confirmed by the source record. Thin but not wrong.

proposals.title: Starlit Night at Miyajima
proposals.currentDescription: From the shin-hanga series Souvenirs of Travel III, this nocturne shows the floating torii of Itsukushima beneath a star-pricked sky. Hasui pairs deep indigo bokashi gradations with sparse highlights to register the hush of Miyajima after dark.
proposals.imageObservation: Woodblock print in blues and teals: the floating torii of Itsukushima and its railed causeway stand in still water, mirrored below; a dark pine branch overhangs from the upper left, a handful of white stars pricks the graded night sky, a hill lies across the bay, and a stone lantern in the right foreground shows two small windows glowing warm yellow. Artist's seal and title cartouche at the left, publisher's mark at the right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Series, subject and technique all check out against the Commons record ("Starlit Night at Miyajima (Hoshizukiyo [Miyajima]), from the series Souvenirs of Travel III", NDL Digital Collections, 昭和3年 = 1928). The graded bokashi sky and the "sparse highlights" (stars and the lit lantern) are both visible.
