The only thing the text leaves out is the foreground stone lantern and the pine branch — an omission, not an error, so the verdict stands.

proposals.title: Meguro Fudō Temple
proposals.currentDescription: A shin-hanga woodblock print by Kawase Hasui of Ryusen-ji, popularly known as the Meguro Fudo temple, in Tokyo. Seen from beside the vermilion main hall, a woman in kimono pauses at the entrance while blossoms show beyond the gate roofs and dappled light falls across the stone steps and lanterns of the precinct. The print was published in 1931; this impression is preserved in the National Diet Library, Tokyo.
proposals.imageObservation: Colour woodblock print of a temple precinct: vermilion pillars and a dark tiled roof at the right, a woman in a blue kimono standing at a doorway at the left, a two-storey vermilion gate behind with cherry blossom beyond, a stone lantern with a white paper lantern at the right, and dappled sunlight across the stone paving and steps. Title, signature and seal at the left, publisher inscription at the lower right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Everything checks: Ryusen-ji is the Meguro Fudo (Commons category 'Ryusen-ji (Meguro) in ukiyo-e'), Showa 6 is 1931, and the NDL Digital Collections credit supports the impression's location. The description's visual detail matches the print closely.

proposals.title: Nichiren bezweert de golven bij Kakuda tijdens zijn verbanning naar Sado
proposals.currentDescription: The Buddhist reformer Nichiren stands in a pitching boat off Kakuda, calming the waves with the Lotus Sutra during his exile to Sado. Kuniyoshi's woodblock print sets red robes against churning blue surf in the dramatic warrior-print idiom of late Edo Utagawa school design.
proposals.imageObservation: A colour woodblock print: a shaven-headed monk in a red robe stands in the bow of a boat crowded with frightened passengers, its prow tipped up by towering blue waves with white crests; grey night clouds and a distant mountainous shore behind, faint characters visible in the water at the left, artist's seal and signature at the left, title cartouche at the right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The Rijksmuseum text (in the source evidence) confirms the reading precisely: Nichiren standing in red robe in a full boat, calming the high waves with the sutra visible in the water, from Kuniyoshi's Kōso goichidai ryakuzu series. The record's year 1833 sits at the start of the Rijksmuseum's 1833-1837 range, which is fine.

proposals.title: Nighthawks
proposals.currentDescription: Edward Hopper's oil on canvas of 1942 shows a late-night diner on a deserted New York street corner, its three customers and white-jacketed counterman sealed behind curving plate glass under harsh electric light. The painting's air of urban solitude has made it the most famous image of Hopper's career and one of the most widely recognized works of American art. The Art Institute of Chicago bought it from the artist within months of its completion in 1942, and it remains there in the Friends of American Art Collection.
proposals.imageObservation: A wedge-shaped corner diner behind a curving band of plate glass, lit hard and yellow-green from within: a man with his back to us at the near end of the counter, a couple seated further along, and a counterman in a white jacket and cap stooping behind the bar; two coffee urns at right, a 'PHILLIES' sign along the top of the diner, and dark empty shopfronts across a deserted street.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Everything matches: three customers, white-jacketed counterman, curved plate glass, deserted corner. The purchase claim is right too — the Art Institute of Chicago acquired the painting in 1942, within months of its completion (Commons gives the date as 21 January 1942), and it is in the Friends of American Art Collection, accession 1942.51 as recorded in the provenance field.

proposals.title: Nihon fūkei senshū
proposals.currentDescription: A large Japanese sailing vessel with billowing white sails occupies the centre of the composition, its hull reflected in the calm blue water, with rocky headlands rising behind. The print belongs to Hasui's Selected Views of Japan series, published in 1923, and depicts the coastal waters off Iwafune in the former Bingo Province. Hasui's characteristic clear sky and precise colour planes give the scene an air of quiet confidence.
proposals.imageObservation: A shin-hanga woodblock print: a wooden coastal sailing boat with an ochre hull and two tall white sails floats on flat blue water that carries a long white reflection, with green-and-ochre hills behind and a smaller sailing boat at left; title cartouche and date at the left margin, artist's seal lower right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Series, subject, 1923 date and woodblock medium all confirmed by the Commons record ('Iwafune in Bingo Province, from the series Selected Views of Japan'). Two small looseness points, not errors: the sails are drawn taut rather than 'billowing', and the reflection in the water is mostly of the sails rather than the hull.

proposals.title: Nude against the light pierre bonnard
proposals.currentDescription: A luminous composition by French Post-Impressionist painter Pierre Bonnard depicting a female figure silhouetted against backlighting. The painting exemplifies Bonnard's characteristic use of color and light, with the nude rendered through subtle chromatic nuances and the interplay of shadow and brilliance. Housed in the Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium.

issues.quote: The painting exemplifies Bonnard's characteristic use of color and light, with the nude rendered through subtle chromatic nuances and the interplay of shadow and brilliance.
issues.problem: Pure boilerplate. The room - the tub, the washstand and mirror, the flowered bed, the lace curtain - is the substance of this picture and goes unmentioned; 'luminous composition' and 'exemplifies' are filler.
issues.evidence: house style - first sentence should describe what is literally in the frame

proposals.imageObservation: A standing nude seen in profile against a lace-curtained window, holding a small bottle to her chest; behind her a bed with a pink floral cover, patterned wallpaper, a washstand with mirror at the left and a large round tub in the lower left foreground.
proposals.reviewerNotes: No claim here is false: the backlit standing nude and the Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium are both confirmed (Commons: 'Nu a contre-jour', Musees royaux des beaux-arts de Belgique; categories place it in the Fin-de-Siecle Museum). Verdict stays accurate per the rule that style does not lower it, but this is a strong candidate for a rewrite pass on style grounds alone.

evidence.objectKey: collection-of-beauty/Nude against the light pierre bonnard.jpg

proposals.title: Old guitarist chicago
proposals.currentDescription: Oil painting by Pablo Picasso from his Blue Period. An elderly blind musician clutches his guitar, rendered in muted blues and grays. The work is held at the Art Institute of Chicago.

issues.quote: An elderly blind musician
issues.problem: Blindness is the conventional reading of the figure rather than anything the picture states; the eyes are simply closed.
issues.evidence: image + knowledge — the Art Institute's and most literature's characterisation of the sitter as blind is interpretive.

metadataIssues.evidence: The picture is a 1903-04 Blue Period work, several years before Picasso's Cubism; the description itself says 'from his Blue Period', so the row contradicts its own text.

proposals.imageObservation: A gaunt, elderly man with closed eyes and bowed head sits cross-legged, cradling a large brown guitar; the whole picture is painted in blues and blue-greys apart from the ochre instrument.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The Commons record for this file came back missing, so the check rests on the image and general knowledge. Everything in the text is right, and note it says 'oil painting' rather than 'oil on canvas' - correct, since the Art Institute records the support as panel. The only real problem is the catalogue row's movement field.

proposals.title: Old Korea-Keith-BRIDE
proposals.currentDescription: A portrait of a Korean bride in traditional hanbok wedding attire. Published in "Old Korea: the Land of Morning Calm" by Elizabeth Keith and Elspet Keith Robertson Scott (Hutchinson & Co. , 1946).

issues.quote: A portrait of a Korean bride in traditional hanbok wedding attire.
issues.problem: Accurate but thin: the kneeling pose, the beaded headdress, the striped sleeves and the painted screen behind are the picture's substance and go unmentioned.
issues.evidence: image

proposals.imageObservation: A young woman kneels on a green floor cushion before a folding screen painted with birds and flowering branches; she wears a green jacket with a red-trimmed collar, an elaborate beaded headdress with red ornaments and long red hair ribbons, and layered skirts striped in red, pink, blue, yellow, green and white; her eyes are lowered and her hands are hidden in her sleeves.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Matches the Commons record exactly ('Korean Bride' from Old Korea: the Land of Morning Calm, Keith and Robertson Scott, Hutchinson & Co., London 1946). The record's year of 1938 and the 1946 publication are not in conflict — the description says 'published in'. A style-only expansion would improve it; nothing to correct.

proposals.title: Ornament with Owl Mocked by Day Birds
proposals.currentDescription: An engraving by Martin Schongauer in which an owl with outstretched wings perches at the base of a dense thicket of curling foliage, harried by the small day birds that dart through the scrollwork above. The owl mocked by daytime birds was a familiar medieval emblem of folly attracting scorn, and Schongauer works the motif into an ornament design of the kind used as a model by goldsmiths and other craftsmen. The sheet bears his monogram and belongs to the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.
proposals.imageObservation: A fine line engraving: a vertical panel of dense curling acanthus scrollwork, an owl with spread wings crouching at the bottom centre, small birds among the foliage at the top and left, and the monogram M+S engraved at the bottom edge.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Every visual claim checks out: owl with outstretched wings at the base, small birds in the scrollwork above, monogram present at bottom centre. Commons categories confirm 'Engravings by Martin Schongauer' and the Met donation. The 'model for goldsmiths and other craftsmen' line is standard, well-established art history about Schongauer's ornament prints rather than a specific unsupported assertion.

proposals.title: Parson Weems’ Fable
proposals.currentDescription: Painting depicting Parson Weems and his famous story of George Washington and the Cherry Tree.

issues.quote: Painting depicting Parson Weems and his famous story of George Washington and the Cherry Tree.
issues.problem: A single sentence lifted verbatim from the Commons file description; it names the subject but describes nothing in the frame - not the curtain Weems pulls back, not Washington's grown-up head, not the hatchet.
issues.evidence: commons imageDescription is word-for-word identical

proposals.imageObservation: Parson Weems at the right draws back a red tasselled curtain and points into the scene: young Washington, with Gilbert Stuart's adult head, holds a hatchet before his father beside a felled cherry tree, in front of a pink Georgian house with figures picking cherries beyond.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Nothing false, but this is the thinnest entry in the batch and is a straight copy of the Commons caption. A rewrite grounded in the image (curtain, pointing parson, adult head on the child's body, hatchet, cherry tree) would be an easy win; date 1939 and Grant Wood's authorship are confirmed by Commons.

proposals.title: Bathers
proposals.currentDescription: A group of nude bathers is arranged beneath arching trees that frame the composition like a vault, their bodies echoing the leaning trunks. One of three large Baigneuses Cézanne worked on between 1894 and 1905; this canvas is in the National Gallery, London. He sacrificed individual likeness to fit the figures to the triangular structure of the trees.
proposals.imageObservation: Roughly ten nude bathers, seated and standing, spread across the foreground beneath tree trunks that lean in from both sides to form a vault; blue-dominated palette with ochre ground and a bank of white cloud in the distance.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Composition matches. Commons gives 'between 1894 and 1905' and the Google Art Project / National Gallery, London categories, so both the date span and the collection are backed. The three large Baigneuses (London, Barnes, Philadelphia) is standard art history. Final sentence is interpretation of the kind the National Gallery's own commentary makes.

proposals.title: Bottle
proposals.currentDescription: A dark bottle, a glass carafe, a stoneware jug and a scatter of lemons stand on a draped table. Watercolour and graphite on paper of about 1902 to 1906, in the Museo Thyssen-Bornemisza in Madrid. Cézanne left much of the sheet bare, letting the white paper carry the highlights between thin washes.

metadataIssues.evidence: commons objectName — 'Bouteille, carafe, cruche et citrons' / 'Bottle, carafe, jug and lemons'; the current title looks like a truncation of the full one.

proposals.imageObservation: A watercolour over pencil on cream paper: a tall bottle at the left, a round-bellied carafe at centre, a white jug with blue floral decoration at the right, and two or three yellow lemons on a dark table top, with blue-grey washes behind and the lower third of the sheet left almost bare.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Medium (watercolour with visible graphite underdrawing), the reserved white paper, the 1902-1906 dating and the Museo Thyssen-Bornemisza all check out against the image and the Commons record. 'Stoneware jug' is a guess about material — the jug reads as tin-glazed earthenware — but it is too small a point to lower the verdict.

proposals.title: Les Grandes Baigneuses
proposals.currentDescription: Nude female figures arranged in two groups beneath a vault of leaning trees, the bodies pared to broad blue and ochre planes. The largest of Cézanne's Bather canvases, oil on canvas, about 210 by 251 cm, worked on over roughly seven years and left unfinished at his death in 1906. It entered the Philadelphia Museum of Art in 1937.
proposals.imageObservation: A large canvas of nude female bathers in two groups at left and right, framed by tall trunks leaning inward to a triangular vault; between the groups a stretch of water, a distant bank with a church spire and two small figures; bodies built from broad blue, ochre and cream planes.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Composition, palette and the two-group arrangement match. The Philadelphia Museum of Art version is the largest of the Bathers at about 210 x 251 cm, was worked on in Cezanne's last years and left unfinished at his death in 1906, and was purchased by the museum in 1937 — all consistent with the Commons date and the Philadelphia categories. I did not find a page contradicting the 1937 acquisition; it is the one claim I would confirm against the PMA record before relying on it.

proposals.title: Houses in Provence: The Riaux Valley near L'Estaque
proposals.currentDescription: Pale ochre houses clustered on a plateau above the Riaux valley, the rocky hillside built up in cool blues and greens beneath a high sky. Oil on canvas painted around 1883 near L'Estaque on the Mediterranean coast, now in the National Gallery of Art, Washington. Cézanne worked the terrain in faceted planes of colour rather than line.
proposals.imageObservation: Landscape in oils: pale ochre houses with red-tiled roofs stand on a terrace mid-slope, surrounded by hillside broken into patches of green, blue-grey and ochre with pale rock outcrops; a narrow band of blue-grey sky runs across the top.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Colours, the ochre houses and the faceted handling all match the image, the c. 1883 date matches the Commons date field and the record, and the National Gallery of Art, Washington is supported by the Commons category 'Google Art Project works in National Gallery of Art, Washington DC'. 'Plateau' is a slightly loose reading of the terrace the houses sit on, not worth a downgrade.

proposals.title: The Bather
proposals.currentDescription: An adolescent boy mid-stride in a pale watery landscape, hands on his hips, his body slightly out of proportion. Oil on canvas of about 1885 based on a studio photograph of a posed model, now in the Museum of Modern Art, New York, from the Lillie P. Bliss Collection.
proposals.imageObservation: A young man in white trunks stands facing the viewer with hands on his hips and head lowered, one leg advanced, in a pale blue-green and ochre landscape with a strip of water behind him.
proposals.reviewerNotes: MoMA and the Lillie P. Bliss Collection are supported by the Commons categories ('Google Art Project works in MoMA', 'Paintings by Paul Cezanne in the Museum of Modern Art'), and the photographic source for the pose is the standard MoMA account. 'Mid-stride' is a slightly generous reading of a mostly static stance but is defensible from the advanced leg.

proposals.title: Madame Cézanne with Green Hat
proposals.currentDescription: Hortense Fiquet, the painter's wife, sits in three-quarter view wearing a broad green hat, her hands folded in her lap. Oil on canvas of about 1891 to 1892, catalogued BF141 in the Barnes Foundation in Philadelphia. Cézanne built the face and bodice from planes of dull violet, ochre and grey-green laid side by side.

issues.quote: sits in three-quarter view
issues.problem: The figure is close to frontal, with only a slight turn of the body; 'three-quarter view' overstates the turn (it is accurate if read as three-quarter length).
issues.evidence: image.

proposals.imageObservation: A woman seated almost frontally in a wooden armchair with scrolled arms, hands clasped in her lap over a blue-grey skirt, wearing a dark blue-black buttoned bodice and a wide green hat trimmed with green foliage; the wall behind is worked in blue, green and grey patches with a dark dado rail.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Sitter, hat, clasped hands, the 1891-92 dating, BF141 and the Barnes Foundation are all confirmed by the Commons record and the image. The colour list in the last sentence ('dull violet, ochre and grey-green') omits the dominant dark blue of the bodice but is not wrong about what is there; not enough to lower the verdict.

proposals.title: Pyramid of Skulls
proposals.currentDescription: Four human skulls are stacked in a low pyramid on a bare tabletop against a dark ground. Oil on canvas painted between about 1898 and 1900, the only Cézanne to push the skulls so close to the viewer. He owned several skulls and returned to them in oil and watercolour in his final decade at Aix.
proposals.imageObservation: Oil still life: four human skulls stacked in a pyramid - one at the top, two large ones in front, a darker one behind right - on a pale surface against a dark brown-black ground.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Count is right (four skulls). The 1898-1900 dating matches the Commons date field and the record year, though the Commons file title says 'c. 1901' - a source disagreement, not a description error. The superlative was worth testing and holds: the literature on this picture states that in no other painting did Cezanne place his objects so close to the viewer. Cezanne did own skulls and painted them repeatedly in his last years at Aix. Minor caveat: the pale plane under the front skulls could be a cloth rather than a 'bare tabletop'; too ambiguous in the reproduction to call an error.

proposals.title: Le Meurtre
proposals.currentDescription: A violent scene in which two figures pin a third to the ground beside a body of water under a heavy sky. Oil on canvas, 64 by 81 cm, painted around 1870 and held by the Walker Art Gallery, Liverpool, under inventory WAG 6242. It belongs to the dark, dramatic subjects of Cézanne's early years.

metadataIssues.evidence: Commons date is '(1867 - 1870)' and the Walker Art Gallery / Art UK entry dates it c.1870; the description's 'around 1870' therefore disagrees with the record's flat 1867 rather than with the sources

proposals.imageObservation: Two figures - one in a white shirt and blue trousers with an arm raised, one in a yellow-brown garment bearing down with both hands - pin a third, prone figure to the ground; dark, heavily loaded paint, a pale patch of water or sky at the left, brooding landscape.
proposals.reviewerNotes: I checked the two specifics that looked like hallucination bait and both are right: Art UK / National Museums Liverpool give The Murder as oil on canvas, H 64 x W 81 cm, accession WAG 6242, Walker Art Gallery. Only the date wobble between description and record is worth noting.

proposals.title: Перед атакой. Под Плевной
proposals.currentDescription: A dramatic military history painting by Vasily Vereshchagin depicting Russian soldiers preparing for battle during the Siege of Plevna (1877), a pivotal engagement of the Russo-Turkish War. The work is part of Vereshchagin's celebrated Balkan series documenting contemporary warfare with unflinching realism. Oil on canvas, held in the Tretyakov Gallery collection.

issues.quote: A dramatic military history painting
issues.problem: Opens on an evaluative label instead of the scene; "celebrated" and "unflinching realism" in the following sentences are the same kind of filler, and the prone infantry, the officers with field glasses and the haystack are never described.
issues.evidence: house style — the first sentence should say what is literally in the frame

proposals.imageObservation: A wide horizontal canvas: rows of Russian infantry in dark greatcoats lie prone in dry stubble with rifles and rolled white kit, waiting; at the left a group of officers stands beside a haystack, one looking through field glasses; smoke drifts across the empty plain beyond a low hedge, and a small tower stands on the ridge at the upper left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Factually it holds: the picture belongs to Vereshchagin's Balkan series, shows Russian troops waiting before the third assault on Plevna (1877), and is in the State Tretyakov Gallery — Tretyakov confirmed at my.tretyakov.ru masterpiece 20707 and by art-catalog.ru, which also gives oil on canvas, 183 × 401 cm, 1881. Verdict kept at accurate because the style problems do not change any fact; a rewrite would still be an improvement if the batch is being edited for house style anyway.

proposals.title: Петр I при Красной горке Айвазовский
proposals.currentDescription: Oil on canvas depicting Tsar Peter I at Red Hill, painted in 1846. The work measures 223 x 335 cm and is housed in the State Russian Museum in Saint Petersburg. Aivazovsky's historical narrative captures a moment from Russian imperial history in his characteristic dramatic style.

issues.quote: Aivazovsky's historical narrative captures a moment from Russian imperial history in his characteristic dramatic style
issues.problem: Style note only: the description never says what is in the frame (night, signal fire, ships, moon). Does not affect the verdict.
issues.evidence: image.

proposals.imageObservation: Night seascape in oil: a standing figure on rocky ground at the right beside a blazing signal fire tended by a second figure, a bare wind-bent tree above; sailing ships stand offshore under a broken moonlit sky; signed and dated lower right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Every checkable claim is confirmed by the Commons file description: oil on canvas, 1846, 223 x 335 cm, State Russian Museum, Saint Petersburg. Only weakness is that it is pure catalogue data with no visual content; left unrewritten because nothing is wrong.

proposals.title: Marriage of Sisley
proposals.currentDescription: A double portrait of Renoir's friend the painter Alfred Sisley standing beside his companion, both in fashionable contemporary dress, the woman's arm through his. Painted in 1868 and now in the Wallraf-Richartz-Museum, Cologne, where it is catalogued as Das Ehepaar Sisley.
proposals.imageObservation: A bearded man in a dark suit and light grey trousers, top hat in his lowered left hand, leans toward a woman in a red-and-yellow striped dress with a white lace-trimmed bodice; her hand is clasped in his and her arm passes through his. They stand on a path in a green garden.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Pose, dress and the linked arms match. The Commons object name is 'Das Ehepaar Alfred Sisley', which supports both the Sisley identification and the German catalogue title quoted. The Wallraf-Richartz-Museum attribution is not in the Commons metadata but is the standard location for this picture. Worth knowing that the identification of the sitters as Sisley and his companion is traditional rather than documented; the description follows the museum's own title, so I did not mark it down.

proposals.title: Porträt des Paul Durand-Ruel
proposals.currentDescription: The art dealer Paul Durand-Ruel seated and contemplative, his dark coat set against a loosely brushed background. Durand-Ruel was the dealer who staked the Impressionists from the 1870s and a friend of Renoir for more than thirty years. Painted in 1910, oil on canvas.
proposals.imageObservation: An elderly man with a white moustache sits in a red armchair in a dark overcoat, one hand at his lapel, against a warm ochre wall scattered with small floral motifs; signed 'Renoir 1910' lower left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Sitter, date and signature all consistent. 'Loosely brushed background' understates a patterned floral wall, but nothing is asserted falsely. Durand-Ruel first backed the Impressionists in the early 1870s, so 'more than thirty years' of friendship by 1910 holds.

proposals.title: Self-portrait
proposals.currentDescription: A bust-length self-portrait with unkempt hair and beard, the painter in a striped shirt and dark tie against a loosely brushed ground. Renoir made it in 1875, oil on canvas, and showed it at the second Impressionist exhibition the following year; it is now in the Clark Art Institute, Williamstown.
proposals.imageObservation: Bust-length self-portrait of a man with tousled dark hair and a straggling beard, in a dark jacket over a striped collar with a dark tie, against a loosely brushed grey-blue ground; signed at lower right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Verified against the Clark Art Institute's own text, which describes the sitter as 'unkempt hair and beard, yet smartly dressed in a striped shirt and dark blue necktie', dates it 1875 and states it was shown at the second Impressionist exhibition in 1876. Commons files it under 'Self-portraits (c. 1875) by Pierre-Auguste Renoir in the Sterling and Francine Clark Art Institute'. Source: clarkart.edu/ArtPiece/Detail/Self-Portrait-(14).

proposals.title: Danse à la campagne
proposals.currentDescription: A couple dancing at an open-air ball, the woman in a red bonnet with a fan, a table of glasses behind them. Oil on canvas of 1883, Musée d'Orsay, Paris, paired with the contemporary Dance in the City. The models were Aline Charigot, later Renoir's wife, and his friend Paul Lhôte.
proposals.imageObservation: A tall canvas: a bearded man in a dark blue suit, seen from behind, dances with a smiling woman in a white dress printed with small red flowers and a red bonnet; her raised hand holds an open fan above his shoulder, his gloved hand is yellow-tan; behind them a table with a white cloth, glasses and a cup, and a straw hat lying on the ground at lower right. Signed and dated at lower left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Red bonnet, fan and the laid table are all visible. The 1883 date, the Musée d'Orsay, the pendant relationship with Danse à la ville and the sitters Aline Charigot and Paul Lhôte are standard and consistent with the Commons categories (Danse à la campagne, Musée d'Orsay).

proposals.title: Portrait of Jean Renoir as a hunter - Jean as a Huntsman
proposals.currentDescription: Renoir's son Jean, aged fifteen, poses full-length with a borrowed gun and the family dog Bob, dressed in a jacket his father thought suited a huntsman. Painted at Les Collettes in 1910, oil on canvas, about 173 by 89 cm. The sitter later became the filmmaker Jean Renoir; the canvas is in the Los Angeles County Museum of Art.
proposals.imageObservation: Full-length oil portrait of a boy in a blue jacket, breeches and cap with a red neck-scarf and tall tan boots, standing in a landscape with his left hand on his hip and his right resting on the muzzle of a grounded rifle; a white-and-brown dog lies at his feet on the right. Signed lower right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The anecdote checks out rather than being invented: Jean Renoir recalled that at Les Collettes, aged fifteen, he wore a jacket that made his father think of a hunter, so he posed with a gun borrowed from one of the farmers and with Bob as the hunting dog. LACMA holds the picture (gift of Jean and Dido Renoir) and gives it as oil on canvas, 1910. Only nit: LACMA's dimensions are about 174.6 x 89.2 cm against the description's 'about 173 by 89 cm' - inside the hedge, so not flagged.

proposals.title: Pierre Auguste Renoir - Paysage à La Roche-Guyon
proposals.currentDescription: A wooded landscape at La Roche-Guyon, a village on a bend of the Seine in the Val-d'Oise. Oil on canvas painted in 1887, two years after Renoir had spent a summer there working alongside Cézanne. The picture is now in the Pérez Simón collection.
proposals.imageObservation: A sunlit landscape framed by two large tree trunks: white chalk outcrops and green slopes fill the middle distance, red-roofed houses cluster below them, and a small figure in a pale hat stands in the grass at centre. Signed 'Renoir' lower right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Date 1887 and the Perez Simon collection are both confirmed by the Commons record (categories include 'The Perez Simon Collection'). La Roche-Guyon is indeed in the Val-d'Oise on a bend of the Seine, and Renoir worked there alongside Cezanne in the summer of 1885, exactly two years earlier - the arithmetic in the description is right. 'A wooded landscape' undersells the chalk cliffs that dominate the middle ground, but is not false.

proposals.title: Sailor Boy
proposals.currentDescription: Robert Nunès in a sailor suit standing before a loosely brushed beach, his father the mayor of Yport on the Normandy coast. Oil on canvas painted in 1883, when Renoir was commissioned to portray the Nunès children, now in the Barnes Foundation, Philadelphia (BF325).
proposals.imageObservation: A boy in a dark blue sailor suit with white-striped collar and a pompom cap stands full-length on a rocky, weed-strewn shore, one hand on his hip and a thin rod in the other, with sea and pale cliffs loosely brushed behind.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Verified: Robert Nunes was the son of Alfred Nunes, mayor of Yport, who commissioned Renoir in 1883 to paint his children Aline and Robert; the picture is BF325 at the Barnes Foundation (web:collection.barnesfoundation.org/objects/5064 via search). 'Beach' is a slightly soft word for the rocky foreshore shown, but not wrong.

proposals.title: Spring Bouquet
proposals.currentDescription: A generous bouquet of spring garden flowers — peonies, lilac, iris, and wild blossoms — overflows a blue-and-white porcelain vase set on a stone ledge. Painted in 1866, the canvas belongs to an early period before Renoir's palette had fully lightened, the muted grey-green ground and dense paint surface recalling his pre-Impressionist formation. The work is held at the Fogg Museum, Harvard Art Museums.
proposals.imageObservation: A tall bouquet of peonies, lilac, iris, daisies and small yellow and white wildflowers spills out of a blue-and-white porcelain jar standing on a pale stone ledge against a mottled grey-green wall; a few blooms have fallen onto the ledge at lower left. Signed 'A. Renoir 1866' at lower right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Spot-check of an earlier 'minor-fixed' verdict: it holds. Every flower named is identifiable in the image, the vase is blue-and-white porcelain on a stone ledge, the ground is grey-green, and the signature carries the date 1866. Provenance and credit confirm the Fogg Museum, Harvard Art Museums, accession 1943.277.

proposals.title: The Artist's Family
proposals.currentDescription: Renoir's wife Aline stands with their eldest son Pierre, the young Jean held by a maid, and a neighbour's daughter gathered in front of a wall. Oil on canvas of 1896, catalogued BF819 in the Barnes Foundation in Philadelphia. The painter set the figures close to the picture plane against a flatly brushed ground.
proposals.imageObservation: Five figures in a garden: a heavy-set woman in a large flowered hat stands at the centre, a boy in a sailor suit and beret at the left holds her hand, a toddler in a white dress and frilled bonnet stands in front, a young woman in white kneels at the right with her arms round the toddler, and a girl in a red dress and straw hat stands at the far right holding a striped ball, with a stone pier and greenery behind.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Figure count, ages and arrangement match; Aline, Pierre (b. 1885, here about eleven, in the sailor suit), Jean (b. 1894, the toddler) and the servant are the standard identifications, and the girl in red is conventionally called a neighbour's daughter. 1896, BF819 and the Barnes Foundation come from the file name and Commons record. 'In front of a wall' is loose - a stone pier and garden fill the background rather than a plain wall - but not worth a downgrade.

proposals.title: The Umbrellas
proposals.currentDescription: A crowd under a canopy of umbrellas, a bare-headed milliner's assistant with her hatbox at the left edge. Renoir worked the canvas in two campaigns, the feathery right-hand figures about 1881 and the firmer left-hand pair around 1885, switching from cobalt to French ultramarine between them. Oil on canvas, National Gallery, London.
proposals.imageObservation: Tall oil: a crowd under a canopy of blue-grey umbrellas; at the left a bare-headed young woman in a dark blue dress carries a large wooden band-box by its handle; centre and right a woman in blue with an umbrella, a girl in a straw hat and a small child holding a hoop.
proposals.reviewerNotes: All three unusual claims verify. The National Gallery's technical work confirms two campaigns (c.1880-81 and c.1885) and a palette change from cobalt blue to French ultramarine; the left-hand woman is conventionally identified as a milliner's assistant with a hatbox, and X-rays show her hat was painted out to leave her bare-headed. Sources: web:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Umbrellas_(Renoir), web:https://www.nationalgallery.org.uk/research/publications/technical-bulletin/renoir-s-umbrellas-unfurled-again.

proposals.title: Plate from Le Brun
proposals.currentDescription: An engraved head labelled 'L'Attention' demonstrates one of the expressions catalogued by Charles Le Brun in his influential 1668 lecture on the passions of the soul. The plate comes from Carington Bowles's English edition published in London around 1785, and the impression belongs to the Wellcome Collection.

metadataIssues.proposed: after Charles Le Brun, printed for Carington Bowles
metadataIssues.evidence: image | the imprint at the foot of the plate names Carington Bowles; the designs are Le Brun's, as the description says

proposals.imageObservation: An engraved head of a man in profile facing left, curly shoulder-length hair, brow drawn together and eye directed forward; captioned 'L'Attention' above with the plate number 2, 'ATTENTION' below, and the imprint 'London: Printed for Carington Bowles, No 69 in St Pauls Church Yard'.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The label 'L'Attention', the Bowles imprint and the London address are all legible in the plate, and the Wellcome credit is in the record. Le Brun delivered his conference on the expression of the passions to the Académie royale in 1668, so that date is right. The Commons record notes the impression is in red/brown ink, while this reproduction reads as black - worth knowing but not a claim the description makes.

proposals.title: Self-portrait
proposals.currentDescription: A bust-length self-portrait, the painter turned slightly with a heavy beard, set before a reversed landscape on the studio wall. Catalogued as FWN 434 and dated about 1875, the canvas was probably worked up in Armand Guillaumin's studio in Paris, whose own river view hangs behind the sitter.
proposals.imageObservation: A bust-length self-portrait: a balding, heavily bearded man in dark clothing turned slightly to the viewer's left, thickly painted; behind him hangs a landscape with water, a tan bank and dark trees, which appears to be oriented oddly against the wall.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Checked the load-bearing claim. The background picture is identified as Armand Guillaumin's Seine view, shown reversed, and the self-portrait is generally said to have been painted in Guillaumin's studio - the description's hedge ('probably') matches the literature's hedge. Commons dates it circa 1875 and files it under Musee d'Orsay, both consistent. FWN 434 matches the file name.

proposals.title: Portrait de madame de Verninac by David Louvre RF1942-16 n2
proposals.currentDescription: Henriette de Verninac, sister of Eugène Delacroix, is shown full-length, seated on a neoclassical chair in an Empire dress of white muslin with a gold-olive shawl, against a neutral grey ground. Jacques-Louis David painted this portrait in 1799; the Louvre acquired it in 1942 (RF 1942-16).
proposals.imageObservation: A young woman seated on a red-and-gilt neoclassical chair, turned to the viewer, in a high-waisted white muslin dress with a gold-olive shawl across her body and over the chair back; dark curls, bare arms, a plain grey wall behind and a tiled floor below. Signed at the lower left, 'David f. anno septimo'.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Spot-check of a prior 'minor-fixed'. Henriette de Verninac was indeed Eugene Delacroix's sister; the inscription visible in the picture ('anno septimo', Year VII of the Republic) is consistent with the 1799 dating, and RF 1942-16 is consistent with a 1942 acquisition. 'Empire dress' is a mild anachronism for 1799 (Directoire), but it is the ordinary term for the style and I did not treat it as a finding.

proposals.title: Portrait of a Woman
proposals.currentDescription: A bust-length likeness of a woman against a neutral ground, her face modelled with the smooth finish Boilly cultivated for small cabinet portraits. Oil on canvas, 22.2 by 17.5 cm, in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York. Boilly produced hundreds of these compact heads for a Parisian middle-class clientele.

metadataIssues.evidence: Commons date is 'between 1781 and 1845', i.e. the artist's working-life span rather than a date for this picture; the sitter's high-waisted white dress, short puffed sleeves and gold comb are Empire fashion of c.1800-1815, not 1781. The description sensibly gives no date.

proposals.imageObservation: Bust-length portrait of a dark-haired woman against a plain dark-brown ground, in a white high-waisted dress with a ruffled collar and a blue sash, a gold comb in her curled hair and pearl drop earrings.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Dimensions and collection verified: Met, oil on canvas, 8 3/4 x 6 7/8 in. (22.2 x 17.5 cm), Bequest of Harry G. Sperling, 1971 (metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/435688). 'Hundreds of these compact heads' is a fair statement of Boilly's small-portrait production. The only problem in this row is the catalogue year, not the description.

proposals.title: Портрет С. П. Кувшинниковой. 1888
proposals.currentDescription: Portrait of Sofia Petrovna Kuvshinnikova painted by Russian Realist master Isaac Levitan. Oil on canvas, executed in 1888. Kuvshinnikova was a contemporary of the artist and notable figure in Russian cultural circles.

issues.quote: Kuvshinnikova was a contemporary of the artist and notable figure in Russian cultural circles
issues.problem: Style only: the description is entirely catalogue data and vague biography, and never says what the portrait looks like. Does not change the verdict.
issues.evidence: image.

proposals.imageObservation: Full-length oil portrait: a woman with short curly hair sits on a wooden chair in a long white dress with a posy of pink flowers at the breast, tan gloves on her hands, against a pale grey wall above a red-brown floor; signed upper right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: 'Oil on canvas' is not stated on the Commons page but is safe for a Levitan portrait of this scale; 1888 and the sitter are confirmed. Nothing is contradicted, so no rewrite - but this is a prime candidate if the ledger ever does a style pass, since it describes nothing visible.

proposals.title: После неудачи
proposals.currentDescription: A painting by Russian realist artist Vasily Vereshchagin (1842–1904), known for his historical and genre scenes. The work continues Vereshchagin's tradition of narrative realism in nineteenth-century Russian art.

issues.quote: The work continues Vereshchagin's tradition of narrative realism in nineteenth-century Russian art.
issues.problem: The description is pure boilerplate biography — it never states that the picture shows a Russian soldier standing over the dead defenders below a fortress wall, which is the whole point of the canvas.
issues.evidence: image — none of the depicted content appears anywhere in the description.

proposals.imageObservation: A Russian soldier in a white uniform stands lighting a pipe, his bayoneted rifle propped against him and blood on his tunic, at the foot of a high sunlit mud fortress wall; around and behind him lie a dozen dead Central Asian fighters in red robes and white turbans, with more soldiers in the left distance and discarded sabres and a rifle in the foreground.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Every asserted fact is right (Vereshchagin's dates 1842-1904, Russian realist, historical and genre scenes), so by the rubric this is 'accurate' with a style failure, not a factual one. It is nevertheless the weakest description in the batch and a strong rewrite candidate; the Commons categories place it in the Turkestan series and in the Russian Museum, both usable grounding for a replacement. Note that record 9's fabricated description in this batch refers to this painting's pendant.

proposals.title: Проход Барскаун
proposals.currentDescription: A mountain landscape from Vasily Vereshchagin's Turkestan series, depicting the dramatic Barskaun Pass. This work exemplifies the Russian painter's fascination with Central Asian geography and his precise, detailed approach to depicting remote landscape formations.

issues.quote: A mountain landscape from Vasily Vereshchagin's Turkestan series, depicting the dramatic Barskaun Pass.
issues.problem: Nothing in the description says what the picture actually contains — the river, the pebble bed, the trees, the flanking slopes. It names the work and then generalises about the artist.
issues.evidence: image vs description

issues.quote: This work exemplifies the Russian painter's fascination with Central Asian geography
issues.problem: Catalogue boilerplate; 'dramatic' and 'exemplifies' are the house style's discouraged register.
issues.evidence: house style

proposals.imageObservation: A sunlit mountain gorge: a shallow river braids over a bank of brightly coloured pebbles in the foreground, scrubby green trees line both banks, bare stony slopes rise steeply on either side to a hazy peak between them.
proposals.reviewerNotes: No claim is false — the Turkestan-series attribution is confirmed by the Commons category, and the site is the Barskaun gorge. The text is pure boilerplate with no visual content, which is a style problem rather than an accuracy one, so I left the verdict at accurate and wrote no replacement. If the parent pass wants to improve style, this is a good candidate for a rewrite that leads with the river and pebble bed. Commons dates it 1869-1870 against the record's 1869; not worth a metadata change since 1869 is the start year.

proposals.title: Queensland Art Gallery - Joy of Museums - Figure with Snow Falling by Takahashi Hiroaki
proposals.currentDescription: A woodblock print by Japanese artist Takahashi Shōtei, held in the Queensland Art Gallery collection. The delicate composition captures a solitary figure amid falling snow, exemplifying the artist's refined treatment of winter landscapes and human presence in nature.

issues.quote: exemplifying the artist's refined treatment of winter landscapes and human presence in nature
issues.problem: Catalogue-boilerplate praise; adds no information and never names what is in the frame (the red cloak, the staff, the pagoda on the ridge).
issues.evidence: style guideline

proposals.imageObservation: A vertical woodblock print, photographed in its gallery frame: a lone figure in a red cloak and a wide pale hat, staff in hand, walks a snow-covered path below a snowy hillside; snowflakes fall across a dark grey-green sky, a snow-laden tree leans in at the left and a small red pagoda stands on the ridge at the upper right. Signature and red seal at lower left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Medium, artist and Queensland Art Gallery holding are all supported (Commons categories 'Takahashi Shotei' and 'Art of Japan in the Queensland Art Gallery'; the file is a visitor photograph taken in the gallery). No factual claim is wrong, so the verdict stays accurate despite the weak second sentence; a rewrite that names the red cloak, staff and distant pagoda would fit house style better.

proposals.title: Bindo Altoviti
proposals.currentDescription: A portrait of the young Florentine banker Bindo Altoviti, who turns over his shoulder to meet the viewer's gaze. The cool palette, soft modeling, and elegant turn of the head exemplify Raphael's late Roman portrait style.
proposals.imageObservation: A young man with long fair hair under a black cap turns his head back over his left shoulder to look out at the viewer; he wears a blue sleeved garment over black, his ringed hand raised to his chest, against a deep green ground.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Confirms the earlier 'accurate' verdict. Pose, palette and the turn of the head are exactly as described; the sitter's identity as the Florentine banker Bindo Altoviti and the c.1515 Roman dating are the standard attribution and match the record and Commons. The description makes no collection claim, so the National Gallery of Art holding in the provenance block is not at issue.

proposals.title: An Elephant
proposals.currentDescription: A chalk drawing of a tame Asian elephant, the wrinkled hide rendered with close hatching and smudged strokes, the trunk extended as the animal walks. Signed and dated 1637, the sheet is one of several studies Rembrandt made of Hansken, a celebrated travelling elephant who visited Amsterdam and other Dutch cities during the 1630s.
proposals.imageObservation: A black chalk drawing on cream paper of an elephant seen from the side, head to the right, hide worked up in dense hatching and smudged strokes, trunk hanging down with the tip curled forward; signed and dated at the lower right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The signature and date 1637 are legible in the sheet, and the medium reads as chalk. Hansken, the Asian elephant shown around the Dutch Republic from 1633, is the accepted subject of Rembrandt's elephant studies. Small nit: the trunk hangs down with a curled tip rather than being 'extended', but the animal is shown mid-stride as described.

proposals.title: Rembrandt Harmenszoon van Rijn - An Old Man in Red
proposals.currentDescription: An oil on canvas portrait painted by Rembrandt between 1652 and 1654, depicting a distinguished elderly gentleman in a deep red robe. The work, measuring 108 x 86 cm, exemplifies Rembrandt's mastery of color and chiaroscuro in portraiture and resides in the Hermitage Museum in St. Petersburg.

issues.quote: exemplifies Rembrandt's mastery of color and chiaroscuro in portraiture
issues.problem: Catalogue boilerplate; adds no information about this picture.
issues.evidence: style — house style is plain and factual

proposals.imageObservation: Half-length oil portrait of a seated old man with a full white beard, in a dark cap and a deep red robe, hands folded in his lap, lit against a near-black ground.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Every checkable claim holds: Hermitage (inv. GE-745), oil on canvas, 108 x 86 cm, between 1652 and 1654 — confirmed by hermitagemuseum.org and by the Commons date field. Verdict stays accurate; the hype clause is a style note only.

proposals.title: Large Self Portrait
proposals.currentDescription: Rembrandt presents himself at forty-six in a dark cloak and broad flat beret, gazing out with composed gravity against a neutral background. Painted in 1652 and now in the Kunsthistorisches Museum in Vienna, the large canvas belongs to the series of self-portraits that spans his entire career and marks a period of mounting financial pressure before the bankruptcy proceedings of 1656.
proposals.imageObservation: A three-quarter-length self-portrait: a middle-aged man in a broad, soft dark beret and a brown-black smock or coat over a dark doublet stands facing the viewer with both hands on his hips, against a warm dark neutral ground.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Rembrandt was born in 1606, so 'at forty-six' is right for 1652; the Kunsthistorisches Museum attribution is confirmed by the Commons categories (Google Art Project works in Kunsthistorisches Museum Vienna) and the 1656 cessio bonorum is standard. The description does not mention the hands-on-hips pose, which is the picture's most distinctive feature — a style note only. Prior ledger status 'minor-fixed' holds.

proposals.title: Rembrandt van Rijn - Zelfportret
proposals.currentDescription: An early self-portrait drawing of Rembrandt van Rijn, circa 1628–1629, in the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam. Executed in pen, ink, and wash, the small work shows the young artist's curly-haired head in three-quarter view with energetic, searching line work. The informal medium and spontaneous handling distinguish it from the more finished self-portrait etchings and paintings of the same years.
proposals.imageObservation: A small drawing on browned paper: a young man's head with a mass of tousled curls, face nearly frontal and slightly turned, drawn in pen and brown ink with broad grey-black wash over the shoulders and a hatched shadow at the right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Medium (pen, ink and wash), scale (record: 9.4 x 12.7 cm), the c.1628-29 date and the Rijksmuseum all agree with the Commons record - the file's own category names it 'Self-portrait with Tousled Hair (RP-T-1961-75)'. 'Three-quarter view' is a slight stretch (the face reads as close to frontal, the body angled), but not enough to lower the verdict.

proposals.title: A Box at the Theater
proposals.currentDescription: Two women in a theatre box, one in black lace resting her arm on the red velvet rail, the younger in white holding pink roses. Renoir reworked an earlier portrait into this image of spectators in 1880, oil on canvas, now in the Clark Art Institute, Williamstown.
proposals.imageObservation: Two figures in a box: a young woman in a black lace-trimmed dress and long white gloves, one gloved hand at her cheek and her elbow resting on a red upholstered surface, and beside her a girl in a white dress with very long dark hair and a white ribbon, leaning forward in profile. A bouquet of pink roses in white paper lies in the girl's lap. Warm red-brown background with a striped gilt panel at the upper left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The one claim worth checking — that Renoir reworked an earlier portrait into this picture — is backed by the Clark's own record, which says the painting appears to have begun as a double portrait of Edmond Turquet's daughters and was reworked into a genre subject after Turquet rejected it. Date, medium and the Clark Art Institute all match Commons. The only softness is 'the red velvet rail': the red surface she leans on could be a banquette or chair back rather than the box rail, but that is not worth a finding.

proposals.title: Portrait of Pierre-Auguste Renoir
proposals.currentDescription: A portrait of the painter Pierre-Auguste Renoir seated with his knees drawn up, in a dark jacket and blue cravat. Oil on canvas, 62 by 51 cm, painted in 1867 and held by the Musée d'Orsay, Paris. Bazille and Renoir shared a studio that year and exchanged portraits.
proposals.imageObservation: A bearded young man sits sideways in a wooden armchair with both feet up on the seat and his knees drawn to his chest, hands clasped around them; dark jacket, white collar, bright blue bow at the throat, pale grey trousers, against a loosely brushed grey-blue ground.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Pose, dress and the blue cravat all match. Date and artist match Commons; 62 x 51 cm and the Musée d'Orsay are the standard published facts for this canvas (Commons also carries the 1970 acquisition reference and '1867 oil on canvas paintings in France'). The shared studio in 1867 and the exchange of portraits — Renoir painted Bazille at his easel the same year — is well established.

proposals.title: Madame Georges Charpentier and her Children
proposals.currentDescription: Madame Georges Charpentier (Marguerite-Louise Lemonnier, 1848-1904) and her children, Georgette-Berthe (1872–1945) and Paul-Émile-Charles (1875–1895)

issues.quote: Madame Georges Charpentier (Marguerite-Louise Lemonnier, 1848-1904) and her children, Georgette-Berthe (1872–1945) and Paul-Émile-Charles (1875–1895)
issues.problem: The description is only the sitters' names and life dates lifted from the Commons title field; it is not a sentence and says nothing about the picture.
issues.evidence: commons — the objectName field carries this exact identification string in several languages.

proposals.imageObservation: Madame Charpentier in a black gown with lace trim sits on a flowered sofa in a Japanese-screened salon; her two children in matching blue dresses sit beside her — one on the sofa arm, one on a large black-and-white dog stretched across the foreground — with a table of flowers, fruit and glass at the right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The names and dates match the Commons record exactly, so nothing here is invented. Strong rewrite candidate on style grounds. If a rewrite is done, note that the younger child, dressed like his sister, is the boy Paul — a well-known feature of the picture but one I would ground on the Commons identification rather than assert from the image.

proposals.title: Reservist of the First Division
proposals.currentDescription: Cubo-Futurist fragments of a soldier's ear, moustache and cap collide with pasted printed paper, a postage stamp and a real thermometer affixed to the canvas. Malevich produced this assemblage in the autumn-winter of 1914 at 53.7 by 44.8 centimetres; it entered the Museum of Modern Art, New York, after the Berlin works left in Hugo Häring's care were acquired in 1935.

issues.quote: after the Berlin works left in Hugo Häring's care were acquired in 1935
issues.problem: A compressed provenance claim. The Häring group and the 1935 Barr acquisition are real, but MoMA's holding of this picture was only settled by a 1999 agreement with the Malevich estate, so 'acquired in 1935' states a contested history more simply than the record supports.
issues.evidence: knowledge; the Commons credit is the MoMA object page, which the description's account goes beyond

issues.quote: in the autumn-winter of 1914
issues.problem: Commons and MoMA give simply 1914; the seasonal precision has no support in the record.
issues.evidence: commons — 'date 1914'

metadataIssues.evidence: The description's own figures, which match MoMA's stated size for this work (about 53.6-53.7 x 44.8 cm). Worth confirming against the MoMA object page before backfilling.

proposals.imageObservation: A Cubo-Futurist canvas: a painted ear, a black moustache and cap-like forms among faceted planes of pink, blue, yellow and grey, with pasted printed fragments reading ОПЕРА, ЧЕТВЕРГЪ and табакерка, a 7-kopeck postage stamp, and a real wooden thermometer with a visible scale fixed to the surface; signed at the lower right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Spot-check of a prior 'accurate' verdict, and the hard-to-believe part turns out to be true: the thermometer really is a physical object attached to the canvas, and the ear, moustache, pasted printed paper and postage stamp are all visible. Only the provenance sentence and the seasonal dating overstate what the record carries; neither is contradicted, so the verdict stays accurate. If the project wants maximum safety, trimming 'autumn-winter of' and the Häring clause would cost nothing.

proposals.title: Resting Girl by François Boucher
proposals.currentDescription: A sensual Rococo oil-on-canvas depicting a reclining young woman, housed in Munich's Alte Pinakothek since 1909. Boucher dispensed with mythological pretense to present pure erotic nudity, a daring choice even during the Enlightenment. One of two known versions; the other (1751) is in the Wallraf-Richartz Museum, Cologne.

issues.quote: A sensual Rococo oil-on-canvas depicting a reclining young woman
issues.problem: The opening sentence editorialises ('sensual') instead of saying what is in the frame — a nude seen from behind, prone on a sofa, with drapery, incense burner and a fallen rose. House style wants the literal description first.
issues.evidence: image — the picture's content is far more specific than 'a reclining young woman'

proposals.imageObservation: A young nude woman lies face down across a green sofa seen from behind, a blue ribbon in her hair, pink and white drapery beneath her, an incense burner and cushion at lower left and a rose on the floor; the painting is photographed in its gilt Rococo frame.
proposals.reviewerNotes: I expected 'housed in Munich's Alte Pinakothek since 1909' to be a fabrication and it is not: the Pinakothek's own essay says the picture has hung in the Alte Pinakothek since 1909-10 (it reached Munich with the Zweibrücken collection in 1799, earlier shown at the Hofgarten and Schleissheim galleries). The two-version claim is also supported — the 1751 version is in the Wallraf-Richartz-Museum, Cologne — though the Pinakothek notes further versions probably existed and are lost, so 'two known versions' should be read as 'two surviving'. Verdict stays accurate; only the thin, editorialising first sentence is worth improving. Sources: https://www.pinakothek.de/en/francois-bouchers-resting-girl , https://www.sammlung.pinakothek.de/en/artwork/ZMLJrPbLJv

proposals.title: Window on the City No. 3
proposals.currentDescription: Faceted Parisian rooftops and the silhouette of the Eiffel Tower dissolve into a grid of prismatic colour. Painted across 1911-12 and now at the Guggenheim, Window on the City No. 3 belongs to Delaunay's Fenêtres series, the first sustained experiment in what Apollinaire would name Orphism.
proposals.imageObservation: An all-over field of small square dots laid over faceted planes of green, blue, rose, grey and white; a pale tapering vertical form runs up the centre and triangular planes fan out around it, with the canvas signed 'r. delaunay 1910-1911' at the lower right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: I pushed on the one specific visual claim, 'the silhouette of the Eiffel Tower'. There is a pale tapering central form that can be read as the tower, but at this resolution it is not unambiguous, and the Guggenheim's own text for this picture (artwork/1019) foregrounds light and the patchwork of triangles rather than naming the tower. I could not fetch guggenheim.org directly (domain blocked), so I am leaving the verdict at accurate rather than flagging a claim I cannot disprove — the tower is a standard element of the Windows-on-the-city group. Two notes for a later editor: the canvas is inscribed 1910-1911 even though the museum and Commons date it 1911-12 (I zoomed the signature to confirm), and the Guggenheim groups the work with the City series while the description assigns it to the Fenêtres.

proposals.title: L'Équipe de Cardiff
proposals.currentDescription: Cardiff rugby players leap for the ball beneath a Ferris wheel, an aeroplane, and a luminous advertising hoarding for Astra. Oil on canvas, 326 x 208 cm, the picture entered the Musée d'Art Moderne de la Ville de Paris as the largest of Delaunay's three Équipe de Cardiff variants from 1912-13.

metadataIssues.evidence: commons file title 'Robert Delaunay, 1913, L'Équipe de Cardiff, oil on canvas, 326 × 208 cm, Musée d'Art Moderne de la ville de Paris' and web:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardiff_Team. The row carries no dimensions even though the description quotes them.

proposals.imageObservation: A tall canvas in flat bright planes: rugby players in blue-and-white and orange strips reach up for a ball in a line-out at the centre; a yellow hoarding lettered ASTRA fills the left, a green hoarding lettered DELAUNAY / NEW YORK - PARIS the lower right, a red-orange big wheel with hanging cars curves across the upper right in front of the dark green Eiffel Tower, and a gold biplane hangs at the top left. Signed and dated at the lower edge.
proposals.reviewerNotes: I specifically checked the 'Ferris wheel' claim, since the red lattice could be read as the Eiffel Tower: magnified, it is unmistakably the rim of the Grande Roue with cars hanging from it, and the Eiffel Tower is the separate dark green taper behind it. The 326 x 208 cm measurement, the Musée d'Art Moderne de la Ville de Paris and the status as the largest of the versions made in 1912-13 are all supported. The Astra hoarding and the aeroplane are both present.

proposals.title: Robert Delaunay
proposals.currentDescription: Oil painting by French Neo-Impressionist Robert Delaunay created in 1906. This small-scale landscape (54 × 46 cm) demonstrates Delaunay's early exploration of light and geometric form, featuring a distinctive solar disc motif characteristic of his experimental approach during this period. Housed in the Musée national d'art moderne in Paris.

issues.quote: demonstrates Delaunay's early exploration of light and geometric form
issues.problem: Style only: never describes the picture's most distinctive feature, the mosaic of divisionist strokes ringing the disc.
issues.evidence: image.

metadataIssues.evidence: Commons categorises the file under 'Neo-Impressionist paintings' / 'Neo-impressionism'; the description likewise calls Delaunay a Neo-Impressionist. Low priority - the field may be an artist-level tag by design.

proposals.imageObservation: Oil on canvas: concentric rings of short divisionist brush-strokes in pink, mauve, green and blue radiate around a white sun disc at the top; below, a horizon and a foreground of flowering plants and dark trees built from the same mosaic of strokes.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Dimensions (54 x 46 cm), 1906 and the Musee national d'art moderne all come from the Commons file title and categories. No claim contradicted.

proposals.title: Rocks at Mouthier by Gustave Courbet
proposals.currentDescription: A close-up view of weathered limestone cliffs near the artist's native Franche-Comté, the river snaking through a narrow valley below. Courbet builds the rock face with palette-knife slabs of paint, asserting landscape as raw geological matter rather than picturesque scenery.

issues.quote: near the artist's native Franche-Comté
issues.problem: Mouthier-Haute-Pierre is in Franche-Comté, not near it; Courbet was born at Ornans in the same region. The preposition is wrong rather than the fact.
issues.evidence: knowledge — Mouthier-Haute-Pierre, Doubs, Franche-Comté.

proposals.imageObservation: A tall pinkish-grey limestone cliff with a green wooded crest fills the right and centre of the canvas above a wooded valley floor; a dark band of water lies across the foreground, and pale sky opens at the left. The rock is laid in with broad flat slabs of paint.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Limestone cliffs, the valley and water below, and the palette-knife handling are all consistent with the image, and the Franche-Comté connection is right in substance. The description does not claim a collection; Commons puts the picture in the Phillips Collection, which the row does not record.

proposals.title: St. Paul
proposals.currentDescription: Paul appears as a forceful, full-haired elder gripping the sword of his beheading and cradling a book, in keeping with Counter-Reformation Pauline iconography. The half-length panel belongs to the Apostolado painted for the Duke of Lerma's collection, circa 1611, and is now in the Museo del Prado.
proposals.imageObservation: Half-length figure of a bearded elder with abundant curling grey-brown hair, in a blue-grey mantle over a brown tunic, gripping an upright sword with a lion-head pommel in one hand and steadying a thick book under the other, against a dark ground.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Sword and book are exactly as described, and the Apostolado del duque de Lerma, the c.1611 date and the Prado (P001657) are all in the Commons record and the row's own provenance block; the row's 83 x 107.5 cm matches the Prado panel. 'In keeping with Counter-Reformation Pauline iconography' is a slight stretch - the sword and book are Paul's attributes long before the Counter-Reformation - but the picture is a Counter-Reformation apostolado, so it is not wrong.

proposals.title: Head of Medusa
proposals.currentDescription: The severed head of the Gorgon lies on a stony ledge, eyes still rolling and snakes writhing into a teeming brood of vipers, scorpions and lizards. Rubens collaborated with the animal specialist Frans Snyders on the reptilian still life, fusing Baroque horror with naturalist precision.
proposals.imageObservation: A severed female head with wide staring eyes lies on a pale stone ledge, its hair turning into a mass of writhing snakes; blood runs from the neck into more small snakes, and around them on the stone are a black-and-yellow salamander, two spiders, a scorpion, a small lizard, a coiled snake and a sprig of green leaves.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The scene matches in detail. 'Scorpions' is plural where I can make out one clearly (plus spiders and a salamander the text does not mention) - a nit, not a finding. The collaboration with Frans Snyders on the snakes and small creatures is the Kunsthistorisches Museum's own attribution and the standard account, though other names (Jan Brueghel, Paul de Vos) have been proposed in the literature; that uncertainty is worth knowing but does not make the sentence wrong.

proposals.title: Saint Christopher Facing Left
proposals.currentDescription: A small copper engraving by Albrecht Dürer showing Saint Christopher wading through the river with the Christ Child on his shoulders, bracing himself on his staff as he strides to the left. Dürer engraved two versions of the subject in 1521, distinguished by the direction the saint faces. This impression, measuring only about twelve by seven centimeters, is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York, which received it in the bequest of Julie Parsons Redmond.
proposals.imageObservation: A fine intaglio print: a bearded giant wades through shallow water carrying the Christ Child on his shoulder, gripping a long staff, with a landscape of trees, a hut and a hermit behind; Duerer's AD monogram on a tablet at lower right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Met object 391279 confirms engraving, 1521, 11.6 x 7.4 cm and credit line 'Bequest of Julie Parsons Redmond, 1960' (web:metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/391279 via search). The Met also holds the companion 'Saint Christopher Facing Right' (391282), supporting the two-versions claim. Catalogue realDimensions 7.5 x 11.9 cm match 'about twelve by seven centimeters'.

proposals.title: 冨嶽三十六景 五百らかん寺さざゐどう-Sazai Hall at the Temple of the Five Hundred Arhats
proposals.currentDescription: Woodblock print depicting the Sazaidō hall of Gohyaku Rakanji temple, part of Hokusai's celebrated series "Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji. " The composition showcases the artist's mastery of perspective and landscape design, with Mount Fuji visible in the distance. From The Metropolitan Museum of Art collection.

issues.quote: The composition showcases the artist's mastery of perspective and landscape design
issues.problem: Empty praise; it also passes over what is actually distinctive here, the row of visitors on the veranda all turned away from the viewer toward Fuji.
issues.evidence: image; corpus house style

proposals.imageObservation: Colour woodblock print: figures on the wooden veranda of a temple hall, several leaning on the railing and looking out over a plain toward a small snow-capped Mount Fuji; title cartouche and signature top left, publisher/censor seals bottom left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Subject, series, Fuji in the distance and the Met provenance are all supported by the image and the Commons metadata. Only the hype sentence is weak; verdict left at accurate per the rules.

evidence.sourceUrl: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:冨嶽三十六景_五百らかん寺さざゐどう-Sazai_Hall_at_the_Temple_of_the_Five_Hundred_Arhats_(Gohyaku_Rakanji_Sazaidō),_from_the_series_Thirty-six_Views_of_Mount_Fuji_(Fugaku_sanjūrokkei)_MET_DP141020.jpg

proposals.title: 冨嶽三十六景 隅田川関屋の里-Sekiya Village on the Sumida River
proposals.currentDescription: A woodblock print from Katsushika Hokusai's celebrated series "Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji," depicting the village of Sekiya along the Sumida River. The composition exemplifies Hokusai's mastery of perspective and color gradation, showing the influence of European compositional techniques on Japanese ukiyo-e printmaking during the Edo period.

issues.quote: depicting the village of Sekiya along the Sumida River
issues.problem: The description never mentions the print's actual subject matter - three galloping horsemen - or the red Fuji that makes it part of the series.
issues.evidence: image

issues.quote: exemplifies Hokusai's mastery of perspective and color gradation
issues.problem: Catalogue boilerplate ('mastery of', 'exemplifies') rather than description.
issues.evidence: house style

metadataIssues.evidence: Commons date field: 'circa 1830 ... -32'; the Met dates the series c.1830-32

proposals.imageObservation: Three riders gallop along a track on horses (black, chestnut, bay) with green sun-hats and bundles, past a thatched building at right; behind them a blue river winds through green fields to a small red-capped Mount Fuji under a graded blue sky. Title cartouche and signature top left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Nothing false, but the text is generic and would benefit from a rewrite naming the riders and the distant Fuji. I left the verdict at accurate because style issues are not supposed to lower it.

evidence.sourceUrl: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:冨嶽三十六景_隅田川関屋の里-Sekiya_Village_on_the_Sumida_River_(Sumidagawa_Sekiya_no_sato),_from_the_series_Thirty-six_Views_of_Mount_Fuji_(Fugaku_sanjūrokkei)_MET_DP141023.jpg

proposals.title: Self-portrait
proposals.currentDescription: Malevich confronts the viewer in a dark green coat against a swirling red-orange background of abstracted figures, rendered in bold, flat colour that prefigures his primitivist turn. The gouache, dated 1910–1911, marks a decisive shift from descriptive form toward the declarative palette of his early avant-garde work.
proposals.imageObservation: A square bust-length self-portrait: the artist faces the viewer with green-blue eyes and heavy dark brows, his face modelled in green, yellow and pink, wearing a green jacket over a white collar and dark tie; behind him a red and orange ground filled with loosely drawn nude figures; signed lower left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Medium (gouache), date (1910-1911) and the red-orange ground of abstracted nudes are all confirmed by the image and the Commons categories, which also place it in the Tretyakov Gallery. The one nit: the jacket reads as a saturated emerald-green rather than 'dark green' — too small to lower the verdict, but a rewrite could say 'green' plainly.

proposals.title: Shaw John Byam Liston Now is Pilgrim Fair Autumn-s Charge
proposals.currentDescription: "Now Is the Pilgrim Year Fair Autumn's Charge" // "The title of the work is an enigma. It appears to be a poetic quotation, but is from none of Shaw's preferred writers, including Christina and Dante Gabriel Rossetti, Tennyson, and Shakespeare. "

issues.quote: The title of the work is an enigma.
issues.problem: The entire description is a verbatim quotation of the Commons file caption, complete with quotation marks and a '//' separator; it never says what the picture shows.
issues.evidence: commons imageDescription is identical, including the double-slash

metadataIssues.evidence: Commons only records '2008 (upload date)', which is the file date, not the painting date - nothing here supports filling the year in

proposals.imageObservation: A crowded allegorical oil beside water: several women in orange, red and gold gowns on a bank, a nude winged Cupid with a quiver, a hooded black-winged figure and a grey-bearded old man, a girl in red holding a small dog, and a veiled pale figure half-immersed in the stream; autumn trees and green fields behind.
proposals.reviewerNotes: No factual claim is contradicted, because the description makes almost no claims of its own. It should be rewritten to describe the picture, keeping the sourced point about the title being untraceable in Shaw's favourite poets. I left proposedDescription null per the accurate-verdict rule; flagging it here so a later pass can pick it up.

proposals.title: Shurygin Levitan 1889
proposals.currentDescription: A bust-length portrait of the landscape painter Isaac Levitan, shown with dark curly hair and a beard, wearing a blue painter's blouse with a white ruffled collar. Painted by Alexander Shurygin in 1889, the work dates to the years when Levitan was consolidating his reputation in Moscow.
proposals.imageObservation: A bust-length portrait of a dark-haired, dark-bearded man with a thick head of curly hair, in a loose dark blue smock over a soft white collar, against a plain grey ground; a watch chain crosses the smock at the lower right. Signed and dated in Cyrillic at lower left, 1889.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Sitter, artist and date are all confirmed by Commons ('Portrait of Isaac Levitan (painting by Alexander Shurygin, 1889)') and by the signature in the canvas. The blue smock and white collar match. The closing clause about Levitan's Moscow reputation is general and unfalsifiable but not a specific unsupported assertion. Commons categories place the picture in the Israel Museum, Jerusalem — worth adding to the record's provenance if that field is being filled.

proposals.title: The Bridge at Villeneuve-la-Garenne
proposals.currentDescription: The cast-iron suspension bridge of 1844 across the Seine, looking toward Villeneuve-la-Garenne, with boats and figures along the bank. Oil on canvas, about 50 by 65 cm, painted in 1872 and acquired from the artist by Durand-Ruel that August; now in the Metropolitan Museum of Art (object 437680).
proposals.imageObservation: An oil landscape: an iron suspension bridge with a stone pier enters from the left over the Seine, boats and small figures on the bank below, white houses and a green-shuttered shopfront along the quay under a blue sky with heaped clouds; signed 'Sisley 1872' lower left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Verified: the bridge was a cast-iron and stone suspension bridge built in 1844 linking Villeneuve-la-Garenne with Saint-Denis, the canvas is 49.5 x 65.4 cm, and Durand-Ruel bought it from the artist on 24 August 1872 (web:en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bridge_at_Villeneuve-la-Garenne via search). Met object ID 437680 is confirmed by the Commons credit.

proposals.title: Snow on Ayase river
proposals.currentDescription: A Japanese woodcut print by Shōtei Takahashi depicting a snowy river landscape. The work exemplifies early 20th-century Japanese printmaking with its serene winter scene. Now held in the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam.

issues.quote: The work exemplifies early 20th-century Japanese printmaking with its serene winter scene.
issues.problem: Generic filler in place of description: the bridge, the boats, the falling snow, the walker with the yellow umbrella and the dog all go unmentioned.
issues.evidence: image

proposals.imageObservation: A wide horizontal print: a blue river curves between snow-heaped banks under falling snow, a low wooden bridge crosses it in the middle distance, small moored boats sit at the near bank, bare trees and a thatched roof stand on the far rise, a figure under a yellow umbrella walks a dog along the crest, and birds cross the grey sky. Signature and seal at right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Artist, medium (woodblock print), subject and the Rijksmuseum attribution are all confirmed by the Commons record, and the 1915 date matches. Purely a style problem.

proposals.title: Snow over Zojoji Temple
proposals.currentDescription: Kawase Hasui's woodblock print of 1953 shows the great red gate of Zojo-ji temple in the Shiba district of Tokyo under heavily falling snow, kimono-clad figures sheltering beneath umbrellas at its base against a darkened sky. The print was commissioned by the Japanese cultural authorities to document the craft of polychrome woodblock printing, subsequently designated an intangible cultural property. It was published by Watanabe Shozaburo in the large oban format, carved by Sato Jurokichi and printed by Ono Gintaro.
proposals.imageObservation: A woodblock print of the great vermilion two-storey gate of Zojo-ji seen at an angle under thick falling snow, its roofs and the ground heavily white, against a dark grey-blue sky. Three small figures with umbrellas — one in a green coat, one in a blue kimono, one in a tan coat — stand on the swept ground before the gate; a tiled wall, a noticeboard and bare trees fill the right. Title inscription at the left, signature and red seal at the lower right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Every specific in the second and third sentences is lifted directly from the Commons record and matches it: commissioned by the Japanese Ministry of Culture to celebrate woodblock engraving, then designated an intangible cultural property (Mukei Bunkazai); published by Watanabe Shozaburo; engraver Sato Jurokichi; printer Ono Gintaro; oban format; published 1953. 'Large oban' adds a word the source does not use, but the record's own realDimensions of 39 x 27 cm supports a large sheet, so I did not raise it. 'Kimono-clad' is loose — one of the three figures wears a Western-cut overcoat — but too small to act on.

proposals.title: Tab V
proposals.currentDescription: An engraving from Tabulae VII uteri mulieris gravidae (Seven Tables of the Pregnant Uterus, 1748-51), the obstetric atlas of the Leiden anatomist Bernhard Siegfried Albinus. The fifth table shows a full-term fetus curled with its limbs drawn up, the umbilical cord running to the opened placenta, whose branching vessels are spread for display; an engraved Latin key fills the lower part of the plate. This impression is in the Wellcome Collection, London.
proposals.imageObservation: An engraved plate headed 'B.S. ALBINI UTERI GRAVIDI TAB.
