V.': at left a detached placenta with its branching vascular tree spread out for display; at right a full-term fetus curled head-down with knees and arms drawn up, joined to the placenta by a thick coiled umbilical cord; two columns of Latin letter-key text fill the lower third.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Every claim checks. The plate header names Albinus and 'TAB. V' directly. Albinus's Tabulae VII uteri mulieris gravidae cum jam parturiret mortuae was published at Leiden by Verbeek in 1748, with an appendix plate in 1751 — so '1748-51' is right, as is 'Leiden anatomist'. The Wellcome attribution is in the credit field. Only thing worth knowing: the engraver was Jan Wandelaar, whom the description does not mention (not an error, just an omission).

proposals.title: Tabi miyage dai nishū
proposals.currentDescription: At dusk, a solitary figure walks along a narrow lane beside the high stone walls and overhanging rooflines of Kōshō Temple in Himi, Etchū Province, a large tree silhouetted against the pale evening sky above. The close, vertical composition directs attention down the darkening passage to the fading light beyond the compound wall. The print belongs to the Souvenirs of Travel II series, published in 1921 (Taishō 10).
proposals.imageObservation: Colour woodblock print, vertical: a narrow lane at dusk between high stone walls with temple roofs and a curved gable at left, a large tree at right, a signpost or lantern midway, a pale yellow-and-pink sky at the end of the lane, and a solitary figure in a broad hat walking away from the viewer.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Everything checks: the solitary walking figure is there (visible under magnification, wearing a broad hat), the stone walls, the overhanging temple rooflines, the tree against the evening sky, and the series and date, which match the Commons description ('from the series Souvenirs of Travel II') and the original date string 大正10年出版 (Taisho 10 = 1921).

proposals.title: Tabi miyage dai sanshū
proposals.currentDescription: A woodblock print from Hasui Kawase's Souvenirs of Travel III series (1926), depicting the torii gate of Gozanoishi Shrine standing in the waters of Lake Tazawa. The large, dark-timbered gate occupies the foreground, its reflection shimmering in the calm lake, with green hills rising beyond under a cloud-dappled summer sky. The composition exemplifies the shin-hanga movement's combination of traditional Japanese subject matter with precise, luminous colour printing.
proposals.imageObservation: Vertical colour woodblock print: a large dark-timbered torii with fence rails standing in shallow lake water, its posts and reflections rippling in the pale blue surface, grey rocks in the foreground, a green tree at the right, green hills across the lake, and a deep blue sky with white cumulus; inscription and red seal in the margins.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Every visual claim matches — torii, reflection, hills, clouds. Series title, subject and the 1926 (Taisho 15) date come straight from the Commons record and the original date string. The closing shin-hanga sentence is generic but not false.

proposals.title: 諸國名橋奇覧 摂洲天満橋-Tenman Bridge at Settsu Province
proposals.currentDescription: A Japanese woodblock print by Katsushika Hokusai from the series Shokoku Meikyo Kiran (Remarkable Views of Bridges in Various Provinces). This print depicts Tenman Bridge at Settsu Province. The work is part of the Metropolitan Museum of Art collection and is available under CC0 public domain dedication.

issues.quote: This print depicts Tenman Bridge at Settsu Province.
issues.problem: The description restates the title and the licence and never says what is actually in the print — the lantern-lit night festival, the crowd on the arch, the boats below.
issues.evidence: image

issues.quote: The work is part of the Metropolitan Museum of Art collection and is available under CC0 public domain dedication.
issues.problem: Licence boilerplate; the record already carries license and credit fields.
issues.evidence: catalogue record — license: CC0, commonsUrl points at the Met donation batch

proposals.imageObservation: A steeply arched wooden bridge crosses the print from left to right, crowded with figures and lined with tall poles carrying round red lanterns; below, pleasure boats hung with lanterns and banners are poled across blue water, with tiled town roofs along the far bank, a temple roof and pines at lower right, and a title cartouche at upper right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Nothing asserted is false: series name, subject, Met provenance and CC0 all match the Commons record. The problems are purely stylistic — no visual content at all — so I did not lower the verdict. Worth a style rewrite pass.

proposals.title: THE ABDUCTION OF THE SABINE WOMEN
proposals.currentDescription: Roman men seize struggling Sabine women in a tangle of figures, a classical history subject. Millet worked the canvas around 1844 to 1847, in the period before he settled at Barbizon and turned to peasant labour; the scene follows the Livy episode long favoured by academic painters.
proposals.imageObservation: A loosely brushed oil sketch in browns and greys: a bare-chested man at the right grasps a woman in white and blue drapery whose head falls back and whose arms are thrown up; other figures are only summarily indicated behind and at the lower left. Signed in red at the lower right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Date 'around 1844 to 1847' matches the Commons date 'Circa 1844-47' exactly; Millet settled at Barbizon in 1849, so 'the period before he settled at Barbizon' is right; the subject is Livy's account of the Sabines. One soft point I chose not to raise as a finding: 'Roman men seize struggling Sabine women' is plural on both sides while the sketch foregrounds a single pair, with the rest of the 'tangle' barely legible.

proposals.title: The Card Sharp on the Boulevard
proposals.currentDescription: A card game at a makeshift table on a sunlit Parisian boulevard, a sharper at work among a mixed crowd of players and onlookers. Oil on panel, 24 by 33 cm, in the National Gallery of Art, Washington. Boilly showed it in 1808 with a pendant of young Savoyards displaying their marmot, among his first street scenes of everyday Paris.

issues.quote: among his first street scenes of everyday Paris
issues.problem: A soft 'first' claim with no backing in the record or the sources I could reach; Boilly had already been painting Paris street subjects earlier in the 1800s.
issues.evidence: catalogue record and Commons carry nothing on this; not settled by the sources checked

proposals.imageObservation: A crowded Paris street scene in front of a tall grey building: a man in a blue jacket and cap, seen from behind, holds out cards to a young woman in green while a mixed crowd of women, children, an old man with a stick and a soldier presses round; a folding trestle table with a mug and coins stands at the right, with a small dog beside it, and a couple in white and dark blue walk past at the left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Checked the physical facts because they are exactly the kind of thing that gets invented, and they hold: NGA record and Wikipedia both give oil on panel, 24 x 33 cm, National Gallery of Art, Washington, shown at the Salon of 1808 with the pendant 'Young Savoyards Showing Their Marmot'. The 'makeshift table' is present (a folding trestle at the right with coins on it), though the cards themselves are being held out by hand rather than dealt on it. Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Card_Sharp_on_the_Boulevard

proposals.title: The Farm at Les Collettes
proposals.currentDescription: The farmhouse at Les Collettes seen through a screen of olive and orange trees, the foliage broken into flickering touches of green and rose. Renoir bought the estate at Cagnes near Nice in 1907 and moved there in 1908, painting the farm repeatedly between 1908 and 1914. Oil on canvas, in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.
proposals.imageObservation: A pale farmhouse with green shutters seen through the twisting trunks and branches of large olive trees, the whole surface broken into flecks of green, yellow, rose and lilac; a small blue-clad figure stands by the house. Signed at lower right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Confirmed against the Met record via web search: Renoir bought Les Collettes at Cagnes in 1907 and moved there in autumn 1908; the estate's groves of olive and orange trees supplied his late motifs; this is one of several views of the farm framed by olive trees painted between 1908 and 1914; oil on canvas, Metropolitan Museum of Art. The record's year 1908 is the start of the Met's 1908-14 range, which is a defensible single-year pick.

proposals.title: The Gold Scab - Eruption in Frilthy Lucre
proposals.currentDescription: Whistler's savage caricature of his former patron Frederick Leyland, painted in 1879 after the Peacock Room dispute and Whistler's bankruptcy, in which Leyland was a creditor. Leyland appears as a scaly, peacock-feathered demon seated on Whistler's White House while playing the piano — a jab at his amateur musicianship — with sacks of money at his feet. The painting is now in the de Young Museum, San Francisco.

issues.quote: with sacks of money at his feet
issues.problem: The money bags sit on and beside the piano and on the ledge at the right; the one nearest the floor is at the right of the composition rather than at the figure's feet.
issues.evidence: image — bags on the piano top and at the right; loose gold coins scattered on the ground

proposals.imageObservation: A grotesque scaly, peacock-plumed figure with a human head, clawed feet and a long feathered tail sits on a white house-shaped block playing a piano; gold-spotted money bags stand on and beside the piano and one sits at the lower right, and the propped sheet music is lettered 'The Gold Scab. Eruption in Frilthy Lucre'.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Everything substantive is right: the peacock-demon caricature of Frederick Leyland, the piano jab, the White House as a seat, the 1879 date after the Peacock Room quarrel and Whistler's bankruptcy, and the de Young Museum, which the Commons file title and categories confirm. The money-bag placement is a trivial nit and does not move the verdict.

proposals.title: The Golden Pavilion
proposals.currentDescription: Yoshida Hiroshi's colour woodblock print of Kinkaku-ji, the Golden Pavilion in Kyoto, from his 1933 Kansai District series. The gilded temple rises over its reflecting pond in the layered, atmospheric colour that defined Yoshida's shin-hanga landscapes. This impression belongs to the San Diego Museum of Art.
proposals.imageObservation: A colour woodblock print of Kinkaku-ji: the three-storey pavilion, rendered in muted rose-brown with a phoenix finial, stands among pines above a still pond that holds its full reflection; small visitors stand on the second-storey veranda. Japanese inscriptions and the seal run down the left margin, with a pencil signature and title below the image.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Subject, medium, the 1933 Kansai District series and the San Diego Museum of Art impression are all confirmed by the Commons record (Series Title: Kansai District, Creation Date: 1933, SDMA accession 1998.101). 'Gilded temple' is a standing epithet for Kinkaku-ji rather than a claim about this sheet — the print itself renders the building in muted rose-brown — so I did not treat it as a colour error. Note for whoever maintains the source data: the Commons imageDescription for this file carries San Diego's label copy for a *Hokusai* Tōkaidō print, which is a museum-side metadata error and should not be mined for description text.

proposals.title: 冨嶽三十六景 甲州犬目峠-The Inume Pass in Kai Province
proposals.currentDescription: A woodblock print from Katsushika Hokusai's celebrated series Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji (Fugaku sanjūrokkei), depicting the mountain pass in Kai Province. This iconic work exemplifies the compositional brilliance and atmospheric perspective characteristic of Hokusai's landscape prints during the Edo period's final decades.

issues.quote: This iconic work exemplifies the compositional brilliance and atmospheric perspective characteristic of Hokusai's landscape prints
issues.problem: Empty praise — 'iconic', 'compositional brilliance' — of the kind house style excludes.
issues.evidence: house style

issues.quote: depicting the mountain pass in Kai Province
issues.problem: Neither sentence says what is in the frame: no Fuji, no pack train, no hills, no travellers.
issues.evidence: image — the print's whole subject (travellers and pack horses on the pass road below Fuji) goes unmentioned

proposals.imageObservation: A horizontal woodblock print: blue Mount Fuji with a snow-flecked summit sits in the middle distance beyond rolling green hills; a train of travellers with laden pack horses moves along a road at lower left and two porters climb the hill at upper right. Title cartouche and Hokusai's signature at upper left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Nothing here is false — woodblock print, the Thirty-six Views series, the Inume Pass in Kai Province and the Edo dating are all confirmed by the Commons record. The verdict is 'accurate' per the rules, but this is a prime candidate for a style rewrite: it is pure boilerplate plus hype and never describes the picture. If someone rewrites it, the frame contains Fuji in blue beyond green hills, a pack-horse train on the road at lower left, and two figures climbing at upper right.

proposals.title: The Sorrows of Love
proposals.currentDescription: A woman supported by a companion grieves while a servant returns her portrait and an unopened letter, signalling the end of an affair. Oil on canvas, 45 by 55 cm, in the Wallace Collection, London. The picture belongs to a set of eleven works on the stages of love that Boilly painted for the Avignon collector Calvet de Lapalun.

issues.quote: an unopened letter
issues.problem: The paper in the maid's hand is folded and small, but whether it is sealed/unopened cannot be settled from the reproduction, and no source describes it that way.
issues.evidence: image — a folded white paper is visible; web:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sorrows_of_Love_(painting) mentions only the returned portrait

proposals.imageObservation: A panelled interior: a woman in a pale yellow gown swoons back into the arms of a second woman in blue-grey who kneels on a red chair; a maid in a black hood holds out a folded letter and steadies an oval framed portrait of the swooning woman against the chair; a Black servant stands in the doorway at left, and a guitar, a strongbox and a small dog occupy the left foreground, with a fire, a mantel clock and roses at right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Every substantive claim checks out. Wikipedia gives oil on canvas, 45 x 55 cm, 1790, Wallace Collection, and confirms the picture is one of eleven works on the stages of love painted for the Avignon collector Calvet de Lapalun. The 'unopened' adjective is the only thing I could not ground; it is small enough that I did not lower the verdict.

proposals.title: The Sower
proposals.currentDescription: A peasant striding across a furrowed field, his arm flung out in the act of casting seed. Pastel and Conté crayon on beige paper, about 47 by 37.5 cm, made around 1865 and held by the Clark Art Institute in Williamstown. Millet returned to the sower motif across his career in oil, pastel and print.
proposals.imageObservation: Chalk/pastel drawing on toned paper: a man in a hat strides left to right across a ploughed field, right arm flung out scattering seed, a seed bag slung at his waist; birds wheel in the sky, and a team of two horses with a ploughman crosses the ridge at upper right. Signed lower right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Medium, support, size, date and collection all check out: the Clark records The Sower, c. 1865, pastel and Conte crayon on beige wove paper, 47 x 37.5 cm (18 1/2 x 14 3/4 in.), Sterling and Francine Clark Art Institute, Williamstown - matching the record's credit line. The image is unmistakably a chalk/pastel drawing, not an oil.

proposals.title: The Tribute Money
proposals.currentDescription: John Singleton Copley's oil on canvas depicts the Gospel episode of the tribute money, in which Christ, asked whether it is lawful to pay taxes to Caesar, points heavenward as a grey-bearded questioner indicates the coin lying in his open palm. The half-length figures press close around Christ, their faces picked out against a dark ground in a deliberately old-masterly manner. Copley gave the painting to the Royal Academy of Arts in London in 1782 as his Diploma Work following his election as a Royal Academician.
proposals.imageObservation: Half-length figures crowded against a dark ground with a patch of cloudy sky at upper left: Christ at the right in a red tunic and blue mantle raises his right index finger and holds out his left palm with a coin in it, while a grey-bearded man in an olive-gold cloak points at the coin; a turbaned man, a bald old man and other heads press in behind.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Image confirms the pointing hand, the raised finger, the coin in the open palm, the half-length crowding and the dark ground. Provenance field (Royal Academy of Arts, inv. 03/994) and web sources confirm the 1782 Diploma Work given after Copley's election as RA in 1779 (he was three years late in supplying it), so 'following his election as a Royal Academician' is right. Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Tribute_Money_(Copley), https://www.royalacademy.org.uk/art-artists/work-of-art/the-tribute-money

proposals.title: The venous and arterial system of the human body. Engraving
proposals.currentDescription: The venous and arterial system of the human body. Engraving by J. Wandelaar, 1726, after a woodcut, 1543.

issues.quote: The venous and arterial system of the human body. Engraving by J. Wandelaar, 1726, after a woodcut, 1543.
issues.problem: The whole description is the Wellcome/Commons catalogue line verbatim. It never says what the plate shows, which breaks house style (first sentence should describe what is literally in the frame).
issues.evidence: commons — the imageDescription field is word-for-word identical to the description under audit.

metadataIssues.evidence: commons imageDescription: 'Engraving by J. Wandelaar, 1726, after a woodcut, 1543.' The catalogued year is the date of the source woodcut, not of this engraving. Flagging only; either reading is defensible.

proposals.imageObservation: A full-length anatomical engraving of a standing human figure stripped to the vascular tree, with the thoracic and abdominal organs shown in place; a Latin heading reads VENARUM ET ITEM ARTERIARUM OMNIUM INTEGRA DELINEATIO above two columns of italic text, and a detached detail of vessels sits at lower right. Laid paper with visible fold lines.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Every factual claim is sourced verbatim from the Commons/Wellcome record, so I cannot call it wrong. But it is a bare catalogue line with zero visual content and would benefit from a rewrite that describes the plate (standing figure, vascular tree, Latin heading, organs in situ). I did not write a replacement because the verdict is accurate and I did not want to introduce ungrounded interpretation. The Commons categories tie the plate to Albinus/Wandelaar's Tabulae and to Vesalius, consistent with the stated 'after a woodcut, 1543'.

proposals.title: The Wetterhorn
proposals.currentDescription: A woodblock print from Hiroshi Yoshida's Europe Series, depicting the Swiss mountain peak of the Wetterhorn. Created in 1925, this shin hanga work exemplifies Yoshida's distinctive blend of traditional Japanese woodblock technique with Western landscape subjects.

issues.quote: exemplifies Yoshida's distinctive blend of traditional Japanese woodblock technique with Western landscape subjects
issues.problem: Boilerplate closing clause; the description never mentions the glacier, the meadow or the flowering trees that occupy the lower half of the sheet.
issues.evidence: image + house style.

proposals.imageObservation: A woodblock print of a violet-blue snow-streaked peak above a glacier tongue, with a green meadow, flowering white trees and a small chalet in the foreground; Japanese inscriptions in the left margin (Taisho 14 / the katakana title), a red seal, and pencil signature 'Wetterhorn / Hiroshi Yoshida' below the image.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The 1925 date is corroborated inside the print itself (the marginal inscription reads Taisho 14, i.e. 1925), matching the Commons date and the catalogue year. The Europe Series attribution comes from the Commons file title; the Wetterhorn is in the Bernese Alps, so 'Swiss mountain peak' is right.

proposals.title: The Wounded Heron
proposals.currentDescription: A heron struck down in a hawking scene sprawls in the foreground, its wing spread on the ground. Watts, then about twenty, bought a dead heron from a poulterer to study the bird; the oil on canvas, 91.4 by 71.1 cm, was his Royal Academy debut in 1837 and now belongs to the Watts Gallery, Surrey.
proposals.imageObservation: A grey heron sprawls dying in the foreground, one wing thrown up high and the other spread flat on the ground, its neck and yellow bill lying on brown earth; in the middle distance a small mounted falconer with a white horse stands against a low landscape and cloudy sky. Signed lower right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: I verified every specific: 91.4 x 71.1 cm oil on canvas, 1837, Watts Gallery in Surrey, Watts aged about twenty, the Royal Academy debut of 1837, and the poulterer anecdote (Watts bought a dead heron from a poulterer's shop). All confirmed by the Watts Gallery / Wikipedia entries for the picture.

proposals.title: A View of the Two Lakes and Mountain House
proposals.currentDescription: Morning mist lifts off the twin Catskill lakes as the white-pillared Catskill Mountain House perches on a cliff above. Cole lived in the village of Catskill from 1836 and painted this 1844 view of the famous hotel that had drawn tourists to the Hudson Valley since 1824.
proposals.imageObservation: A wide morning landscape: two linked lakes lie in a wooded basin with a long ridge behind, a white colonnaded hotel sits on a shelf of cliff at the left, mist hangs in the valley at the right, and a small figure with a staff stands on a rock outcrop in the foreground among blasted trees and boulders.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The lakes, the mist and the white-pillared Catskill Mountain House on its cliff are all in the frame. Cole settling in the village of Catskill in 1836 and the Mountain House opening to tourists in 1824 are both standard and uncontroversial; the 1844 date matches Commons and the record.

proposals.title: 'Three Sisters' by Yamakawa Shūhō
proposals.currentDescription: A four-fold screen painted in ink and color on silk by the nihonga artist Yamakawa Shuho in 1936. Three young women in kimono are grouped around a white motor car: one leans against the front fender holding a handbag, another sits inside the open rear door, and the third looks out through the back window, a quietly modern image of well-to-do life in 1930s Japan rendered in the flat, elegant manner of traditional figure painting. The screen is in the Honolulu Museum of Art.
proposals.imageObservation: Four-panel painted screen in pale, near-monochrome colour: three young women in kimono around a cream-white sedan car - one standing at the left beside the front wing with a small dark handbag, one seated in the open rear doorway, one seen through the rear side window; a vase of flowers inside the car.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Confirmed against the Honolulu Museum record (object 11822.1): ink and colour on silk, four-panel screen, 1936, 168 x 338.2 cm. The museum identifies the sitters as the daughters of the industrialist Kuhara Fusanosuke, which the description does not claim - 'well-to-do life' is a fair paraphrase. Record's realDimensions (335.3 x 167.6) differ trivially from the museum's; not worth a change.

proposals.title: Toshogu Shrine
proposals.currentDescription: A colour woodblock print of the Tōshō-gū shrine at Nikkō, designed by Yoshida Hiroshi in 1937. Towering cryptomeria trunks frame the lantern-lined approach to the shrine, rendered with the soft gradations Yoshida carried from his watercolour training into woodblock. This impression belongs to the San Diego Museum of Art.
proposals.imageObservation: A vertical woodblock print: two enormous cryptomeria trunks flank a view up a stone stair to a red-and-gold shrine gate with a grey tiled roof; stone lanterns stand at both sides of the paved forecourt, small figures in kimono gather at the foot of the steps, and the sky is a pale gradated pink. Pencil-signed 'Hiroshi Yoshida' with the title at the lower margin.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The 1937 date, the San Diego Museum of Art ownership and the Nikkō Tōshō-gū subject are all in the Commons record, and the cryptomeria, the gate and the stone lanterns are all in the frame. 'Lantern-lined approach' is a slight stretch — I can see two flanking stone lanterns rather than a row — but it is defensible and I did not treat it as a finding. Note that the Commons imageDescription carries an unrelated SDMA label ('Ejiri Station No. 19, 53 Stations on Tokaido Road'), which is a museum data error, not something this description repeats.

proposals.title: Line Fishing
proposals.currentDescription: Fishing boats work the swell off Hastings under a turbulent sky, the figures and rigging set against pale sea-light. Turner treats the everyday coastal labor with the atmospheric breadth of his mature marine paintings.

issues.quote: under a turbulent sky
issues.problem: The sky is bright and hazy — sunlight breaking through high cloud — rather than turbulent or stormy; the sea is choppy but the weather reads as fair.
issues.evidence: image

proposals.imageObservation: A bright hazy marine: three or four open boats crowded with figures ride a green-grey swell in the foreground, a two-masted sailing vessel behind them at the left, and the Hastings cliffs and town dissolve into pale sunlight and cloud across the middle distance.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Spot-check of a prior 'accurate' verdict. Subject (boats and figures off Hastings), handling and the mature-marine framing are right, and the Commons categories place the picture in the Victoria and Albert Museum, which the description does not claim. 'Turbulent' is an atmosphere nit, not enough on its own to drop the verdict; the record's 1835 matches Commons ('ca. 1835 (painted) - 1839').

proposals.title: Un Bar aux Folies-Bergère by Édouard Manet
proposals.currentDescription: Manet's final major work, painted in 1881–1882, depicts a barmaid at the famous Folies-Bergère cabaret in Paris. The composition masterfully captures the ambiguity of modern urban life through the barmaid's reflected image and the bustling entertainment venue behind her. This oil painting is housed in the Courtauld Gallery in London and remains a pivotal work of Impressionism.

issues.quote: The composition masterfully captures the ambiguity of modern urban life
issues.problem: Praise substituting for description; the bottles, oranges, roses and the trapeze legs at upper left — the details that make the picture legible — go unmentioned.
issues.evidence: image

proposals.imageObservation: A barmaid in a dark bodice with lace trim and a black choker stands behind a marble counter set with bottles, a bowl of oranges and roses in a glass; behind her a large mirror reflects her back, a top-hatted man she faces, and the crowded, gaslit balconies of the hall, with a trapeze artist's legs at the upper left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: No factual finding. Last major work, 1881-82, Courtauld Gallery, the reflected barmaid and the hall behind — all correct and matching the Commons record (date '1881-1882', categories 'Featured pictures of paintings in London'). The catalogue year 1881 is the early bound of a two-year execution, which seems reasonable to leave as is.

proposals.title: 冨嶽三十六景 常州牛掘-Ushibori in Hitachi Province
proposals.currentDescription: A woodblock print from Katsushika Hokusai's iconic "Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji" series, depicting the landscape of Ushibori in Hitachi Province (in present-day Ibaraki, Japan). Created circa 1830-32, this work exemplifies the ukiyo-e tradition with its characteristic use of Prussian blue and compositional depth. The print is part of the Metropolitan Museum of Art's collection and is in the public domain.

issues.quote: iconic
issues.problem: Empty intensifier; house style avoids it.
issues.evidence: style

issues.quote: depicting the landscape of Ushibori in Hitachi Province (in present-day Ibaraki, Japan)
issues.problem: The print's actual subject - the moored thatched boat and its occupants, the reeds, the herons, Fuji small at the right - is never described. 'The landscape of Ushibori' is as far as it goes.
issues.evidence: image

issues.quote: is in the public domain
issues.problem: Licence boilerplate in a description; the licence field already carries it.
issues.evidence: catalogue record - license field says CC0

proposals.imageObservation: A colour woodblock print dominated by blues: a long thatched cargo boat lies diagonally across the foreground with figures inside, one rinsing something over the side; reeds fill the banks, two herons fly at the left, and a snow-capped Mount Fuji sits low on the right horizon. Title cartouche and signature top left, publisher and censor seals bottom right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: No factual error: circa 1830-32 matches the Commons date exactly, the Met attribution is right, Ushibori is in present-day Ibaraki, and the print is heavy with Prussian blue. Only style problems, which per the brief do not move the verdict - but this is a candidate for a rewrite that actually describes the boat.

proposals.title: Van Gogh -Die Brücke von Langlois in Arles mit Wäscherinnen
proposals.currentDescription: Washerwomen kneel along the canal bank as a horse-cart crosses the wooden drawbridge at Arles. Van Gogh returned to the Pont de Langlois several times in 1888, drawn to its clean geometry and Provençal light reminiscent of Japanese prints.
proposals.imageObservation: A yellow wooden lift-bridge on stone abutments crosses a blue canal; a horse and covered cart are on the deck, and a group of washerwomen in coloured dress crouch at the near bank with a boat drawn up beside them, among yellow-green grasses. Signed 'Vincent' lower left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Everything in the description is in the picture (washerwomen at the bank, horse-cart on the drawbridge) and the March 1888 Arles date and Kroller-Muller ownership match the record. The Japanese-print comparison is standard Van Gogh scholarship and is phrased as an influence rather than a documented statement.

proposals.title: Van Gogh
proposals.currentDescription: Vincent van Gogh's oil painting depicting an olive grove in Saint-Rémy-de-Provence, created during his stay at the Saint-Paul-de-Mausole asylum. The work exemplifies his distinctive post-impressionist style with bold brushstrokes and vibrant color treatment of the Provençal landscape.

issues.quote: exemplifies his distinctive post-impressionist style with bold brushstrokes and vibrant color treatment
issues.problem: Generic art-appreciation filler; says nothing a reader could not guess from the artist's name.
issues.evidence: house style

issues.quote: depicting an olive grove in Saint-Rémy-de-Provence
issues.problem: The description never mentions the picture's most striking feature — the orange-red earth and the banded yellow-green sky.
issues.evidence: image

proposals.imageObservation: A grove of gnarled olive trees with silver-green foliage over ground worked in orange-red and blue strokes, under a sky striped yellow, green and red. No figures.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Nothing false: the 1889 Saint-Rémy olive groves were painted during the Saint-Paul-de-Mausole stay, and the Commons record confirms the date and the Faille number (F586). Verdict stays accurate, but this is another boilerplate-plus-hype entry worth a style rewrite; it also omits the Gothenburg Museum of Art, which the record does carry.

proposals.title: The Road of the War Prisoners
proposals.currentDescription: Vasily Vereshchagin (Russian, 1842-1904). The Road of the War Prisoners, 1878-1879. Oil on canvas, 71 1/4 x 117 11/16 x 2 1/4 in.

issues.quote: Vasily Vereshchagin (Russian, 1842-1904). The Road of the War Prisoners, 1878-1879. Oil on canvas, 71 1/4 x 117 11/16 x 2 1/4 in.
issues.problem: The whole description is a museum tombstone copied from the Commons imageDescription, truncated mid-line. It never says the picture shows a snowbound road strewn with the frozen dead and circling crows — which is the entire subject.
issues.evidence: commons — imageDescription reads 'Vasily Vereshchagin (Russian, 1842-1904). The Road of the War Prisoners, 1878-1879. Oil on canvas, 71 1/4 x 117 11/16 x 2 1/4 in. (181 x 298.9 x 5.7 cm). Brooklyn Museum, Gift of Lilla Brown in memory of her husband John W. Brown, 06.46'

metadataIssues.proposed: widthCm 298.9, heightCm 181 (the Brooklyn Museum's own figures; 320.5 x 202.6 looks like a framed measurement)
metadataIssues.evidence: commons imageDescription — '71 1/4 x 117 11/16 x 2 1/4 in. (181 x 298.9 x 5.7 cm)', which is also what the description text in the record itself states in inches

proposals.imageObservation: A wide snow-covered plain under a pale blue sky, a rutted road running back to the horizon beside a receding line of telegraph poles; crows wheel overhead and hop on the snow, and the bodies of dead prisoners in ragged clothing lie scattered along both verges of the road in the foreground.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Nothing in the text is false — it is the Brooklyn Museum's own credit line — so I did not lower the verdict, but this is the weakest description in the batch on house-style grounds and should be rewritten to describe the picture. Note also the dimension conflict: the description's inches convert to 181 x 298.9 cm while the record's realDimensions say 202.6 x 320.5 cm. I would trust the museum figures and treat the wikidata pair as framed dimensions.

proposals.title: Self portrait of Louis-Leopold Boilly
proposals.currentDescription: A self-portrait of Boilly in middle age, bust-length and turned slightly toward the viewer. Oil on canvas, about 1805, in the collection of the Château de Versailles. The painter renders his own features with the close finish he applied to his commissioned heads.
proposals.imageObservation: Bust-length oil portrait of a man in his forties with dark curly hair, round wire-rimmed spectacles, white cravat and a brown coat with a raised collar, set against a plain dark ground, facing the viewer.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Commons confirms circa 1805, oil on canvas, bust length, Musee national du Chateau de Versailles. Nothing contradicted. Optional improvement only: the spectacles are the most conspicuous feature of the picture and go unmentioned.

proposals.title: Along the Seine
proposals.currentDescription: A riverside scene along the Seine on the outskirts of Paris, painted during the artist's Asnières period with Bernard and Signac. The handling shows the impact of Neo-Impressionist contact, with broken touches of pure colour modeling the embankment, water, and screen of trees.
proposals.imageObservation: A pale sandy path along a river bank with a row of slim trees casting shadows across it, a single small figure in blue with a yellow hat walking away, blue water at right and a low far bank; short directional strokes throughout, the sky streaked in blue and white.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Matches: Asnieres-period riverside, Van Gogh Museum, 1887 (record and Commons agree); the divisionist-influenced broken touch is plainly visible. The lone walking figure is the only notable thing left unmentioned. Van Gogh's summer 1887 work at Asnieres alongside Bernard and Signac is well documented.

proposals.title: Arrangement in Gray: Portrait of the Painter
proposals.currentDescription: Whistler portrays himself in a broad black hat and light grey coat, holding paintbrushes against a near-uniform grey ground. The carefully tuned tonal intervals, with face and hat providing the principal points of contrast, exemplify the musical analogies for picture-making that underlie his Arrangement titles. Painted around 1872, the work is known as Arrangement in Gray: Portrait of the Painter.
proposals.imageObservation: Half-length self-portrait against a plain warm-grey ground: the painter in a wide-brimmed black hat and a pale grey coat over a white shirt and black tie turns toward the viewer, holding a bundle of brushes in his left hand; the butterfly monogram appears in a faint dark roundel at the left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Spot-check of the earlier 'minor-fixed' pass holds up: hat, grey coat, brushes, near-uniform grey ground and the tonal reading are all confirmed by the image, the circa-1872 date matches Commons, and the title matches the Commons objectName. The butterfly monogram is visible and could be added, but its absence is not an error. Commons credit 'DIA' points to the Detroit Institute of Arts; the description makes no collection claim, so nothing to check there.

proposals.title: The Song
proposals.currentDescription: A woman in a white dress sits absorbed in thought on a red upholstered chair in a grand interior, leaning her head on her hand as another figure plays piano in the background. Arched ceilings, a heavy table bearing books and flower arrangements, and a distant gilded figure set an atmosphere of cultivated leisure. Chase painted the work in 1907, using his characteristic fluid handling to animate the richly appointed space.
proposals.imageObservation: A vaulted grey-gold interior with a stone column: a woman in a white dress sits on a red upholstered chair at the right, head propped on her hand; behind her a second figure sits at a black grand piano, and at the left a long dark table holds papers, a red book and a potted plant beside a tall arrangement of white and pink flowers. A small gilded figure stands near the column; a red patterned rug covers the floor. Signed at lower left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The earlier 'fabricated-fixed' rewrite holds up: every element it names — white dress, red chair, hand to head, pianist behind, vaults, laden table, gilded figure — is in the picture, and the 1907 date matches the Commons record. It does not claim a collection, which is the right call; Commons puts it in the Crystal Bridges Museum of American Art but the catalogue row has no provenance.

proposals.title: 諸國瀧廻リ 美濃ノ国養老の滝-Yōrō Waterfall in Mino Province
proposals.currentDescription: A woodblock print by Hokusai from his series "A Tour of Waterfalls in Various Provinces" (Shokoku taki meguri), depicting the famous Yōrō Waterfall in Mino Province, Japan. Created circa 1832, this print exemplifies Hokusai's mastery of landscape composition and his fascination with natural waterfalls as subjects.

issues.quote: exemplifies Hokusai's mastery of landscape composition and his fascination with natural waterfalls as subjects
issues.problem: Empty appreciation rather than information; 'mastery' and 'fascination' assert nothing checkable.
issues.evidence: house style - later sentences should add grounded context (technique, collection, date), not praise

issues.quote: depicting the famous Yōrō Waterfall in Mino Province, Japan
issues.problem: The description never says what is in the frame - the fall of water, the travellers, the shelter - only which subject it names.
issues.evidence: image; house style asks the first sentence to describe the frame

proposals.imageObservation: A colour woodblock print in blues and greens: a tall waterfall drops in fine parallel white-blue threads from a wooded cliff into a dark pool, with two travellers and a thatched shelter on the rocks below; title cartouche upper left, artist signature and seals upper right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Every factual claim checks out against Commons (series, subject, circa 1832, woodblock print). Verdict left at accurate because the only problems are stylistic, but this is a good candidate for a rewrite that actually describes the print, and the Met provenance/collection could be named.

evidence.objectKey: collection-of-beauty/諸國瀧廻リ_美濃ノ国養老の滝-Yōrō_Waterfall_in_Mino_Province_(Mino_no_Yōrō_no_taki),_from_the_series_A_Tour_of_Waterfalls_in_Various_Provinces_(Shokoku_taki_meguri)_MET_DP141263.jpg

proposals.title: Suzukawa River
proposals.currentDescription: A color woodblock print by Hiroshi Yoshida, dated 1935 in the margin, showing snow-capped Mount Fuji rising beyond a stand of pines and farm buildings along the Suzukawa river, the mountain and trees doubled in the still water of the foreground. Yoshida trained as a Western-style painter, and his prints join Japanese woodblock technique to a naturalist's handling of light and atmosphere, produced under his close supervision in his own studio.
proposals.imageObservation: Colour woodblock print with wide paper margins: snow-capped Mount Fuji beyond a low shore, a stand of dark pines and a thatched farm building at the middle distance, small boats at the water's edge, and the mountain and trees reflected in the still foreground water; Japanese inscription in the left margin, pencil title 'Suzukawa' and signature in the lower margin.
proposals.reviewerNotes: I magnified the left margin: it carries the jizuri (self-printed) seal characters and 昭和拾年作 — 'made in Showa 10', i.e. 1935 — so 'dated 1935 in the margin' and the claim about printing under Yoshida's own supervision are both grounded in the sheet itself. Fuji, pines, farm building and the reflection all match.

proposals.title: Zentralbibliothek Zürich - Portät von Anna Magdalena Schweizer geb Hess im Alter von 27 Jahren - 000003019
proposals.currentDescription: Anna Magdalena Schweizer, née Hess (1751–1814), is shown in a precise profile view, her hair swept up and secured with a ribbon bow. Henry Fuseli executed this pencil portrait drawing on 15 March 1779, when the sitter was 27 years old; it is preserved in the Zentralbibliothek Zürich.
proposals.imageObservation: A graphite drawing on aged paper of a woman in strict right-facing profile, her hair piled high and bound with a broad pleated ribbon tied in a bow, long ringlets falling behind; a faint pencil inscription runs along the lower edge.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Commons supports every specific: 'Portrait of Anna Magdalene Schweizer, nee Hess, 1751-1814, at the age of 27', date '15 March 1779', credit Zentralbibliothek Zurich, and categories '1779 portrait drawings of women' and 'Drawings by Johann Heinrich Fussli in the Zentralbibliothek Zurich'. The only thing I cannot settle from a reproduction is pencil versus another dry medium; graphite is what it looks like and what the categories imply.

proposals.title: Haeckel Gorgonida
proposals.currentDescription: Gorgonian octocorals with skeletal spicules detailed beside whole polyps and branch fragments. Eunicella and Primnoella illustrate the eight-tentacled polyps and calcareous sclerites that stiffen the proteinaceous gorgonin axis of the colony.
proposals.imageObservation: A monochrome lithographic plate on a black ground, arranged as a grid of pale specimens: expanded eight-tentacled polyps, whorled branch segments, forked and spiny skeletal spicules, and a large diagonal branch at the centre with polyps emerging along it.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Confirms the earlier 'accurate' verdict. The Commons imageDescription lists the numbered figures and includes both Eunicella verrucosa (polyps and a branch with polyps) and two Primnoella species (whorls of polyps along a branch), plus several isolated skeleton spicules — exactly the mix the description reports. The octocoral anatomy (eight tentacles, calcareous sclerites, proteinaceous gorgonin axis) is correct.

proposals.title: Haeckel Lacertilia
proposals.currentDescription: A gathering of lizards including the flying dragon Draco volans, the Texas horned lizard Phrynosoma cornutum and a Trioceros chameleon. The plate compares cranial casques, dermal spines and gliding membranes as variations on a single squamate body plan.
proposals.imageObservation: Eight lizards arranged over a rocky ground: a horned chameleon on a branch at the top left, a spiny agamid at the top right, a flying dragon with its orange striped patagium spread at the left, a horned lizard, a crested basilisk running across the centre, a flat-bodied gecko, a frilled lizard with its ruff open at the lower left, and a thorny devil at the lower right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: All three species named in the description are on the plate and in the Commons species list for it (Draco volans, Phrynosoma cornutum, Chamaeleon montium = Trioceros montium). Casques, spines and gliding membranes are all visibly present, so the second sentence is a fair account of what the plate sets side by side. Plate 79 of Kunstformen der Natur, as the record's credit says.

proposals.title: Haeckel Peridinea
proposals.currentDescription: Marine dinoflagellates magnified to reveal their armored cellulose plates, flagellar grooves, and projecting horns. Species like Ceratium tripos and Ornithocercus magnificus dominate the composition, their delicate sail-like extensions translated into precise lithographic line.
proposals.imageObservation: A monochrome grey lithographic plate of eleven numbered dinoflagellates, drawn large: plated, pitted and reticulate cell walls, long trailing flagella, girdle grooves, projecting horns and spines, and broad sail-like membranous extensions; no colour anywhere on the sheet.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Both named species are in the Commons key (Ceratium tripos as figure 1, Ornithocercus magnificus as figure 2) and both are large and central in the composition. Armoured plates, flagellar grooves and horns are all visible. Importantly the description does not claim colour, which would have been wrong — this plate is monochrome — and 'precise lithographic line' is exactly right for it.

proposals.title: Haeckel Platodes
proposals.currentDescription: Plate 75 of Kunstformen der Natur (1904) surveys the diversity of parasitic flatworms, ranging from cercariae larvae with forked tails — including Cercaria dichotoma as studied by Johannes Müller — to adult monogeneans such as Diplozoon paradoxum (shown as a mated pair) and the mature proglottids and scolex of Taenia solium. Disc-shaped and elongated adult forms dominate the composition alongside the smaller larval stages, together illustrating the full span of platyhelminth body plans.

issues.quote: together illustrating the full span of platyhelminth body plans
issues.problem: Slight overreach and in tension with the description's own opening: every figure on the plate is a parasitic form (trematodes, monogeneans, cestodes); free-living turbellarians, a large part of the phylum, are not represented.
issues.evidence: commons - the full figure list contains only parasitic taxa

proposals.imageObservation: Lithographic plate on a dark green ground: about sixteen flatworm figures - forked-tailed cercaria larvae at the upper left, a large yellow-and-white elongated form at the centre with four suckers below, disc- and heart-shaped adults at the bottom corners, a crossed pair of worms at bottom centre, and a spiny head structure at the middle right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Spot-check of a prior 'minor-fixed'. Every named organism in the description appears in the Commons figure index for plate 75: Cercaria dichotoma (Johannes Muller), Diplozoon paradoxum 'mated pair from below', and Taenia solium mature proglottid and head. Nothing is fabricated; only the closing generalisation overreaches.

proposals.title: Haeckel Polycyttaria
proposals.currentDescription: Colonial radiolarians shown as gelatinous spheres studded with individual cells and symbiotic zooxanthellae. The plate documents social plankton, where dozens of single-celled organisms cohabit in a shared transparent matrix.
proposals.imageObservation: A natural-history plate of twelve numbered figures of colonial radiolarians: mostly spherical gelatinous colonies studded with blue central capsules and yellow granules, plus several spiny and branching skeletal forms drawn in grey, on a cream ground.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Matches plate 51 (Polycyttaria) of Kunstformen der Natur; the Commons imageDescription itself mentions 'colony with symbiotic zooxanthellae', which is what the yellow bodies are. The only softness is 'shown as gelatinous spheres' - four of the twelve figures are spiny or branching skeletal forms rather than spheres - but the generalisation holds for the plate as a whole.

proposals.title: Albuca Cornuta
proposals.currentDescription: Albuca cornuta, its bulb sending up broad glaucous leaves and a bare stalk carrying a raceme of green-and-white flowers. The style here ends in three projecting horns, the feature that names the species. Drawn for the second volume of Les Liliacees (1804).
proposals.imageObservation: A bulbous plant with long strap-shaped grey-green leaves arching from the base and a tall bare stalk bearing a raceme of nodding green-and-white flowers; small numbered dissection studies of the floral parts run along the bottom edge.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Leaves, bare scape and green-and-white raceme all match. The 'style ending in three projecting horns' is presumably taken from the plate's dissection figures, which are too small to read in this reproduction - I could not confirm or refute it and did not treat it as an error. Les Liliacees vol. 2 is consistent with the record's 1804.

proposals.title: Commelina Communis
proposals.currentDescription: Commelina communis, the Asiatic dayflower, its lance-shaped leaves on a hollow ascending stem and its flowers enclosed in a heart-shaped spathe, the two upper inner segments a clear blue. The text describes six unequal stamens, three of them bearing fertile anthers, shown enlarged at the foot of the sheet.
proposals.imageObservation: A dayflower: sprawling stems with lance-shaped, parallel-veined leaves and small three-petalled flowers, the two upper petals clear blue with yellow anthers at the centre, each emerging from a folded heart-shaped bract; four numbered grey dissection figures along the foot of the sheet — a flower with spread stamens, a capsule, an opened capsule and seeds.
proposals.reviewerNotes: I magnified the foot of the sheet: figure 1 is indeed a flower with its stamens spread, so 'shown enlarged at the foot of the sheet' is supported. Commelina communis does carry six stamens of which three are fertile, and the blue upper petals and heart-shaped spathe are visible. The 'hollow ascending stem' and the exact wording of Thory's text could not be checked with c82.net blocked.

proposals.title: Gladiolus Lineatus
proposals.currentDescription: A flowering stalk of Gladiolus lineatus from the Iridaceae, its veined funnel-shaped blooms set in a spike above sword-shaped leaves. The plate appears in the seventh volume of Les Liliacees (1812), stipple-engraved in colour and finished by hand in watercolour.
proposals.imageObservation: A single flowering stem carrying a spike of about four open creamy-white star-shaped flowers with fine dark veins on each tepal and small yellow throats, with further buds above, rising among long sword-shaped green leaves; three small separately drawn dissection details (anther, stigma) sit at the lower left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Veined flowers in a spike above sword-shaped leaves is exactly what the plate shows. Les Liliacees ran to eight volumes of roughly sixty plates each, so plate 400 falls in volume seven, whose parts appeared 1811-12 — consistent with the record's year of 1812. The stipple-engraved-and-hand-finished statement is correct for the series. Two small softnesses I did not act on: 'funnel-shaped' is a stretch for blooms that open flat from a slender tube, and the description omits the dissection studies at the lower left.

proposals.title: Hyacinthus Romanus
proposals.currentDescription: Hyacinthus romanus, slender scapes rising above keeled linear leaves to a loose cylindrical raceme of about twenty small flowers that pass from greenish to white. Redoute was flower painter to Empress Josephine; this plate ran in the sixth volume of Les Liliacees (1811).
proposals.imageObservation: Two slender scapes carrying loose cylindrical racemes of many small white flowers, greenish in bud, rising above long arching strap-like leaves; at the lower right a monochrome study of the bulb with its roots, and along the bottom left a row of small dissected floral parts.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Scapes, keeled linear leaves and the greenish-to-white raceme all match; 'about twenty' flowers is a fair reading of the larger raceme. Redouté as flower painter to Empress Josephine is uncontested, and volume 6 of Les Liliacées (1811) is consistent both with the record's year and with this plate's sequence number in the set. The description omits the bulb study and the dissections, which is an omission rather than an error.

proposals.title: Ixia Fusco-Citrina
proposals.currentDescription: Ixia fusco-citrina carries a short head of jonquil-yellow flowers, each division stained with a brown lustrous blotch at its inner base. The plate belongs to the iris family in the Linnaean class Triandria monogynia. Below, the dissection figures enlarge the flower's stamens in the period's botanical convention.
proposals.imageObservation: A stipple-engraved plate of a corm plant: a short head of six-tepalled lemon-yellow flowers, each with a dark brown blotch at the base of the segments, above long narrow ribbed leaves rising from a corm with pale stolons and bulbils; two uncoloured outline dissection figures sit at the lower left, one a flattened flower with its stamens, one a single stamen and style.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Confirms the earlier 'accurate' verdict. Flower colour, the brown basal blotch, the short head and the two dissection figures are all visible; Ixia is Iridaceae and falls in the Linnaean class Triandria Monogynia, so both taxonomic statements hold.

proposals.title: Ixia Longiflora
proposals.currentDescription: Ixia longiflora bears oblong segments spread above a slender cylindrical tube the length of a finger, set in a loose spike along the stem. The French text notes several varieties, one white flushed with rose and banded yellow on the lower divisions. The work belongs to the iris family in Triandria monogynia.
proposals.imageObservation: Pale yellow six-pointed star-shaped flowers on long slender tubes, loosely spaced along a slim stem, with narrow grass-like leaves and a small brown corm at the base; grey dissection figures at the lower left and right, including an enlarged flower and a stamen/style detail.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The long tube, spreading oblong segments and loose spike all match the plate. Ixia is Iridaceae and sits in Linnaeus's Triandria Monogynia, so that sentence is right. The claim about the French text listing a white variety flushed with rose could not be checked (c82.net blocked) and is not contradicted by anything here.

proposals.title: Leucoium Autumnale
proposals.currentDescription: Leucoium autumnale, the autumn snowflake, its slender threadlike leaves and one or two small white nodding bells on a fine stalk. The plate belongs to the Narcissus family in the Jussieu classification line and was drawn for the third volume of Les Liliacees (1805), printed in colour and finished by hand.
proposals.imageObservation: Two small bulbs with long pale roots, each sending up a very fine stalk carrying one or two small white nodding bell-shaped flowers; the leaves are barely developed, mostly sheathing the bulb necks. Sparse, delicate colouring on a white ground.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The one-or-two nodding white bells on a fine stalk match the plate exactly, as do the bulbs. The threadlike leaves the description mentions are only faintly indicated in this reproduction — a small looseness, not an error. Volume 3 (1805) matches the record's year and the plate's sequence number; the Jussieu/Narcissus placement is consistent with how Les Liliacées was organised, though I could not verify the plate's exact family heading.

proposals.title: Mayanthemum Canadense
proposals.currentDescription: Maianthemum canadense, the Canada May lily, distinguished from its European cousin by near-sessile, more oblong leaves, glabrous on both faces, with sharper reticulated veining. The plate was printed in colour from a single stipple-engraved plate and finished by hand.
proposals.imageObservation: A botanical plate on white ground: a slender stem carrying two broad heart-shaped leaves and a short raceme of small white flowers with yellow anthers, drawn down to a sheathing scale, a thin creeping rhizome and fine roots.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The near-sessile leaves are visible (the upper leaf is sessile, the lower very short-stalked), which matches the stated distinction from the European Maianthemum bifolium, and the leaf surfaces are drawn without hairs. Colour-printing from a single stipple-engraved plate with hand finishing is the standard and correct account of Redoute's technique for Les Liliacees. Nothing here contradicts the image or the record; ledger 'accurate' confirmed.

proposals.title: Ornithogalum Luteum
proposals.currentDescription: Ornithogalum luteum, growing from a hazelnut-sized bulb to a single channelled leaf and a terminal umbel of three to seven yellow flowers, green on the outside. A collar of opposite bracts sits below the blooms, with stamen and ovary figures enlarged at the foot. Redoute drew it for the sixth volume of Les Liliacees (1811).

issues.quote: with stamen and ovary figures enlarged at the foot
issues.problem: No enlarged analytical figures appear in the rendered image — only the whole plant and a figure number '1' at the foot.
issues.evidence: image

proposals.imageObservation: A whole plant drawn against blank paper: a brown tunicked bulb with a spray of fine white roots at the foot, one long broad channelled leaf rising well above the flowers, and a slender stem carrying a terminal umbel of about six yellow star-shaped flowers whose outer segments are green-backed, with two opposite leaf-like bracts just below the umbel. A small figure number '1' sits at the lower left. No enlarged dissection figures are visible in this image.
proposals.reviewerNotes: I did not lower the verdict on this one, deliberately. The file name (lilies-302-1) and the '1' printed at the foot of the image both suggest c82.net has split a multi-figure plate into parts, in which case the dissection figures the description mentions are real but live in a sibling image. Everything else matches the plate: single channelled leaf, umbel of yellow flowers green on the outside, collar of opposite bracts, bulb with roots. Plate 302 also falls in the sixth volume of Les Liliacees on a 60-plates-per-volume count, consistent with the 1811 date in the record. If a later pass wants to be strict, the safe edit is to delete the clause about the enlarged figures and change nothing else.

proposals.title: Pontederia Cordata
proposals.currentDescription: Pontederia cordata, an aquatic plant of still waters with long-petioled heart-shaped leaves and a spike of blue almost two-lipped flowers held above the surface. The text notes a variety gathered by Fraser in South Carolina. Redoute drew it for the second volume of Les Liliacees (1804).
proposals.imageObservation: A whole aquatic plant: two long-petioled, heart-shaped blue-green leaves, a dense spike of pale blue two-lipped flowers on a stout stalk emerging from a sheath, sheathing basal stems tinged pink, and a row of small dissected flower parts at the lower left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Leaf shape, the sheath, the spike of blue two-lipped flowers and the dissections all match the plate, and volume two of Les Liliacees is consistent with the record's 1804. The one claim I could not check is the variety 'gathered by Fraser in South Carolina' - c82.net is blocked, so I could not read the plate's text. John Fraser did collect in the Carolinas and supplied plants to European growers, so it is plausible rather than confirmed; a later agent should not treat it as verified.

proposals.title: Tulipa Cornuta
proposals.currentDescription: Tulipa cornuta, a tall slender tulip whose six narrow segments draw out into long horn-like points, the bud forming a sharp inverted cone before opening. The plate places it among the Liliaceae of Jussieu; Redoute drew it for the eighth and last volume of Les Liliacees (1814).
proposals.imageObservation: Three slender stems, each with six very narrow tepals drawn out into long horn-like points - two open (one showing a yellow interior with dark stamens, one pink) and one still closed - with long grass-like leaves; white ground.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Spot-check of a prior 'accurate'. The horn-like segments are exactly what the plate shows, and the volume claim holds: BHL gives Les Liliacees tome huitieme as 1814-1816, so 'eighth and last volume ... (1814)' is consistent with the record year. The Jussieu family attribution comes from the plate's printed caption, which is cropped out of this restoration - unverifiable here but not contradicted.

proposals.title: Tulipa Gesneriana
proposals.currentDescription: Tulipa gesneriana, the garden tulip, its single large terminal flower of six vivid yellow petals streaked with broad converging red bands, rising above three oblong half-clasping leaves on a smooth stem. The source text notes that the varieties of this species are too numerous to catalogue in full. Redouté drew this yellow-and-red variety for the eighth volume of Les Liliacées (1814).
proposals.imageObservation: Botanical plate: a single tulip on a smooth stem, its six tepals yellow with broad crimson flames converging from the base, three long oblong grey-green leaves clasping the stem below.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Flower, colour pattern, leaf count and habit all match the plate. The volume-eight attribution is consistent with the plate number (lilies-477 of 486) and with the record's 1814 date; the source-text claim is properly hedged as 'the source text notes'.

proposals.title: Rosa Aciphylla
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa aciphylla, a low shrub under three feet with stiff dark-brown branches and sparse hooked prickles, its small flowers carrying five tiny petals of white faintly tinged with pink. Redoute drew it for Les Roses, issued in three folio volumes; this plate belongs to the 1821 volume.
proposals.imageObservation: A single long, near-vertical dark reddish-brown cane with scattered hooked red prickles, hung with many small compound leaves and about five small open white flowers faintly tinged pink, with several pink-tipped buds.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Stem colour, sparse hooked prickles, small five-petalled white-tinged-pink flowers all match the plate. Les Roses was indeed issued in three folio volumes (1817, 1821, 1824) and plate 070 sits in the second volume, consistent with the record's year of 1821. The 'under three feet' habit is a Thory-type claim the image cannot settle; c82.net was unreachable.

proposals.title: Rosa Alba
proposals.currentDescription: A form of Rosa alba, the white rose, its pale blooms set among grey-green foliage on an upright shrub. The stipple engraving was printed in colour from a single plate and finished by hand in watercolour, the method used across all three volumes.
proposals.imageObservation: A single white double rose with several green buds at the top of a green, near-smooth cane, above long, narrow, grey-green toothed leaflets.
proposals.reviewerNotes: 'pale blooms' is plural where the plate shows one open flower plus buds — too trivial to act on. The technical sentence (colour-printed stipple engraving finished by hand, used throughout the three volumes of Les Roses, 1817-1824) is standard, well-established fact about the publication and is not contradicted by anything in the record.

proposals.title: Rosa Alba
proposals.currentDescription: The double white rose, Rosa alba flore pleno, its many-petalled bloom packed above pale foliage. The botanist Claude-Antoine Thory wrote the descriptive text that accompanied Redoute's plates for Les Roses.
proposals.imageObservation: Botanical plate on white: one fully open double white rose with a yellow stamen boss, two unopened buds, and grey-green pinnate foliage on a thorny stem.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Image matches the name: a double white rose with many petals. Claude-Antoine Thory did write the botanical text accompanying Redoute's plates in Les Roses - well established. c82.net could not be fetched, so the plate's own caption text was unavailable, but nothing in the description depends on it.

proposals.title: Rosa Alba Foliacea
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa alba foliacea, a branching shrub nearly free of prickles, its full white corolla over three inches across with five or six ranks of heart-notched petals above grey-backed leaves. Two of the calyx lobes stay simple while three are leafy, a trait noted in Thory's text.
proposals.imageObservation: A large white semi-double rose with a yellow centre, surrounded by buds whose calyx lobes extend into long leafy tips, above grey-green leaflets on stems that show no prickles.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The two checkable visual claims hold: the stems are effectively free of prickles and the buds show the leafy (foliaceous) sepals the varietal name refers to; some sepals are simple and some expanded, consistent with 'two simple, three leafy'. The corolla width ('over three inches') is from the unfetchable plate text.

proposals.title: Rosa Alba
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa alba in its royal form, a very large bloom of many petal ranks in white shading toward flesh-pink, borne several together at the branch tips. The French text likens it to the Cuisse de Nymphe and names it the English maiden's blush.
proposals.imageObservation: One very large white-to-blush double rose in full bloom with three tight pink buds around it, on a prickly stem with toothed pinnate leaves, on a plain white ground.
proposals.reviewerNotes: c82.net source unavailable. 'Cuisse de Nymphe' / 'Great Maiden's Blush' is the standard vernacular pairing for Rosa alba regalis, so the naming claim is consistent with general knowledge; the image supports the bloom colour, petal ranks and the cluster of buds at the branch tip.

proposals.title: Rosa Alpina
proposals.currentDescription: A variegated form of the Alpine rose, Rosa alpina, its smallish petals streaked bright red on a pink ground, the thornless shrub reaching three or four feet. Redoute drew it for Les Roses (1817-1824); this plate is from the 1821 volume.
proposals.imageObservation: Two open five-petalled roses, pink with darker radial streaks on a pale ground and yellow stamens, one spent flower with a small green hip, smooth thornless green and reddish stems, toothed leaflets.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Streaking, thornless stems and the Les Roses date range (1817-1824) all match. The height figure is unverifiable but plausible plate text; nothing is contradicted.

proposals.title: Rosa Alpina
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa alpina pendulina, its long thornless stems carrying nodding single flowers of five rose-violet petals above oval doubly toothed leaflets, the elongated ovaries curving down after pollination. Redoute drew it for Les Roses; this plate appeared in the 1817 volume.
proposals.imageObservation: A stipple-engraved botanical plate of a rose branch: one open single flower of five deep pink petals with a yellow centre, a bud and a pendulous elongated hip at right, smooth (thornless) pale stems, oval serrate leaflets, and a small uncoloured outline dissection of the hip and receptacle at lower left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Thornless stems, the nodding elongated ovary/hip and the five-petalled single flower are all visible and match R. pendulina. 'Rose-violet' is at the edge of what the plate shows (the petals read as deep carmine pink), and 'doubly toothed' cannot be resolved at this reproduction size — neither is enough to lower the verdict. The 1817 volume-one attribution is consistent with the catalogue year; c82.net could not be fetched to confirm the plate's volume.

proposals.title: Rosa Alpina Vulgaris
proposals.currentDescription: The common Alpine rose, Rosa alpina vulgaris, its pink flowers borne on smooth thornless stems above toothed foliage. Les Roses documents species roses and early garden cultivars before the rise of the modern hybrid.

issues.quote: Les Roses documents species roses and early garden cultivars before the rise of the modern hybrid.
issues.problem: Generic filler about the book that says nothing about this plate; house style asks the later sentences to add grounded context.
issues.evidence: catalogue record | the sentence would fit any of the ~170 plates in the set

proposals.imageObservation: A rose with three open flowers of deep magenta-crimson with yellow stamens, one spent flower and one bud, on smooth reddish-brown stems entirely free of prickles, with toothed compound leaves of seven to nine leaflets.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The thornless stems are the diagnostic feature of Rosa alpina (R. pendulina) and the plate shows them clearly, so the description's central claim holds. 'Pink flowers' understates a strong purple-crimson, but is a wording nit rather than a wrong colour, so I did not lower the verdict.

proposals.title: Rosa Andegavensis
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa andegavensis, the Anjou rose, with five-petalled flowers that begin pale pink and turn white, the gland-bristled calyx and stalk shown beneath sharply toothed foliage. Redoute drew it for Les Roses; this plate belongs to the 1821 volume.

issues.quote: the gland-bristled calyx and stalk
issues.problem: Glandular bristles are consistent with the species but are not resolvable at this reproduction size, and no source text was available.
issues.evidence: image at this resolution cannot settle it; c82.net blocked

proposals.imageObservation: Two open white five-petalled roses with yellow stamens at the top of a stem, one bud flushed pink, and a spent flower with reflexed sepals figured separately at the left; sharply toothed leaflets and small hooked prickles along the stem.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Name, colour behaviour (buds flushed pink, flowers white), petal count and foliage all match the plate. 'The 1821 volume' is consistent with Les Roses volume two and with plate number 059 and the catalogue year.

proposals.title: Rosa Banksiæ
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa banksiae, the Lady Banks rose, a rampant near-thornless climber bearing small sweetly scented flowers in primrose-like umbels of ten or more on long stalks. The leaflets are glossy on both faces; Redoute drew the rose for the 1821 volume of Les Roses.
proposals.imageObservation: A climbing stem with an umbel of small white double flowers — about four fully open and six or more in bud — on long radiating stalks, with narrow pointed leaflets; the woody stem shows no prickles.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Near-thornlessness and the umbel of ten or more small flowers on long stalks are both borne out by the plate; the 1821 volume matches the record's year. 'Glossy on both faces' and 'sweetly scented' cannot be settled from a reproduction but are conventional for R. banksiae and read as carried over from the plate's botanical text. The description never says the flowers are white and double, which they are — an omission, not an error.

proposals.title: Rosa Berberifolia
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa berberifolia, the barberry-leaved rose, a small two-foot shrub with simple alternate leaves and solitary canary-yellow flowers, each petal marked with a purple blotch at the claw. The bristly ovary and lobed calyx appear below the bloom in this 1817 plate.
proposals.imageObservation: A botanical plate of a rose with simple, alternate, toothed grey-green leaves on bristly stems, bearing solitary bright yellow five-petalled flowers each with a dark maroon-purple blotch at the base of every petal; a dissected flower showing the bristly ovary and lobed calyx sits at mid-left and a detached petal at bottom.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Simple (uncompound) alternate leaves and the purple basal blotch are the diagnostic features of Rosa berberifolia (Hulthemia persica) and both are plainly visible. The 'two-foot shrub' height comes from Thory's text and is not checkable from the image, but it is consistent with the species. Source site (c82.net) unfetchable, as flagged in the record.

proposals.title: Rosa Bifera
proposals.currentDescription: A white form of Rosa bifera, the four-seasons rose, its full pale bloom set among toothed foliage. The botanist Claude-Antoine Thory supplied the text that accompanied Redoute's plates for Les Roses.
proposals.imageObservation: A single white double rose in full bloom with a yellow centre, several unopened pink-tinged buds, and thorny stems carrying toothed, blue-green leaflets on a plain white ground.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Both claims hold: the plate is a white form of Rosa bifera (the 'quatre saisons' / four-seasons rose) and Claude-Antoine Thory wrote the text for Redoute's Les Roses. Source page (c82.net) unreachable, so the botanical wording could not be compared against Thory's original, but nothing in it conflicts with the image.

proposals.title: Rosa Bifera
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa bifera in its perfumers' form, a four- or five-foot bush bearing very fragrant rose-pink flowers of four or five petal ranks above oval toothed leaflets. Known as the Puteaux rose, it was the variety most used in the perfume trade.
proposals.imageObservation: A stipple-engraved botanical plate on white ground: one large double rose-pink flower, a second half-open bloom to its left, two buds above, ovate serrate leaflets on a prickly stem, and a detached hip/receptacle study at the lower left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Flower colour, doubling and foliage all match the plate. 'Puteaux rose'/'rose des parfumeurs' for Rosa bifera officinalis and its use in the perfume trade are standard; the bush height ('four or five foot') comes from Thory's text and could not be checked because c82.net is behind a bot challenge — it is plausible and low-risk, so I left it.

proposals.title: Rosa Bifera Variegata
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa bifera variegata, a four-seasons rose whose nearly round leaflets are blotched with irregular yellowish marks, its fragrant near-double flowers gathered in an upright corymb. Redoute drew it for Les Roses; this plate is from the 1824 volume.
proposals.imageObservation: Botanical plate: one large open pink double rose with a small yellow centre, three or four buds above it, and roundish green leaflets conspicuously blotched with yellow, on a strongly prickly stem.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The variegation - the whole point of the variety name - is plainly visible and correctly described, as is the near-round leaflet shape and the upright head of flower and buds. 'Four-seasons rose' is the standard reading of Rosa bifera (quatre saisons), and the 1824 volume matches the record year. Fragrance is not checkable from a plate but is a species character, not an invented anecdote.

proposals.title: Rosa Biserrata
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa biserrata, the mountain rose, a three- or four-foot shrub with curved prickles, doubly toothed leaflets each ending in a gland, and pale-pink solitary flowers. It was found on Mont Valerien near Paris by Dr Merat, whose description Thory reproduced.
proposals.imageObservation: A single white-to-palest-pink five-petalled rose with a yellow centre, a spent flower, and one ripe orange-red ovoid hip, on an arching cane with strongly hooked prickles and doubly toothed leaflets.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Confirmed by web search that this plate is 'Rose des montagnes a folioles bidentees (Rosa Biserrata), collected by Dr Merat before 1812 at Mont Valerien near Paris' in Les Roses vol. 2 (web:meisterdrucke.lu plate caption). The hooked prickles and doubly toothed leaflets are visible. The flower reads nearer white than 'pale-pink' in this reproduction - too small a nit to lower the verdict.

proposals.title: Rosa Bracteata
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa bracteata, the Macartney rose, a trailing shrub with slender hairy branches and glossy leaflets, its fragrant white flowers wrapped at the base by overlapping fringed bracts. The petals are broad and heart-notched, tipped with a small point.

issues.quote: glossy leaflets
issues.problem: The leaflets in the plate are rendered matte and greyish rather than glossy; the claim is true of the living species but is not what the sheet shows.
issues.evidence: image — leaflets are painted with a dull, slightly grey-green surface and no highlights.

proposals.imageObservation: A single large white rose with five broad, notched petals and a dense yellow boss of stamens, one bud below it enclosed in overlapping green bracts, pinnate leaves of many small oval leaflets, and a stem set with short red prickles, on a plain white ground.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Rosa bracteata (the Macartney rose) is a trailing/scrambling shrub with conspicuous fringed bracts, which the plate shows around the bud; the broad heart-notched petals with a small point are visible. The c82.net source page is Cloudflare-blocked, so Thory's wording could not be read; nothing in the text conflicts with the image or with standard descriptions of the species.

proposals.title: Rosa Brevistyla
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa brevistyla, the short-styled rose, a dense six- to eight-foot bush with reddish hooked prickles, its faintly scented yellowish-white flowers borne three or four together in a short corymb. The fused styles rise as one short glabrous column from the centre of the bloom.
proposals.imageObservation: A stipple-engraved botanical plate of a rose branch on white ground: four open single flowers with five broad creamy-white petals and yellow stamens, plus several green buds, carried together at the top of a reddish-brown stem armed with red hooked prickles, above compound green leaves.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Everything checkable against the image holds: reddish hooked prickles, yellowish-white flowers, three-to-four flowers in a short corymb. The bush height ('six- to eight-foot') and the fused short style column are Thory-type botanical statements that the image cannot settle and c82.net could not be fetched; they are consistent with the epithet brevistyla ('short-styled') and I found nothing to contradict them, so I left the verdict at accurate rather than inventing a problem.

proposals.title: Rosa Campanulata
proposals.currentDescription: A white-flowered form of Rosa campanulata, the bell rose, its pale blooms set among toothed foliage. Redoute was flower painter to Empress Josephine, whose garden at Malmaison held the most celebrated rose collection of the age, from which Les Roses grew.
proposals.imageObservation: Several white double roses, open and in bud, on a prickly stem with sharply toothed green leaflets, plain white ground.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Image supports white double blooms and toothed foliage.
