The second sentence is standard, well-established Redoute biography (flower painter to Josephine; the Malmaison rose collection behind Les Roses) rather than a claim about this plate; 'most celebrated rose collection of the age' is a conventional superlative, not a fabrication. Note that Les Roses appeared after Josephine's death, so 'from which Les Roses grew' should be read as origin, not literal commission.

proposals.title: Rosa Canina Grandiflora
proposals.currentDescription: A large-flowered dog rose, Rosa canina grandiflora, its five soft-pink petals paler toward the claw and yellowish at the base, set above glabrous leaflets and hooked prickles. The branching shrub bears nearly round hips that ripen red, drawn for Les Roses (1817-1824).
proposals.imageObservation: A dog-rose branch with one large single pink flower of five petals, pale toward the base around a yellow centre, several rounded red-brown hips/buds beside it, smooth dark leaflets and stout hooked red prickles on the stems.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Petal colour and pale base, glabrous leaflets, hooked prickles and rounded reddening hips are all visible. The '1817-1824' span for Les Roses is correct and consistent with the catalogue year of 1824.

proposals.title: Rosa Carolina
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa carolina in its corymb-flowered form, light-pink petals notched at the tip above ovate leaflets and reddish stems with scattered prickles. Claude-Antoine Thory, who wrote the text, treats it as a variety of Michaux's R. caroliniana rather than the species Willdenow named.
proposals.imageObservation: Stipple plate of a rose: a corymb of five or six single mid-pink flowers with yellow centres above ovate, toothed leaflets on green-and-red stems with a few small prickles; a single red hip is shown separately at the foot.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The taxonomic sentence checks out against Thory's own text as reproduced on c82.net (found via search since the site itself is Cloudflare-blocked): the variety is described there as a variety of 'R. Caroliniana de Michaux, which Willdenow incorrectly presented as the true species', with 'smooth, reddish branches ... scattered, unequal, nearly straight prickles'. Only wobble: the plate's flowers read as mid rose-pink rather than 'light-pink' — too small to call an error.

proposals.title: Rosa Centifolia
proposals.currentDescription: The hundred-petalled cabbage rose, Rosa centifolia, its rounded bloom packed with rose-pink petals that deepen toward the centre, above doubly toothed dark-green leaflets and bristly ovaries. Thory noted the rose had already been figured by Clusius and earlier botanists.
proposals.imageObservation: Botanical plate on white ground: one large fully double cabbage rose, outer petals pale pink and the packed centre deep rose-red, with five red buds around it, mid-to-dark green serrated leaflets and a stem set with red prickles.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The Thory/Clusius claim checks out: the c82.net page for this plate lists the rose as figured in Clusius, Miller, Knorr, Lawrence, Roessig and others (surfaced via search; c82.net itself 403s). Petal colour and foliage match the plate.

proposals.title: Rosa Centifolia
proposals.currentDescription: An anemone-flowered cabbage rose, Rosa centifolia anemonoides, its pink corolla in five or six ranks with the short inner petals folded and cupped like an anemone. The variety can be kept only by grafting, then layered to raise own-root plants, per Thory's text.
proposals.imageObservation: Botanical plate: two pink cabbage-rose blooms, each with broad outer petals and a mass of short folded inner petals; the left flower shows a ring of yellow stamens at the centre. Prickly stems, five-leaflet leaves, three buds.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The morphology described (pink corolla in several ranks, short inner petals folded and cupped anemone-fashion) matches the plate. The propagation note ('kept only by grafting, then layered') is attributed to Thory and cannot be checked because c82.net is behind a bot challenge - plausible for a sterile double garden variety, flagged here only so a later reader knows it is unverified.

proposals.title: Rosa Centifolia
proposals.currentDescription: A red-flowered cabbage rose, Rosa centifolia in the form called the Cumberland rose, its full double bloom above toothed leaflets and prickled stems. The plate is a stipple engraving printed in colour from a single plate and finished by hand in watercolour.
proposals.imageObservation: Botanical plate: one large, fully double deep-rose-pink cabbage rose with many incurved petals, six or seven buds on bristly stalks, broad toothed leaflets and a stout stem armed with red hooked prickles.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The "Cumberland rose" name is confirmed: RMN Images d'Art and The Old Print Shop both catalogue this plate as "Rosa Centifolia Anglica rubra / Rosier de Cumberland" (web:art.rmngp.fr, web:oldprintshop.com/product/137757). The stipple-engraving-printed-in-colour-and-finished-by-hand technique is the documented method for Les Roses and is repeated in those dealer records. One nit I did not raise to a finding: the bloom reads as deep rose-pink rather than "red", but the variety epithet is literally rubra, so the wording is defensible.

proposals.title: Rosa Centifolia
proposals.currentDescription: A celery-leaved cabbage rose, Rosa centifolia bipinnata, its finely divided leaflets set below a full pink double flower. Redoute was flower painter to Empress Josephine, whose garden at Malmaison held the rose collection from which Les Roses grew.
proposals.imageObservation: One full, globular pink double rose with several buds at the top of a thorny stem, above leaves whose leaflets are deeply cut and lobed rather than simple ovals — the 'celery-leaved' character.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The dissected foliage and the single full pink flower match the description exactly. The Malmaison sentence is the standard account of Les Roses (Redouté was Josephine's flower painter and her collection underpinned the book); some scholarship notes that many plates were drawn from other collections after her death in 1814, so the sentence is conventional rather than precise, but it is not a fabrication.

proposals.title: Rosa Centifolia
proposals.currentDescription: The Vilmorin rose, a cabbage rose with nearly full flowers of a transparent flesh-pink, borne singly or in twos and threes above light-green woolly-backed leaflets. Thory notes the variety, kept by grafting, was named for the nurseryman who first distributed it.
proposals.imageObservation: A single stem carrying one fully open, very double flower of pale flesh-pink with four unopened buds around it, above compound leaves of five broad green leaflets; the stem is set with fine straight prickles.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The plate is published as 'Rosa centifolia carnea - Rosier Vilmorin', which supports 'the Vilmorin rose'; Vilmorin was a Paris seedsman and nurseryman, so 'named for the nurseryman who first distributed it' is consistent, though it comes from Thory's text, which I could not read (c82.net is behind Cloudflare). 'Borne singly or in twos and threes', 'kept by grafting' and 'woolly-backed leaflets' are species/variety statements from that text and cannot be checked against the plate, which shows one open flower; nothing in the image contradicts them.

proposals.title: Rosa Centifolia
proposals.currentDescription: The carnation rose, a cabbage rose variety with a small pink corolla above ovate pointed leaflets, woolly beneath, and stems set with unequal reddish prickles. The variety can be multiplied only by grafting or layering, according to Thory's text.

issues.quote: The variety can be multiplied only by grafting or layering, according to Thory's text.
issues.problem: Attributed to Thory's accompanying text, which could not be read: c82.net is behind a bot challenge and no other transcription surfaced. Plausible for a sterile double cultivar but unchecked.
issues.evidence: sourceEvidence note - c82.net unfetchable; no confirming source found

proposals.imageObservation: A rose stem carrying a corymb of about eight double pink flowers with ragged, carnation-like petals and yellow stamens, plus three buds; large broadly ovate, pointed, toothed leaflets below, and reddish prickles scattered along the stem. A small monochrome petal study sits at the lower left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Visual claims hold: cabbage-rose type, pink, ovate pointed leaflets, unequal reddish prickles. 'A small pink corolla' is singular where the plate shows a full cluster of about eight flowers - thin rather than wrong, so I have not rewritten it. The 'woolly beneath' and propagation details are Thory-flavoured and cannot be checked while c82.net is blocked.

proposals.title: Rosa Centifolia
proposals.currentDescription: A crenate-leaved cabbage rose, Rosa centifolia crenata, with rounded leaflets deeply scalloped and heart-shaped at the base, below a many-petalled pink flower whose inner petals are crumpled. Thory records the bloom as scented, though less so than the common cabbage rose.
proposals.imageObservation: A single many-petalled pink cabbage rose with crumpled inner petals at the top of a prickly stem, with buds and broad, strongly veined toothed leaflets below.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Flower form matches. 'Thory records the bloom as scented, though less so than the common cabbage rose' is a claim about the plate's letterpress that could not be checked - c82.net is behind a Cloudflare challenge. It is plausible and hedged as an attribution rather than stated as the picture's content, so I left it. Leaf margins read serrate rather than clearly crenate in the reproduction, but the varietal name is 'crenata', so the description is following the plate.

proposals.title: Rosa Centifolia
proposals.currentDescription: A leafy-bracted cabbage rose, Rosa centifolia foliacea, its pink double flower set among enlarged leaf-like bracts at the calyx. Les Roses was issued in three folio volumes between 1817 and 1824, this plate in the second.
proposals.imageObservation: One large fully double pink rose with a deeper rose centre, one half-open bud and several tight buds, surrounded by leafy sepal appendages and large green leaves; the stem below is armed with red prickles.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Pink double flower and the enlarged leaf-like bracts at the calyx, which are the defining trait of the 'foliacea' form, are both visible. The publishing claim (three folio volumes, 1817-1824, this plate in the second) matches the standard bibliography for Les Roses and the record's 1821 date.

proposals.title: Rosa Centifolia Minor
proposals.currentDescription: The Bordeaux rose, a small cabbage rose forming a bush about a foot and a half high, its flowers in fours and sixes with seven or eight ranks of pink petals smaller than the common centifolia. The leaflets are nearly round and woolly beneath, per Thory's description.
proposals.imageObservation: One large pink cabbage-rose bloom, tightly packed with petals, plus two small buds, above ovate toothed leaflets on a bristly stem.
proposals.reviewerNotes: 'The Bordeaux rose' checks out: R. centifolia minor is the Rose de Bordeaux / Gros Pompon de Bourgogne, described by Thory in Redoute (Trees and Shrubs Online cites Thory in Redoute vol. III p.33). The counts ('flowers in fours and sixes', 'seven or eight ranks') are species botany from Thory, explicitly attributed in the text, and are not contradicted by the single bloom shown.

proposals.title: Rosa Centifolia
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa centifolia in the form called the Unique rose, its full bloom shading from white toward pink across the petals. Redoute drew it for the first volume of Les Roses, issued in 1817.
proposals.imageObservation: One large fully double white rose with a faint pink flush toward the outer petals, several pink-tinged buds, prickly stems and broad green leaflets, on a plain white ground.
proposals.reviewerNotes: c82.net could not be fetched. Independent sources confirm Rosa centifolia mutabilis is the 'Rosier unique' / 'Unique blanche', a white centifolia whose buds and outer petals carry a red-pink tint, matching both the image and the description's colour claim. Plate 43 of Les Roses falls in the first volume, consistent with the record's 1817. Sources: NYPL Digital Collections record and treesandshrubsonline.org on Rosa centifolia.

proposals.title: Rosa Centifolia
proposals.currentDescription: A cabbage rose that carries two variations on one plant, the leafy-bracted and the proliferous forms, with a pink flower growing through from its own centre. Thory notes the foliage otherwise matches the many centifolias already figured in the work.
proposals.imageObservation: A cabbage rose plate: one large double pink bloom with a second bud pushing up through its centre, flanked by buds whose calyces are drawn out into conspicuous leafy lobes, on prickly stems with broad toothed leaflets.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Both stated variations are visible: the proliferous flower growing through its own centre, and the leafy-bracted (foliaceous) calyces on the buds. The Thory attribution is hedged and consistent with the plate.

proposals.title: Rosa Damascena Aurora
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa damascena in its Aurora form, a full bloom of six or seven rows of petals in rose tinted toward yellow, clustered in an umbel above five rounded leaflets. The strongly arching petiole sets this variety apart. Redoute drew it for Les Roses, issued in folio volumes between 1817 and 1824.
proposals.imageObservation: A full double pink rose with a yellowish centre nodding on a strongly arched stalk, with four buds clustered beside it, above stout prickly canes and broad five-leaflet leaves.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Arching flower stalk, the cluster of bloom plus buds, and the five rounded leaflets all match the plate. 'Petiole' is loosely used for what is strictly the peduncle, but the arching feature it points at is genuinely visible.

proposals.title: Rosa Damascena Italica
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa damascena italica, the autumn-flowering Quatre-Saisons of Italy, its soft pink flowers carried in threes above bright green oval leaflets. An elongated red hip appears at maturity. Redoute drew it for the third volume of Les Roses, published in 1824.
proposals.imageObservation: Two large, fully double, soft pink roses side by side with a third deep-red bud and a further pink bud above them, on a green prickled stem with broad oval mid-green leaflets. No hip is shown.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Soft pink flowers in a cluster of about three with oval leaflets matches the plate. Les Roses volume three is 1824, consistent with the record's year and with plate 132. The red hip 'at maturity' is a statement about the plant rather than about the plate, so its absence from the image is not a contradiction; it is unverifiable here because c82.net could not be fetched. 'Bright green' slightly overstates a mid-green foliage — too trivial to act on.

proposals.title: Rosa Damascena
proposals.currentDescription: The York and Lancaster rose, a damask whose four or five rows of petals are most often white streaked and spotted with pink, the same shrub also throwing all-pink and all-white flowers. The sticky red-glanded stems and calyces are fragrant. Claude-Antoine Thory wrote the descriptive text for the plate.
proposals.imageObservation: Two open white roses heavily streaked and flecked with pink, with pink-tipped buds, coarsely toothed green leaflets and stems carrying red prickles and glandular bristles, on a white ground.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Image matches the York and Lancaster rose (Rosa damascena variegata): striped white-and-pink flowers, red-glanded stems. Thory wrote the letterpress for Les Roses, so the attribution of the text is safe. The claims about the shrub also throwing all-pink and all-white flowers and about the scent come from the plate's text, which could not be fetched (c82.net is behind a bot challenge); they are consistent with standard descriptions of this rose but are not independently verified here.

proposals.title: Rosa Eglanteria Luteola
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa eglanteria luteola, a smaller many-branched form of the yellow eglantine to about three feet, with seven to eleven small near-round leaflets. The five canary-yellow petals are notched at the apex and the flower carries a disagreeable scent. The stipple plate was printed in colour and finished by hand.
proposals.imageObservation: One large open five-petalled canary-yellow rose with three yellow buds, on many-branched brown canes set with straight prickles; leaves of numerous small rounded leaflets.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Petal count, colour, straight prickles and the small near-round leaflets all match the plate. The 'disagreeable scent' is a well-known characteristic of the yellow eglantine (Rosa foetida). The 'about three feet' height is unverifiable from image or record but is the kind of detail Thory's text supplies.

proposals.title: Rosa Eglanteria
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa eglanteria in its red form, the Austrian copper known in gardens as the Rose Capucine or Rose d'Autriche, the same plant sometimes bearing yellow and red flowers on one stock. The globular hip stays constant across the species. Claude-Antoine Thory supplied the botanical text for the plate.
proposals.imageObservation: Botanical plate on a white ground: two open single roses with copper-red petals and yellow reverses around yellow stamens, a yellow-and-red bud cluster above, grey-green pinnate leaflets, a pale prickly cane, and a small globular orange hip drawn separately at lower left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The image supports every checkable claim: the red form with yellow showing on the same stock (the yellow bud at top and the yellow petal reverse in the upper flower), and the globular hip drawn as a separate figure at the foot. Thory's authorship of the botanical text for Les Roses is standard. 'Rose Capucine' / 'Rose d'Autriche' as garden names for the Austrian Copper is well attested but could not be verified against the source page (c82.net returns 403).

proposals.title: Rosa Farinosa
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa farinosa, a much-branched shrub whose three to seven leaflets are covered both sides with a soft whitish down. Five very pale pink petals form each flower, gathered in a terminal corymb above an egg-shaped hip that ripens dull red. Claude-Antoine Thory wrote the descriptive text for the plate.
proposals.imageObservation: A much-branched rose with a single open flower of five very pale, almost white petals with a yellow centre, two buds, and greyish, mealy-looking compound leaves of five to seven leaflets on pale stems with a few small prickles.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Foliage colour (whitish, downy-looking), leaflet count and the very pale five-petalled flower all match the plate. Claude-Antoine Thory did write the text for Les Roses, so that attribution is correct. 'Gathered in a terminal corymb' and the egg-shaped hip ripening dull red are from the text, not visible here - the plate shows one open flower and no ripe hip.

proposals.title: Rosa Fœtida
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa foetida, a shrub to six feet whose small near-scentless flowers carry five soft pink petals that the sun quickly fades, usually borne singly. The ovoid orange-red hips give off a fetid smell when crushed. Redoute drew it for Les Roses, issued in folio volumes between 1817 and 1824.
proposals.imageObservation: Two open five-petalled pink roses with yellow stamens, one spent flower whose petals have fallen, and one bud, on a slender prickly stem with pinnate leaves.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Image supports single (five-petalled) pink flowers borne singly. The habit ('shrub to six feet'), the scent claims and the orange-red hips are not visible in the plate and could not be checked (c82.net blocked); they read as paraphrase of Thory's accompanying text. Note that Rosa foetida in the modern sense (Austrian briar) is yellow-flowered - here the plate itself is pink, so the description follows the plate rather than the modern species concept, which is the right choice but worth knowing.

proposals.title: Rosa Gallica
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa gallica as the common Provins rose, its large semi-double flowers of fine purple-red borne singly or in pairs at the branch tips. Oval pointed leaflets sit on bristly petioles set with glands and small hooked prickles. The descriptive text accompanying the plate was written by Claude-Antoine Thory.
proposals.imageObservation: One large semi-double purple-red rose with visible yellow stamens at the centre, three buds around it, borne on a bristly stem set with small prickles, with oval pointed leaflets, some grey-green underside showing.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Flower form, colour, bristly glandular stem and leaflet shape all match the plate. Thory's authorship of the accompanying text in Les Roses is standard and uncontested, though the c82.net source page was unreachable to confirm this particular plate's text.

proposals.title: Rosa Gallica Agatha
proposals.currentDescription: An Agatha form of Rosa gallica, a proliferous rose from whose softer-pink flower a second bloom emerges, sometimes a third from the centre of that. The flattened stalk often carries leafy bracts in tiers. Redoute drew it for the third volume of Les Roses, published in 1824.
proposals.imageObservation: Botanical plate: a full double soft-pink rose from whose centre a leafy shoot with a small bud rises, plus a second bud at the left and leafy bracts along the flattened stalk; broad toothed leaflets and a green stem with a few red prickles below.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The proliferation — a shoot with a second flower growing out of the centre of the first — is clearly drawn, as are the leafy bracts on the flower stalk, so the two visual claims hold. Les Roses vol. 3 is 1824, matching the record year. The "sometimes a third from the centre of that" detail is presumably Thory's and cannot be checked (c82.net blocked); it is hedged with "sometimes", so I did not raise it.

proposals.title: Rosa Gallica Agatha
proposals.currentDescription: An Agatha form of Rosa gallica grown as the Agathe Royale, its very double corolla of bright rose petals rolled and crumpled at the centre and wedged between calyx and styles. The flower carries no stamens. The stipple engraving was printed in colour and finished by hand.
proposals.imageObservation: A single very full, flat-topped pink rose whose innermost petals are small, folded and crumpled, with four buds around it and a thorny stem carrying five-leaflet leaves. No stamens are visible.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The image supports the two checkable visual claims — a very double corolla with rolled and crumpled central petals, and no visible stamens. 'Agathe Royale' matches the plate name in the id (agatha regalis). The technical sentence (colour-printed stipple engraving finished by hand) is the documented process for Les Roses. c82.net could not be fetched, so Thory's phrasing about the petals being 'wedged between calyx and styles' is unverified but harmless.

proposals.title: Rosa Gallica Agatha
proposals.currentDescription: An Agatha form of Rosa gallica grown as the Agathe Carnee, its many close-set petals a softer pink than the Agathe Prolifere. Firm dark-green leaflets, downy beneath, sit below flowers borne several together at the branch tips, and the hip is rarely seen. Claude-Antoine Thory wrote the descriptive text for the plate.
proposals.imageObservation: One densely double pale-pink flower at the top of a prickly stem, with pink buds and several spent flower heads showing green leafy sepals, over firm dark-green toothed leaflets.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Matches the Agathe group of Rosa gallica: very full, close-set petals, flowers at the branch tips. The comparison with 'Agathe Prolifere', the downy leaf undersides and 'the hip is rarely seen' come from the plate's letterpress, which could not be fetched; none of them is contradicted by the image.

proposals.title: Rosa Gallica Auelianensis
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa gallica aurelianensis, the Duchesse d'Orleans, a gallica to four feet whose lightly scented flowers carry five or six rows of deep rose petals, usually borne in threes. Large firm leaflets sit on glandular-bristly stalks, and the hips ripen red. Redoute drew it for the third volume of Les Roses, published in 1824.
proposals.imageObservation: One large, fully double deep-rose flower opening far enough to show a centre of yellow stamens, flanked by three dark crimson buds; large firm leaflets below, and a stem covered in red prickles and gland-tipped bristles.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Deep rose petals in many rows, large firm leaflets and glandular-bristly stalks are all visible. 'Usually borne in threes' and 'the hips ripen red' are species-level statements from Thory's text that the plate neither shows nor contradicts. Volume three of Les Roses published 1824 matches the record's year. The vernacular name 'Duchesse d'Orleans' for aurelianensis could not be independently confirmed (c82.net unreachable) but is consistent with the Latin epithet.

proposals.title: Rosa Gallica
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa gallica grown as a Provins rose, its rose-purple bloom set above the toothed leaflets of the French rose. Redoute drew it for Les Roses, which grew out of Empress Josephine's celebrated rose collection at Malmaison, where he served as her flower painter.
proposals.imageObservation: A single large semi-double rose, deep rose-pink flushed purple with a yellow ring of stamens, plus one dark red bud, on a prickly stem with sharply toothed blue-green leaflets.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Bloom colour and toothed leaflets match. The Malmaison/Joséphine framing is the standard account of Les Roses and Redouté's post as her flower painter; 'grew out of' is a loose but defensible summary (Joséphine died in 1814, three years before the first volume). The variety name in the id ('coerulea') is not mentioned in the description, but nothing asserted is wrong.

proposals.title: Rosa Gallica Gueriniana
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa gallica gueriniana, the Rosier Guerin, a French rose shown in flower above its toothed leaflets. Les Roses documented species roses and early garden cultivars before the rise of the modern hybrid, and Redoute drew this plate for the third volume, published in 1824.

issues.quote: a French rose shown in flower above its toothed leaflets
issues.problem: The one visual statement omits the plate's most striking feature, the near-black purple of the open flower against the crimson bud.
issues.evidence: image

proposals.imageObservation: Botanical plate: a very dark purple-crimson double rose, densely quartered, dominates the left; above it a crimson half-open flower and a bud; below, green toothed leaflets on a stem with fine prickles. White ground.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Nothing asserted is contradicted: it is a gallica plate showing a flower above toothed leaflets, and the third volume of Les Roses did appear in 1824, matching the record's year. The second sentence is generic Les Roses boilerplate; a rewrite that names the dark purple bloom would serve the reader better, but there is no factual defect to fix.

proposals.title: Rosa Gallica
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa gallica latifolia, the broad-leaved Provins rose, with deep-pink double flowers of five or six petal ranks notched at the tip and unusually large dark-green leaflets. The fruit ripens almost ellipsoid and bright red. The stipple engraving was printed in colour and finished by hand, the method used across all three folio volumes.
proposals.imageObservation: A single deep-pink double rose with two buds at the top of a prickly stem, above unusually large, broad leaflets in a grey-green to mid-green; plain white ground.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Flower colour, doubling and the conspicuously broad leaflets match the name and the plate. The leaflets read more grey-green than 'dark-green' in this reproduction — too small a nit to lower the verdict. The fruit description comes from Thory (no fruit is shown) and is unverified. The technique sentence is correct for Les Roses: colour-printed stipple engraving finished by hand.

proposals.title: Rosa Gallica
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa gallica pontiana, the rose of Andre du Pont, a bushy Provins shrub bearing large bright-red flowers of seven or eight petal ranks with a light fragrance. Its leaflets are firm and finely double-toothed on hairy stalks. The plate was printed in colour from a single stipple-engraved plate and finished by hand.

issues.quote: on hairy stalks
issues.problem: Thory's description of this rose (as rendered in secondary sources) says the leaflets are smooth above and hairy beneath; it does not describe hairy petioles. The image cannot settle it either way.
issues.evidence: web:search summary of Thory's text for Rosa gallica pontiana - 'firm and brittle, finely doubly-toothed, smooth above and hairy below with some glands along the margin'

proposals.imageObservation: A plate of a large fully double rose in deep crimson-pink with paler outer petals, plus three buds, on stems with compound leaves of three to five broad toothed leaflets and a bristly lower stem.
proposals.reviewerNotes: 'The rose of Andre du Pont' is well supported - the plate's French title is 'Rosier du Pont', after the rosarian Andre Dupont. The 'seven or eight petal ranks' and 'light fragrance' come from Thory and I could not verify them directly; they are plausible and not contradicted. The bloom reads as deep carmine rather than a pure 'bright-red', but within the range of a hand-coloured plate that is not worth a correction.

proposals.title: Rosa Gallica
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa gallica regalis, the Royal Provins, a semi-double rose of four or five petal ranks in a pink deeper than the common cabbage rose, its blooms often more than three inches across. A few central stamens have turned into small crumpled petals. Redoute drew it for Les Roses, issued in folio volumes between 1817 and 1824.

issues.quote: its blooms often more than three inches across
issues.problem: A measurement that cannot be checked against the image, the record or any source I could reach.
issues.evidence: c82.net is bot-blocked; the Thory passage surfaced by search does not include a diameter.

proposals.imageObservation: One large, fully open pink rose of many overlapping petal ranks with small crumpled petals at the centre, three buds around it, and coarse dark green leaflets on a prickled stem.
proposals.reviewerNotes: I initially read the flower as too full for 'semi-double', but Thory's own text for this plate (surfaced by search from the c82.net transcription) reads: corolla semi-double, composed of four to five rows of petals of a deeper pink than the ordinary hundred-petalled rose; at the centre only a few stamens, some transformed into irregular ruffled petals. That matches the description almost word for word, so the botanical vocabulary is the source's, not an invention. One loose end: a secondary print-seller listing dates this plate to Les Roses vol. 1 (1817) while the catalogue row says 1821 - too weak a source to act on, but worth noting if someone revisits the redoute-roses dates.

proposals.title: Rosa Gallica Rosea
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa gallica rosea in a single form, five rose-pink petals more than three inches across and heart-notched at the tip, above large leaflets downy beneath. The fruit ripens globular and red. The plate was printed in colour from a single stipple-engraved plate and finished by hand in watercolour.
proposals.imageObservation: Two large single rose-pink flowers with five broad notched petals and yellow stamens, on a prickly stem with large leaflets whose paler undersides are turned to the viewer.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Petal count, notched tips, colour and the downy pale undersides all match the plate; the printing-technique sentence is the standard, correct account of Les Roses.

proposals.title: Rosa Geminata
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa geminata, the twin-flowered rose, with branches that arch and lie along the ground like the field rose, bearing five large satin-white petals tinged faintly with pink. The calyx tube swells at the middle between the forms of the white and damask roses. The stipple engraving was printed in colour and finished by hand in watercolour.
proposals.imageObservation: One large open flower of five broad satin-white petals with a yellow-orange centre, and four green buds carried in pairs, on an arching pale green stem with red-tipped prickles and grey-green compound leaves.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Five large satin-white petals and the paired ('geminata') buds are visible; the faint pink is on the buds rather than the open bloom, which is a fair reading rather than an error. The stipple-engraved-and-hand-finished technique statement is correct for Les Roses. The trailing habit and the calyx-tube observation are Thory-type claims the image cannot settle.

proposals.title: Rosa Hudsoniana
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa hudsoniana scandens, a climbing Hudson rose able to cover arbours, its smooth red-brown branches free of prickles. The solitary or paired flowers carry three or four ranks of soft pink petals and open in May. Claude-Antoine Thory supplied the botanical text that accompanied Redoute's plates.
proposals.imageObservation: Two open roses, one pale pink and one deeper rose, each with three or four ranks of petals and a yellow centre, plus three buds; the stems are green and entirely free of prickles, the leaflets green and toothed.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Flagging for a human rather than as an error: the description calls the branches 'red-brown', and in this plate they are plainly green (zoomed to check). The 'free of prickles' half is confirmed by the image. Because these Redoute entries demonstrably paraphrase Thory's text — which for the neighbouring Rosa indica plate contains colour statements the plate does not show — the colour may be his and not an invention, and the c82.net source text could not be fetched (Cloudflare). 'open in May' and 'able to cover arbours' are likewise unverifiable from image or record.

proposals.title: rosa indica
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa indica, the China rose described by Linnaeus, forming bushes of about two feet with nearly thornless branches and five simply toothed leaflets. Its solitary flowers show five heart-notched petals ranging from the softest pink to deepest purple. The plate was printed in colour from a single stipple-engraved plate and finished by hand.
proposals.imageObservation: A plate of a China rose: a nearly thornless green stem with compound leaves of three and five glossy toothed leaflets, carrying two solitary single flowers of deep crimson-purple with yellow stamens, plus buds.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The stated colour range 'from the softest pink to deepest purple' reads as Thory's account of the species' variability rather than a claim about this plate, and the plate itself sits at the deep-purple end, so it is not contradicted. Leaflet counts in the image are three to five rather than a uniform five; too small a drift to act on. The stipple-engraving-printed-in-colour-and-finished-by-hand sentence is the standard, correct account of Les Roses' technique.

proposals.title: Rosa Indica Acuminata
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa indica acuminata, a small China rose of about two feet with leaflets washed a wine tint beneath, its lightly scented solitary flowers carrying five always-pointed petals of white flushed with pink. The long stamens curl back over the styles as in all the India roses. Claude-Antoine Thory wrote the descriptive text for the plate.
proposals.imageObservation: A slender rose spray with two solitary open flowers, each of five white petals faintly flushed lilac-pink and drawn to a distinct point, plus one spent flower; several leaflets at the right are washed grey-violet on their undersides; sparse red prickles on a green stem.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Pointed (acuminate) petals, solitary flowers, white flushed pink and the wine-tinted leaf undersides are all visible in the plate. Thory as author of the text for Les Roses is correct for the series. Two claims I could not settle and did not act on: the two-foot height, and 'the long stamens curl back over the styles' — in this plate the stamens read as a short yellow boss rather than long and reflexed, but the reproduction is not sharp enough for me to call it contradicted.

proposals.title: Rosa Indica Caryophillea
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa indica caryophillea, the carnation Bengal, an elegant China rose under twenty inches with eight to ten ranks of deep rose petals, some crossed by a white line, that crimp and ruffle so the open flower resembles a carnation. The fruit is ovoid and smooth. Claude-Antoine Thory supplied the botanical text for the plate.

issues.quote: some crossed by a white line
issues.problem: No white striping is visible on the petals in this reproduction; the blooms read as uniformly deep crimson.
issues.evidence: image — no white lines legible at this resolution

proposals.imageObservation: Four fully double roses in deep crimson-carmine, their many narrow petals crimped and irregularly folded, on a green stem with a few small prickles; the leaflets are broad, glossy and pointed, and one dark bud is shown at right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The crimped carnation-like petals, the deep rose colour and the China-rose habit all match the plate, and the file URL (roses-148) matches Les Roses pl. 148, sold as 'Monthly Rose', i.e. a Rosa indica/Bengal. The height, the petal-rank count and the ovoid fruit read as Thory's text, which I could not fetch to confirm; they are the kind of specific detail that is either quoted or invented, and nothing here suggests invention. The white-line detail is the only thing that visibly does not appear, and it may simply be lost in the restoration.

proposals.title: Rosa Indica Dichotoma
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa indica dichotoma, a China rose to two feet or more under glass, its forked branches armed with scattered hooked prickles and glossy five to seven leaflets. The scented flowers gather at the branch tips on repeatedly forking peduncles. The plate was printed in colour from a single stipple-engraved plate and finished by hand.

issues.quote: glossy five to seven leaflets
issues.problem: The leaves in the plate carry three or five leaflets; I see no seven-leaflet leaf.
issues.evidence: image - leaf groups counted at lower left (five) and centre (three)

proposals.imageObservation: A plate of a China rose with forking green stems carrying scattered small prickles, glossy compound leaves of three and five leaflets, and three double flowers in deep crimson-purple plus a bud, the flowers gathered toward the branch tips.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The leaflet-count range most likely comes straight from Thory's text (which describes the species, not only the specimen drawn), so this is a low-confidence nit rather than an error to fix. The forking peduncles that give 'dichotoma' its name are clearly visible, as is the clustering of flowers at the branch tips.

proposals.title: Rosa Indica
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa indica fragrans, the fragrant China rose, its very large nodding flowers often more than two and a half inches across, a flesh-tinged white that looks almost transparent. The globular ovary and calyx lobes are smooth. The stipple engraving was printed in colour and finished by hand, the method used across all three volumes.
proposals.imageObservation: A large blush-white double rose, tilted slightly forward, with one bud at the upper right and a dissected flower at the right showing yellow stamens and styles; smooth green ovaries on the buds, glossy pointed leaflets, a few red-brown prickles on the stem.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Colour ('flesh-tinged white'), the smooth globular ovary and the printing method (colour-printed stipple engraving finished by hand, used throughout Les Roses) all check out against the plate and standard accounts. The flower size ('more than two and a half inches') is Thory's measurement and could not be verified — source site unreachable — but is not doing load-bearing work.

proposals.title: Rosa Indica Fragranas
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa indica fragrans in a single form, the tea-scented rose, with five fairly large heart-notched petals of soft pink that carry a sweet fragrance far. The long stamens fold back over the styles as in all India roses, and the fruit ripens from red to black. Claude-Antoine Thory wrote the descriptive text for the plate.
proposals.imageObservation: Two single soft-pink roses of five broad, notch-tipped petals with yellow stamen bosses, one bud and one spent flower, above dark toothed leaflets on a thorny stem.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The visual claims (single form, five large notched petals, soft pink) match exactly. Two botanical assertions - 'the long stamens fold back over the styles as in all India roses' and 'the fruit ripens from red to black' - are not visible in the plate and could not be verified because the source text (c82.net) is behind a bot challenge; 'as in all India roses' is a universal claim that a later pass may want to soften.

proposals.title: Rosa Indica
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa indica multipetala, a Bengal rose forming a bushy shrub of three or four feet, its green branches armed with strong reddish hooked prickles. The double flowers, deeper pink than the common China rose, open from a bright-red bud, the crumpled central petals nearly hiding the stamens. The plate was printed in colour from a single stipple-engraved plate and finished by hand.
proposals.imageObservation: A green stem armed with reddish hooked prickles bearing one large, fully double pink rose with crumpled central petals, two dark crimson unopened buds and two opening buds, above compound leaves of three to five smooth leaflets.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Green branches, strong reddish hooked prickles, deep-red buds and crumpled central petals hiding the stamens all match the plate. 'Three or four feet' is from Thory's text and cannot be checked (c82.net blocked). The stipple-engraving-printed-in-colour-and-finished-by-hand sentence is the standard and correct account of how Les Roses was produced.

proposals.title: Rosa Indica
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa indica in its dwarf Bengal form, a low shrub under a foot tall with sparse straight prickles and solitary pink flowers of four or five ranks of notched petals. Thory's text notes it was raised from seed and flowers without pause from mid-May to the first frosts.
proposals.imageObservation: A low, much-branched rose with three open flowers - two densely double, one half open - in soft pink, plus several pointed buds, on thin nearly smooth stems with small leaflets.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The Thory claims check out. A search-surfaced transcription of the Les Roses text for Rosa indica pumila states the shrub reaches only about eight to ten inches, that its branched stems carry scattered nearly straight thorns, that it was obtained from seed (by M. Colleville) and that it flowers without interruption from mid-May until the frosts - matching 'under a foot tall', 'sparse straight prickles', 'raised from seed' and 'mid-May to the first frosts' in the description. Source: c82.net page text as indexed by search (the page itself is Cloudflare-blocked).

proposals.title: Rosa Indica
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa indica in a near-white Bengal form, its pale petals set above glossy leaflets on a slender stem. The stipple engraving was printed in colour from a single plate and finished by hand, the method used across all three volumes of Les Roses.
proposals.imageObservation: A near-white double rose fully open, with a second half-open bloom above it and several buds, on a prickly stem with grey-green toothed leaflets.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Subject (a near-white Bengal/China rose) and the printing method are both sound. 'Glossy leaflets' is the one soft spot — in this reproduction the foliage reads matte and slightly glaucous — but leaf sheen is not reliably judgeable from a restored scan, so I have not made it a finding.

proposals.title: Rosa Indica
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa indica in a crimson-violet form, its nearly full corolla gathered in an umbel at the branch tips above five or seven pointed leaflets edged in colour. The text marks it as a sub-variety of the crimson-flowered Indian rose, set apart by its deep violet-crimson tone.
proposals.imageObservation: Deep crimson-to-violet double roses clustered at the tips of the branches, with buds; leaves of five to seven pointed leaflets, some edged reddish; a prickly stem; plain white ground.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Colour, doubling and the clustered arrangement at the branch tips all match the plate. The sentence attributed to 'the text' could not be checked (c82.net blocked) but restates what the varietal name subviolacea already asserts.

proposals.title: Rosa Inermis
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa inermis, the thornless rose, a dense bush four or five feet high with smooth green branches free of prickles and soft-pink double flowers two inches or more across. Thory's text notes it as one of the first roses to flower in the garden each year.
proposals.imageObservation: A single large soft-pink double rose with two buds, on smooth green stems that carry no prickles at all; leaflets are broad, toothed and dark green.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The thornless stems and soft-pink double flowers are exactly as described. The habit claims ('a dense bush four or five feet high', 'two inches or more across') and the flowering-time note attributed to Thory cannot be checked from the plate or from c82.net (bot challenge); they are plausible for a plate description drawn from Thory's text and nothing contradicts them, so I did not touch them. If a later pass can reach the c82/Thory text, these are the sentences to confirm.

proposals.title: Rosa Leucantha
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa leucantha, a tall leafy bush with strong red hooked prickles and large flowers of five white petals faintly pink at the top, notched at the heart, gathered in a corymb. The plate appeared in the first volume of Les Roses, issued in 1817.
proposals.imageObservation: A branching stem with strong pink hooked prickles, carrying a cluster of six or seven white five-petalled flowers with yellow stamens at the top left, plus buds and dark receptacles, above compound leaves of five to seven grey-green leaflets.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Everything checkable in the plate matches: hooked reddish prickles, five white petals notched at the tip, flowers gathered in a corymb. 'Faintly pink at the top' is at the edge of what the reproduction shows (the petals read as white). The volume/date claim only restates the record's own year of 1817, which is the year of the first volume of Les Roses.

proposals.title: Rosa Lheritieranea
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa lheritieranea, a climbing rose laden with flowers whose four or five ranks of petals curl back over the stamens, violet-pink and white toward the claw, each often crossed by a pale line. Claude-Antoine Thory supplied the botanical text for the plate.
proposals.imageObservation: A crowded cluster of semi-double violet-pink to crimson roses with several ranks of petals rolling back from yellow stamens; the petals pale toward the base and several carry a pale central stripe. Buds and one spent flower accompany them on a nearly prickle-free green stem with large leaflets.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The petal ranks, reflexing over the stamens, the violet-pink colour paling to white at the claw and the pale line on individual petals are all visible in the plate. Thory's authorship of the text is correct for Les Roses. 'A climbing rose' is consistent with R. lheritieranea being a Boursault climber; the plate shows only a cut spray, so the habit is not verifiable from the image but is not contradicted.

proposals.title: Rosa Mollissima
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa mollissima, a four-foot rose of the soft-leaved group whose oval leaflets are so downy they feel like fine cloth, bearing flowers of four ranks of petals in a softened carmine and white. The plate belongs to the second volume of Les Roses, issued in 1821.
proposals.imageObservation: A spray of five pale pink semi-double roses, two of them fully open with yellow stamens showing, on a stem with oval, matte grey-green leaflets that read as downy.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Nothing in the description is contradicted by the plate: the flowers are pale carmine-pink with a few ranks of petals and visible stamens, and the leaflets are oval and matte. Two specifics could not be checked because c82.net is behind a bot challenge — the four-foot height and the 'four ranks of petals'. Both are the kind of detail Thory's text supplies and neither is doing load-bearing work, so I left the text alone. Volume 2 of Les Roses is correctly dated 1821.

proposals.title: Rosa Montezumae
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa montezumae, a wild rose with pink bloom and toothed leaflets on a thorned stem. The plate comes from the first volume of Les Roses, published in 1817; the stipple engraving was printed in colour and finished by hand in watercolour.
proposals.imageObservation: A branching stem with two open pale-pink five-petalled flowers with yellow stamens, one bud and one spent flower, small toothed leaflets and scattered prickles on a bare white ground.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Everything asserted is either visible (single pink blooms, toothed leaflets, prickles) or is the standard, uncontested account of how Les Roses was produced (colour-printed stipple engraving finished by hand; volume 1, 1817, matching the record's year). The only looseness is 'pink bloom' in the singular where the plate shows two — not worth a verdict.

proposals.title: Rosa Moschata
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa moschata, the musk rose, with strong broad hooked prickles, oblong dark-green leaflets and faintly scented white flowers borne in a panicle on slender glandular stalks. Claude-Antoine Thory wrote the descriptive text that accompanied Redoute's plate.
proposals.imageObservation: Botanical plate: a branching musk rose with white five-petalled flowers and yellow stamens borne in a many-flowered panicle, buds on slender stalks, mid-green pointed leaflets, red hooked prickles on the stem, and a single detached red hip figured at lower left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Thory's text for this plate (recovered through search of the c82.net page) reads: flowers in panicles, slightly fragrant, white, on slender pedicels with glandular hairs; stems armed with strong, broad, hooked prickles. The description paraphrases it closely, including 'faintly scented', which at first looks wrong for a musk rose but matches the source.

proposals.title: Rosa Moschata
proposals.currentDescription: A semi-double musk rose, its white corolla of three or four ranks of petals above leaflets woolly beneath, differing from the single form only in its fuller flower and sparser prickles. Thory's text recounts the rose's musk scent and its use in distilling attar of roses in the East.
proposals.imageObservation: A corymb of many white semi-double roses with yellow stamens at the top of a leafy stem; long pointed leaflets, paler on their undersides, a few prickles low on the stem; plain white ground.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The visual claims (semi-double white flowers, clustered bloom, sparse prickles) match the plate. The two claims sourced to Thory's text — the musk scent and attar distilling, and the comparison with the single form — could not be checked because c82.net is behind a bot challenge; they are consistent with what is generally written about Rosa moschata but are unverified here. Left unchanged.

proposals.title: Rosa Muscosa
proposals.currentDescription: A white form of the moss rose, its petals a white washed with very tender pink, otherwise matching the ordinary moss rose in habit and the glandular growth that names it. Thory's text notes the flower is never truly white, despite the name it was given.
proposals.imageObservation: A white double rose in full bloom with a faint pink flush at the centre, three unopened buds whose sepals and stalks are covered in dense green glandular 'moss', and a stem thickly set with fine bristles below.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The image supports every visual claim: white petals with a very faint pink tint at the heart, the mossy glandular calyces and bristly stems that name the moss rose. The sentence attributed to Thory ('the flower is never truly white') cannot be verified because c82.net is behind a bot challenge, but it is consistent with what the plate shows rather than contradicted by it, so I left it alone rather than 'fixing' it.

proposals.title: Rosa Mucosa Anemone-Flora
proposals.currentDescription: An anemone-flowered moss rose, an upright eighteen-inch bush thick with straight prickles, its four or five ranks of deep-pink petals converging toward the centre, some flecked with paler pink. Thory's text records it was raised from seed by M. Lemeunier and named for his town, La Fleche.
proposals.imageObservation: A moss rose: one open deep-pink many-petalled flower, some petals streaked paler, and two buds whose calyx tubes are thick with moss-like bristles; the stems are densely covered in fine straight prickles.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The Lemeunier / La Fleche anecdote survives checking: searches surface this variety as 'Muscosa Anemone-flora — La Mousseuse de la Fleche', and a related centifolia variety carries the epithet 'lemeunierana' (Ser. in DC., Prodr. 2: 619, 1825), so the name and the raiser are both attested outside the description. The eighteen-inch height is unverifiable but consistent with a Thory-derived text.

proposals.title: Rosa Multiflora
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa multiflora in a flesh-pink form, its many small flowers clustered along arching canes above toothed leaflets. The stipple engraving was printed in colour from a single plate and finished by hand, the method used across all three volumes of Les Roses.
proposals.imageObservation: Arching canes carrying several tight clusters of small, double, pale flesh-pink flowers with green buds, above sharply toothed leaflets.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Colour-printed stipple engraving finished by hand is the documented technique of Les Roses, and the visual (clustered small double pink flowers on arching canes) matches. Nothing here that the image or general knowledge contradicts.

proposals.title: Rosa Multiflora
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa multiflora in a broad-leaved purple form, its flowers larger than the pink type and its leaflets three or four times bigger, rounded and broad. Thory's text records that Noisette introduced it to France, having found it near London grown from seed received from Japan.
proposals.imageObservation: A dense corymb of small double roses ranging from pale pink through rose to deep crimson-purple, carried above unusually large, broad, rounded leaflets on a green stem with a few scattered bristles.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The broad rounded leaflets and the purple-toned cluster match the description. The Noisette anecdote is confirmed: Noisette saw the plant in a market-gardener's garden near London in 1817 and was given the whole plant, raised from seed received from Japan, and Thory published the variety in Redoute & Thory, Roses vol. 2 (1821), which also matches the record's year.

proposals.title: Rosa Muscosa
proposals.currentDescription: A very double moss rose, its many ranks of petals crumpled and rolled at the centre, barely showing the spreading styles, the bloom sometimes more than three inches across. The moss-like glandular growth on the calyx names the rose; Claude-Antoine Thory supplied the botanical text.
proposals.imageObservation: Botanical plate: one very double pale-pink moss rose in full bloom, its centre petals crumpled and deeper pink, with several buds whose calyces and stems are covered in dense mossy glandular bristles; grey-green leaves below.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The visual claims all check out: very double bloom, crumpled rolled centre, no visible styles/stamens, and the mossy glandular calyx that gives the moss rose its name. 'sometimes more than three inches across' is a size figure I cannot verify (c82.net blocked) but it is hedged and harmless. Thory as author of the Les Roses text is correct.

proposals.title: rosa noisettiana
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa noisettiana, a tall shrub bearing clusters of pale rose-washed double flowers that open in succession at the branch tips, set among five to seven leaflets. Named for Philippe Noisette, it carried as many as a hundred and thirty blooms in a single panicle. The stipple engraving was printed in colour and finished by hand.
proposals.imageObservation: Botanical plate: a dense head of many white to blush semi-double flowers with yellow stamens, with pink buds opening around and below them, on stems with compound green leaves.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The 130-flowers-in-a-panicle detail, which looked like the classic hallucination signature, checks out: descriptions of Rosa x noisettiana report groups of up to 130 flowers blooming in succession. The rose is named for Philippe Noisette, who sent it from Charleston to his brother in Paris. Leaflet count and the successive opening at branch tips are consistent with the plate.

proposals.title: Rosa Noisettiana Purpurea
proposals.currentDescription: A rose-flowered Noisette, smaller in every part than the Philippe Noisette type, its bright pink petals deepening rather than fading as they age. Redoute drew it for the third volume of Les Roses (1824), the descriptive text supplied by Claude-Antoine Thory.
proposals.imageObservation: A tall prickly reddish stem carrying clusters of small deep pink to purplish double flowers and many buds, with toothed leaflets; white ground.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The comparison with the Philippe Noisette type and the ageing-colour claim are plate-text paraphrase that I cannot verify either way, but nothing in the image contradicts them; Thory as author of the Les Roses text and the vol. 3 / 1824 dating are both correct.

proposals.title: rosa orbessanea
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa orbessanea, the Rosier d'Orbessan, shown in flower with its foliage on a single folio sheet. Redoute drew it for Les Roses, issued in three volumes between 1817 and 1824; the plate was stipple-engraved, printed in colour, and finished by hand in watercolour.
proposals.imageObservation: A pale pink semi-double rose at the top of a densely bristled stem, with a bud and a spent flower on a side branch and abundant toothed pinnate foliage.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Description is generic but everything it asserts is supported: single sheet showing flower and foliage, Les Roses in three volumes 1817-1824, and the stipple-engraving / colour-printing / hand-finishing technique standard for the series.

proposals.title: Rosa Parviflora
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa parviflora, a low North American shrub reaching about two feet, its double flowers a pretty rose colour paler at the centre than the edge, above five-leaflet foliage. The stipple engraving was printed in colour from a single plate and finished by hand in watercolour.
proposals.imageObservation: Two fully double pink roses, the centres paler than the outer petals, with several bristly buds on a branching, sparsely prickled stem; compound leaves mostly of five serrated leaflets.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Double flowers, the paler centres, and the five-leaflet foliage all check out against the plate on magnification. 'A low North American shrub reaching about two feet' is a habit claim I could not verify (c82.net unreachable), but Rosa parviflora is a North American species and the height is not contradicted by anything, so I left it.

proposals.title: Rosa Pimpinellifolia
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa pimpinellifolia in a white double form, the burnet rose with small leaflets and pale blooms. Redoute drew it for the second volume of Les Roses (1821); Claude-Antoine Thory wrote the accompanying botanical text.
proposals.imageObservation: A burnet rose branch with one fully open white double flower with a yellow centre, two white buds in dark purple calyces, many small rounded leaflets, and reddish stems densely armed with fine straight prickles.
proposals.reviewerNotes: White double form, small leaflets and pale blooms are all confirmed by the plate. The 1821 second-volume attribution agrees with the catalogue year; Thory's text authorship is standard for Les Roses. c82.net unreachable, so the volume assignment is knowledge-based rather than source-confirmed.

proposals.title: Rosa Pimpinellifolia Major
proposals.currentDescription: A sub-variety of the burnet rose with five large petals irregularly streaked in greyish-white, pale rose, and deeper pink, yellow toward the claw, above leaflets in sevens to elevens. The branches bristle with many fine, nearly straight prickles, and the small hips ripen from red to black. Claude-Antoine Thory supplied the botanical text.
proposals.imageObservation: Two open five-petalled roses whose whitish petals are irregularly streaked and flushed with crimson and pink, around a broad ring of yellow stamens; below them a low branching plant with many small oval leaflets in long pinnate ranks and canes densely covered in fine straight bristles, plus two dark buds or hips.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Everything checks against the plate: five streaked petals, the yellow centre, many-paired small leaflets, densely bristly nearly straight prickles. The blackening hips are a real trait of the burnet rose, and Thory did write the botanical text for Les Roses. The file URL (roses-106) matches Les Roses pl. 106, sold as 'Variegated flowering variety of Burnet Rose', which confirms the identification.

proposals.title: Rosa Pimpinellifolia
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa pimpinellifolia, the burnet rose, reaching three to four feet in cultivation with prickly reddish stems and large fragrant white flowers tinged yellow at the claw. Its black hips hang nodding at maturity. Redoute drew it for the first volume of Les Roses (1817).
proposals.imageObservation: Single five-petalled white roses with dense yellow stamens on a densely prickly stem with small pinnate leaflets; a black, rounded hip is drawn separately at the lower right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Burnet rose correctly identified; the black hip is actually depicted, which is the checkable part. Height ('three to four feet'), scent and the yellow claw come from the unfetchable plate text but are consistent with the species. 'Prickly reddish stems' is a shade off - the stems here read greenish-brown with reddish bristles - but too small to call. The plate is the variety mariaeburgensis (per the id); the description treats it as the species, which is an omission rather than an error.

proposals.title: Rosa Pimpinellifolia
proposals.currentDescription: A small burnet rose barely a foot high, the plate showing a single shoot cut near the root, its brown stems crowded with straight prickles and bearing white, heart-notched five-petalled flowers that hold a cupped form. The hips ripen from red to black. Claude-Antoine Thory wrote the descriptive text for the plate.
proposals.imageObservation: A slender burnet-rose shoot with dark reddish-brown stems densely covered in straight prickles and bristles, small many-leafleted pinnate leaves, and about six small white five-petalled flowers with yellow stamens; no hips are shown.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Straight prickles, white notched petals and the single cut shoot all match the plate. 'The hips ripen from red to black' cannot be checked against the image (no hips are drawn) but is true of Rosa pimpinellifolia, and Thory's authorship of the Les Roses text is well established. 'Barely a foot high' is consistent with the 'pumila' form named in the id but is not independently verifiable; it is a species claim rather than a picture claim, so it does not lower the verdict.

proposals.title: Rosa Pomponia
proposals.currentDescription: A nearly single form of the pompon rose, a slender shrub under two feet with flowers of six or seven petals, less prickly than the double pompon. Its small elongated red hips often abort before ripening. Redoute drew it for the second volume of Les Roses (1821).
proposals.imageObservation: A slender rose branch with pale pink, nearly single flowers of about five or six petals around yellow stamens, several buds, prickly stems, and small elongated red hips at the right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The near-single flowers, the sparse prickles and the small elongated red hips are all visible and match the description. Height ('under two feet'), the comparison with the double pompon, and the note that the hips abort come from Thory and cannot be checked from the image, but none is contradicted. Les Roses volume two is 1821, which matches the record's year.

proposals.title: Rosa Pomponia
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa pomponia, the pompon rose, a low branchy bush with five wrinkled grey-green leaflets and sweetly scented double flowers in a pretty rose that deepens toward the centre. The pedicels and calyx carry sticky black stalked glands. The stipple engraving was printed in colour and finished by hand.

issues.quote: sticky black stalked glands
issues.problem: The stalked glands on the pedicels and calyx in the plate read reddish-brown, not black.
issues.evidence: image — glandular bristles on the flower stalks and sepals are drawn in a red-brown tone

proposals.imageObservation: Botanical plate: a branchy spray with four open pink double flowers (globular, deeper pink at the centre), several buds, grey-green toothed leaflets and stems and pedicels set with fine bristly glands; white ground.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Flower form (double, pompon, deepening toward the centre), the glandular pedicels and the general leaf character all match the plate; leaf counts of five leaflets are visible on several leaves. The colour of the glands is the only thing I would soften, and it is minor enough not to move the verdict. The height/scent claims come from Thory's text and could not be checked (c82.net 403).

proposals.title: Rosa Pomponiana
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa pomponiana, a fairly bushy sub-shrub under a metre with five oval leaflets and small, usually double flowers of deep purple-red, long confused with the Pompon de Bordeaux. The botanist De Candolle described it in the Flore Francaise, the source Thory reproduced for this plate.

issues.quote: long confused with the Pompon de Bordeaux
issues.problem: Possibly a slip for 'Pompon de Bourgogne', the famous small pompon that Redoute plates separately as Rosa Pomponia Burgundiaca and that is the variety usually cited as the source of confusion. 'Pompon de Bordeaux' does exist as a rose name, so I cannot call it wrong - only unverified.
issues.evidence: web search - Redoute/Thory plate 'Rosa Pomponia Burgundiaca; Rosier Pompon de Bourgogne' is a separate, well-documented plate; no source found linking this plate to a 'Pompon de Bordeaux'

issues.quote: The botanist De Candolle described it in the Flore Francaise, the source Thory reproduced for this plate.
issues.problem: Plausible bibliography (De Candolle's Flore francaise, 1805-1815, is the right kind of source and Thory routinely quoted it) but not confirmed for this species.
issues.evidence: web search - Flore francaise authorship confirmed, the specific Rosa pomponiana entry not

proposals.imageObservation: A bushy rose about as wide as it is tall, with two fully double crimson pompon flowers, several buds, and many five-leaflet leaves on slender green stems.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Visual claims hold: bushy habit, leaves of five leaflets, small very double deep crimson-purple flowers. Both flagged items are cheap for a human with Thory's text to settle; neither is contradicted by anything I have, so I left the verdict at accurate with low confidence rather than inventing a correction.

proposals.title: Rosa Pomponiana Muscosa
proposals.currentDescription: A mossy pompon rose under a foot high, its stem crowded with small prickles mixed with glandular hairs and its pedicels and calyx coated in sticky branched growth like moss. The corolla runs to eight or ten rows of petals in the colour of the ordinary pompon. Redoute drew it for the third volume of Les Roses (1824).
proposals.imageObservation: A moss rose: two open pink double flowers with many small petals, and a crowd of buds whose pedicels and calyces are thickly coated in green-brown branched mossy glands; the stem is dense with fine prickles.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The mossy glandular calyces and pedicels, the prickly stem and the many-rowed pompon flowers are all clearly in the plate; the third volume (1824) matches the record's year. 'Under a foot high' cannot be checked from a plate that shows only a cut stem, but is consistent with the dwarf pompon it names.

proposals.title: Rosa Rapa
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa rapa in a semi-double form, the Rosier Turneps, shown in flower with its foliage. Redoute drew it for the second volume of Les Roses (1821); the stipple engraving was printed in colour from a single plate and finished by hand.

issues.quote: shown in flower with its foliage
issues.problem: House style asks the first sentence to say what is literally in frame; this one is close to contentless (colour, semi-double form and the cluster of blooms go unmentioned).
issues.evidence: image — three semi-double crimson-pink blooms in a cluster plus several buds

proposals.imageObservation: A stem carrying a cluster of three semi-double crimson-pink roses at the right, a nodding bud at the upper left and several buds, with green leaflets on two side branches and a bristly stem.
proposals.reviewerNotes: No factual problem: the semi-double form, volume/date (vol. 2, 1821) and the colour-printed-and-hand-finished stipple technique are all correct, and 'Rosier Turneps' is the name Redouté/Thory use for Rosa rapa. Only a style thinness, so I left the verdict accurate and wrote no replacement.

proposals.title: Rosa Reclinata
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa reclinata in its single-flowered form, a near-thornless climber with seven-leaflet leaves and soft pink, heart-notched petals, the buds bending toward the ground before opening then straightening. Its hips are nearly round and red. Redoute drew it for the third volume of Les Roses (1824).
proposals.imageObservation: A single five-petalled pink rose with a ring of yellow stamens and notched petal tips, one spent flower or bud with reflexed sepals above it, leaves of five to seven leaflets, and a stem carrying a scattering of curved prickles.
proposals.reviewerNotes: I initially suspected 'near-thornless' contradicted the visible prickles, but the botanical literature describes Rosa x reclinata (the Boursault rose) as a sparsely armed climber whose buds nod before opening — which matches both the epithet and the description. The plate does show a fair number of prickles, so 'near-thornless' is at the generous end of accurate. Hips are not shown; that claim rests on Thory. Sources: treesandshrubsonline.org/articles/rosa/rosa-x-reclinata/. Plate 154 is consistent with volume three, 1824.

proposals.title: Rosa Reclinata
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa reclinata in its near-double form of about twenty petals, otherwise identical to the single Rosier a Boutons Renverses, a tall climber whose buds nod earthward before rising to open. The stipple engraving was printed in colour and finished by hand, the method used across all three volumes.
proposals.imageObservation: Botanical plate: pink semi-double roses, one fully open with many petals and a cluster of others at left, several buds hanging over on their stalks, dark green leaflets on a stout green stem.
proposals.reviewerNotes: 'Tall climber' and the nodding buds check out: Trees and Shrubs Online describes Rosa x reclinata as a sparsely armed climber with semi-double purplish-pink flowers whose buds nod in the bud stage, the source of the epithet. 'About twenty petals' could not be checked but matches a semi-double.

proposals.title: rosa redutea glauca
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa redutea glauca, a shrub to about three feet with glaucous five-part leaves rose-tinged beneath and white petals washed with pink, marked inside with dark red dots and striped outside with reddish bands. The name honours Redoute himself, flower painter to Empress Josephine. The plate was drawn for the first volume of Les Roses (1817).
proposals.imageObservation: Three open white roses flushed with pink, yellow stamens, on reddish prickly canes with glaucous grey-green pinnate leaves tinged rose at the stalks; one bud and two young hips.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Colour, glaucous foliage and rose-tinged stalks match the plate; Redoute was flower painter to Empress Josephine and the epithet honours him, both well established. I could not confirm 'five-part leaves' - several leaves in the plate appear to carry seven leaflets - nor the 'dark red dots' inside the petals at this resolution; a later pass with the full-size image could settle the leaflet count.

proposals.title: Rosa Redutea
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa redutea in its rubescens form, shown in flower with its foliage on a single sheet. Named for Redoute, the plate appeared in the first volume of Les Roses (1817); it was stipple-engraved, printed in colour, and finished by hand in watercolour.
proposals.imageObservation: Botanical plate: one open five-petalled rose-red flower with a yellow centre, two buds, a green hip with long sepals, and blue-green pinnate leaflets on a densely prickly stem.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Rosa redutea was named for Redoute, and vol. 1 of Les Roses is 1817, matching the record year. The stipple-engraved, colour-printed, hand-finished technique is the established method of the publication. Nothing in the description conflicts with the image; it is thin but not wrong.

proposals.title: Rosa Rubifolia
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa rubifolia, the bramble-leaved rose, to three or four feet with reddish hooked prickles, soft crisped leaflets, and clusters of five-petalled flowers in soft rose that fade to white. Its styles are fused into a smooth column as in Rosa arvensis. Redoute drew it for the third volume of Les Roses (1824).
proposals.imageObservation: Two clusters of single five-petalled roses — one soft pink, one nearly white with a yellow eye — plus tight buds; the leaflets are large and crisped, and the stems carry stout hooked red prickles.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The visual claims (hooked reddish prickles, crisped leaflets, clusters of five-petalled pink flowers fading paler) all match. The botanical aside about the styles fused into a column, as in Rosa arvensis, is correct for R. setigera / rubifolia and is not something the reproduction can show either way. The stated height ('three or four feet') cannot be checked; R. setigera is normally a long, trailing climber, so if a later pass can reach Thory's text, that is the phrase to confirm.

proposals.title: Rosa Rubiginosa
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa rubiginosa, the sweetbriar, a hedgerow rose to five or six feet with hooked prickles and rough leaflets whose glandular undersides give off a winey scent when crushed. Its flowers gather two to five at the branch tips on bristly stalks. The stipple engraving was printed in colour and finished by hand.
proposals.imageObservation: A sweetbriar branch with three open pale-pink single flowers and buds clustered at the tip, strongly hooked red prickles along the stems, small rounded serrate leaflets, and a separate enlarged red-brown hip figured at lower right.
proposals.reviewerNotes: The cluster of two to five flowers at the branch tip, the hooked prickles and the bristly flower stalks are all visible. Height ('five or six feet') and the scent of the crushed leaves are Thory-style textual facts I cannot check against the image, but both are standard sweetbriar description and not the confident-specific kind of claim that usually signals fabrication. Colour-printed stipple engraving finished by hand is correct for Les Roses.

proposals.title: Rosa Rubiginosa
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa rubiginosa, the sweetbriar of Crete, shown with its prickled stems and glandular foliage. The stipple engraving was printed in colour from a single plate and finished by hand, the method used across all three volumes of Les Roses.
proposals.imageObservation: A single open five-petalled pink rose with a broad yellow centre, on a stem carrying stout hooked reddish prickles; small rounded leaflets, several buds, and a glandular-bristly receptacle below the flower.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Everything asserted is either visible (prickled stems, glandular foliage) or is the standard account of Redoute's technique for Les Roses (colour-printed stipple engraving finished by hand). Note the artwork as catalogued is Nicholas Rougeux's digital restoration after Redoute, so the technique sentence describes the original plate rather than the file; that is how the rest of the folder reads too, so I did not treat it as an error.

proposals.title: Rosa Rubiginosa
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa rubiginosa in its woodland eglantine form, a tall briar with hooked spines, five pale-green leaflets and small soft-pink flowers notched at the petal tips. The ovoid hips ripen red and keep a few of the bristles from the young calyx tube.
proposals.imageObservation: Three single pale-pink five-petalled flowers with notched petal tips and yellow centres on a branching briar with red hooked prickles, pinnate green leaflets, and a cluster of bristly unripe hips at the left.
proposals.reviewerNotes: Everything asserted is visible in the plate (hooked spines, notched petals, bristly calyx tubes on the young hips) or is standard for R. rubiginosa (red hips). The hips in the plate are still green-red rather than ripe, but the description says they 'ripen red', which is a statement about the plant, not the sheet.

proposals.title: Rosa Rubiginosa
proposals.currentDescription: Rosa rubiginosa, here the form named for Queen Elizabeth, with its glandular sweetbriar foliage and prickled stems. Redoute was flower painter to Empress Josephine, whose garden at Malmaison held the rose collection from which Les Roses grew.
proposals.imageObservation: Two large semi-double pink roses with yellow stamens, buds with glandular bristly receptacles, prickled stems and toothed leaflets on a white ground.
proposals.reviewerNotes: I treated 'named for Queen Elizabeth' as a likely hallucination and checked it: the plate is catalogued as 'Rosa Rubiginosa Zabeth; Rosier rubigineux Reine Elisabeth' / 'Eglantine de la Reine Elisabeth' (NYPL Digital Collections; The Old Print Shop), so the claim holds. Second sentence is context-only, but nothing in it is wrong (Redoute was Josephine's flower painter).

proposals.title: Rosa Rubiginosa
